text: summary A whoop is a 65–75 mm aircraft with prop guards running on a single cell 1S . It is what people most often start with, and it is the most convenient thing to train on at home. It is not built like a 5": one “5-in-1” board instead of a stack, an ELRS receiver inside the flight controller firmware, and half of the voltage loss comes from the connector and the cell itself. After this module you choose a micro class for the job, calculate 1S sag from internal resistance and the connector, understand what you pay for an AIO, stay out of the “Betaflight 2025.12 + radio on ELRS 4.x” trap, and know which Betaflight parameters set a whoop apart from a five-inch. The lab needs no hardware: calculating the drop across the connector and finding three errors in a training diff . theory Micro classes: what to choose The answer to “which size do I get first”: for an apartment — 65 mm 1S, for a yard with no wind — 75 mm 1S, for a park — 3–3.5" under 250 g. It makes sense to buy the first aircraft as a BNF ready-made, for your own radio : you will have to solder during repairs anyway, and building from scratch is better left for the second one. The order of purchases, the radio, the goggles and the budget of the whole kit are in f-starter-kit . Class Power Motors, KV Props Dry weight Battery Flight time Where to fly --- --- --- --- --- --- --- --- Whoop 65 mm 1S 0702 less often 0802 , 23,000–30,000 31 mm, 2–3 blades 15–20 g 1S 260–300 mAh 3–4 min estimate room, hall Whoop 75 mm 1S 0802, 22,000–28,000 40 mm 20–24 g 1S 450–580 mAh 5–7 min apartment, yard in calm air Whoop 75–85 mm 2S 1002–1103, 10,000–15,000 estimate 40–50 mm 30–45 g estimate 2S 300–450 mAh 3–5 min estimate yard, outdoors Toothpick 2–3" 1S–3S S to match the motor KV, f-aero-props , “KV for the prop”; estimate 1102–1404, 5,000–11,000 estimate open 2–3" 35–80 g estimate 2S–3S 300–550 mAh 3–6 min estimate outdoors, park 3.5" under 250 g 3S–4S S to match the motor KV, f-aero-props , “KV for the prop”; estimate 1404–1505, 3,000–4,600 estimate 3.5" 110–160 g, takeoff weight < 250 g estimate 4S 650–850 mAh 5–9 min estimate park, freestyle Where the numbers come from. The 65 and 75 mm rows are manufacturer product pages and Oscar Liang's review as of November 2026: the record 65 mm build is 15.4 g, a production BNF is 17.1 g, typically 18–20 g; the BETAFPV Air75 II is 20.2–21.3 g, 0802 motors at 22,000 / 25,000 / 28,000 KV, claimed time 6:50–7:30 on 480 mAh. The claimed time is a calm hover. Rows marked “estimate” are orders of magnitude from catalogs, not verified on specific products. KV for your cell count and where to start within the range from the middle; closer to the top for a light and racing build, to the bottom for a heavy one — the rule “KV × cell count is almost constant for one prop” and Oscar Liang's table in f-aero-props : a 75 mm whoop on 2S is listed there at 12,000–14,000 KV, a 3.5" on 4S at 2500–4000 cinewhoop and freestyle ; the estimates in this table agree with them in order of magnitude. The table follows a single logic: the smaller the prop, the higher the KV and RPM and the lower the efficiency f-aero-props . An 0802 motor at 28,000 KV on 3.8 V gives about 106,000 RPM with no load. Hence 3–7 minutes of flight and currents of up to 9 A per motor BETAFPV 0802 28,000 KV datasheet: 9 A, 34 W . 1S or 2S. 1S is quieter, lighter and safer indoors. 2S gives a thrust margin for outdoors, but it is hard to control in a room. 85 mm frames are usually built for 2S. Weight also determines the rules: the 250 g threshold applies in many countries, but “under 250 g” does not mean “no rules” f-regulations . Brushed and brushless. The first whoops of the mid-2010s flew on 6 and 7 mm brushed motors: cheap, but the brushes wore out within tens of flights, and thrust dropped from pack to pack. From about 2018–2019 the class moved to brushless 0603–0802 motors with four ESCs on the same board. Betaflight still supports brushed builds: protocol BRUSHED , 16 kHz PWM, motor_idle 700 by default. There are almost no new boards for them. 1S physics: sag, cell and connector On a 5" on 6S, a 0.3 V loss is 1.3 % of the voltage. On a whoop on 1S, the same 0.3 V is 8 %. That is why on 1S every milliohm is counted: U at the board = E − I · R cell + R wire + R connector . - R cell. Small cells have a large one: tens of milliohms. The calculations in this module assume 60 mΩ for 300 mAh an assumption; measure your own cell with the charger . With wear and in the cold it grows 1.5–2 times f-power . - R wire. 22 AWG is 53 mΩ/m. A 2 × 40 mm pigtail gives 4.2 mΩ. - R connector. There are two contacts in the circuit: positive and negative. Connector Contact Current per the manufacturer Contact resistance Remarks --- --- --- --- --- PH2.0 JST PH, 2 mm pitch crimp, AWG 32–24 wire 2 A per contact JST datasheet, AWG 24 ; BETAFPV states 4.5 A for the whoop version ≤ 10 mΩ new, ≤ 20 mΩ after testing JST a signal connector used as a power connector; leaving the market BT2.0 BETAFPV 1.0 mm “banana” 9 A continuous, 15 A peak no figure; estimate — a few mΩ, like the A30 the BETAFPV standard; 22 AWG wire A30 GNB “banana” 15 A, 30 A peak 1.6 mΩ partially mechanically compatible with BT2.0 GNB27 GNB “banana” 9 A continuous, 15 A peak seller's product page; the name hints at 27 A — not confirmed not published not compatible with A30 and BT2.0 The A30 and GNB27 data are taken from seller product pages citing GNB, not from a datasheet. The conclusion does not change because of that: the PH2.0 contact is an order of magnitude worse. At 10 A an aged PH2.0 pair eats 0.40 V and heats up by 4 W, an A30 — 0.03 V and 0.3 W calculation in the practice section . {{diagram:chart-micro-connector-sag With the same cell E = 3.90 V, 60 mΩ a board with an aged PH2.0 sees 3.30 V already at 5.8 A, and with an A30 — only at 8.9 A: the connector takes away a third of the available current.}} The answer to “BT2.0 or PH2.0”: get BT2.0 or A30 and do not mix standards within one battery fleet

text: summary The difference between an assembler and an engineer is not the soldering iron but the method: an engineer knows what the aircraft must do requirements , how it is built architecture , what proves that it does it tests , and leaves a trail that someone else can pick up the work from documentation . This module introduces the method at the very start of the course — using your first build as the example — and sets the format of the “engineering folder”, which from now on is mandatory in every capstone project. The second half covers the “requirement → hypothesis → experiment → log → decision” loop, an error budget per the GUM with a guard-band decision rule, change management and reproducibility; in the lab a Python script checks the T/W ≥ 2.5 requirement with uncertainty and shows which experiment to do next. theory Why a beginner needs this Without requirements, any tuning “worked” or “didn't work” by feel. Without an architecture, troubleshooting is trial and error. Without tests, you don't know what yesterday's change broke. Without documentation, in a month you are a stranger to yourself. The method costs an hour at the start and saves days later; in large projects see the accident analyses its absence costs aircraft and reputations. 1. Requirements A requirement is a statement of what the aircraft must do that can be verified . Format: ID, text, criterion, verification method. ID Requirement Criterion Verification --- --- --- --- R-01 Hovers with a 30 g payload for at least 15 min ≥ 15:00 down to 3.5 V/cell A flight on a timer, a voltage log R-02 T/W at takeoff mass ≥ 2.5 calculated T/W ≥ 2.5; hover throttle in the log ≤ 63 % in ArduPilot — MOT_THST_HOVER ≤ 0.40 Thrust table + log R-03 On loss of link it terminates the flight in place after 1.5 s DROP after 1.5 s a 5" over a safe area: it falls nearby rather than flying away; for 7–10" and flights over people — AUTO-LAND or GPS Rescue, bf-failsafe , “What to choose” A ground test without props + log R-04 Video and RC are not lost up to 1 km at an altitude of 50 m LQ 70%, video without dropouts A field test with recording R-05 Takeoff mass ≤ 900 g scales Weighing Why R-02 has this criterion: at T/W 2.5 the thrust fraction in hover is 1 / 2.5 = 0.40, while the throttle, because thrust is nonlinear, is 56–63 % the 0.65 curve and the square law, the “Hover throttle” table in f-physics . A “throttle ≤ 40 %” criterion would require T/W 4.1–6.25 and would fail even when the requirement is met; 63 % = √ 1 / 2.5 is the upper bound for T/W 2.5. Rules: measurable “fast” is not a requirement, “accelerates to 15 m/s in 3 s” is ; one requirement — one verification; safety and legal requirements — in a separate group S-xx ; the source of every number is stated. 2. Architecture A diagram of blocks and links: what is connected to what, over which interface, where the power comes from. For a drone — three layers on one sheet: - Power : battery → ESC; battery → 5 V BEC → FC, RX, GPS; 9 V BEC → VTX. Currents on the arrows. - Data : RX —CRSF→ FC UART1 ; GPS —UBX→ FC UART2 ; FC —DShot→ ESC; FC —MSP/OSD→ VTX UART3 ; FC —Blackbox→ flash. - Mechanics : where everything sits, masses, center of mass. The architecture answers the question “why exactly this way” with one sentence per decision: “GPS on a mast — the compass away from the power wires see interference ”. {{diagram:eng-architecture-layers The example's architecture on one sheet: power and data as different lines, each data arrow labeled with the interface and port; you label the currents on the power arrows with your own numbers.}} 3. Tests Each requirement → a test with the expected result, the actual result and a date. Tests can be: - Ground without props : ports, motor direction, failsafe, the firmware's pre-flight checks. - Simulation SITL for INAV/ArduPilot/PX4 : missions, failsafe, geofence. - Bench : thrust, current, vibration spectrum. - Flight : hover, range, time. The regression rule: after any configuration change, the ground tests are run, plus the flight test that the change affects. The test table is a living document. 4. Documentation and the change log The minimal engineering folder a git repository : my-drone/ README.md — what it is, what it's for, current state, how to run it requirements.md — the requirements table architecture.md — power/data/mechanics diagrams images + text tests.md — the test table with results config/ — diff all / parameters with date and firmware version logs/ — key logs with a note on what is in them CHANGELOG.md — date, what changed, why, how it was verified The change log is one line per change: 2026-11-08 — D-term 25→30 on roll; goal: remove bounce-back; verification: log 0042, overshoot 12%→6% . This is what “data-driven tuning” means. Traceability The thread requirement → architectural decision → test → result. If it is missing, the project cannot be considered finished: it is unclear what has been proven. In the self-assessment rubric of the capstone projects this is a separate row — “Systems thinking”. What it looks like in professional practice Accident investigation reports the “Analysis of real accidents” module name the same causes time after time: there were no requirements for failures, no failsafe tests, the configuration was changed without a record, the documentation did not match the aircraft. The method is not bureaucracy; it is what separates an engineered aircraft from a pile of parts. {{diagram:traceability Traceability: every requirement has a test, every test has a requirement; a change shows which tests to run again.}} 5. The method loop: requirement → hypothesis → experiment → log → decision Requirements say what must be. The method loop answers how to find out whether it is met, and what to do if it isn't. There are five steps, and each leaves a record in the folder. 1. text: summary A tuned aircraft is useless until your hands know how to control it, and learning on a real one means paying with propellers, motors and other people's safety. This module gives the order of training: a simulator with your own radio in USB joystick mode, Acro mode from the first hour, the same rates in the simulator and in Betaflight, a ladder of exercises with verifiable criteria, a whoop indoors, the first flights in a field with a spotter, and a training log up to the hundredth battery. After this module you can read rates from a configuration and calculate °/s from them, choose a simulator for your computer and draw up a personal plan with measurable gates between the rungs. The lab: a calculation with the real applyActualRates formula and a four-week training plan. theory Why the simulator comes first and how many hours A simulator teaches one thing: the “eyes → fingers” link. It does not convey fear, wind, battery sag or video interference, but a crash in it costs a press of the reset button. How many hours are needed before the first real flight — there is no single figure, and the sources disagree: Source What it says Date --- --- --- Oscar Liang, beginner's guide “at least 5 to 10 hours” in a simulator before the first flight updated in November 2026 Unmanned Tech, knowledge base “Most pilots benefit from 10-20 hours”; also there: the quality of practice matters more than the quantity March 2026 RotorVillage, store blog “10 to 15 hours”, the minimum — “at least three hours” April 2026 Simulator pages Steam, velocidrone.com do not name a number of hours verified 18.11.2026 IntoFPV forum, the thread “starting out with no simulator” opinions differ: some pilots hardly flew in a simulator, some consider it mandatory May 2021 The course's conclusion: hours are a time estimate, not a criterion. The criterion is an exercise performed to its condition the ladder below . The 5–20 hour range shows how long the first four rungs usually take. Your own radio instead of a gamepad Simulators accept a gamepad and a keyboard, but learning on them is not worth it. Oscar Liang: “Avoid using Xbox controllers or keyboards for simulator training”. The reason is mechanical: on a gamepad both sticks are spring-loaded and the travel is short, while on a radio the throttle stick stays where it was left. You will have to buy a radio anyway, so muscle memory is built on it from the first hour. An EdgeTX radio the current stable version is 2.12.5 connects with a USB cable as an HID joystick; no receiver or aircraft is needed: - Radio Setup → USB Mode : Ask , Joystick , Storage , Serial — what the radio does when the cable is connected. With Ask the radio asks for the mode every time; this is the default value 2.12.5 source, hal/usb_driver.h . - Model Setup → USB Joystick → Classic : channels 1–8 go to the axes X, Y, Z, rotX, rotY, rotZ, Dial, Slider, channels 9–32 — to buttons 1–24. The simulator will see the arm switch on channel 5 as an axis. - Advanced : Interface mode Joystick / Gamepad / MultiAxis , Circular cutout and the mode of each channel None , Btn , Axis , Sim . The manual advises starting with Classic. Windows may detect the radio only as a Joystick. After changing the settings the cable must be reconnected. Black-and-white radios with less than 1 MB of flash have no Advanced mode. Create a separate model for the simulator with the RF module turned off, and in the simulator itself go through stick calibration and assign arm to the same switch that will be used on the aircraft. How to build a model and set up the radio itself is in link-edgetx . Simulators Prices and requirements are taken from the store pages on 18.11.2026; the “what for” assessments are from Oscar Liang's review August 2026 . More important than the brand are a stable frame rate and one simulator for the whole training period. The physics differs in all of them, so the transfer to a real aircraft gives the skill, not the exact feel. Rates: the same numbers in the simulator and in Betaflight Rates translate stick deflection into a commanded angular rate. In Betaflight 2025.12 the default type is ACTUAL , and the formula in applyActualRates fc/rc.c is: ω x = C·x + M − C · x · x⁵·e + x· 1 − e , where C = rc_rate ·10, M = srate ·10, e = expo /100, x is the stick deflection from 0 to 1. C is the rate “at center” Center Sensitivity , M is at full stick Max Rate , and e changes only the shape of the curve. The default is 7/67/0: center 70 °/s, maximum 670 °/s. text: summary Betaflight is open-source firmware for multirotor flight controllers with a focus on low-latency control and flexible configuration. This article covers the chain from installing the configurator to the first safe flight. After reading you will be able to: - flash an FC and make a backup of the configuration diff all ; - set up ports, the receiver, modes and sensor calibration; - check the motors and failsafe before flying. theory What Betaflight is Betaflight is a fork of Cleanflight the successor of Baseflight / the STM32 port of MultiWii . The main emphasis of the stack is performance : minimum latency and a high gyro loop rate up to 8 kHz . Supported hardware: flight controllers on STM32 F4, F7, H7, G4 , AT32F435 , APM32 and RP2350 the last two — from 2025.12; 4.5 does not have them . Firmware features: - multiple PID profiles; - gyro and D-term filtering; - digital ESC protocols DShot , ProShot ; - Blackbox for logs; - the CLI for precise configuration. Firmware architecture The firmware is modular, and its tasks run in real time. The main tasks: - Gyro task — reading the gyro up to 8 kHz , the filters. - PID task — the output to the motors from the setpoint vs gyro error. - RX task — the receiver CRSF, SBUS, ELRS and others . - Scheduler — distributing time between the tasks. The PID loop: the pid_process_denom setting defines the PID loop rate. Example: gyro at 8 kHz , pid_process_denom = 1 the default → PID at 8 kHz ; = 2 → 4 kHz . On an F4/G4 with bidirectional DShot and a gyro above 4 kHz the firmware itself raises the denom to at least 2 and changes DSHOT600 to DSHOT300. Firmware versions and compatibility The course follows Betaflight 2025.12 checked against 2025.12.5 . Starting with this branch the version number is calendar-based: year.month.patch. The previous significant branch is 4.5 the course counts renames from 4.5.3; the latest release is 4.5.5, and the 4.5-maintenance branch carries the number 4.5.6, but that is not a release: the src/ code matches 4.5.5 except for the version number in version.h ; the SITL in the module “Betaflight from scratch” is built from it . The 2026.6 tags exist, but they are not the course's target version. What 2025.12 added to 4.5: - altitude and position hold the ALTHOLD and POS HOLD modes , with a common autopilot ap_ for them and for GPS Rescue; - disarm on impact at landing landing_disarm_threshold , a new turtle crashflip_rate ; - for wings: S-term, speed-based TPA, TPA curves; - a chirp generator for system identification the CHIRP mode ; - new gyros IIM-42653, ICM-456xx , the APM32 and RP2350 platforms. In its day the 4.5 branch brought M10 GPS and a reworked GPS Rescue, Earth referencing for Angle / Horizon, fonts for HD VTXs and an RPM filter with harmonic weights — all of that is kept in 2025.12. Important: the 4.5 → 2025.12 transition like 4.4 → 4.5 before it requires a Full Chip Erase and setting things up section by section. Old CLI dumps are incompatible line for line because of renames, ranges and changed meanings of settings — see the table at the end of the theory. The Betaflight ecosystem Besides the firmware there is the configurator. From 2025.12 it is Betaflight App : a web application and PWA https://app.betaflight.com that works through WebUSB / WebSerial , with a version number that matches the firmware before 2025.12 — Betaflight Configurator 10.10, a separate program with its own numbering; a web version was already available for 4.5 . There is a native application for Android. In the course the word “configurator” means Betaflight App; the tab names are the same. Target, unified target and Cloud Build Firmware is built for a target — a description of the board: the processor, which pins go where resource , which gyro is on which SPI bus. Since 4.3 almost all boards are unified targets : one binary per processor family for example, STM32F405 plus a text board config board_name , manufacturer_id , a set of resource / set lines that the configurator loads when flashing. Cloud Build 4.4+ builds the binary on a server with the selected set of features: the receiver protocol, the OSD analog USE_OSD_SD and/or HD USE_OSD_HD , GPS, the magnetometer, telemetry, LED, servos or the WING package, altitude and position hold — what you did not select is not in the firmware the typical causes of “the receiver is silent” and “the OSD disappeared after 2025.12” . version in the CLI shows the version, target, date and git revision of the build; the BUILD KEY the key for reproducing the build is printed by status , and build.betaflight.com returns the list of options for that key. What the scheduler does every 125 µs fc/tasks.c describes the tasks with a period and a priority; scheduler/scheduler.c selects them. The critical ones: GYRO reading, filters and PID taskMainPidLoop : RC command → PID → mixer → DShot — at the gyro rate / pid_process_denom . The rest get what is left: RX receiving and processing frames, event-driven , SERIAL , BATTERY_ , GPS , OSD per osd_framerate_hz , BLACKBOX , TELEMETRY , LED_STRIP . The CLI tasks command shows the actual period, the average and maximum time of every task and the CPU load; status — the gyro rate, the load and the arming flags. Overload 85–90% on an F4 at 8 kHz means skipped tasks, jitter and the LOAD flag: the fix is pid_process_denom = 2 or disabling features. text: summary UART is the basis for connecting the receiver, GPS, telemetry, VTX and other devices to the flight controller in Betaflight. The Ports tab decides whether control reaches the firmware at all. In this article: - how to read a pinout and not take the port used by USB; - wiring for SBUS, CRSF/ELRS, FPort, IBUS, Spektrum; - Serial Rx in the Ports tab + the protocol choice in the Receiver tab; - typical failures MSP , limits, F4/SBUS . theory What a UART is and why ports are configured A UART is a serial interface: a pair of TX transmit and RX receive lines. In the Ports tab every physical UART is given a role: Serial Rx , GPS , telemetry, MSP and so on. The rule: one UART carries one main role for its data stream at a time. Combining, for example, Serial Rx and Telemetry Output on one port without understanding the protocol often produces a conflict and “breaks” the saving of settings. Receiver types and wiring The protocol determines both the wiring and the Serial Receiver Provider setting in the configurator. - SBUS FrSky, Futaba, some DJI — in BF: SBUS . The receiver signal → RX of the chosen UART not TX . - CRSF TBS Crossfire, ExpressLRS — in BF: CRSF . For a serial ELRS receiver the move from 3.x to 4.x changes nothing in the ports the same CRSF, 420000 baud ; an on-board SPI ELRS receiver takes no port, but under 2025.12 it stays on ELRS 3 and will not link with a module on 4.x link-elrs . Receiver RX → FC TX , receiver TX → FC RX the classic crossover connection for full duplex . - FPort FrSky — FrSky FPort ; one wire, and the inversion/pin depend on the board and the version — check the FC manual. - IBUS FlySky, Turnigy — IBUS , signal → RX . - Spektrum DSM — SPEKTRUM1024 / SPEKTRUM2048 , the signal wire per the receiver documentation. F4 and SBUS: some boards have no hardware inverter for the inverted SBUS signal — use the dedicated SBUS pin on the FC or another protocol — for a new build CRSF ELRS : it is not inverted and is full duplex link-protocols , “new builds — CRSF” ; FPort — only if you already have a FrSky receiver, and it has the same dependence of inversion on the board; otherwise an external inverter is needed. Betaflight 4.4+ and Cloud Build From 4.4.0 , a Cloud Build puts only the selected receiver protocols into the firmware. By default only CRSF is selected in Firmware Flasher; SBUS and GHST also have to be selected by hand. IBUS , Spektrum and others must be selected explicitly for the build — otherwise the receiver is “silent” with any wiring. A separate case is an ELRS receiver wired on the board over SPI a whoop AIO : it needs no UART, and its code lives in the Betaflight firmware. In 2025.12 this is ELRS 3 ELRS_OTA_VERSION_ID 3 , so such a board will not link with a transmitter on ELRS 4; ELRS 4 support for SPI receivers appears only in 2026.6. The options: a transmitter on 3.x for this model, or a separate receiver on a UART link-elrs . MSP limits MSP is needed by the configurator and by some devices. The limit: no more than three ports with MSP enabled at the same time; with a fourth the port configuration is considered invalid and at boot all of it is reset to defaults. The check is made by isSerialConfigValid in io/serial.c the same in 4.5 and 2025.12.5 : USB VCP, on which MSP is mandatory, counts toward the three; MSP can share a port only with telemetry, Blackbox or VTX MSP + Displayport , and any other pair of functions on one port — except a few pairs with Serial RX for example, an SBUS receiver on the RX line and FrSky Hub, LTM or MAVLink telemetry on the TX line — also makes the configuration invalid. A port with only the VTX_MSP bit and no MSP is invalid too: this function is allowed only in a pair bitCount == 1 in the same function . {{diagram:bf-serial-valid-tree The port check at boot: more than three ports with MSP or a disallowed pair of functions on one port — and the whole port configuration is reset to defaults.}} Tip: the USB connection to the PC usually uses a separate channel; do not reassign it to the receiver without understanding the board schematic. The serial command: what is actually stored The Ports tab is a wrapper around serial <id <function mask <msp baud <gps baud <telemetry baud <blackbox baud : the port identifier in 2025.12 — a name: UART1 , UART3 , VCP , SOFT1 …; diff writes names, for example serial UART3 64 … . In 4.5 — a number: 0 = UART1, 1 = UART2, … 20 = VCP/USB, 30+ = SoftSerial; 2025.12 accepts the numbers too , the function bit mask MSP = 1, GPS = 2, … Serial RX = 64, Blackbox = 128, ESC Sensor, SmartAudio, Tramp, MSP DisplayPort — their own bits; the exact values are in the serialPortFunction_e enum in src/main/io/serial.h , and the baud rates. That is why diff all contains lines such as serial UART3 64 115200 57600 0 115200 in 4.5 — serial 2 64 115200 57600 0 115200 — UART3 = Serial RX. Reading them is useful when moving configs between boards: UART numbers differ from board to board. The bits of the function mask serialPortFunction_e , src/main/io/serial.h ; the same in 4.5 and 2025.12, except for bit 262144 added in 2025.12 — GIMBAL, a serial gimbal ; the port mask is the sum of the bits of its functions: Bit Function Ports tab label Bit Function Ports tab label --- --- --- --- 1 MSP 1024 ESC Sensor ESC 2 GPS 2048 SmartAudio VTX TBS SmartAudio 4 FrSky Hub telemetry FrSky 4096 IBUS telemetry iBUS 8 HoTT telemetry HoTT 8192 IRC Tramp VTX IRC Tramp 16 LTM telemetry LTM 16384 RunCam Device Protocol Camera RunCam Protocol 32 SmartPort telemetry SmartPort 32768 TF lidar Benewake LIDAR 64 Serial RX Serial Rx 65536 FrSky OSD OSD FrSky Protocol 128 Blackbox Blackbox logging 131072 VTX_MSP VTX MSP + Displayport 512 MAVLink telemetry MAVLink Examples in 2025.12 notation; in 4.5 the numbers 1, 0 and 2 instead of the names : serial UART2 64 … — the receiver; serial UART1 131073 115200 … — an HD system DJI/Walksnail/HDZero : 131073 = MSP 1 + VTX_MSP 131072 , and the 131072 bit alone without MSP gives no OSD bf-hd-osd-

text: summary The receiver sends stick positions to the flight controller using one of several serial protocols. Today the two main ones are the old SBUS FrSky, Futaba and CRSF TBS Crossfire, ExpressLRS . This module explains the physical difference between them, what an “inverted” signal is, why SBUS caused endless problems on F4 controllers, and how to wire each protocol correctly. theory What a UART frame is UART sends bytes serially: a start bit, 8 data bits, an optional parity bit, stop bits. In the idle state the line sits at logical one — the high level. The start bit pulls it down to zero, and the receiver catches that edge and starts counting. What “inverted” means In an inverted signal everything is the other way around: idle is low, a one is low, a zero is high. The data is the same, only the electrical levels are flipped. If you feed an inverted signal into a regular UART, the receiver sees garbage: it waits for the start bit in the wrong place. SBUS - 100000 baud, 8 data bits, even parity, 2 stop bits 8E2 ; - the inverted signal is the protocol standard, not an exception; - 25-byte frame: 16 proportional channels of 11 bits, 2 digital channels, frame lost and failsafe flags; - one-way: receiver → controller only, telemetry goes back over a separate wire SmartPort . The phrase “uninverted SBUS” means a signal that someone flipped back for compatibility. It's a workaround, not a different protocol. Why F4 struggled with SBUS The UART of STM32F4 microcontrollers can't invert its input in hardware. F7, H7 and G4 have a bit for this in the USART register, and inversion is enabled in software. That's why F4 boards put a separate hardware inverter on one UART the pad is usually labeled SBUS , and on the other ports SBUS didn't work without modification. CRSF - a regular uninverted UART, 8N1; - full duplex on two wires TX and RX : channels down, telemetry up over the same port; - the spec speed is 416666 baud for full duplex; it can negotiate higher for lower latency; - the frame has a packet type and a CRC, and the protocol is extensible: channels, telemetry, link statistics, device parameters. Hence the practical rule: CRSF doesn't need an inverter and works on any free UART of any series. CRSF inside per the TBS spec Frame: sync 0xC8 or address length type payload CRC8 ; length = frame size − 2 from 2 to 62 ; CRC8 with polynomial 0xD5 is calculated over the type and payload. The extended header adds destination/origin addresses for device parameters, MSP over CRSF . Key types: - 0x16 RC Channels Packed — 16 channels of 11 bits in 22 bytes; center = 992 ticks = 1500 µs, conversion us = ticks − 992 ·5/8 + 1500 i.e. 172…1811 ticks ↔ 988…2012 µs . With a “cut” type failsafe, frames simply stop arriving — the spec recommends the FC wait ~1 s before its own failsafe procedure. - 0x14 Link Statistics — uplink RSSI of antennas 1/2 dBm·−1 , uplink LQ % , SNR dB , active antenna, RF profile, TX power, downlink RSSI/LQ/SNR. This is exactly where the OSD gets LQ and RSSI dBm. - Telemetry: 0x08 Battery, 0x02 GPS, 0x1E Attitude, 0x21 Flight Mode and others — the FC sends them to the receiver, and the receiver to the radio. Routing: a device with several CRSF ports forwards frames between them a star without loops — that's how the radio sees the FC through the module. {{diagram:crsf-frame CRSF frame: 26 bytes for 16 channels, frame type and CRC8.}} Betaflight receives CRSF at 420000 baud by default serialrx_provider = CRSF ; the spec says 416666 8N1 — the difference is within UART tolerance < 1% . SBUS inside A 25-byte frame every 7–14 ms: 0x0F , 22 bytes × 11-bit channels 1–16 , a flags byte channels 17/18, frame lost , failsafe , 0x00 . Values 172…1811 ↔ 988…2012 µs the same scale as in CRSF — not a coincidence . The receiver sets the failsafe flag when the link is lost — the firmware must read it Betaflight reads the flag automatically , otherwise the FC failsafe will never trigger while the receiver “holds” the last values. {{diagram:sbus-frame SBUS frame: 25 bytes, 16 channels of 11 bits and a flags byte with the failsafe indicator.}} Comparison by latency and reliability Protocol Direction Speed Update Frame latency CRC --- --- --- --- --- --- PWM per channel → — 50 Hz 20 ms no PPM → — ~50 Hz 20+ ms no SBUS → +S.Port separately 100 kbaud, inverted 70–140 Hz 7–14 ms no parity only CRSF ↔ 420 kbaud up to 1 kHz depends on the link 1–4 ms CRC8 Ghost, FPort ↔ 420 k / 115.2 k high / 100 Hz low / medium yes The course's takeaway: new builds — CRSF ELRS/Crossfire/Tracer ; SBUS — only for old hardware. Worked example: the receiver doesn't work F405, an SBUS receiver connected to RX3 , in Ports — Serial RX on UART3, in Receiver — SBUS; no channels. Diagnosis: UART3 on this board has no hardware inverter → garbage. Solutions: move it to the port with the inverter the SBUS / RX1 pad per the board description , or enable serialrx_inverted = ON only on F7/H7, or switch the receiver to CRSF ELRS — then any UART works. Checking with a logic analyzer: idle low = inverted signal the “Measurements” module . practice Connecting CRSF / ExpressLRS to Betaflight 1. Wires crossed over: receiver TX → controller RX, receiver RX → controller TX. Plus 5 V and GND. 2. Ports: enable Serial RX on that UART. 3. Receiver: Serial, CRSF provider, telemetry enabled. 4. In the CLI, check that the port isn't inverted and isn't half-duplex: get serialrx set serialrx_provider = CRSF set serialrx_inverted = OFF set serialrx_halfduplex = OFF save Connecting SBUS 1. On F4 — only to a UART with a hardware inverter the SBUS pad per the board schematic or to a receiver that can output an uninverted signal. 2. On F7/H7 — to any UART, Betaflight will enable the inversion itself. 3. Provider SBUS . Touch the serialrx_inverted parameter only if the receiver outputs uninverted SBUS. Check Receiver tab: the channels move together with the sticks, the channel order matches AETR , the range is around 1000–2000. What you should get and what to writ

text: summary Modes are what you put on switches: arming, self-leveling, the beeper, the failsafe test, flip over after crash. The OSD is what you see in the goggles: voltage, time, link, warnings. This module explains how AUX channel ranges work, which modes are mandatory and which are dangerous, and how to build an OSD that warns you in advance instead of reporting what has already happened. It adds a working switch layout from several 7–10" drones, made so that the hands remember it, and the “machine” level of the OSD: which bits make up osd_ _pos , how the three OSD profiles work and how to change them from a switch, the bit numbers in osd_warn_bitmask and osd_stat_bitmask for 4.5 and 2025.12, and how craft_name differs from pilot_name . The lab is reading aux lines, thresholds and stick commands, then encoding and decoding positions and masks with a Python model of the osd.h macros the run is in the text . theory How the Modes tab works Every mode is bound to an AUX channel and a range of values 1000–2000 µs . When the switch is inside that range, the mode is active. Several modes can share one channel in different ranges a three-position switch . The check is in the tab itself: move the switch and watch which mode is highlighted. Mandatory - ARM — always a separate two-position switch, with no neighbors on the channel. On the bench — props off. - ANGLE — self-leveling. Even if you fly ACRO, keep it on a switch: it saves you when you lose orientation in Stage 2 failsafe ANGLE is turned on automatically, no switch is needed for that . - BEEPER — to find the drone in the grass. - FAILSAFE — a failsafe test from a switch see the failsafe module , the STAGE1 mode. Useful - AIR MODE — the PID controller works at zero throttle; for ACRO it is almost always enabled permanently without a switch . - PREARM — a second switch without which arming is impossible. A must for heavy drones. - FLIP OVER AFTER CRASH — to turn over from the ground after a crash. Only when the drone is lying still and the props touch nothing. - HORIZON — self-leveling that still allows flips; ACRO TRAINER — an angle limit in ACRO for training. - GPS RESCUE — return to home by GPS a separate switch and a separate setup . - BLACKBOX — log only on a switch, if the flash is small. - OSD DISABLE , VTX PIT MODE , PARALYZE — situational. An example layout A layout from several drones of one team, the same on all of them so that there is nothing to think about in the air: ARM on AUX1, ANGLE on AUX3, FAILSAFE STAGE1 on AUX6, BEEPER on AUX7, PREARM on AUX8. The rule: the same switches on every drone you fly. {{lesson:bf-led-buzzer What exactly BEEPER turns on, how to make it beep by itself on link loss through rxfail , and in what order to search for a crashed aircraft.}} OSD The elements are selected in the OSD tab, and the position is stored in the osd_ _pos parameters. The minimum set for safety: voltage average per cell — osd_avg_cell_voltage_pos , a timer, link quality / RSSI, the flight mode, warnings, craft_name . For long range — mAh drawn, GPS satellites, the direction and distance to home. The warnings osd_warn_bitmask : low voltage, failsafe, RXLOSS, arming disable flags. The voltage thresholds are set so that the warning arrives with a margin for the return, not in the last few percent; the numbers by chemistry and class and the check after landing are in f-power “Voltage thresholds” . The analog OSD the MAX7456 chip and the digital one MSP DisplayPort for Walksnail/HDZero/DJI are set up in the same tab, but the set of elements and the resolution differ. The aux command and mode logic aux <index <mode id <aux channel <start <end <logic : the rule index, the mode id — the permanentId from msp/msp_box.c ARM = 0, ANGLE = 1, HORIZON = 2, FAILSAFE = 27, PREARM = 36 , not the number from the enum in fc/rc_modes.h , the AUX channel 0 = AUX1 , a range of 900–2100 in steps of 25, logic 0 = OR, 1 = AND the mode is active only if all the AND rules of that mode are met at the same time — this is how “ARM only if PREARM on the same channel” or two-switch combinations are made . The ranges for a three-position switch: 900–1300, 1300–1700, 1700–2100 — with a margin, so that jitter does not toggle modes at a boundary. A radio switch arrives over CRSF as ≈988 / 1500 / 2012 µs ±100 % of travel; the conversion in crsfReadRawRC in rx/crsf.c : 172 → 988, 992 → 1500, 1811 → 2012 , so 200–312 µs remain to the range boundary. adjrange is the same for in-flight adjustments PID, rates, profile selection from a switch or a pot; of the profiles only the rate, OSD and LED profiles are switched this way, and there is no adjustment for the PID profile neither in 4.5 nor in 2025.12 . The slots, the functions and the VTX on a switch vtx are in the bf-adjustments module. {{diagram:bf-aux-ranges The team layout on the AUX axis: the switch positions ≈988 / 1500 / 2012 µs lie 200–312 µs from the range boundaries, so jitter does not toggle a mode.}} All the mode permanentId values of 2025.12 boxes in msp/msp_box.c ; the numbers 9, 10, 14, 16, 18, 21, 22, 38 belong to removed modes and are not used . The list differs from 4.5 in four lines: id 3 ALTHOLD and id 11 POS HOLD in 4.5 these numbers are empty , id 55 CHIRP absent in 4.5 and the name of id 29 — in 4.5 “3D DISABLE / SWITCH”. The Modes tab shows only the modes that are in the build and make sense for the configuration for example, SERVO1–3 — only with servos : id Mode id Mode --- --- --- --- 0 ARM 32–34 CAMERA CONTROL 1–3 RunCam, bf-features-tour 1 ANGLE 35 FLIP OVER AFTER CRASH turtle 2 HORIZON 36 PREARM 3 ALTHOLD altitude hold, from 2025.12 55 CHIRP from 2025.12, ctl-sysid 11 POS HOLD GPS position hold, from 2025.12 4 ANTI GRAVITY 37 GPS BEEP SATELLITE COUNT 5 MAG 39 VTX PIT MODE link-vtx 6 / 7 HEADFREE / HEADADJ 40–43 USER1–4 PINIO: VTX/camera power 8 CAMSTAB servo gimbal, bf-servos-pwm 44 PID AUDIO 12 PASSTHRU 45 PARALYZE 13 BEEPER 46 GPS RESCUE 15 LEDLOW turn the LED strip off 47 ACRO TRAINER 17 CAL

This module explains how it works, how to choose a procedure for your drone and how to

text: summary Failsafe is what the drone does when the link to the radio is lost. In Betaflight 4.3+ it is a two-stage process: a short “guard” Stage 1, then Stage 2 with the selected procedure DROP, AUTO-LAND or GPS-RESCUE . This module explains how it works, how to choose a procedure for your drone and how to test failsafe safely with a switch, without turning the radio off in the air. theory How Betaflight decides the link is lost After 150 ms without valid packets 100 ms in 4.5 the FC sets RXLOSS. The channels hold their last values for 300 ms from the last good packet not from the detection of the loss , then get the rxfail values. That is Stage 1; Stage 2 is when there has been no signal for longer than failsafe_delay from the last good packet. {{diagram:failsafe-stages Failsafe timing diagram: loss detection, the short hold, Stage 1 and Stage 2.}} {{lesson:link-elrs Why an ELRS receiver simply goes silent on link loss, when it declares a disconnect itself, and what link margin each packet rate has.}} Stage 1 — the guard period It lasts failsafe_delay in tenths of a second: 15 = 1.5 s; 1.5 s by default the same in 4.3–4.4; what changed between 4.4 and 4.5 is failsafe_recovery_delay : 1.0 → 0.5 s . By default the sticks are centered, the throttle is at zero and the switch positions are held. The value for each channel is set in Betaflight App Stage 1 - Channel Fallback Settings or with the rxfail command. If the signal returns during Stage 1, control is restored instantly. How to choose failsafe_delay . Stage 1 is a fall: after the 300 ms hold the throttle gets its rxfail value, and by default that is minimum RX_FAILSAFE_MODE_AUTO in rx/rx.c ; only airmode keeps stabilization going. A free fall over t seconds is h = ½·g·t²: with the default 1.5 s 1.2 s at minimum throttle the aircraft loses up to 7 m, with 1.0 s 0.7 s — up to 2.4 m ignoring air resistance, hence “up to” . A shorter delay means less altitude lost before the Stage 2 procedure, but a dropout longer than the delay antenna orientation, foliage, the edge of coverage then triggers Stage 2: with DROP that is a disarm in the air, and with AUTO-LAND and GPS Rescue control comes back only after failsafe_recovery_delay and for Rescue — also after the sticks are moved . The course rule an estimate : - DROP, a 5" within visual range — the default 15: the margin against a false disarm matters more than a few meters of fall; - AUTO-LAND and GPS Rescue at altitude — 10 1 s , as in “A worked example: 7" long range” below: at 250 Hz that is 250 lost packets in a row, at 50 Hz — only 50, so on the slow packet rates do not go below 10; - the check — in the radio's telemetry RQly , link-edgetx find the longest LQ dropout to zero in ordinary flights: the delay should be at least twice as long a course guideline ; otherwise fix the link first link-elrs , “Link margin” , not the delay. Stage 2 — the procedure It is selected with the failsafe_procedure setting: - DROP the default — an immediate disarm, the motors stop. Re-arming is possible after failsafe_recovery_delay of a stable signal 0.5 s by default in 4.5 and 2025.12 and with the ARM switch turned off. - AUTO-LAND — the sticks are centered, the throttle is at failsafe_throttle , the Stage 1 modes are applied, and after failsafe_landing_time seconds before 2025.12 — failsafe_off_delay , in tenths of a second, default 10 = 1 s — a disarm. Re-arming — after failsafe_recovery_delay of a stable signal, as with DROP. - GPS-RESCUE — needs GPS: the drone flies home and lands. To regain control you need a signal for failsafe_recovery_delay and a stick deflection greater than failsafe_stick_threshold 30% of stick travel . A subtlety: if the throttle was at minimum for ≥10 s before Stage 2, a simple disarm happens except for GPS Rescue . Stage 2 is not possible for the first 5 s after boot. Video after a disarm: vtx_low_power_disarm ON or UNTIL_FIRST_ARM lowers the VTX power on the ground, but not while failsafe is active vtxGetSettings in io/vtx.c checks !failsafeIsActive . After DROP the aircraft is disarmed, but failsafe stays active until the signal is recovered — the VTX keeps transmitting at flight power, and a crashed aircraft can be found by its picture link-vtx . failsafe_landing_time is in seconds, default 60, range 0–250 in 4.5 its place is taken by failsafe_off_delay : tenths of a second, default 10, range 0–200 . If the build has altitude hold and there is an altitude source baro or GPS , AUTO-LAND descends through ALT_HOLD flight/alt_hold_multirotor.c : faster when high, slower near the ground. A new PID profile setting, landing_disarm_threshold 0–250, default 0 = off , disarms on ground impact: after takeoff, with the sticks centered and zero throttle or in ALT_HOLD and therefore in AUTO-LAND as well — but only when it runs through ALT_HOLD; with a fixed failsafe_throttle the throttle is not zero, and this disarm does not trigger , if the accelerometer jerk is greater than the threshold × 10 disarmOnImpact in flight/pid.c ; the comment on the default in pid.c:243 says “relatively safe values are around 100”, while the comment at the check itself, pid.c:968 , says “eg around 10” — the source comments contradict each other, so the threshold is chosen from a log, as below . Without it AUTO-LAND disarms when failsafe_landing_time runs out or earlier, if crash recovery triggered . 4.5 does not have this setting. How to check the threshold: debug_mode = EZLANDING logs jerk × 1000 in debug 7 flight/pid.c ; the disarm triggers when the jerk is greater than landing_disarm_threshold × 10, that is, in log units — when debug 7 is greater than the threshold × 10,000 near the ground in ALT_HOLD the jerk is multiplied by 1.5, and the boundary in the log is the threshold × 10,000 / 1.5 . In a log of several landings and sharp throttle chops in flight, debug 7 at touchdown must be above this boundary, and its maximum in the air — below it. Несовпадение версии SD-карты — самая частая причина «после обновления пропали звуки и скрипты». - EdgeTX Buddy buddy.edgetx.org — веб-прошивальщик в Chromium-браузере: пульт в режиме DFU выключен, подключён по USB — способ входа свой у каждой модели , Buddy сам скачивает прошивку и собирает SD-карту. - Через загрузчик — .bin кладут в /FIRMWARE , из меню SD-карты выбирают Flash bootloader , затем включают пульт с зажатыми внутрь горизонтальными триммерами на большинстве моделей и в загрузчике выбирают Write Firmware . text: summary ExpressLRS ELRS is an open radio control system that has become the standard in FPV. This module explains the main trade-offs: packet rate versus range, 2.4 GHz versus 900 MHz, how much airtime to give to telemetry. And it teaches you to read LQ and RSSI in the log so you can tell a link problem from a setup problem. theory Packet rate: latency versus sensitivity Packet rate is how many control packets per second the radio transmits. More packets means lower latency, but each packet is shorter and the receiver sensitivity is worse. That's why high rates are for racing and close-in freestyle, and low rates are for long-range flights. 2.4 GHz modes in ELRS 3.x: - LoRa: 50, 150, 250, 500 Hz — the main set, the lower the farther; - FLRC: F500, F1000 — minimal latency, shorter range; F1000 requires a serial receiver and a high UART speed; - D250, D500 — FLRC 1000 Hz with repetition: in D500 each packet is sent twice, in D250 four times, more reliable under interference; - Full Resolution modes for example 100Hz Full, 333Hz Full — all channels at full resolution for wings and complex mixes. On 900 MHz 868/915 the rates are lower: 25, 50, 100, 200 Hz. The longer wavelength bends around obstacles better and gets through foliage — the choice for wings and long routes. Telemetry: the 1:N ratio The telemetry ratio shows which packet out of N is given to the return channel. Telemetry interval = ratio × 1000 / packet rate ms . For example, 500 Hz at 1:128 means a telemetry packet every 256 ms. There are two packet types: LINK link statistics, roughly every 512 ms, always present and DATA flight controller telemetry and MSP . If you need to push a lot of data to the radio GPS, the Lua configurator , you set the ratio more frequent 1:8, 1:4 . Binding phrase The binding phrase is not a password and not encryption. A UID is computed from it, which sets the frequency hopping pattern. A unique phrase is needed so you don't interfere with neighbors that have the same pattern. The radio and the receiver must have the same phrase and the same major ELRS version. {{diagram:elrs-uid-model-match Phrase → MD5 → UID: bytes 2–5 set the hopping, 4–5 the CRC, and with Model Match the low 6 bits of UID5 carry the model number. The link comes up on the high bits, channels reach the FC only when everything matches.}} LQ and RSSI - RQly uplink LQ — how many of the radio's last 100 packets reached the receiver; - TQly — the same for telemetry in the opposite direction; - RSSI — signal strength in dBm; the margin is counted down to the sensitivity threshold of the current packet rate. LQ answers the question “are the packets getting through”, RSSI answers “how much margin is left”. LQ 100% with RSSI right at the threshold means you're at the edge, even if everything flies: per the ELRS documentation, LQ falls “off a cliff” as soon as RSSI approaches the sensitivity limit. That's why the RSSI warning in the OSD is set 5–10 dB above the mode's threshold: for 250 Hz −108 dBm — around −103…−98 dBm. Modes and sensitivity — table ELRS 3.x, from the Signal Health documentation Band Mode Packets/s Sensitivity When --- --- --- --- --- 2.4 GHz 50 Hz 50 −115 dBm maximum range on 2.4 2.4 GHz 150 Hz 150 −112 long range with good latency 2.4 GHz 250 Hz 250 −108 the standard for freestyle/racing 2.4 GHz 500 Hz 500 −105 minimal latency, close range 2.4 GHz F1000 FLRC 1000 −104 racing, short distance 900 MHz 25 Hz 25 −123 extreme range 900 MHz 50 Hz 50 −120 long range 900 MHz 100 Hz Full 100 −112 balance 900 MHz 200 Hz 200 −112 close range on 900 Every −3 dB of sensitivity = ×0.71 in range; 50 → 250 Hz on 2.4 = −7 dB ≈ ×0.45. The range calculation is in the “Link Budget” module, interactive below. The latency the pilot feels Packet interval 1/rate: 250 Hz → 4 ms, 50 Hz → 20 ms; plus processing in the radio EdgeTX mixer at the module rate, ~1–3 ms , CRSF at 420 kbaud ~0.6 ms , RC smoothing in the FC rc_smoothing_auto_factor , 1–10 ms . Going 150 → 250 Hz is noticeable in racing, 250 → 500 is barely noticeable against the filters and the motor the “Stick-to-Motor Latency” widget in the “Control Theory” module . Switch mode Hybrid / Wide : Wide gives 4 full channels, a 1-bit ARM AUX1 and 7 channels AUX2–AUX8 with 64/128 positions; the “Full Res” modes 100 Hz Full, 333 Hz Full — 8, 12 or 16 channels at 10 bits 8ch, 12ch Mixed, 16ch Rate/2 for wing/gimbal servos. {{diagram:latency-chain What makes up the latency from the stick to the aircraft's response; the largest contributions come from the radio packet and motor inertia.}} Dynamic power and telemetry Dynamic Power Dyn : the module raises power by itself when the onboard LQ/RSSI drop, and lowers it up close; it requires telemetry ratio ≥ 1:64 . Telemetry ratio 1:128 — telemetry interval = 128/250 s ≈ 0.5 s at 250 Hz: enough for voltage/LQ, slow for GPS coordinates for long range — 1:16…1:32 or Std ; Race disables telemetry while armed and doesn't suit long range . The telemetry channel is the same link, so MAVLink telemetry over ELRS airport/MAVLink mode, MAVLink since 3.5.0 shares bandwidth with control — for a GCS, a separate modem or 4G is better. Worked example: setup for a 7" long range 900 MHz 100 Hz Full −112 or 2.4 GHz 150 Hz −112 — choose by the interference environment and antennas 900 means bigger antennas, better diffraction around obstacles ; power per the budget for 10 km with a 12 dB margin the “Link Budget” module ; telemetry 1:32; Dynamic Power ON; Wide switch mode; warnings in EdgeTX: RSSI dBm sensor 1RSS / 2RSS ≤ −100 “caution”, ≤ −105 “turn back”; LQ RQly < 70% warning; in the OSD osd_rssi_dbm_pos , osd_link_quality_pos ; receiver failsafe — no pulses the default , in the FC — GPS Rescue/RTH. practice {{widget:elrs-calc}} Where the radio link sits in the “stick → motor” chain and how much it really weighs next to RC smoothing, filters and the motor: {{widget:link-latency}} Choosing a mode for the task 1. text: summary Стандартные виджеты цветного пульта показывают по одному числу. Свой Lua-виджет собирает на одном экране то, что нужно именно тебе в поле: качество связи с цветом, батарею с пересчётом на банку, режим полётника и последние значения после обрыва. Модуль разбирает по исходникам EdgeTX 2.12.5 пять типов Lua-скриптов и где каждый лежит на SD-карте, устройство виджета create , update , refresh , background , useLvgl , когда пульт вызывает каждую функцию, опции, рисование на цветном экране, чтение сенсоров CRSF/ELRS, быстродействие и отладку. Лабораторная — виджет LinkBox целиком: код, проверка синтаксиса luac и тест-стенд на настольном Lua 5.3, который подменяет lcd и телеметрию подставными функциями stubs и прогоняет полёт с обрывом связи. Железо не нужно; установка на TX16S или TX15 — в конце, по желанию. theory Пять типов скриптов и где они лежат В EdgeTX Lua — это язык расширений: прошивка даёт скрипту функции getValue , lcd.drawText , playFile … и вызывает его в своём цикле. Тип скрипта определяется папкой на SD-карте и тем, кто его запускает пути — radio/src/sdcard.h , загрузка — radio/src/lua/interface.cpp и widgets.cpp : Тип Папка Кто запускает Пульты Ограничения 2.12.5 --- --- --- --- --- Widget /WIDGETS/<имя /main.lua экран: виджет ставят в зону только цветные имя папки до 13 символов; до 50 опций; ~20 000 инструкций на вызов Telemetry /SCRIPTS/TELEMETRY/<имя .lua экран телеметрии модели Display только монохромные имя файла до 6 символов, экранов до 4 Function /SCRIPTS/FUNCTIONS/<имя .lua Special function Lua Script по тумблеру все имя до 8 символов Mix /SCRIPTS/MIXES/<имя .lua Model → Custom Scripts, выходы — источники миксов все, где собрано с LUA_MIXER имя до 6 символов; до 6 входов и 6 выходов Tool /SCRIPTS/TOOLS/ файл или папка с main.lua вручную из меню Tools / Apps все один за раз, на весь экран Пояснения к таблице. Telemetry-скрипты загружаются только в сборках PCBTARANIS , то есть на монохромных пультах interface.cpp:706–729 ; на TX16S их экранов нет вообще — ту же задачу решают виджеты. Длины имён — из dataconstants.h : LEN_SCRIPT_FILENAME 6 для mix и telemetry, LEN_FUNCTION_NAME 8 для function имя хранится в модели без .lua . Опция сборки LUA_MIXER в 2.12.5 включена по умолчанию radio/src/CMakeLists.txt:56 и во всех целях оставлена ON ; без неё пропадают только mix-скрипты. Есть и шестой, редкий тип — /SCRIPTS/RGBLED для пультов с RGB-подсветкой, его запускает Special function RGB LED . Постоянных скриптов одновременно может быть девять на цветном пульте mix + function + RGB LED и семь на монохромном mix + function + telemetry — MAX_SCRIPTS ; следующий даёт «Too many Lua scripts». Виджеты в этот счёт не входят: у них своя Lua-среда. Папка виджета — не длиннее 13 символов: буфер пути LEN_FILE_PATH_MAX + 6 + 5 + 1 widgets.cpp:46–48, 187, 203 , более длинную папку пульт молча пропускает. {{diagram:edgetx-lua-script-types Выбор типа решает задача: экран на цветном пульте — только виджет, на монохромном — telemetry-скрипт; действие по тумблеру — function, расчёт канала — mix.}} Главное правило выбора: mix-скрипт не для основных каналов. Если он упал с ошибкой, все строки миксов с его выходами отключаются mixer.cpp:899–906 , и канал теряет этот источник прямо в полёте. Экран, озвучка и логика тревог — в виджете или function-скрипте, управление — в обычных миксах. Анатомия виджета Виджет — файл main.lua , который при выполнении возвращает таблицу . title: VTX tables and changing the video channel
summary: The video transmitter (VTX) is controlled by the flight controller: Betaflight knows which frequencies and power levels the VTX has from the VTX table. This module explains how the table is built, how FACTORY and CUSTOM modes differ, and gives you a procedure for changing channels when yours is take
headings: Why a table Syntax FACTORY vs CUSTOM Two ways to write the same channel Frequencies and the law Channel physics: frequencies, bandwidth, spacing Power: what actually changes Control protocols and their gotchas Worked example: four vehicles at the field Procedure for changing channels when yours is taken Changing it via the CLI Verification
text: summary The video transmitter VTX is controlled by the flight controller: Betaflight knows which frequencies and power levels the VTX has from the VTX table. This module explains how the table is built, how FACTORY and CUSTOM modes differ, and gives you a procedure for changing channels when yours is taken — for example, by a crashed drone that keeps broadcasting until the end of the shift. theory Why a table VTX control protocols SmartAudio, IRC Tramp, MSP send either a band/channel number or a frequency. So that the OSD and the radio show the right values, Betaflight stores a table: a list of bands, 8 channels each, and a list of power levels. Syntax vtxtable bands 5 vtxtable channels 8 vtxtable band 1 BOSCAM_A A FACTORY 5865 5845 5825 5805 5785 5765 5745 5725 vtxtable band 5 RACEBAND R FACTORY 5658 5695 5732 5769 5806 5843 5880 5917 vtxtable powerlevels 3 vtxtable powervalues 14 20 26 vtxtable powerlabels 25 100 400 Fields of a band line: number, name, letter, mode, eight frequencies. A frequency of 0 blocks the channel. FACTORY vs CUSTOM - FACTORY: Betaflight sends the VTX a band and channel number, and the VTX uses its built-in table. The frequencies in the FC table are for display only — which is why they must match the VTX's real table. - CUSTOM: Betaflight sends the frequency itself. You can set any frequencies within the VTX's capabilities. IRC Tramp and RTC6705 work only in CUSTOM. Two ways to write the same channel A channel is written as letter+number R1, F4, E5 or as a band-channel pair 5-1 . They are the same thing if your table matches the table of whoever gave you that channel. On non-standard VTXs the band letters and numbers may not match the usual ones — compare by frequency in MHz, not by letter. Frequencies and the law Tables from the internet often contain frequencies you aren't allowed to transmit on. The Betaflight documentation warns you outright: almost nobody can legally use a stock table without editing it. The allowed range and power are set by local regulations. Channel physics: frequencies, bandwidth, spacing 5.8 GHz analog video occupies ~20–27 MHz of bandwidth around the carrier with audio subcarriers up to ±6.5 MHz ; channels in the tables are spaced 17–37 MHz apart, so adjacent channels of the same band overlap . Practice at the field: 4–6 vehicles fly at once without interference with spacing ≥ 37–40 MHz the classic set R1, R3, R5, R7 or R2, R4, R6, R8 on Raceband with 37 MHz steps ; 8 vehicles only with planning across the whole grid and reduced power. Digital systems DJI O3/O4, Walksnail, HDZero occupy 20–40 MHz and have their own channel grid and limits on the number of simultaneous systems usually 8 for Walksnail/HDZero, fewer for DJI on wide channels . Power: what actually changes Doubling power = +3 dB = ×1.41 √2 in free-space range the “Link Budget” module ; 25 → 800 mW = +15 dB ≈ ×5.6 in range — but an 800 mW+ VTX heats up without airflow on the ground — thermal protection and picture degradation , jams your neighbors, and for video the range is usually limited by the receiving side patch/helix on the ground, sensitivity . Pit mode 0.1–1 mW for powering up at the field is mandatory when flying with a team; vtx_low_power_disarm in Betaflight lowers power on the ground automatically. Control protocols and their gotchas - SmartAudio TBS, versions 1/2/2.1 : a single wire from an FC TX pin → VTX, 4800 baud, no inversion needed, but some VTXs need a pull-up Betaflight always sends 2 stop bits ; versions break compatibility — in the CLI vtx_info shows what the VTX replied. - IRC Tramp : also a single wire, its own commands, always CUSTOM frequencies. - MSP digital systems over MSP DisplayPort : VTX settings go over the same UART as the OSD; the table is built from what the air unit reports. Check: CLI get vtx → vtx_band/channel/power/freq ; vtx_info → what the device reported; vtxtable → the table. {{diagram:vtx-power-index-map The same line set vtx_power = 3 gives 400, 500 or 200 mW depending on the transmitter's table, and the module's table has no level 4 at all.}} Worked example: four vehicles at the field Analog, Raceband 37 MHz step: R1 5658 … R8 5917 , 200 mW power. Four vehicles — R1, R3, R5, R7: at least 74 MHz between any two, no interference. A fifth one asks for the “free” F2 5760 : it sits between R3 5732 and R5 5806 with 28 and 46 MHz of spacing — R3 will get interference. The right options: put the fifth on a digital system different modulation, but it still occupies bandwidth — its channel goes into the table too , or switch to a 6-channel grid with 37 MHz steps at ≤ 100 mW and spread the pilots across the field — tight, but it works. The wrong option is “I'll switch to whatever isn't taken in the OSD”: the field's table of occupied frequencies the “Field Operations” module is kept before anyone powers up. {{diagram:vtx-four-pilots Worked example: four analog vehicles on R1/R3/R5/R7 with 74 MHz spacing; the “free” F2 interferes with R3.}} practice Procedure for changing channels when yours is taken 1. Find out which frequencies are taken: your neighbors, other pilots at the field, a “broadcasting” crashed drone. 2. Convert all taken channels to MHz using their VTX's table — not by letter. 3. Pick a free frequency with the largest possible spacing from your neighbors. A guideline for analog is at least ~37 MHz, like between adjacent Raceband channels: closer channels noticeably interfere with each other. 4. Find that frequency in your table and write down the band and channel. 5. Change it on one or two transmitters/drones first, check the picture and interference with neighbors. 6. Only after a successful test — on all the other drones. Changing it via the CLI get vtx set vtx_band = 4 set vtx_channel = 1 save Switch the video receiver goggles, ground station to the same frequency. For digital systems Walksnail, DJI, HDZero the channel is changed in their menu; the selection logic is the same. Verification 1. The new frequency is visibl

text: summary One 5″ quadcopter Betaflight 2025.12, an ELRS receiver, DShot ESCs, an analog or digital VTX goes from a blank board to a recorded hover. The order is the 17 setup steps of the course. Steps already covered in other modules are given here in one line: what to press in this firmware and where to go for the details. What the course has not covered before is described in detail: calibrating vbat_scale , ibata_scale and ibata_offset with a multimeter and the charger's mAh the formulas are checked against the 4.5 and 2025.12 sources — they are the same , motor order and direction motor_output_reordering , resource , DShot commands through dshotprog and the Motor direction dialog , calibrating PWM ESCs, the preflight check and the first hover with abort criteria, and the basics of GPS Rescue. The main path is Betaflight SITL built from source. The lab: a config and a failsafe test in SITL, then the same config on a real aircraft, battery calibration, diff all and a log of a 60-second hover. theory The map of the steps: what, where and with what {{diagram:bf-setup-flow The 17 steps go strictly in order: configuration, modes, failsafe and the backup are checked in SITL; the receiver, motors, ESCs and battery — only on the bench without props; the props go on at step 15.}} Step Where Betaflight 2025.12: tab / CLI Details --- --- --- --- --- 1 Firmware, a backup of the old config SITL, USB Firmware Flasher, diff all bf-intro 2 Orientation, mixer SITL, USB Setup, mixer QUADX , align_board_ bf-intro 3 UART ports SITL CLI only , USB Ports, serial bf-ports 4 Receiver, bind bench Receiver, serialrx_provider = CRSF link-elrs 5 Channels, endpoints, centers bench Receiver, map , min_check , max_check here, link-protocols 6 Motor protocol bench Motors, motor_pwm_protocol f-motors-esc 7 Order and direction bench, props off Motors, motor_output_reordering , dshotprog here, bf-cli 8 ESC calibration PWM only bench, props off Motors, the master slider here 9 Accelerometer SITL, bench Setup → Calibrate Accelerometer bf-intro 10 Voltage and current bench + flight Power & Battery, vbat_scale , ibata_scale , ibata_offset here 11 Modes, arming, arming disable flags SITL Modes, aux , status bf-modes-osd 12 Failsafe: set up and check SITL + bench Failsafe, failsafe_ bf-failsafe 13 OSD and video bench OSD, Video Transmitter bf-modes-osd, link-vtx 14 GPS and GPS Rescue if there is a GPS bench + field gps_rescue_ , ap_hover_throttle here, bf-failsafe 15 Preflight and the first hover field — here 16 The first tuning field filters, PID, sliders bf-filters, bf-pid 17 Log, diff all , restore SITL + field Blackbox, CLI bf-blackbox, bf-cli What Betaflight SITL can and cannot do This section and the lab below were verified on SITL 4.5.x the 4.5-maintenance branch, commit 7dcc851 : version.h says 4.5.6, but there is no such release; the latest release is 4.5.5, and the src/ code matches it except for the version number in version.h ; for 2025.12 the lab will be rerun, and the known differences are named along the way. SITL is the same firmware built with an ordinary gcc for Linux make TARGET=SITL . The sensors are virtual GYRO=VIRTUAL, ACC=VIRTUAL, BARO=VIRTUAL , and the UARTs are replaced by the TCP ports 127.0.0.1:576x : UART1 = 5761, UART2 = 5762. The config is stored in eeprom.bin in the current folder, and save and exit terminate the process — it has to be started again. SITL talks to a simulator over UDP: it receives the aircraft state FDM on port 9003 and the RC channels on 9004, and sends the motors to 9002 Gazebo and 9001 RealFlight . Without a simulator the aircraft does not fly, but the CLI, the modes, the arming disable flags, failsafe and diff all work as on a board. What SITL 4.5 does not have: this can be seen in src/main/target/SITL/target.h in 2025.12 the file is in src/platform/SIMULATOR/target/SITL/ , where the relevant USE_ are disabled, and in the CLI responses: - DShot. The default protocol is DISABLED , so the MOTOR_PROTO flag is set. In SITL PWM is used, and the DShot settings dshot_bidir and dshot_idle_value — the 4.5 name; in 2025.12 it is motor_idle are not in the SITL 4.5 CLI. - Serial receiver, ADC, OSD, VTX, GPS, Blackbox, resource . The CLI answers get gps_provider and get blackbox_device with INVALID NAME , and resource with UNKNOWN COMMAND . In SITL 2025.12 a virtual GPS gps_provider = VIRTUAL and Blackbox blackbox_device = VIRTUAL are enabled in target.h . - Link loss. Once the first RC UDP packet has arrived, rxRCFrameStatus in sitl.c always returns “frame received”. If the RC stream is stopped, there will be no RXLOSS flag. Failsafe in SITL is checked with the FAILSAFE mode on a switch. Voltage and current sensors: the formulas from the source src/main/sensors/voltage.c the formula did not change in 2025.12 converts an ADC reading to a voltage in units of 0.01 V : V = ADC · vbat_scale · Vref_mV / 10 + 0xFFF · 5 / 0xFFF · vbat_divider / vbat_multiplier The voltage is directly proportional to vbat_scale 110 by default with vbat_divider 10 and vbat_multiplier 1: V = U_pin · vbat_scale / vbat_divider · vbat_multiplier = U_pin · 110/10 = 11 · U_pin — a 10 kΩ : 1 kΩ resistor divider; that is, vbat_scale = the divider ratio × 10, not × 100 as in INAV . Hence new = old × V_multimeter / V_FC . A step of one unit is 0.9 %, which on a full 6S pack is ≈ 36 mV per cell. The lab criterion an error of less than 50 mV per cell is achievable without fractional values. src/main/sensors/current.c : centiAmps = mV · 10000 / ibata_scale + ibata_offset / 10 , that is, the current in mA is 10000 · mV / ibata_scale + ibata_offset . ibata_scale is in mV per 10 A 400 = 40 mV/A, an ACS758 sensor , and ibata_offset is in mA. The betaflight.com documentation gives the same units. The current is inversely proportional to scale, so new = old × mAh_FC / mAh_charger . The offset correction: new_offset = old_offset + I_ammeter − I_FC × 1000 . A negative ibata_scale range −16000…16000 is needed if the sensor is fitted “

text: summary A reference module on the most frequent Betaflight question: “why won't it arm”. Here is the full table of the 29 arming disable flags of version 2025.12 armingDisableFlagNames in fc/runtime_config.c ; 4.5 has 26 flags : what sets each flag in the source and how to clear it. It covers where to read these flags: the Setup tab, status in the CLI, MSP_STATUS_EX , the OSD warning and the beeper code. Then — arming with a switch and with the sticks, PREARM, disarm, airmode. The protections that act after arming are covered separately: runaway takeoff prevention the thresholds and the deactivation conditions are taken from fc/core.c , yaw spin recovery and crash recovery. One more section is about what swapped motors, a wrong rotation direction and the wrong prop look like on takeoff. A Python lab: a flag mask decoder on real masks, including the trap with bit numbers in the 4.5 → 2025.12 transition, and the runaway logic reproduced from the source on synthetic data. Then on hardware: clearing the flags one at a time without props, the motor order and direction test, the first arm without props and the first low hover with abort criteria. theory Where to read the flags {{diagram:bf-arming-flag-groups The arming disable flags 26 in 4.5, 29 in 2025.12 come down to five actions: move the switch or throttle, let the sensors settle, close the app/CLI/menu, fix the motor protocol or ESC, and after RUNAWAY, CRASH and PARALYZE — disarm or reboot.}} The reasons for an arming block are stored in a single 32-bit mask armingDisableFlags_e , fc/runtime_config.h . It is visible in four places: - Betaflight App → Setup → Arming Disable Flags. The app gets the mask through MSP_STATUS_EX . The response has a byte with the number of flags 29 in 2025.12, 26 in 4.5 and the uint32 of the mask itself msp/msp.c . - CLI, the status command. The line Arming disable flags: lists the names of all set flags from the lowest bit to the highest cliStatus . The documentation warns that on some stripped-down builds only hex is printed. Then decode the mask with the table for your version step 1 of the practice . - OSD, the Warnings element. The flags are shown only while the ARM switch is on and arming is blocked. The names alternate every 0.5 s. ARM_SWITCH before 2025.12 — ARMSWITCH is hidden if there are other reasons osd/osd_warnings.c . - The beeper. The code sounds on every failed arm attempt with a new reason: tryArm → beeperWarningBeeps ffs flags . First 4 fast beeps of 50 ms in 4.5 — 5; beeperWarningBeeps in io/beeper.c , then N/5 long ones 250 ms and N%5 short ones 50 ms . N = bit number + 1. The beeper reports only the lowest bit , that is, the most critical reason: the flags are sorted by importance. Example: 1 long + 1 short = 6 = RUNAWAY . {{lesson:bf-led-buzzer The other beeper signals: the priorities of the conditions, the beeper mask, RX_LOST after a crash and the DShot beacon through the motors.}} All 29 flags of Betaflight 2025.12 The code is the number for the beeper bit + 1 . title: Digital FPV video: DJI, Walksnail, HDZero, OpenIPC
summary: The analog VTX from the “VTX Tables” module means minimal latency and graceful degradation into noise. Digital systems give you a picture that's many times sharper, onboard HD recording and a high-resolution OSD, but they pay for it with compression, latency that depends on the mode, and the “cliff”
headings: What changes when you go digital Four families HD OSD: MSP DisplayPort Frequencies and neighbors How to choose Step 1. Inventory your system Step 2. HD OSD Step 3. Latency Step 4. Edge of range on the ground
text: summary The analog VTX from the “VTX Tables” module means minimal latency and graceful degradation into noise. Digital systems give you a picture that's many times sharper, onboard HD recording and a high-resolution OSD, but they pay for it with compression, latency that depends on the mode, and the “cliff”: a freeze instead of snow. This module explains how analog, frame-synchronous digital HDZero , compressed video DJI, Walksnail and the open OpenIPC + WFB-ng combo fundamentally differ; how to hook up HD OSD via MSP DisplayPort in Betaflight, INAV and ArduPilot; and how to pick a system for the task rather than by the marketing. The lab is measuring the latency and the behavior at the edge of range of your own system. theory What changes when you go digital - Compression. Camera → H.264/H.265 encoder → radio → decoder → screen. The encoder looks for similarities between frames; the lower the bitrate, the more it has to “make things up”. Hence the artifacts on fast passes over grass and trees — where frames are least alike. - Latency is not one number. Manufacturers quote the minimum in the best mode high frame rate, strong signal . At the edge of range, systems lower the bitrate and frame rate, and latency grows. Compare systems by measuring in your own modes, not by the box. - Degradation. Analog at the edge means noise and stripes, but there's still a picture, and the pilot sees where they're flying. Digital holds a clean picture almost to the end, then freezes or breaks up into blocks. Behavior at link loss is the main safety question for long-range flights: what the pilot will see one second before losing video, and what the aircraft will do. - Onboard recording. Digital air units record video without radio losses — that's the “HD DVR” for flight review, as opposed to recording in the goggles. Four families System Principle Strength Limitations --- --- --- --- Analog 5.8 GHz uncompressed composite signal minimal and constant latency, graceful degradation, cheap low sharpness, interference shows immediately HDZero digital without inter-frame compression, synchronous with the camera frame low and stable latency, predictable for racing less sharp than compressed systems, blocks at the edge DJI O3/O4 , Walksnail Avatar compressed H.264/H.265 video with bitrate adaptation best picture, onboard recording, good range latency depends on the mode, closed ecosystem, fewer simultaneous channels OpenIPC + WFB-ng open IP camera firmware + Wi-Fi adapters in monitor mode, FEC openness, tunable for the task, MAVLink telemetry in the same channel built and configured by hand, higher latency than FPV systems Latency, resolution and range figures for specific models change with every generation and firmware — check the manufacturer's documentation for your version and, most importantly, measure. HD OSD: MSP DisplayPort In digital systems the OSD is drawn by the goggles or the air unit, and the flight controller only sends what to draw, using the MSP DisplayPort protocol over UART. - Betaflight 4.4+ : a UART on the Ports tab — MSP function for the air unit Peripherals: VTX MSP + DisplayPort ; in the CLI set osd_displayport_device = MSP , video system set vcd_video_system = HD . OSD elements are laid out on a larger canvas. - INAV : a UART with MSP DisplayPort for HD OSD, OSD type per your system's documentation. - ArduPilot : SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 42 DisplayPort , OSD_TYPE = 5 MSP DisplayPort . - VTX control channel, power on digital systems goes either through the same MSP or from the goggles menu — analog VTX tables aren't needed here. Frequencies and neighbors Digital systems also work in 5.8 GHz and occupy a wider band, so fewer of them fit in the air at the same time than analog aircraft on Raceband. At a shared field, agree on channels in advance; mixed analog + digital is a common source of mutual interference. Power and permitted channels — per your country's rules.
