This module explains dipole, patch, cloverleaf and “T” antennas, the difference between linear and circular polarization, what gain in dBi is and why it always comes at the cost of beamwidth, how to read a radiation pattern and ori
headings: How an antenna radiates Radiation pattern and gain Worked example: where the dipole's null is What dBi buys you in range Polarization SWR and matching Placement on the aircraft Connectors: the quiet cause of a “bad antenna” Step 1. Inventory Step 2. Orientation Step 3. SWR Step 4. Ground range test
text: summary The antenna is half of the radio link, and the most underrated half. This module explains dipole, patch, cloverleaf and “T” antennas, the difference between linear and circular polarization, what gain in dBi is and why it always comes at the cost of beamwidth, how to read a radiation pattern and orient antennas on the aircraft and on the ground, what SWR measures and when an antenna is “the wrong one.” It ends with a ground range test. theory How an antenna radiates A half-wave dipole is two conductors, each a quarter wave long. λ = c/f: 2.4 GHz → 12.5 cm quarter 3.1 cm , 915 MHz → 32.8 cm quarter 8.2 cm , 5.8 GHz → 5.2 cm quarter 1.3 cm . An antenna is “tuned” when its size matches the frequency — then the energy goes out into the air instead of reflecting back. Radiation pattern and gain An isotropic radiator an imaginary one radiates equally in all directions — 0 dBi. A real antenna redistributes energy: a dipole gives 2.15 dBi in the plane perpendicular to its axis and nothing along the axis the “donut” . Gain always comes from narrowing the beam. An 8–9 dBi patch covers a sector of ~60–70°, a 12–14 dBi directional Yagi about ~30°. On the aircraft you need an omnidirectional antenna its attitude keeps changing ; on the ground, a directional one, if there's someone to aim it. The main consequence for the aircraft: a dipole/“T” antenna mounted vertically does not radiate up or down. If the aircraft is directly overhead, you get a null. That's why the two receiver antennas diversity are mounted at 90° to each other. Worked example: where the dipole's null is A vertical dipole on the radio, the aircraft at 100 m altitude. Elevation angle θ = atan h/d , angle from the dipole axis is 90° − θ, relative gain ≈ sin² angle from the axis : Aircraft distance Elevation angle Pattern loss --- --- --- 1 km 5.7° 0 dB 300 m 18° −0.5 dB 100 m 45° −3 dB 30 m almost overhead 73° −10.8 dB Takeaway: at long range the dipole works perfectly, and the null happens close in and overhead — where you have plenty of power margin. That's why you hold the radio's antenna side-on to the aircraft don't point its tip at it , and on the aircraft a second antenna at 90° covers the first one's null. What dBi buys you in range +6 dB of gain = ×2 range in free space. An 8 dBi patch on the ground instead of a 2 dBi dipole gives +6 dB — double the range, but only inside the beam sector : once the aircraft leaves the sector, you lose more than you gained. A directional antenna without aiming a tracker or a pilot turning the radio is a trap for flights that go “around in a circle.” Polarization - Linear dipole, “T”, monopole : the field oscillates in one plane. The receiving antenna must be in the same plane: a 90° rotation gives up to 20–30 dB of loss in theory, 10–20 in practice because of reflections. When the aircraft banks, the polarization gets misaligned. - Circular cloverleaf, helical, circularly polarized patch : the field rotates — right-hand RHCP or left-hand LHCP . Antenna orientation barely matters; reflections reverse the direction of rotation and get attenuated less multipath — cleaner video . You pay ~3 dB when receiving circular with a linear antenna and vice versa. RHCP↔LHCP costs 15–20 dB: don't mix them. - For 5.8 GHz video — circular on both ends; for 900 MHz/2.4 GHz RC — linear dipoles mounted orthogonally. SWR and matching SWR shows how much of the power is reflected from the antenna back into the transmitter. 1.0 is ideal; 1.5 — 4% reflected −0.18 dB , 2.0 — 11% −0.5 dB , 3.0 — 25% −1.25 dB . High SWR heats the VTX and can kill it; it affects range less than you'd think as long as it's ≤ 2. It's measured with an antenna analyzer NanoVNA — affordable . An antenna is “the wrong one” when the SWR minimum is not at your frequency trimmed for / designed for another band , the connector is damaged, or the coax ground is torn off. Placement on the aircraft - Antennas go outside the carbon: carbon is a conductor, it shields and detunes the antenna. - Receiver: two antennas at 90°, away from the VTX and power wiring; tail “whiskers” pointing down and back at 45°. - Video: antenna on top or on the bottom so that there is no frame or battery between it and the ground/pilot; for flying far and low — on the bottom. - GPS: on top, ceramic patch horizontal, with a ground plane under it. - Keep the pigtail cable as short as possible: thin RG178 coax loses ~1 dB per 30 cm at 5.8 GHz. Connectors: the quiet cause of a “bad antenna” SMA and RP-SMA look the same, but one has the pin in the plug and the other in the jack: “it screwed on” doesn't mean “it connected” — the center contact may not touch. U.FL/IPEX is rated for a few dozen mating cycles and pops off from vibration if not secured — a drop of glue or heat shrink on the cable. MMCX holds better but also needs cable strain relief. {{diagram:polarization-loss Polarization mismatch loss: matched — 0 dB, linear to circular — 3 dB, crossed or opposite hand — 20 dB and more.}} {{diagram:chart-antenna-patterns Radiation patterns: a vertical dipole has a null along its axis above and below the aircraft , a patch radiates forward in a sector and barely sees backward. Models: dipole sin²θ, patch cos⁴θ with a −20 dB back lobe.}} {{widget:antenna-pol}} practice Step 1. Inventory For every antenna on the aircraft and on the ground: band, type, polarization and the hand of circular , gain, connector SMA/RP-SMA, U.FL/MMCX . Check that polarizations match in every link. Step 2. Orientation Sketch the patterns the dipole donut, the patch sector projected onto the aircraft in typical attitudes: hover, 45° bank, flying out to 1 km at 100 m altitude elevation ~6° . Make sure that in every attitude both ends “see” each other outside a null. Step 3. SWR NanoVNA if you have one : 1. Sweep range: 5.6–6.0 GHz for video or 2.3–2.6 GHz, 850–950 MHz for RC . 2. SOL calibration Short–Open–Load at the end of the very cable the antenna will be connected to, otherwise you're measuring the

text: summary “Will it make 10 km?” is a question of arithmetic, not faith. A link budget is a sum in decibels: transmitter power + antenna gains − cable losses − free-space attenuation must be above the receiver sensitivity, with a margin for fading. This module teaches you to calculate it for RC and video, turn the margin into an expected range, set the RSSI warning threshold and compare the calculation with a field test — and shows why 900 MHz goes farther than 2.4 GHz at the same power, and why 5.8 GHz video is the weak link. theory Decibels in five minutes dB is a logarithmic measure of a ratio: 3 dB ≈ ×2 in power, 10 dB = ×10, 20 dB = ×100. dBm is power relative to 1 mW: 0 dBm = 1 mW, 20 dBm = 100 mW, 27 dBm = 500 mW, 30 dBm = 1 W. Doubling the transmitter power gives +3 dB — the same as a slightly better antenna. Doubling the range costs 6 dB see below . Free-space path loss FSPL FSPL dB = 20·log₁₀ d, km + 20·log₁₀ f, MHz + 32.44. Range 915 MHz 2.4 GHz 5.8 GHz --- --- --- --- 1 km 91.7 100.0 107.7 5 km 105.6 114.0 121.7 10 km 111.7 120.0 127.7 30 km 121.2 129.6 137.3 Every doubling of range is +6 dB; going from 915 MHz → 2.4 GHz costs 8.4 dB at the same range, → 5.8 GHz another 7.7 dB. This is the physics of the receiving antenna's aperture, not “penetrating power.” The budget equation Prx = Ptx + Gtx + Grx − Lcable − FSPL − Lextra , margin M = Prx − Ssens. - Ptx — transmitter power in dBm. - G — antenna gain in dBi dipole 2, patch 8, Yagi 12 . - Lcable — pigtails/cables 0.5–2 dB . - Lextra — polarization 3 dB linear↔circular , mismatch, obstacles, the Fresnel zone near the ground flying low over the surface costs another 6–20 dB . - S — receiver sensitivity in dBm for the given mode for ELRS, from the mode table: 2.4 GHz 50 Hz −115, 150 Hz −112, 250 Hz −108, 500 Hz −105; 900 MHz 25 Hz −123, 50 Hz −120, 100 Hz −117, 200 Hz −112 . Margin M: 10–15 dB is the minimum for a reliable link with fading multipath, aircraft maneuvering ; 20 dB is comfortable; 0 is the edge, the link will keep dropping. RC example: ELRS 2.4 GHz, 250 Hz, 250 mW Ptx = 24 dBm, Gtx = 2 radio dipole , Grx = 2 onboard dipole, but we count 0 because of orientation , Lcable = 1, polarization another −3 in banks. Prx at 10 km = 24 + 2 + 0 − 1 − 120 − 3 = −98 dBm. S 250 Hz = −108 → 10 dB margin. Switching to 50 Hz −115 gives 17 dB — or the same reliability at ~22 km. Raising power to 1 W +6 dB is the same as doubling the range. Video example: analog 5.8 GHz 800 mW Ptx = 29 dBm, onboard cloverleaf 2, ground patch 8, cables −1.5, S of a typical analog receiver ≈ −90 dBm video starts getting noisy long before it's lost . At 5 km: 29 + 2 + 8 − 1.5 − 121.7 = −84 dBm → 6 dB margin, the picture will have interference. Digital systems work down to −100…−105 dBm, but cut out abruptly at the threshold. Video almost always limits range before RC does — hence 900 MHz/1.2–1.3 GHz video for long-range flights and directional antennas on the ground. How to turn the budget into an RSSI threshold The ELRS rule: warning when RSSI is ~8–10 dB above the mode's sensitivity; the critical failsafe threshold is at the sensitivity. For 2.4 GHz 250 Hz: warning at −98…−100 dBm, at −105 — turn back. In EdgeTX — a voice warning on RSSI dBm and on LQ <70% at 250 Hz is a reason to worry . Why the calculation doesn't match the field Multipath ground reflections add up out of phase , obstacles in the Fresnel zone the first-zone radius at 2.4 GHz over 5 km is ~12 m: flying low over the ground costs 6–20 dB , onboard interference it reduces effective sensitivity , the real antenna orientation. That's why a range test is mandatory and a 10–15 dB margin is the minimum. {{diagram:chart-link-two-ray The module's 2.4 GHz example: flying at 10 m, the ground reflection eats 10 dB at 5 km, and the −98 dBm warning comes at 3.9 km instead of 10 km; at 120 m the break point moves beyond 5.9 km and only short dips remain.}} {{diagram:link-budget-chain Worked budget example: ELRS 2.4 GHz, 250 mW, 10 km — received power of −98 dBm against a sensitivity of −108 dBm gives a 10 dB margin.}} {{diagram:chart-link-margin Received power from the free-space formula against ELRS sensitivity thresholds the table from the link-elrs module . The margin is the distance from the curve to the threshold; a real flight needs 10–15 dB for fading, antenna rotation and the aircraft body.}} {{widget:link-margin}} practice Step 1. RC budget table For your link: power, mode and its sensitivity, antennas, cables. Calculate the margin at 1, 3, 5, 10 km. Find the range where the margin = 12 dB — that's your working limit. Step 2. Video budget table The same for the video system, with the real sensitivity of the receiver/goggles. Compare the limits: what fails first. Step 2a. Inputs = the module's worked example: ExpressLRS 2.4 GHz, 250 Hz sensitivity -108 dBm, ELRS 4.1 src/src/common.cpp:100 , 250 mW, dipole on the radio, 0 dBi effective on board, 1 dB cables, 3 dB polarisation loss. text: summary Frying a flight controller port is easier than it seems: 5 V on a 3.3 V pin, swapped TX/RX with power coming from two sources, I2C without pull-ups, CAN without a terminator. This module is a practical procedure for connecting any device: identify the interface and levels → find a port and its power → check with a multimeter before power-up → configure the protocol in the firmware → confirm the data with an analyzer. With examples: GPS+compass, rangefinder, ESC telemetry, digital video system, DroneCAN node. theory Three buses and their character Bus Wires Speed Addressing Typical devices Main pitfalls --- --- --- --- --- --- UART TX, RX, GND +power 9600 – 2 Mbaud; GPS 57600–230400 depends on the firmware: Betaflight 57600, ArduPilot sets 230400 , CRSF 420000, MSP 115200 point-to-point GPS, receiver, telemetry, VTX, rangefinder, companion TX↔RX crossed; inversion SBUS ; one port — one device I2C SDA, SCL, GND 100/400 kHz 7-bit address, many devices on the bus compass, barometer, OLED, some rangefinders no pull-ups; identical addresses; long wires 30 cm — trouble SPI CLK, MOSI, MISO, CS up to tens of MHz by CS gyro, OSD, flash, sometimes baro on-board only; almost never brought out CAN DroneCAN CAN_H, CAN_L, GND +power 1 Mbit/s node ID 1–125 GPS/compass, ESC, current sensors, servos, rangefinders no 120 Ω terminators at the ends; twisted pair; identical node IDs Levels and power - FC logic is 3.3 V . Most inputs tolerate 5 V “5V tolerant” , but not all: read the MCU datasheet STM32F4/F7/H7 — most GPIOs are 5V-tolerant, except pins with analog functions . Rule: if in doubt — a 1k/2k divider at the FC input or a level shifter. - Port power : the 5 V and 9 V pads on the FC come from on-board BECs with a limit typically 5 V/2–3 A, 9 V/2–3 A total for all loads . Powering a Raspberry Pi or a digital air unit “from the pad” overloads the BEC; power it from a separate BEC. - Common ground — always. A device with its own power and no common ground with the FC means garbage on the UART or a fried port. - Two power points a device powered from the FC and from the companion's USB at the same time — reverse current through the BEC. A diode or a single power source. UART: details - FC TX → device RX, FC RX ← device TX. - Inversion : SBUS and some protocols are inverted; on an F4 without a hardware inverter you need an external one or a port with an inverter; F7/H7 — software inversion Betaflight serialrx_inverted . CRSF is not inverted, one line in each direction. - Single wire : ESC telemetry KISS/BLHeli_32 protocol is one-way ESC → FC : it arrives on one RX pin from all ESCs in turn over a common wire, the request goes over the DShot signal; VTX SmartAudio/Tramp is true half-duplex: one wire to the TX pin, data both ways. - One device per UART except half-duplex protocols designed specifically for that . I2C: details - Pull-ups of 2.2–4.7 kΩ on SDA and SCL to 3.3 V — usually already on the FC; a second device with its own pull-ups lowers the combined resistance — fine down to ~1 kΩ equivalent. - Addresses: compass HMC5883 0x1E, QMC5883 0x0D, IST8310 0x0C/0x0E, baro BMP280 0x76/0x77, MS5611 0x76/0x77. Two devices with the same address — a conflict. - Length: short wires, twisted with ground; on a GPS mast 15–20 cm is fine, 50 cm is already risky drop to 100 kHz . {{diagram:i2c-transaction An I2C transaction bit by bit — exactly what the logic analyzer sees when “the sensor can't be found.”}} {{diagram:chart-i2c-pullup-window The pull-up must lie between the red line 0.97 kΩ and the mode's curve: at 100 pF a single 4.7 kΩ is too weak for 400 kHz, while two in parallel 2.35 kΩ are inside the window.}} DroneCAN: when and how When: the aircraft is large long wires → UART/I2C pick up noise , there are many devices, you need ESC and sensor telemetry on one bus, redundancy. In ArduPilot: CAN_P1_DRIVER = 1 enable port 1 , CAN_D1_PROTOCOL = 1 DroneCAN , reboot; GPS GPS_TYPE = 9 GPS1_TYPE in 4.6+ — DroneCAN, the compass is detected automatically. The bus: twisted pair, 120 Ω terminators at both ends many devices have a terminator jumper , node power per the spec usually 5 V , unique node IDs the autopilot hands them out as a DNA server with dynamic allocation; CAN_D1_UC_NODE is the autopilot's own node ID . Connection procedure always the same 1. Device datasheet: interface, levels, power V, mA , protocol and speed. 2. FC map: a free port, its inverter/power, the BEC limit. 3. Wires labeled; TX/RX crossed; common ground. 4. Before power-up : multimeter — no short from 5 V/3.3 V to GND, the device's power will come from the right pad. 5. Power up through a smoke stopper. The voltage at the device is normal. 6. Firmware: port → function → protocol/speed. Check the data GPS: satellites; compass: heading changes when you rotate; ESC telemetry: RPM on the motors tab . 7. If there's no data — analyzer on the line: are there bytes, what speed, inversion. {{diagram:periph-connect-flow The multimeter and smoke stopper come before the firmware; if there is no data, the next step is an analyzer on the line: are there bytes, what baud rate, is there inversion.}} practice Step 0. Bus calculation before soldering Checks four decisions from the theory: the I2C pull-up window versus bus capacitance, sensor address overlaps, the UART load of UBX-NAV-PVT and the CAN bus resistance. Runs on any computer with Python 3; save as periph_lab.py : python """Peripheral bus checks: I2C pull-up window, address conflicts, UART load of a GPS, CAN termination.""" import itertools I2C: TI SLVA689 from the I2C-bus spec : Rp_min = Vcc - VOL / IOL, Rp_max = tr / 0.8473 Cb VCC, VOL, IOL = 3.3, 0.4, 3e-3 TR = {"100 kHz": 1000e-9, "400 kHz": 300e-9, "1 MHz Fm+ ": 120e-9} rp_min = VCC - VOL / IOL print f"1 I2C pull-up window at {VCC} V: Rp_min = {rp_min:.0f} Ohm" for cb_pf in 50, 100, 200, 400 : cells = for mode, tr in TR.items : rmax = tr / 0.8473 cb_pf 1e-12 bad = "Fm+" not in mode and rmax < rp_min Fm+: the I2C spec UM10204 allows 20 mA

text: summary On a 5" quad everything lives on UART and I²C. On an X8, a VTOL or any vehicle with wires longer than half a meter, that ends in interference, a shortage of ports and “GPS drops out on throttle”. DroneCAN moves the GPS, compass, current sensor, rangefinders, airspeed and even ESCs onto a single four-wire differential bus. This module is the system level on top of “Connecting peripherals” and “Protocols”: bus physics and checking it with a multimeter, node IDs and their automatic allocation DNA , ArduPilot and PX4 setup, ESCs over CAN and the bus load budget, updating node firmware, and AP_Periph — how to make your own node from an STM32 board. theory Why a bus when you have UART - Noise immunity. CAN is a differential pair: interference couples into both wires equally, and the receiver looks at the difference. A meter of wire next to an X8 power bus is normal for CAN and guaranteed glitches for I²C. - One port, many devices. GPS, compass, current sensor, rangefinder, airspeed, 8 ESCs — on one bus, through a splitter. - Telemetry and diagnostics for free. Every node reports on itself NodeStatus : health, mode, uptime , and the node firmware can be updated from the ground station. - Redundancy. Two CAN ports on the flight controller mean two independent buses; critical nodes are duplicated. The price: more expensive peripherals, slightly more complex setup, and the bus has to be built correctly physically. Bus physics - 1 Mbit/s the DroneCAN standard . The longer the bus, the stricter the requirements; on a vehicle it's a few meters, which is not a limitation. - 120 Ω terminators at both ends of the bus, and only at both ends. Check with the power off: a multimeter between CAN_H and CAN_L should show ~60 Ω two 120 Ω in parallel . 120 Ω means one terminator, infinity means none, 40 Ω means three. - Dronecode/Pixhawk connector : JST-GH 4 pin — 1: +5 V, 2: CAN_H, 3: CAN_L, 4: GND. The H/L pair is twisted. - Topology is a line , not a star: short stubs off the trunk. Splitters CAN hub/splitter make the “line” internally. - Power over the bus: the 5 V from the flight controller is current-limited — a GPS with compass and a couple of sensors are fine, ESCs and servos are powered separately. DroneCAN on top of CAN DroneCAN formerly UAVCAN v0 defines what goes in the frames: the 29-bit frame identifier carries the priority, the message type and the sender's node ID; long messages are split across several frames. The node ID is 1…127; the flight controller is usually 10 in ArduPilot CAN_D1_UC_NODE and 1 in PX4 UAVCAN_NODE_ID . DNA dynamic node allocation : a new node without an ID asks the server for one, and the flight controller hands out a free one and remembers it by the node's unique ID. That's why peripherals “just plug in and work”. It breaks when nodes are moved between vehicles or settings are copied: two nodes with the same stored ID means a conflict. The fix is clearing the DNA table on the flight controller or a fixed ID on the node. {{diagram:dronecan-dna-flow The node ID is tied to its unique ID in the flight controller's table: a moved or copied node gives a duplicate ID and “Duplicate Node”; the fix is clearing the table with bit 0 of CAN_D1_UC_OPTION or a fixed ID.}} Cyphal UAVCAN v1 is the next, incompatible version of the protocol; ArduPilot and most peripherals use DroneCAN, PX4 supports both. When buying peripherals, check that they speak DroneCAN. ArduPilot setup What Parameters Value --- --- --- Enable port CAN1 CAN_P1_DRIVER 1 first driver Driver 1 protocol CAN_D1_PROTOCOL 1 = DroneCAN Bitrate CAN_P1_BITRATE 1000000 GPS over CAN GPS1_TYPE before 4.6 — GPS_TYPE 9 = DroneCAN Current sensor BATT_MONITOR 8 = DroneCAN Rangefinder RNGFND1_TYPE 24 = DroneCAN ESCs over CAN CAN_D1_UC_ESC_BM bitmask of the outputs sent to the bus as ESC commands The node's compass is picked up automatically it shows up in the compass list . After changing CAN_ , reboot. In Mission Planner: Setup → Optional Hardware → DroneCAN/UAVCAN shows the nodes, their parameters and firmware update; that's also where SLCAN mode is, which turns the flight controller into a USB-CAN adapter for DroneCAN GUI Tool. PX4 setup UAVCAN_ENABLE : 2 — sensors, 3 — sensors and ESCs; after that, nodes are discovered automatically, and which data to accept is chosen with the UAVCAN_SUB_ parameters. ESCs over CAN: UAVCAN_ENABLE = 3 , then output mapping on the Actuators tab in QGC. The details differ between versions — check the DroneCAN section of the PX4 docs for your version. ESCs over CAN and bus load The ESC command esc.RawCommand carries 14 bits per motor: for 8 motors that's 14 bytes of payload, i.e. a multi-frame message of ~3 frames. At 400 Hz that's ~1200 frames/s. A CAN frame with 8 data bytes and an extended identifier is ~130–150 bits with bit stuffing; at 1 Mbit/s the bus carries ~7000 frames/s. ESC commands take ~15–20 %, plus ESC telemetry coming back, GPS, compass, current sensor. Rule: keep the bus load below ~50 %, and put ESCs and navigation sensors on different buses if there are many nodes. AP_Periph: your own node AP_Periph is ArduPilot firmware that turns an STM32 board your own or an off-the-shelf one: GPS modules, “CAN adapters” into a DroneCAN node. The same hwdef as flight controllers, and ArduPilot drivers run on the node: GPS, compass, baro, rangefinders, airspeed, LEDs, all the way up to a CAN → PWM/DShot ESC bridge the node takes ESC commands from the bus and outputs them to ordinary ESCs . This is the way to go when you need a CAN sensor that isn't sold. {{diagram:dronecan-bus DroneCAN on a vehicle: a linear bus with 120 Ω terminators at the ends; the flight controller allocates node IDs DNA , GPS, current sensor and ESCs on one pair of wires.}} practice Step 1. Check the bus with the power off Build the bus: flight controller → splitter → GPS/compass → current sensor or any two nodes . text: summary Most “mysterious” failures are a cold solder joint, a chafed wire or a connector that was hanging by a thread. This module is about the craft: how to solder power pads and thin signal wires without cold joints, which solder and flux to use, how to tin, how to strip insulation, route harnesses, secure them and protect them from vibration, and how to check connections mechanically and electrically before flying. theory The physics of soldering Solder wets metal only at a high enough temperature and on a clean surface. Flux dissolves the oxides. A cold joint is solder that set without wetting one of the sides: dull, grainy, balled up. It conducts today and breaks from vibration tomorrow. - Temperature : 330–370 °C for leaded solder Sn63/Pb37, melts at 183 °C , 370–400 °C for lead-free. Big power pads need a big tip and power 60–80 W , otherwise the pad won't heat through and you get a cold joint; small FC pads need a fine tip and brief contact ≤ 3 s , otherwise the pad lifts. - Solder : 0.6–0.8 mm flux-core for signal wires, 1.0 mm for power. Leaded is easier for beginners lower temperature, better flow . - Flux : no-clean or rosin; active acid flux — never on electronics. Rosin residue — wash it off with isopropyl alcohol: it's hygroscopic and can conduct. - Tinning : before joining, tin both the wire and the pad. The joint — press the tinned wire against the tinned pad, heat until they merge, hold still until it sets 1–2 s . Wires - Silicone insulation, stranded — for everything on board: flexible, tolerates soldering-iron heat. - Strip insulation with a gauge-matched stripper, not a knife: nicked strands break. - Tinned length = pad depth; an extra tinned section becomes stiff and breaks at the boundary — the wire should bend at the insulation, not at the joint. - Heat shrink on every exposed section, especially the power ones. Wire gauge: calculate, don't guess A copper wire is a resistor. Resistance per meter 20 °C by gauge: AWG mΩ/m Where on board --- --- --- 10 3.3 battery → PDB on heavy aircraft 60–100 A 12 5.2 6S battery on 10" and X8 14 8.3 battery on 5", phases of powerful motors 16–18 13–21 4-in-1 ESC on 5", phases 20–22 33–53 5 V BEC, VTX, camera 26–28 134–213 UART, I²C signals, sensors Worked example: a 10" on 6S, 60 A peak current, positive and negative 15 cm each 0.3 m of loop . 14 AWG: R = 8.3·0.3 = 2.5 mΩ, a 0.15 V drop, 9 W of heating in the wire at peak. 18 AWG: 0.38 V and 23 W — the wire heats up, the insulation softens, and the drop adds to the battery sag. 12 AWG: 0.09 V and 5.6 W. Criterion course guideline, the same as in el-power-design : the drop on the power pair at peak current ≤ 1 % of the pack voltage — 0.22 V for 22.2 V; continuous current no higher than the gauge rule there. 14 AWG 0.15 V, 0.7 % and 12 AWG 0.09 V pass, 18 AWG 0.38 V, 1.7 % does not. For a 5" the table's “14 AWG” row holds with short leads: a 0.2 m loop at a 100 A peak — 0.17 V. Conclusion: power gauge is chosen by peak current and length, not “like everyone else”; short power wires are a free voltage bonus. {{widget:wire-drop}} Contact: where you lose more than in the wire A bad joint or an old connector is 1–5 mΩ instead of fractions of a mΩ. At 50 A every extra milliohm is 2.5 W of heat in a spot the size of a pea; the connector plastic melts before anything is noticeable in flight. Per the Amass datasheet an XT60 is 30 A continuous 60 A instantaneous ; an XT90 is 45–55 A continuous depending on the wire 12–8 AWG , an AS150 75 A on 8 AWG the rule is in el-power-design . A connector that's warm after a flight while the wires are cold is a candidate for replacement. Crimping vs soldering Crimping with the right tool gives a gas-tight joint that isn't afraid of vibration; soldering a crimp makes the strands stiff at the edge and the wire breaks next to it. Signs of a bad crimp: strands sticking out of the barrel, the insulation not gripped by the second pair of tabs, the wire rotates. Test: pull with 2–3 kg of force for 26–28 AWG — it shouldn't come out. Connectors Soldering XT30/XT60: connector mated to its pair so the plastic doesn't warp , heat the pads until the solder flows, insert the wire, add more solder. JST-SH/GH pins — crimp, don't solder; crimp with the right tool or buy ready-made harnesses. Connectors under vibration — secure them a drop of hot glue on the housing, not on the pins . Harnesses and vibration - A wire breaks where one point is rigid and the next one isn't: at the joint, at the zip tie. Secure it 3–5 cm from the joint, not right next to it. - A harness has a loose bend, it's not pulled tight especially to an FC on soft mounts . - Chafe protection: sleeving/heat shrink where it touches carbon; sharp frame edges — dress them. - Signal wires — twisted with ground, routed separately from power; power + and − — twisted see interference . - Nothing in the prop zone or in the folding path of a folding frame's arms. Checking 1. Visually : a shiny cone of solder, the wire outline is visible, no balls or bridges. 2. Mechanically : a light pull test on each wire; wiggle it at the joint. 3. Electrically : continuity test of neighboring pads for shorts, the resistance of a power joint — fractions of a mΩ a multimeter can't see it, but heating under load will show it . 4. Under load : props off, throttle for a minute, a thermal camera or a finger carefully on each joint: a hot one is a bad one. 5. Vibration test : motors at low throttle without props for 30 s — nothing rattles or comes loose. {{diagram:wiring-chain A reliable connection: preparation, soldering, strain relief, harness mounting and a check under current.}} practice Step 1. Practice On a scrap board/old ESC: 10 joints with 20 AWG, 10 joints with 28 AWG. Cut one power joint crosswise — the solder should fill the whole cross-section with no voids. Step 2. Power soldering on the build XT60 → PDB/ESC with 14 AWG. Check: pull test, continuity, heating under load without props . Step 3. Signal harness Receiver → F

summary: A quadcopter with a failed motor is a falling object; a hexa and an X8 can keep flying — if the power, signals and firmware are designed for it. This module covers which failures each layout survives and why (yaw moments), how to distribute power on a heavy aircraft (buses, fuses, dual BECs, a backu
headings: What each layout survives Powering a heavy aircraft Per-arm currents on an X8 Firmware behavior on a failure Step 1. Failure table Step 2. Power diagram Step 3. Motor failure in SITL Step 4. Test stand
text: summary A quadcopter with a failed motor is a falling object; a hexa and an X8 can keep flying — if the power, signals and firmware are designed for it. This module covers which failures each layout survives and why yaw moments , how to distribute power on a heavy aircraft buses, fuses, dual BECs, a backup receiver , how to compute per-arm currents on an X8 and choose wire gauges and connectors, and how to test the behavior on a motor failure in SITL and on a test stand — before it happens in the air. theory What each layout survives - Quad : a failure of any motor means loss of yaw and roll control; a controlled crash at best. Redundancy is geometrically impossible. - Hexa 6 arms : one motor fails — the remaining five can hold altitude and roll/pitch, but yaw holds poorly the CW/CCW balance is broken : the aircraft slowly spins and lands. You need T/W ≥ 2 on the remaining motors. ArduPilot and PX4, without special settings, simply “give more throttle” to the others through the mixer — this works if there's thrust margin. - X8 coaxial octo : one motor fails — its coaxial partner and the opposite pair compensate for both thrust and moment: the most survivable layout with 8 motors on 4 arms. The price is a 10–20% efficiency loss of the coaxial pair. - Flat octo : like a hexa, but with a bigger margin; survives two failures in favorable positions. - VTOL : a lift motor failure in vertical mode — like a quad; in forward flight the lift motors aren't needed — a different failure logic. What else fails more often than a motor: the ESC overheating, breakdown , the power connector, the flight controller's BEC, the receiver, the GPS, one of two IMUs. Redundancy starts with a failure table, not with extra motors. Powering a heavy aircraft Example: an X8 on 6S, 8 motors of the 4008/4006 380KV class MN4006 table, 15×5 : hover ~3.6–3.9 A per motor, maximum ~15–16 A: hover ~30 A, peak ~130 A. - Buses : a single power bus from the battery is a single point of failure. Option: two batteries in parallel through diode/ideal-diode ORing modules, or simply two parallel batteries with a fuse on each; one fails — you fly on the second. - Fuses : on each battery ANL/MIDI at 1.3 × the branch's maximum current , on the companion/payload branch, on the BEC. On the motors — no: the current is pulsed, so a fuse will either blow for nothing or fail to protect. - Dual BECs : two 5 V BECs with diode ORing for the FC and receiver a Pixhawk-class board accepts three sources: power module, USB, servo rail — with priority . One BEC fails — the aircraft lives on. - Receiver : two receivers primary CRSF + a backup on another band or one with diversity; ArduPilot: RC_OPTIONS bit 10 multiple receivers — a backup input on another UART; PX4 — RC ↔ MAVLink control fallback COM_RC_IN_MODE ; RC_MAP_ only assigns channels , INAV — at the very least one receiver with diversity antennas. - GPS/compass : two GPS units with blending GPS_AUTO_SWITCH on DroneCAN, two compasses with priority. - IMU : H7 flight controllers have two or three IMUs — the EKF switches on its own EK3 has several cores . Per-arm currents on an X8 Each arm has two motors: arm current = 2 × motor current. Hover ~7.5 A, maximum ~32 A per arm. Arm wire 12–14 AWG; an XT60 arm connector 30 A continuous, 60 A instantaneous per the Amass datasheet is at its limit at full throttle; an XT90 45 A on 12 AWG has margin. Central distribution board: 4 arms × 32 ≈ 130 A peak — copper bus bars or a 150+ A PDB, an AS150 on each battery: with two batteries in parallel each connector carries ~65 A at peak and ~15 A in hover, within the 75 A of the Amass catalogue; on a single battery 130 A exceeds both the AS150 and the XT90 60 A for a minute ; capacitors at the input of each ESC pair. Drop across a 30 cm 12 AWG arm wire at 32 A: R = 0.0172 × 0.6 / 3.31 ≈ 3.1 mΩ → 0.10 V, 3.2 W of heat at peak — acceptable; with 14 AWG ≈ 5.0 mΩ it's 0.16 V and 5 W, tolerable, but with less margin for long sessions. {{diagram:x8-power-redundancy The module's X8 power scheme: the aircraft survives the loss of one battery or one BEC, there are no fuses on the motors, and for an arm at ~32 A an XT60 is at its limit while an XT90 has margin.}} Firmware behavior on a failure - ArduPilot : the mixer normalizes the outputs; on saturation the priority is roll/pitch, then throttle, yaw last MOT_YAW_HEADROOM . A motor failure shows up in RCOU one channel at maximum, its neighbor at minimum and in the ESC telemetry RPM 0 . There's a thrust loss check the message “Potential Thrust Loss n ” : the mixer enables thrust boost and excludes the lost motor from yaw control; but survivability is still determined by thrust margin and geometry. - PX4 : has motor failure detection from ESC telemetry FD_ACT_EN — 0 by default since 1.18, enable it explicitly; thresholds MOTFAIL_C2T , MOTFAIL_OFF , MOTFAIL_TIME , before 1.18 FD_ACT_MOT_ and an action: the COM_ACT_FAIL_ACT failsafe warning/Hold/Land/Return/Terminate , while CA_FAILURE_MODE = 1 removes the motor from the mixer. - INAV : the mixer has no special logic; a hexa/X8 with thrust margin keeps flying, yaw degrades. {{diagram:redundancy-schemes What each layout survives when one motor fails.}} practice Step 1. Failure table For your layout: failure of a motor each position , ESC, battery/connector, BEC, receiver, GPS, compass, IMU → does it survive / what's noticeable / what to do. A “countermeasure” column: redundancy, detection, failsafe. Step 2. Power diagram Draw the buses with fuses, dual BECs ORing , separate branches for the companion/payload. Per-arm currents, wire gauges, connectors, capacitors. Check the drops by calculation the widget in the “Electricity 101” module . Step 3. Motor failure in SITL ArduPilot SITL: SIM_ENGINE_FAIL — a bitmask of motors motor 1 → 1, motor 3 → 4, in the code engine_fail & 1<<i , SIM_ENGINE_MUL = 0 — a complete failure 0.5 — loss of half the thrust in Loiter on a hexa/X8 -f hexa / -f octa-quad , watch RCOU , altitude, yaw. text: summary A “top”-level engineer isn't limited to what's for sale: if you need a 100 A current sensor with I²C, a power board for a specific frame, an adapter for the companion with the right connectors, you draw the board yourself. This module takes you through the full cycle in KiCad on a real example — an INA226 current sensor board with a shunt: calculating the shunt and the calibration register, the schematic and the ERC check, footprints, layout with current in mind trace width per IPC-2221 and electromagnetic compatibility, DRC for the fab's capabilities, output files for manufacturing, and testing the finished board on a flight controller. theory When to make your own board - The board you need doesn't exist, or doesn't fit in size, connectors or current. - Many identical vehicles: your own power and distribution board removes hand-soldered wiring — the main source of failures in the field module “Wiring” . - Educational value: layout forces you to understand where interference on the compass and gyro comes from. Don't: a flight controller from scratch as your first project — that means high-speed layout, an IMU, certified firmware; start with peripherals. The KiCad cycle 1. Schematic Schematic Editor : symbols, connections, net names, component values. ERC electrical rules check catches unconnected pins, two outputs on one net, forgotten power PWR_FLAG flags . 2. Footprints : each symbol gets a package 0603, SOT-23-6, MSOP-10, a JST-GH connector . A footprint error is the most expensive one: the board arrives and the chip doesn't fit. 3. Layout PCB Editor : board outline, layer stackup, component placement, traces, copper pours, vias. 4. DRC design rules check — the fab's rules: minimum trace width and clearance, holes, edge clearances. 5. Output : Gerber files for the layers, a drill file, a BOM bill of materials , a position file for automated assembly; a 3D view to check packages and connectors. {{diagram:kicad-design-flow Every check — ERC, DRC, the 3D view — sends you back on an error to the step where the mistake was made; the fab's rules are loaded into Board Setup before routing.}} Example: an INA226 current sensor The INA226 is a digital current and voltage monitor over I²C: it measures the drop across a shunt ±81.92 mV range, 2.5 µV step and the bus voltage up to 36 V — up to 8S , and computes current and power. - Shunt. Maximum current 100 A with an 81.92 mV range → R ≤ 0.82 mΩ; take 0.5 mΩ: 50 mV at 100 A, with margin. Power in the shunt, I²R: 5 W at 100 A, 0.8 W at 40 A continuous — a 2512 package or two shunts in parallel, wide copper pads for heat dissipation. - Resolution. A 2.5 µV step / 0.5 mΩ = 5 mA — it won't get more precise than that. The calibration register: CAL = 0.00512 / Current_LSB · R_shunt = 0.00512 / 0.005 · 0.0005 = 2048. - Support components. 100 nF at the supply pin, I²C pull-ups usually already on the flight controller — don't duplicate them without need , the address set by pins A0/A1, a TVS diode on the battery rail, an I²C connector with the Dronecode pinout JST-GH . - In the flight controller. ArduPilot: BATT_MONITOR — INA2xx type, the I²C bus and address BATT_I2C_BUS , BATT_I2C_ADDR , the maximum current and shunt resistance — via the INA2xx driver parameters for your version; to verify, compare with a clamp ammeter module “Measurements” . Layout for current - Trace width for a given current per IPC-2221: I = k·ΔT^0.44·A^0.725 outer layer k = 0.048, A is the cross-section in mil² . For 1 oz copper 35 µm and a +10 °C rise: 2 A — ~0.8 mm, 5 A — ~2.8 mm, 10 A — ~7.2 mm. Tens of amps are not carried by a trace: pours on both sides, 2 oz copper, rows of vias, wires and bus bars soldered to pads. - Kelvin connection of the shunt : the sense traces to the INA226 leave from the middle of the shunt pads as a separate pair, not from the power trace — otherwise the drop across the copper adds to the measurement. {{diagram:chart-trace-width Outer-layer trace width vs. current per IPC-2221: 1 oz and 2 oz copper at a 10 °C rise and 1 oz at 20 °C.}} Layout for EMC - Solid ground. On a 4-layer board: signal — ground — power — signal. The current returns along the ground directly under its trace; a slot in the pour under a trace is an antenna. - Keep high-current loops short. In a buck converter, the input capacitor goes right next to the switch and the diode/low-side switch: the loop with fast current is the main radiator on the board. - Sensitive circuits apart. IMU, compass, analog measurements — away from converters and power rails; a compass on a board with current is a bad idea module “Interference” . - Differential pairs CAN, USB — two traces side by side, equal length, over solid ground; the 120 Ω CAN terminator goes on the end node of the bus. - Connectors : ESD protection at external connectors, a keyed connector against reverse polarity, standard pinouts. Fab capabilities Cheap two-layer boards: trace and clearance from ~0.127–0.15 mm, holes from ~0.3 mm, 1 or 2 oz copper. Load the specific fab's rules into Board Setup before layout — DRC then checks exactly those. practice Step 1. Calculation For your vehicle: maximum and continuous current, battery voltage. Pick a shunt INA226 range, power, package , calculate the resolution and the calibration register, the width of the power traces or decide that the current runs through wires soldered to the shunt pads . Step 2. Schematic and ERC A new KiCad project. INA226, shunt, 100 nF, TVS, a power connector and an I²C connector JST-GH, 4 pins: +5 V, SCL, SDA, GND . Choose the address. ERC with no errors; explain or fix every warning. Step 3. Layout and DRC A two-layer board: the shunt's power pads on both sides with vias, a Kelvin pair to the INA226, a ground pour on the bottom, the I²C connector at the edge. text: summary До сих пор ты подбирал мотор и АКБ под уже существующую раму. Здесь — обратная задача: есть ТЗ груз, время, ветер , нужно получить взлётную массу, ёмкость АКБ, мотор с пропом и схему аппарата. Проблема в том, что всё зависит от всего: больше АКБ — больше масса — больше мощность — нужна ещё больше АКБ. Модуль даёт замкнутую модель: бюджет массы через массовые доли, энергию через Вт·ч/кг с учётом глубины разряда и резерва, мощность висения по теории импульсов с коэффициентом качества FM, снятым с даташита мотора, проверку T/W и запаса на ветер, выбор схемы. Лабораторная — Python-скрипт, который крутит цикл «масса ↔ АКБ ↔ мощность» до сходимости на реальных даташитах T-Motor MN4014 и Molicel P45B, а на железе — взвешивание и сверка тока висения с прогнозом. theory ТЗ в числах ТЗ «чтобы долго летал и возил камеру» не проектируется. Каждое требование — число с критерием: Требование Значение в примере Как проверяется --- --- --- Полезная нагрузка 1.0 кг камера + подвес масса, входит в бюджет Время 25 мин висения до резерва 20 % энергия АКБ Ветер работа при 10 м/с, возврат на 15 м/с 1.5 × ветер наклон и запас тяги Запас тяги T/W ≥ 2 на просевшей АКБ таблица мотора Бортовое питание 10 Вт FC, GPS, приёмник, подвес добавка к мощности Бюджет массы и массовые доли Взлётная масса m = груз + авионика + силовая установка + АКБ + рама. Раму удобно задавать долей f_frame от взлётной массы ориентир для карбоновых рам 600–800 мм — 15–20 %, уточняется взвешиванием , потому что рама растёт вместе с аппаратом. Тогда масса замыкается так: m = m_груз + m_авионика + m_моторы + m_АКБ / 1 − f_frame Почему время полёта упирается в потолок: мощность висения P ∝ m^1.5 см. ниже , энергия E ∝ m_АКБ = f_АКБ·m. Значит t ∝ f_АКБ / √m при тех же пропах: каждый следующий килограмм батареи тащит за собой рост мощности. Выход из тупика — не «ещё банка», а больший диск: при постоянной нагрузке на диск P ∝ m, и время перестаёт падать с ростом аппарата. Энергия: Вт·ч/кг, глубина разряда, резерв Даташит Molicel INR-21700-P45B: типично 4500 мА·ч, 3.6 В, 16.2 Вт·ч , масса 70 г max → 231 Вт·ч/кг на элемент в даташите 242 Вт·ч/кг — видимо, по типичной массе ≈ 67 г, а масса в даташите дана только максимальная . Дальше цифра только падает: - сборка никель, провода, балансир, термоусадка — около +10 % массы → ≈ 210 Вт·ч/кг на пакет; - глубина разряда DoD : под нагрузкой и на холоде до отсечки снимается не вся энергия; закладываем 85 %; - резерв на посадку и непредвиденное: 20 % от доступного остаётся в АКБ. Итог: 210 × 0.85 × 0.8 ≈ 143 Вт·ч на килограмм пакета реально уходит в полёт. Время: t = S·P·E_ячейки·0.85·0.8 / P_висения . Мощность висения: теория импульсов и FM Из теории диск-актуатора Leishman, гл. 2 идеальная мощность висения при тяге T и суммарной площади дисков A: P_ideal = T^1.5 / √ 2·ρ·A Реальный проп тратит больше профильное сопротивление, концевые потери, закрутка . Отношение FM = P_ideal / P_реальная — коэффициент качества figure of merit . У полноразмерных несущих винтов FM ≈ 0.7–0.8, у маленьких пропов ниже. Для расчёта удобнее «системный» FM — относительно электрической мощности из таблицы мотора, тогда в нём сразу сидят КПД мотора и ESC. Пример по таблице T-Motor MN4014 KV330 22.2 В : проп 15×5, 75 % газа — 1430 г при 173.2 Вт. T = 14.03 Н, A = π·0.1905² = 0.1140 м², P_ideal = 99.4 Вт, FM_sys = 99.4 / 173.2 = 0.574 . По всем строкам таблицы — 0.55–0.59 для 15×5 и 0.53–0.60 для 17×5.8. Это число калибрует всю модель. Нагрузка на диск Нагрузка на диск DL = T / A Н/м² . Из формулы выше удельная мощность P/T = √ DL / 2ρ / FM: меньше нагрузка — больше граммов на ватт. Тот же аппарат 4.29 кг на четырёх 15″ — 92 Н/м² и 9.3 г/Вт, на четырёх 17″ — 72 Н/м² и 10.7 г/Вт. Разница 13 % мощности — это 3.7 минуты полёта в примере ниже. Проп, мотор, KV 1. Диаметр — самый большой, что влезает в раму с зазором между пропами большой диск = низкая DL . 2. KV — чтобы на полном газу мотор крутил проп до нужной тяги: обороты под нагрузкой ≈ 0.75–0.85 × KV × U. Для MN4014: 330 × 22.2 = 7326 об/мин без нагрузки, по таблице 6000 об/мин с 15×5 0.82 и 5400 с 17×5.8 0.74 . Скорость конца лопасти 17″ при 5400 об/мин — π·0.432·90 ≈ 122 м/с M ≈ 0.36 , до шумных околозвуковых режимов далеко. 3. Ток висения — не выше ~40 % длительного тока мотора: у MN4014 длительный 25 А 180 с , на висении 1073 г с 17×5.8 — около 4.8 А. 4. T/W на просевшей АКБ : таблица снята при 22.2 В, а Li-Ion под нагрузкой во второй половине разряда даёт около 3.4 В/банку 20.4 В . Тяга ∝ U², так что максимум падает в 20.4/22.2 ² = 0.84 раза. Ветер и запас тяги В ветер V аппарат наклоняется на угол θ = atan D / mg , где D = ½·ρ·V²·CdA. Для возврата против ветра нужна воздушная скорость с запасом — берём 1.5 × ветер ориентир курса: тогда путевая скорость против ветра — половина скорости ветра, и возврат не затягивается . Тяга в установившемся полёте √ mg ² + D² должна оставлять запас на управление: не больше 80 % максимума ориентир курса: тот же запас 20 %, что в f-mechanics — его съедает просадка напряжения на 10 % . Тот же 1.5 × ветер стоит за правилом порывов в ops-weather порывы ≤ 50–60 % максимальной скорости . T/W ≥ 2 закладываем отдельно — это запас на манёвр и стабилизацию. CdA — самое слабое место модели в примере 0.06 м² принято, а не измерено ; на железе его уточняют по углу наклона в известный ветер. Ограничение наклона в ArduPilot: ATC_ANGLE_MAX в градусах по умолчанию 30; до Copter 4.7 — ANGLE_MAX в сантиградусах, 3000 . Энергию считаем по висению: на 8–12 м/с индуктивная мощность падает, так что это консервативно. Таблицы производителей сняты на новом моторе в комнате и обычно оптимистичны на 5–10 %. text: summary Таблица тяги производителя снята на его ESC, его пропе и при его температуре; твоя связка может отличаться на 5–15 %, и узнать это можно только на стенде. Модуль учит собрать стенд на ESP32 тензодатчик + HX711, INA226 для тока и напряжения, оптодатчик для оборотов , откалибровать его масштаб, тара, дрейф, ползучесть , посчитать неопределённость, кривую г/Вт, C_T и коэффициент качества FM. Основной путь — обработка реалистичного набора данных по таблице T-Motor MN4006 KV380 + 15×5; в разделе про железо — сборка и калибровка настоящего стенда. theory Что меряет стенд и зачем Минимум — четыре величины с одной меткой времени: тяга T, напряжение U, ток I, обороты n. Из них: P = U·I, удельная тяга T/P г/Вт и C_T. Датчик реактивного момента Q добавляет мощность на валу P_вал = 2π·n·Q, а с ней КПД привода и FM пропа. {{diagram:stand-signal-chain Стенд — это четыре канала с одной меткой времени. Безопасность лимит тока, таймаут команды живёт в ESP32 и не зависит ни от HX711, ни от ПК.}} Тензодатчик и HX711 Балочный тензодатчик — мост Уитстона из четырёх тензорезисторов. Выход пропорционален нагрузке и напряжению возбуждения: U_вых = S·U_exc·F/F_ном, где S — чувствительность в мВ/В. У типовой дешёвой балки серия TAL220 S = 1.0 ± 0.15 мВ/В, нелинейность и гистерезис ±0.05 % FS, ползучесть ±0.1 % FS за 30 мин, температурный уход нуля ±0.2 % FS на 10 °C. Для балки на 5 кг это ±2.5 г нелинейности, ±5 г ползучести и ±10 г ухода нуля на 10 °C. Отсюда главное правило: тара до и после каждого прогона. HX711 — 24-битный АЦП для моста. Канал A с усилением 128 даёт полную шкалу ±0.5·AVDD/128 ±20 мВ при 5 В . Скорость 10 или 80 отсчётов/с вывод RATE; курс берёт 10: каждый отсчёт усредняется в 8 раз дольше, поэтому шум ниже, а на ступени газа 10 с это всё равно 100 отсчётов, из которых первые секунды после шага отбрасываются; 80 — только для быстрых процессов, например разгона мотора после шага газа, ценой шума — ориентир курса , формат — дополнительный код, насыщение на 800000h / 7FFFFFh. Плотность воздуха ρ = p / 287.05·T_K , при 20 °C и 101.325 кПа это 1.204 кг/м³. Меряй её в день прогона: при 35 °C она на 5 % ниже, и тяга на тех же оборотах тоже. title: The plane: stability, CG, static margin, drag polar
summary: «Аэродинамика крыла» дала правило «ЦТ впереди нейтральной точки на 5–15 % САХ». Здесь ты считаешь это сам: САХ трапециевидного крыла, нейтральную точку летающего крыла и самолёта со стабилизатором (через коэффициент объёма ГО), статический запас и точку балансировки, а затем поляру сопротивления: ма
headings: САХ и где её искать Нейтральная точка и статический запас Триммирование и reflex у летающего крыла Поляра, качество и две «лучшие» скорости Что неверная центровка делает в полёте и в логе Место в системе Шаг 1. Данные рабочего примера Шаг 2. Скрипт Шаг 3. Читаем результат Переход на реальное железо
text: summary «Аэродинамика крыла» дала правило «ЦТ впереди нейтральной точки на 5–15 % САХ». Здесь ты считаешь это сам: САХ трапециевидного крыла, нейтральную точку летающего крыла и самолёта со стабилизатором через коэффициент объёма ГО , статический запас и точку балансировки, а затем поляру сопротивления: максимальное качество, скорость максимальной дальности и скорость максимальной продолжительности. Рабочий пример — Skywalker 1830 по данным производителя. Лабораторная — Python-скрипт с расчётом и сверкой с ЦТ из инструкции, затем балансировка реального планера, тест планирования и проверка триммера тангажа по логу ArduPlane/INAV. theory САХ и где её искать Средняя аэродинамическая хорда САХ, MAC — хорда условного прямоугольного крыла с теми же моментами. Все проценты центровки считаются от неё, а не от корневой хорды. Для трапециевидной консоли с корневой хордой c_r, концевой c_t, сужением λ = c_t/c_r, полуразмахом b/2 и стреловидностью передней кромки Λ: - MAC = ⅔·c_r· 1 + λ + λ² / 1 + λ ; - положение по размаху y_MAC = b/2 /3 · 1 + 2λ / 1 + λ ; - передняя кромка САХ смещена назад от корневой на x_LE = y_MAC·tg Λ. У прямого крыла x_LE = 0 и MAC ≈ S/b. Нейтральная точка и статический запас Нейтральная точка NP — положение ЦТ, при котором момент тангажа не зависит от угла атаки: dCm/dα = 0. Статический запас SM = x_NP − x_CG /MAC. Его физический смысл: dCm/dCL = −SM. При SM = 10 % прирост C_L на 0.1 порыв задрал нос даёт пикирующий момент ΔCm = −0.01, который возвращает самолёт. При SM = 0 возврата нет, при SM < 0 возмущение растёт, и автопилот держит планер только до насыщения руля. Летающее крыло. NP ≈ аэродинамический фокус крыла: четверть САХ, отложенная от её передней кромки: x_NP = x_LE + 0.25·MAC. ЦТ ставят на 5–10 % САХ впереди. Самолёт со стабилизатором. Стабилизатор сдвигает NP назад Etkin, MIT 16.333 : h_n = h_ac + η·V_h· a_t/a_w · 1 − dε/dα , где h — доли САХ от её передней кромки, h_ac ≈ 0.25; - V_h = S_h·l_h/ S·MAC — коэффициент объёма ГО : площадь стабилизатора S_h на плечо l_h от четверти САХ крыла до четверти хорды ГО , делённые на S·MAC. У тренеров и FPV-самолётов 0.4–0.7; для своего проекта старт — 0.6 ориентир курса: в разобранном примере Skywalker 1830 при 0.6 весь диапазон ЦТ из инструкции даёт запас 6.6–11 %, при 0.5 задний край — только 2.2 % , у готового планера V_h не выбирают, а замеряют; - a = 2π·AR/ 2 + √ AR² + 4 — наклон C_L α крыла и ГО конечного удлинения, 1/рад; - dε/dα ≈ 2a_w/ π·AR — скос потока от крыла на стабилизаторе; - η ≈ 0.9 — торможение потока у ГО. Фюзеляж и мотор впереди крыла сдвигают NP вперёд на несколько % САХ: формула оптимистична, поэтому не целься в нижнюю границу 5 %. Точнее NP считает XFLR5 метод вихревой решётки : строишь крыло и ГО, подбираешь положение ЦТ, при котором кривая Cm α становится горизонтальной — это и есть NP. Триммирование и reflex у летающего крыла Момент относительно ЦТ: Cm = Cm0 − SM·C_L. Ровный полёт — это Cm = 0, то есть C_L,trim = Cm0/SM. При положительном запасе нужен положительный Cm0. У самолёта его даёт стабилизатор с отрицательным углом установки. У крыла хвоста нет, а обычный несимметричный профиль имеет Cm0 < 0 порядка −0.05…−0.1 , поэтому крылья летают на профилях с отогнутой вверх задней кромкой reflex , на стреловидности с круткой законцовок или с элевонами, поднятыми на 2–4 мм. Пример: SM = 8 %, крейсерский C_L = 0.35 → нужен Cm0 = 0.08·0.35 = +0.028. При SM = 15 % — уже +0.053: больше отгиб, больше балансировочное сопротивление, ниже C_Lmax. Поэтому у крыльев запас держат 5–10 %, а не 15. Поляра, качество и две «лучшие» скорости Поляра сопротивления: C_D = C_D0 + k·C_L², k = 1/ π·e·AR . C_D0 — вредное сопротивление фюзеляж, камера, антенны, шероховатость пены , e — коэффициент Освальда эллипс — 1.0, прямоугольное крыло — около 0.7 по NASA, трапеция с AR ≈ 8 — 0.75–0.85 . - Максимум качества L/D max = 1/ 2√ C_D0·k при C_L = √ C_D0/k → скорость V_md. Для электросамолёта масса не меняется это скорость максимальной дальности : энергия на километр пропорциональна силе сопротивления. - Минимум мощности при C_L = √ 3·C_D0/k , V_mp = V_md/3^¼ ≈ 0.76·V_md — скорость максимальной продолжительности . - Ограничение снизу — сваливание: V_s = √ 2mg/ ρ·S·C_Lmax . У нагруженных FPV-самолётов V_mp часто оказывается ниже 1.2·V_s, и продолжительность на деле упирается в AIRSPEED_MIN . - Во встречный ветер для дальности лети быстрее V_md: грубое правило планеристов — прибавить около половины встречной составляющей. {{diagram:chart-stability-polar Для 2.7 кг и C_D0 0.040 максимум качества 11.3 приходится на 10.8 м/с, а минимум мощности 8.2 м/с лежит ниже сваливания 9.4 м/с: продолжительность ограничивает AIRSPEED_MIN, а не поляра. Вершина качества пологая: 12 м/с стоят всего на 2.3 % больше энергии на километр.}} Что неверная центровка делает в полёте и в логе - Задний ЦТ SM < 5 % : самолёт «нервный», перерегулирует по тангажу, плохо держит скорость, склонен к сваливанию на крыло и штопору; AUTOTUNE выдаёт маленькие коэффициенты. При SM < 0 после броска задирает нос, и руль упирается в упор. - Передний ЦТ SM 20 % : нужен постоянный руль вверх, растёт балансировочное сопротивление, не хватает руля на выравнивание при посадке, самолёт тяжело отрывается от земли. - ArduPlane : документация по ЦТ предлагает смотреть интегратор тангажа PIDP.I после первого полёта. Стабильно больше нуля — самолёту не хватает руля вверх тяжёлый нос или неверный триммер руля высоты , меньше нуля — хвост тяжёлый. Ещё смотри CTUN.Pitch против CTUN.NavPitch качание — малый запас и выход руля высоты в RCOU против SERVOn_TRIM . SERVO_AUTO_TRIM = 1 подстраивает триммеры серв в полёте, но не более чем на 20 % от центра, а PTCH_TRIM_DEG задаёт угол тангажа ровного полёта. Оба параметра исправляют триммер, но не центровку. - INAV : fw_level_pitch_trim градусы — тангаж ровного полёта в самовыравнивающихся режимах, feature FW_AUTOTRIM — автотриммирование средних точек серв. Признак тот же: устойчивая ненулевая I-составляющая тангажа в Blackbox. Место в систем

text: summary Регулятор выдаёт три момента и тягу, а моторов 4, 6 или 8, и стоят они где угодно. Перевод делает миксер в PX4 — control allocation . Ты соберёшь его на Python так же, как PX4: матрица эффективности, псевдообратная, нормировка, последовательная десатурация. Затем прогонишь неудобные случаи: dead cat с ЦТ не по центру, манёвр на упоре, гексу без мотора, наклонные моторы, и перенесёшь результат в Betaflight mmix , ArduPilot FRAME_CLASS 15 + Lua и PX4 CA_ , вкладка Actuators . Лабораторная: свой фрейм в Python и PX4 SITL, отказ мотора в SIH, на железе — тест моторов без пропов и лог висения. theory Матрица эффективности B Каждый мотор i с нормированной командой uᵢ ∈ 0, 1 создаёт силу и момент. PX4 считает их по формуле из ActuatorEffectivenessRotors.cpp одинаково в 1.15, 1.16 и 1.17 : - тяга: Fᵢ = CT · aᵢ , где aᵢ — единичная ось ротора CA_ROTORn_AX/AY/AZ , по умолчанию 0, 0, −1 , то есть вверх в осях FRD ; - момент: Mᵢ = CT · pᵢ × aᵢ − CT · KM · aᵢ , где pᵢ — положение ротора относительно ЦТ в метрах CA_ROTORn_PX/PY/PZ , KM — отношение реактивного момента к тяге: положительное у CCW-ротора, отрицательное у CW умолчания CT = 6.5, KM = 0.05 . Столбцы Mx My Mz Fx Fy Fz ᵀ образуют матрицу B размером 6×N; нужно найти u, при котором B·u равно запрошенным моментам и тяге. У коптера с вертикальными моторами строки Fx и Fy нулевые, независимых осей четыре. Псевдообратная и нормировка При N 4 решений бесконечно много. PX4 берёт псевдообратную M = pinv B , то есть решение с минимальной нормой u, и нормирует столбцы ControlAllocationPseudoInverse.cpp : крен и тангаж приводит к общему масштабу, рыскание к максимуму 1, тягу к среднему по моторам. Так MC_ RATE_K значат одно и то же на любой раме, но если геометрия меняет физическую эффективность оси, меняется и усиление контура шаг 5 . Betaflight и ArduPilot получают готовые коэффициенты roll/pitch/yaw/throttle на мотор ArduPilot приводит их к ±0.5 в normalise_rpy_factors . Знаки различаются — главная ошибка при переносе: Прошивка Где матрица Знак pitch у заднего мотора Рыскание у CW --- --- --- --- PX4 считается из CA_ROTORn_ отрицательный нос вверх = +My KM < 0 ArduPilot add_motor_raw n, roll, pitch, yaw, order отрицательный как PX4 −1 Betaflight mmix n THR ROLL PITCH YAW положительный mixerQuadX −1 документация: 1 = CCW Насыщение: кто уступает первым Когда команда выходит за 0, 1 , кто-то уступает: - PX4 CA_METHOD = 1 или 2 = Auto, которое для мультиротора выбирает последовательную десатурацию, ControlAllocationSequentialDesaturation.cpp . При MC_AIRMODE = 0 тягу разрешено только уменьшать, затем ужимаются крен и тангаж, рыскание добавляется последним и режется первым; для него верхнюю границу временно поднимают на 15 % MINIMUM_YAW_MARGIN . При MC_AIRMODE = 1 тягу можно и поднять ради крена/тангажа, при 2 — ещё и ради рыскания. CA_METHOD = 0 просто обрезает выходы, и оси начинают влиять друг на друга. - ArduPilot AP_MotorsMatrix::output_armed_stabilizing . Сначала ограничивается рыскание до того, что влезает при «лучшем» газе, но не меньше MOT_YAW_HEADROOM /1000 умолчание 200 → 0.2 . Если roll+pitch+yaw всё равно шире диапазона, они масштабируются вместе, а газ сдвигается; ставятся флаги limit. . Air-mode в Acro включается через ACRO_OPTIONS бит 0 или RC-опцию 84. - Betaflight mixer.c , mixer_type = LEGACY по умолчанию; варианты 2025.12.5 — LEGACY, LINEAR, DYNAMIC, EZLANDING. LINEAR и DYNAMIC — другой способ уместить размах в 0…1, общая функция applyMixerAdjustmentLinear , отличаются формулой сдвига каждого мотора; EZLANDING — ограничение для посадки, bf-features-tour . Ориентир курса: LEGACY для обычной сборки; другой тип — только как эксперимент со сравнением двух логов одного манёвра. Если размах roll+pitch+yaw больше 1, все три оси делятся на размах одинаково, после чего газ сдвигается так, чтобы всё уместилось. Без airmode при газе ниже 50 % размах дополнительно ужимается до 0.5…1. Приоритет крена над рысканием получается раньше, на PID: pidsum_limit = 500 против pidsum_limit_yaw = 400. Отказ мотора на гексе На гексе X с чередованием вращения PNPNPN после потери одного мотора псевдообратная сама загоняет противоположный мотор в 0, и висение держат четыре оставшихся. Каждый тянет W/4 вместо W/6 — в 1.5 раза больше. Мотор на нуле упирается в границу, и в части направлений запаса по моменту нет шаг 4 . Раскладка PPNNPN пример MotorMatrix_fault_tolerant_hex.lua в ArduPilot часть отказов переживает с запасом по всем осям. Как реагируют прошивки: - PX4. CA_FAILURE_MODE = 1 убирает отказавший мотор из матрицы в 1.15–1.18 это единственный режим, кроме 0 = Ignore . Об отказе узнают от детектора по току ESC: в 1.18 — FD_ACT_EN по умолчанию 0 , проверка выключена , ожидаемый ток MOTFAIL_C2T = 35 А при полной тяге, допуск MOTFAIL_OFF = 10 А в обе стороны, MOTFAIL_TIME = 1 с esc_check_params.yaml , v1.18.0 ; в 1.15–1.17 — FD_ACT_EN = 1, FD_ACT_MOT_THR = 0.2, FD_ACT_MOT_C2T = 2.0 А/%, FD_ACT_MOT_TOUT = 100 мс. Действие задаётся в COM_ACT_FAIL_ACT . В ветке main режимы расширены: 1 и 2 вдобавок останавливают или реверсируют противоположный мотор гексы. - ArduPilot. Детектор thrust_loss_check включает thrust boost, если 1 с аппарат снижается при газе ≥ 90 % или упоре по газу и целевом наклоне < 15°. В GCS приходит сообщение «Potential Thrust Loss N ». Мотор с наибольшим фильтрованным выходом считается потерянным и исключается из расчёта насыщения; детектор дисбаланса тяги работает только при ≥ 6 моторах. - Betaflight. Отдельной обработки отказа мотора нет. Наклонные моторы Если ось мотора наклонить по касательной к окружности на угол θ в ту же сторону, куда действует его реактивный момент, плечо r тоже начинает работать на рыскание: Mz = CT · r · sinθ + KM · cosθ , а вертикальная тяга падает как cosθ . При r = 0.246 м и KM = 0.05 наклон 10° даёт ×1.84 по рысканию ценой 1.5 % тяги; боковые силы пар взаимно гасятся. Как выбрать θ: по логу определить, во сколько раз не хватает рыскания рыскание упирается в насыщение на манёвре , решить r·sinθ + KM ·cosθ / K

text: summary Blackbox Explorer and MAVExplorer show plots; an engineer needs numbers you can compare before/after and put in a report. This module is a minimal stack: Python + pandas + numpy + scipy + matplotlib; how to read a Betaflight log via blackbox_decode into CSV and an ArduPilot log .bin via pymavlink , how to build a gyro spectrum with Welch's method, and how to write reusable metric functions: overshoot, settling time, bounce-back, loop jitter. All the code works, with expected numbers. theory Stack and installation bash python3 -m venv ~/uav-venv && source ~/uav-venv/bin/activate pip install pandas numpy scipy matplotlib pymavlink blackbox_decode comes from the betaflight/blackbox-tools repository built with make ; it turns a .BFL into a CSV with one row per PID loop. Reading logs Betaflight CSV : columns time us , gyroADC 0..2 deg/s; after the filters it is gyroADC , before them gyroUnfilt a separate blackbox field in 4.5, enabled by field selection; debug_mode = GYRO_SCALED writes the unfiltered gyro into debug , setpoint 0..3 , motor 0..3 , rcCommand 0..3 , axisP/I/D/F ... , eRPM ... with ESC telemetry. python import pandas as pd, numpy as np df = pd.read_csv "log.01.csv", skipinitialspace=True df.columns = c.strip for c in df.columns t = df "time us " .to_numpy / 1e6 fs = 1 / np.median np.diff t logging rate, Hz 8000/4000/2000 gyro_roll = df "gyroADC 0 " .to_numpy ArduPilot .bin : python from pymavlink import mavutil m = mavutil.mavlink_connection "flight.bin" rows = while msg := m.recv_match type="ATT" is not None: rows.append msg.to_dict att = pd.DataFrame rows ; att "t" = att "TimeUS" / 1e6 For high-rate gyro data use IMU usually 1 kHz with RAW IMU in LOG_BITMASK or the batch samples ISBH/ISBD up to several kHz for spectra; INS_LOG_BAT_MASK . Spectrum: why Welch and not a single FFT An FFT of the whole log is noisy and depends on its length. Welch's method cuts the signal into overlapping windows, takes the FFT of each and averages them: an estimate of the power spectral density with controlled resolution Δf = fs / nperseg . python from scipy.signal import welch f, pxx = welch gyro_roll, fs=fs, nperseg=1024, noverlap=512, window="hann" pxx_db = 10 np.log10 pxx + 1e-12 With fs = 8000 and nperseg = 1024 the resolution is 7.8 Hz; a motor peak at 250 Hz shows up as a bump 2–3 bins wide. Compare logs only with the same fs and nperseg. The segment for the spectrum is a hover or steady flight of 10–20 s, without full throttle otherwise the peaks smear across frequencies . Spectrogram python from scipy.signal import spectrogram f, tt, S = spectrogram gyro_roll, fs=fs, nperseg=512, noverlap=256 imshow 10 log10 S , aspect="auto", origin="lower", extent= tt 0 , tt -1 , f 0 , f -1 It shows whether the peaks move with RPM motors or stay put resonance — see the “Signals and Spectra” module. Step response metrics From a setpoint → gyro pair on one axis: - Error e t = setpoint − gyro. - Overshoot — how far gyro flies past the setpoint after a step, in % of the step size. - Settling time — after how many ms gyro stays within ±5% or ±2% of the setpoint. - Bounce-back — after a sharp stick stop setpoint → 0 gyro swings to the opposite side: the rebound amplitude in % of the peak value before the stop. - Delay — the lag between setpoint and gyro at the cross-correlation maximum. A convenient implementation doesn't search for steps by hand but builds a step response by deconvolution like PID Toolbox : compute the impulse response of the setpoint→gyro system over windows and integrate it. Simpler for a start — pick the segments where d setpoint/dt is large and measure on them. python def step_metrics sp, gy, fs, thr=200.0 : """Find fast setpoint steps deg/s per sample threshold and measure response.""" d = np.diff sp idx = np.where np.abs d thr / fs 1000 0 res = for i in idx: seg_sp, seg_gy = sp i:i + int 0.25 fs , gy i:i + int 0.25 fs if len seg_gy < 10: continue target = seg_sp -1 ; base = sp i step = target - base if abs step < 50: continue resp = seg_gy - base / step normalised 0→1 overshoot = max 0.0, resp.max - 1.0 100 inside = np.abs resp - 1.0 < 0.05 settle = next k for k in range len inside if inside k: .all , None res.append {"t": i / fs, "step": step, "overshoot_pct": overshoot, "settle_ms": None if settle is None else 1000 settle / fs} return pd.DataFrame res Bounce-back : python def bounce_back sp, gy, fs, big=200.0 : """After setpoint returns to ~0 from a large value big deg/s , measure gyro reversal % of peak .""" out = hi = np.abs sp big for i in range 1, len sp : if hi i - 1 and not hi i : peak = sp i - 1 win = gy i:i + int 0.2 fs rev = -np.sign peak win out.append 100 max 0.0, rev.max / abs peak return np.array out Reference values for a 5" Betaflight : overshoot 5–15% is good; bounce-back < 10% is good, 25% means too much D or poor mechanics. {{diagram:step-metrics-anatomy What the functions compute: overshoot — the overshoot above a normalized step, settling time — entering ±5 % for good, bounce-back — the rebound after the stick is released, in percent of the peak the response shape is schematic .}} {{diagram:chart-dpy-sitl-roll-step A real roll step from the lab's ArduCopter 4.7.2 SITL log: the target RDes is acceleration-limited and rises for about 100 ms, the response R lags by 30 ms at the 50 % level and enters the ±5 % band after 202 ms without overshoot.}} Loop jitter python dt = np.diff t 1e6 µs print dt.mean , dt.std , np.percentile dt, 99.9 At 8 kHz the mean is 125 µs and the std a few µs; std 10 means an overloaded processor, gaps mean dropped log writes. {{diagram:log-analysis-pipeline A Python log analysis pipeline: CSV → DataFrame → common time axis → spectra and metrics → report.}} practice Step 1. Read Your own log Betaflight CSV or ArduPilot .bin → DataFrame, fs computed, the first 5 rows and the column description printed. Step 2. Spectrum Pick 10 s of hover, run welch on all three axes, plot in dB up to fs/2, label the peaks with their frequencies. Save a PN

Practice on synthetic data Step 1. Spectrogram Step 2. Harmonics ↔ eRPM Step 3. Resonance Step 4. The filter, numerically
text: summary Betaflight and ArduPilot filters are signal processing, and tuning them by intuition means tuning blind. This module gives you the minimum theory without which you can't read a spectrum: sampling and the Nyquist frequency, aliasing why 10 kHz interference shows up as 2 kHz , what a spectrum and a spectrogram are, how to find motor harmonics and tell them apart from frame resonance, and what LPF and notch filters do in both the frequency domain attenuation and the time domain delay . With Python code and the link to eRPM. theory Sampling and Nyquist The gyro is sampled at a rate fs Betaflight: 8 kHz on F4/F7/H7 with MPU6000/ICM42688; ArduPilot: 1–4 kHz with batch logging up to 8 kHz . The Kotelnikov–Nyquist theorem: frequencies up to fs/2 can be represented without distortion. Anything above “folds over” aliasing : a signal of frequency f fs/2 appears at f − k·fs . Example: fs = 8 kHz, 10 kHz interference → seen as 2 kHz. A worse example: ArduPilot logs the IMU at 1 kHz while sampling internally at 4 kHz — a motor harmonic at 600 Hz ends up at 400 Hz in the log. Hence: spectra only from data with a known fs, batch logging for frequencies above 500 Hz, and the gyro's hardware anti-aliasing filter configurable on the ICM42688 is mandatory. Spectrum: what's on the axes The horizontal axis is frequency Hz , the vertical axis is power dB or deg²/s²/Hz . “A peak at 250 Hz, 20 dB above the noise” means 100 times more power than the background. The Welch spectrum averages over time — good for a steady segment hover . A spectrogram is the spectrum over time: color is power, the vertical axis is frequency; you can see the peaks move with throttle. Resolution: frequency versus time A spectrum over N samples resolves frequencies in steps of Δf = fs/N and describes a segment of duration N/fs. 8 kHz and N = 512: Δf ≈ 15.6 Hz over 64 ms; N = 4096: Δf ≈ 2 Hz, but over half a second — a peak that “moved” with throttle smears into a band. For hover you use long windows fine frequency resolution , for a spectrogram of maneuvers — short ones. The Hann window the default in scipy.signal.welch reduces the “leakage” of a strong peak's power into neighboring frequencies; without a window, a false “skirt” that looks like noise appears around the motor harmonic. Motor harmonics The motor fundamental is f₁ = RPM/60. Betaflight with ESC telemetry computes it from eRPM: RPM = eRPM / pole pairs ; a 2207 typically has 7 pairs 14 magnets → motor_poles = 14 . On the spectrogram these are sloped lines, repeated at 2f₁, 3f₁ blades, imbalance . Four motors give four close lines that merge into a band. Check: take the eRPM from the log at the same moment, compute f₁, compare with the peak position — a match within ±5 Hz confirms it's a motor. Resonance versus motors - A peak that is horizontal on the spectrogram independent of throttle is a resonance of the frame/mount/wires. Fixed with mechanics or a static notch. - A sloped peak tracks eRPM is a motor. Fixed with the RPM filter it tracks on its own or balancing. - A broad “cushion” at the bottom, 20–80 Hz, growing with sharp moves — propwash and aerodynamics; it can't be filtered without losing response; it's addressed with D-term and mechanics. What a filter does — two points of view A 1st-order LPF PT1 with cutoff frequency fc: in the frequency domain −3 dB at fc, then −20 dB/decade ×10 in frequency = ×0.1 in amplitude . In the time domain — delay : the group delay at low frequencies ≈ 1/ 2π·fc ; a 100 Hz PT1 delays the useful signal by ~1.6 ms. PT2/PT3 cascades cut steeper −40/−60 dB/decade but delay more. Betaflight: gyro_lpf1_static_hz , dterm_lpf1_static_hz , throttle-based dynamic LPF; ArduPilot: INS_GYRO_FILTER , ATC_RAT_ _FLTD/FLTE/FLTT . A notch centered at fₙ with a width Q : a deep dip only around fₙ, little delay outside the band. Narrow high Q — precise, but misses when RPM changes; wide — more robust, but delays more. The RPM notch is narrow because it knows the frequency; the dynamic notch searches for the peak itself Betaflight dyn_notch_count/q/min_hz/max_hz ; ArduPilot's harmonic notch INS_HNTCH_ with tracking by throttle, RPM or FFT . The price of any filter is delay; the price of delay is stability margin the “Control Theory” module . The goal of filter tuning: minimum delay with motor noise below the level that heats the motors D-term noise . Ballpark numbers 5" 6S hover: f₁ ≈ 250–350 Hz, peaks 20–30 dB above the background before filtering, ≤ 5 dB after the RPM notch. The delay of the gyro LPF + D LPF chain in a good 5" tune is 1–2 ms; with “heavy” filtering it's 4–6 ms, and that's already noticeable in bounce-back. {{diagram:peak-diagnosis How to identify a peak in the gyro spectrum by how it behaves with throttle, and how to deal with it.}} {{diagram:chart-gyro-spectrum A model gyro spectrum: at the bottom, the vehicle's motion the useful signal , motor harmonic peaks moving with throttle , a narrow frame resonance peak staying put and the noise floor.}} {{diagram:chart-aliasing Aliasing at 1 kHz sampling: everything above 500 Hz “folds” into the 0–500 Hz band — a 700 Hz vibration looks like 300 Hz in the data. That's why the anti-aliasing filter must come before sampling, not after.}} practice Step 0. Practice on synthetic data Before trusting your own log analysis, check it on a signal where the answer is known: python import numpy as np from scipy import signal fs = 8000; t = np.arange 0, 10, 1 / fs rpm = np.interp t, 0, 5, 10 , 12000, 21000, 12000 throttle up and down phase = 2 np.pi np.cumsum rpm / 60 / fs motor fundamental follows rpm x = 2.0 np.sin phase + 0.8 np.sin 2 phase motor 1x and 2x + 1.0 np.sin 2 np.pi 180 t frame resonance, fixed + np.random.default_rng 0 .normal 0, 0.5, t.size noise floor f, P = signal.welch x : 2 fs , fs, nperseg=2048 first 2 s: near-steady print "peaks Hz :", sorted int v for v in f signal.find_peaks 10 np.log10 P , prominence=10 0 f2, t2, S = signal.spectrogram x, fs, nperseg=512, noverlap=384 Expected:
