The frame rate Moving to real hardware
text: summary A servo on a Betaflight quad is not “plug in and it works”: the firmware has to support servos in Cloud Build — the SERVOS option , the output has to sit on a timer that is not used by DShot, the power has to come from a separate BEC, and smix is not applied on a quad at all. This module separates three different kinds of “PWM” motor PWM/OneShot, DShot, the 1000–2000 µs servo pulse at 50–333 Hz , explains STM32/AT32 timers and channels, how to read timer , resource , dma show and how to move a servo to a free pad, goes through the servo and smix commands from the source the same in 4.5 and 2025.12 and the SERVO_TILT and CHANNEL_FORWARDING features, and builds a simple pan/tilt gimbal. The lab: a Python script parses the real SpeedyBee F405 V4 config from the 4.5-config branch and the F405 timer table from the source, finds the pads that can do 50 Hz with DShot600 on the motors, and computes the servo pulse with the servos.c formulas; then the bench without props, a servo on a separate BEC, a tester or an oscilloscope, and a gimbal test. theory Three different kinds of “PWM” on one board A beginner calls everything that comes out of a pad “PWM”. In fact these are three different signals: Signal What is transmitted Period / frequency In Betaflight 2025.12 --- --- --- --- Motor PWM a 1000–2000 µs pulse motor_pwm_rate 480 Hz 200–32000 ; for PWM always asynchronous and no higher than 480 Hz, for OneShot/Multishot — only with use_unsynced_pwm motor_pwm_protocol = PWM , old ESCs with calibration OneShot125 / 42 / Multishot a short pulse of 125–250 / 42–84 / 5–25 µs once per PID loop synchronous the same setting; analog, calibration is needed DShot150/300/600 a digital 16-bit frame with a CRC; DShot600 = 600 kbit/s, a 1.667 µs bit, a frame of ≈ 26.7 µs once per PID loop, there is no “frequency” DSHOT600 by default; on F4/G4 with bidir the firmware sets DSHOT300 by itself config/config.c Servo pulse a width of 1000–2000 µs center 1500 sets the angle 50 Hz 20 ms for analog servos, up to ~333 Hz for digital ones servo_pwm_rate 50 50–498 DShot is not PWM: the ESC reads bits, not the pulse width. A servo does not care how often the pulse arrives within its specification ; what matters is the width . An analog servo at 333 Hz may hum and heat up — set a frequency above 50 Hz only for digital servos and per the datasheet the servo_pwm_rate description in INAV says that most digital servos support about 330 Hz . At 498 Hz the period is 2008 µs — a 2000 pulse still fits, but the CLI servo limit up to 2500 µs no longer does. PWM inputs are alive too: feature RX_PPM and RX_PARALLEL_PWM input_filtering_mode , OFF by default capture the receiver pulses with a timer in input capture mode. USE_RX_PPM / USE_RX_PWM in both 4.5 and 2025.12 are in the non-cloud block of common_pre.h , and they are not in the option list of the Cloud Build API. For a cloud build, assume they do not exist. Timer, channel, pad In STM32 and AT32F435 PWM is generated by a hardware timer TIMx: a counter with a prescaler PSC and a period ARR. A timer has up to 4 channels CH1–CH4 TIM1/TIM8 also have the complementary CH1N–CH3N , and each channel is routed to one or two pins through an alternate function AF. A channel selects only the pulse width the CCR register , while the period and the clocking are shared by the whole timer. Hence the main rule: all the outputs of one timer run one protocol at one frequency. The numbers from the lab F405, a timer on the 84 MHz bus : - DShot600: PSC 6, ARR 19 → a 1.667 µs bit MOTOR_DSHOT600_HZ 12 MHz, MOTOR_BITLENGTH 20 ; - a 50 Hz servo: PSC 83, ARR 19999 → a 1 µs tick, a 20 ms frame servoDevInit → pwmOutConfig …, PWM_TIMER_1MHZ, 1 MHz / servo_pwm_rate, … . One timer cannot hold both modes. Betaflight does not check this: timerAllocate refuses only if the same pin-channel is taken, and hands out a neighboring channel of the same timer without question. The servos are initialized after the motors fc/init.c : motorDevInit before servoDevInit , so a servo on a channel of a motor timer will overwrite its time base, and DShot on those motors will break. The same goes for everything that lives on a timer: LED_STRIP 800 kHz + DMA , CAMERA_CONTROL hardware PWM at 84 MHz / 128 , PPM. DShot comes in two kinds. Timer + DMA : every motor pad is a channel of its timer plus a DMA stream. Bitbang : the motors are toggled as GPIO through DMA, and the clock is set by a “pacer” timer, TIM1 or TIM8 dshot_bitbang_timer AUTO/TIM1/TIM8 . With bitbang the timers of the motor pads are free, but TIM1/TIM8 must not be touched. dshot_bitbang = AUTO on F4 enables bitbang only together with dshot_bidir , and on F7/H7/G4/AT32 — always isDshotBitbangActive . The board config can override this: the SpeedyBee F405 V4 has DEFAULT_DSHOT_BITBANG = OFF . A servo does not need DMA; the dmaopt of a servo pad may be −1. How to read the board map - resource — which functions are assigned to which pins resource SERVO 1 B15 . resource show — who actually owns the pins after boot, resource show all — plus timer show and dma show . - timer show — which channels of which timers are taken and by what TIM12: CH2 : SERVO 1 , timer <pin list — which timers a pin has AF9: TIM12 CH2 , timer <pin AF<n — select one. timer list without a pin prints “NOT IMPLEMENTED YET” in both 4.5 and 2025.12 . - dma show — the DMA streams in use, dma pin <pin <opt — change the stream. - Numbering: resource SERVO and resource MOTOR count from 1 , while servo , smix and the Servos tab count from 0 . resource SERVO 1 = servo 0 in the tab. - resource SERVO 2 B10 , when B10 holds MOTOR 7 , only prints NOTE: B10 already assigned to MOTOR 7. and does not unassign the motor. Free it explicitly: resource MOTOR 7 NONE . - servoDevInit takes SERVO 1, 2, 3… in order and stops at the first empty one. SERVO 1 NONE + SERVO 2 B10 = no servos at all. {{diagram:bf-servo-timer-map On the SpeedyBee F405 V4 the motors M1–M4 take all of TIM4 and TIM3, so a servo goes on TIM2 the M7 pa

summary: A WS2812/SK6812 strip, the beeper and the DShot beacon (“the motors beep”) show the state of the aircraft and help to find it in the grass. This module goes through them from the Betaflight 2025.12 source (the 4.5 differences are named where they occur): the power, current and signal level of the st
headings: The strip hardware Build, resource, timer The `led` line The palette and `mode_color` Profiles and brightness The beeper: hardware and CLI Conditions, priorities, sound RX_LOST, RX_LOST_LANDING and WAS_EVER_ARMED `rxfail` and the BEEPER switch The DShot beacon and the ESC beacon Finding a crashed aircraft Reference table Place in the system Step 1. Parsing `led` lines Step 2. The grid and the colors Step 3. The current budget Step 4. The beeper masks Step 5. The RX_LOST and beacon timeline Step 6. Conditions, `rxfail` and “who beeps after a crash” Step 7. The config Moving to real hardware
text: summary A WS2812/SK6812 strip, the beeper and the DShot beacon “the motors beep” show the state of the aircraft and help to find it in the grass. This module goes through them from the Betaflight 2025.12 source the 4.5 differences are named where they occur : the power, current and signal level of the strip, resource LED_STRIP and why an LED on a motor's timer breaks DShot, the led syntax, the color palette with inverted saturation, mode_color , the RACE/BEACON/STATUS profiles; all the beeper conditions with their priorities and sounds, the exact code of RX_LOST / RX_LOST_LANDING and the role of the WAS_EVER_ARMED flag, rxfail for the BEEPER switch, beacon and the procedure for finding a crashed aircraft. The labs: a Python port of the firmware's parser and color math the 16×16 grid, the current budget, the beeper masks, the beacon timeline and a second script — the condition table from the source, rxfail , “who beeps after a crash” in four scenarios; then the bench without props: a multimeter before power, the strip current, and checks of RX_LOST, rxfail and the beacon. theory The strip hardware The WS2812 WS2811, SK6812 is an LED with a built-in driver and three wires: 5 V, GND, DIN . The LED pad on the board → DIN of the first one, DOUT → DIN of the next; the number = the order along the wire, from zero. Two strips in parallel from one DIN show the same thing. - Current a course guideline . Up to 60 mA per LED at full white ≈ 20 mA per channel at a value of 255 , 20 mA on average — Adafruit's rule of thumb. The Betaflight documentation: a NeoPixel Jewel 7 in white ≈ 350 mA. The estimate: I ≈ N · 3 · 20 mA · V / 255, where V = 255 · ledstrip_brightness / 100 integer math, as in the firmware ; in Python — n 3 20 255 b//100 /255 . 16 white LEDs at 100 % — 960 mA, 32 — 1.92 A, almost 10 W. - The BEC check a course guideline . Margin = I_BEC − I_other − I_strip, and it must be no less than 20 % of I_BEC − I_other . Example: a 2 A BEC, the receiver, camera and GPS at 0.9 A, 16 white LEDs at 0.96 A → a margin of +140 mA against the required 220 mA → the strip goes on a separate BEC. The 4 Hz failsafe blinking with a 50 % duty cycle gives half on average, but the peak is the full current. - Why not from the board's 5 V. The flight controller's BEC 1–3 A, see the specification already feeds the receiver, camera and GPS. A long strip in white sags the rail — the receiver and the FC itself suffer. The documentation advises a separate BEC or half of the strip from another BEC with a common ground . - Signal level. DIN reads a “1” from 0.7·VDD: at 5 V that is 3.5 V, while an MCU pin gives 3.3 V. The solutions: a 74AHCT125/74HCT245 buffer powered from 5 V Adafruit , or powering the strip below 4.7 V through a diode in the positive lead 3.3 / 0.7 = 4.71 V — the recipe from the Betaflight documentation . - Supporting parts Adafruit . A 300–500 Ω resistor in the data line at the first LED, not at the FC; a 500–1000 µF ≥ 6.3 V capacitor across the strip's supply; on a live circuit — ground first, data last. Build, resource, timer Cloud Build: the LED_STRIP option; LED_STRIP_64 — 64 LEDs instead of 32 on an F411 the build will fail . Without the option config.c clears feature LED_STRIP on every boot. The pin: resource LED_STRIP 1 <pin , usually already set by the board config. The driver light_ws2811strip_hal.c , on F4 — light_ws2811strip_stdperiph.c takes the pin's timer and a DMA stream , then rewrites the prescaler and period of the whole timer for 800 kHz: a 1.25 µs bit, a “1” ≈ 2/3 of the period, a “0” ≈ 1/3. No DMA, or the channel is taken — initialization silently returns false: the strip is dark, the motors are unharmed. It is dangerous when the LED is on the same timer as a motor . A timer has one time base PSC/ARR for its 4 channels, and DShot through DMA sets its own: DSHOT600 = 12 MHz × 20 ticks pwm_output_dshot.c . The strip is initialized after the motors fc/init.c and overrides the prescaler, while DShot rewrites the period ARR for itself on every frame. Both break: the motor gets a frame at the wrong rate the ESC does not start or beeps “no signal” , and the strip gets garbage. With dshot_bitbang AUTO: on F4 — with bidirectional DShot, on other MCUs — always, except PROSHOT a pacer timer, TIM1 or TIM8, is needed. bbFindPacerTimer looks for it after the strip and skips the ones in use. If the LED took the last suitable one an F411 has only TIM1 , the motors are given motorWriteNull , and they do not spin. The check: resource , timer show the lines LED_STRIP and MOTOR 4 next to each other under one TIMn: — a conflict , dma show DMA2 Stream 7: LED_STRIP . Moving it — timer <pin list , then resource / timer / dma pin , save details in bf-cli . The led line led <i <x ,<y :<directions :<functions :<color , i = 0…31. Per parseLedStripConfig : - x, y 0…15 — atoi and a 4-bit mask: 17 silently becomes 1. 0,0 is the north-west, with the nose at the top. - Directions N E S W U D . The F function takes the color of the first bit in the order N,E,S,W,U,D : “SE” = the color of E DARK_VIOLET , not S RED . - The base function — one: C color, F flight mode/orientation, A arm state, L battery, S RSSI, G GPS, R thrust ring; 2025.12 added P GPS bar, E battery bar, U altitude 4.5 does not have them . Each base letter overwrites the previous one. - Overlays — any number: T by AUX, Y rainbow, O Larson scanner, B blink, V color by VTX frequency, I indicators from the sticks, W warnings. The function block is ≤ 10 characters, otherwise an error. - Color — a palette index 0…15; 16 and above silently become 0. The trap: a line that packs into zero 0,0::C:0 ends the strip — updateLedCount counts up to the first zero entry. A zero in the middle cuts off the tail. The behavior of the functions in STATUS: - L / S : hue = max −30 + 1.5·percent, 0 : red at ≤ 20 %, yellow at 60 %, green at 100 %. The charge is computed from mAh with bat_capacity 0, otherwise from the voltage between vbat_min_cell_voltage and vbat_max_cell

title: IMU sensors: physics, errors, calibration
summary: The autopilot knows about the world only what its sensors tell it, and each of them lies in its own way. This module covers the physics of the MEMS gyroscope, accelerometer and magnetometer at the level an engineer needs: bias (zero offset), noise (ARW/VRW), temperature drift, scale error and non-or
headings: MEMS gyroscope MEMS accelerometer 6-position accelerometer calibration Magnetometer Barometer (briefly; more in the altitude module) What the firmware does with raw data Step 1. Gyro noise and bias at rest Step 2. Temperature drift Step 3. Accelerometer calibration Step 4. Compass: hard iron
text: summary The autopilot knows about the world only what its sensors tell it, and each of them lies in its own way. This module covers the physics of the MEMS gyroscope, accelerometer and magnetometer at the level an engineer needs: bias zero offset , noise ARW/VRW , temperature drift, scale error and non-orthogonality; what exactly the 6-position accelerometer calibration and the compass calibration hard/soft iron calibrate, and how to measure gyro bias and noise yourself. The result is an “IMU datasheet” for your own flight controller, with numbers. theory MEMS gyroscope A vibrating mass inside the chip; when the body rotates, the Coriolis force deflects it perpendicularly, and a capacitive sensor measures the deflection, which is proportional to angular rate. The output is three angular rates in °/s or rad/s , with a typical range of ±2000 °/s ICM42688: up to ±2000, 16 bits → 0.061 °/s per LSB . Errors: - Bias b — the output at zero rotation: a few °/s “out of the box”; after zero calibration on the ground ArduPilot — at power-up INS_GYR_CAL = 1 , Start-up only , Betaflight — at power-up what remains is bias instability of 0.01–0.1 °/s, which wanders with time and temperature. When you integrate ω to get an angle, a 0.05 °/s bias gives 3° per minute — that's why you can't get the angle from the gyro alone. - Noise — white, characterized by Angle Random Walk: ARW ≈ 0.1–0.5 °/√h for consumer MEMS; in a 1 kHz bandwidth that's ~0.1 °/s RMS. On a spectrum it's the flat floor that the motor peaks sit on. - Temperature drift of the bias: 0.01–0.05 °/s per °C; the board warming up by 20 °C after power-up causes a noticeable shift. ArduPilot: INS_TCAL_ temperature calibration , IMU heating on the Cube/some H7 boards BRD_HEAT_TARG . - Scale and non-orthogonality : a 0.5–1% error — over a 360° rotation that's a 2–4° error; rarely calibrated you need a rate table . - g-sensitivity : linear acceleration vibration! changes the output — yet another path by which vibration corrupts the estimate. MEMS accelerometer A proof mass on a spring; it measures specific force : at rest it reads +1 g upward the support reaction force , in free fall — 0. Hence the key fact: the accelerometer does not measure motion acceleration separately from gravity; in a steady hover it sees ~1 g along the vehicle's “up,” and in a coordinated turn — also along “up” which is why the roll angle from the accelerometer is wrong in a turn . Errors: bias tens of mg, i.e., a 1–3° horizon error without calibration , scale 1–2% , axis non-orthogonality, temperature drift, clipping saturation at ±16 g from impacts and vibration — VIBE.Clip in ArduPilot , vibration aliasing into the band. 6-position accelerometer calibration The vehicle is placed on 6 faces ±X, ±Y, ±Z up . In each one the truth is known: exactly +1 g on one axis, 0 on the others. From the six measurements you solve a system for 3 biases + 3 scales so does ArduPilot: INS_ACCOFFS + INS_ACCSCAL , an ellipsoid without cross terms — non-orthogonality is not calibrated; INS_ACC _ID is only the sensor identifier . Betaflight calibrates only the zero from a single position level — the scale error remains, but for Acro it doesn't matter. Rule: calibrate at the temperature you fly at; after a hard crash, redo it. Magnetometer Measures the magnetic field µT or mGauss on three axes; the heading is the projection of the Earth's field ~25–65 µT, inclination up to 70° at mid-latitudes — a large vertical component, which is why the heading is wrong without knowing roll/pitch . - Hard iron — a constant field from magnetized parts and DC currents on board: it shifts the measurement sphere away from the origin. Calibrated as an offset COMPASS_OFS_ ; the “compass dance” — rotating about all axes to fill the sphere. - Soft iron — ferromagnetic materials distort the field: the sphere becomes an ellipsoid. Calibrated with a matrix COMPASS_DIA_ , COMPASS_ODI_ . - Current-induced interference see the EMI module : depends on throttle → compassmot , COMPASS_MOT_ . - Compass orientation relative to the FC COMPASS_ORIENT — a common mistake with an external compass; ArduPilot can detect it automatically during calibration. {{diagram:compass-cal-choice-tree In ArduPilot two questions set the compass calibration method — can you rotate the aircraft, and does the field depend on throttle; current interference is subtracted with CompassMot or MagFit only after the mechanics are fixed.}} Barometer briefly; more in the altitude module Pressure → altitude via the standard atmosphere; errors: temperature drift, prop airflow, weather 1–3 m drift in half an hour , solar heating. Resolution of good MEMS baros is ~10 cm, noise ~0.5 m unfiltered. What the firmware does with raw data ArduPilot: INS_GYRO_FILTER / INS_ACCEL_FILTER 20 Hz LPF for accel by default , notches, then EKF3 estimates gyro and accelerometer bias in flight EKF states: XKF1.GX/GY/GZ — gyro bias, XKF2.AX/AY/AZ — accel bias . Betaflight — filters and a complementary attitude filter the “Attitude” module . {{diagram:imu-error-model MEMS error model: calibration removes scale and misalignment, the EKF estimates the bias, and mechanics and filters deal with noise and vibration.}} practice Step 1. Gyro noise and bias at rest A 60 s log on the ground, motors off ArduPilot: LOG_DISARMED = 1 , IMU ; Betaflight: blackbox with blackbox_mode = ALWAYS or via a switch . For each of the three axes: the mean bias after zero calibration and the std noise . Expected: bias < 0.1 °/s, std 0.05–0.3 °/s at 1 kHz. Step 2. Temperature drift The same log right after powering up a cold board and again after 10 minutes of warm-up: the shift in the mean. If it's 0.2 °/s, enable/check temperature calibration or heating. Step 3. Accelerometer calibration 6-position via Mission Planner / QGC ArduPilot or level + calibration in Betaflight. Check: level with a spirit level on the frame! , AHRS roll/pitch ≤ 0.5°; on its side — 90 ± 1°. Step 4. Compass: hard iron Before calibratio

title: Attitude: Euler angles, quaternions, complementary filter
summary: “Which way is up” is the first question an autopilot answers a thousand times per second. The gyro gives a fast but drifting answer; the accelerometer a slow and noisy one, but without drift; the compass gives heading. This module explains why Euler angles break (gimbal lock) and firmware lives on q
headings: Representing attitude Integrating the gyro Complementary filter What this is in firmware Why yaw is special Step 1. Recording the IMU Step 2. Your own filter Step 3. Experiments Step 4. Yaw What you should get and what to record
text: summary “Which way is up” is the first question an autopilot answers a thousand times per second. The gyro gives a fast but drifting answer; the accelerometer a slow and noisy one, but without drift; the compass gives heading. This module explains why Euler angles break gimbal lock and firmware lives on quaternions, how to integrate angular rate, how a complementary filter works in Python, ~40 lines and how it relates to ArduPilot's DCM and to Mahony/Madgwick in Betaflight/INAV. Lab: your own filter on an IMU recording against ATT from the log. theory Representing attitude - Euler angles roll φ, pitch θ, yaw ψ — convenient for humans. The problem: at θ = ±90° roll and yaw merge gimbal lock , and the equations for the angle rates contain a division by cos θ. For freestyle with loops that's unacceptable. They're used only for output ATT.Roll/Pitch/Yaw . - Rotation matrix DCM — 3×3, the columns are the aircraft axes in the earth frame. No singularities, but 9 numbers with 6 constraints; it needs orthonormalization after integration. - Quaternion q = w, x, y, z , q = 1 — 4 numbers, one constraint, no singularities, cheap multiplication. The standard in Betaflight since 3.x , INAV, PX4 vehicle_attitude.q , EKF3 states 0–3 . Quaternion → Euler conversion for output : φ = atan2 2 wx + yz , 1 − 2 x² + y² ; θ = asin 2 wy − zx ; ψ = atan2 2 wz + xy , 1 − 2 y² + z² . {{widget:attitude-3d}} Integrating the gyro Angular rate ω in body axes changes the quaternion: q̇ = ½ · q ⊗ 0, ω . Discretely over a step Δt: q ← q ⊗ cos ω Δt/2 , ω/ ω · sin ω Δt/2 , then normalize. Gyro only → drift at the bias rate 0.05 °/s → 3°/min plus accumulated noise. Complementary filter The idea: trust the gyro at high frequencies and the accelerometer gravity at low frequencies. The Mahony algorithm: 1. Predict “down” in body axes from the current q: v = R q ᵀ · 0, 0, 1 . 2. The measured “down” is the normalized accelerometer with a minus sign: −a/ a the accelerometer measures specific force; at rest in FRD it reads 0, 0, −g . 3. The error is the cross product e = −a/ a × v small when they agree; its direction is the correction axis . 4. Correct the angular rate: ω' = ω + Kp·e + Ki·∫e Ki is the gyro bias estimate! . 5. Integrate ω' into q. Kp sets the time constant of “trust” in the accelerometer: τ ≈ 1/Kp; Kp = 0.5 → ~2 s. During maneuvers a ≠ 1 g — the accelerometer lies; the standard protection is to reduce Kp when a − g is large ArduPilot DCM: AHRS_GPS_GAIN , using GPS for centripetal correction; Betaflight: imu_dcm_kp , disabling correction under large accelerations . The compass is added the same way for the yaw axis: the error between the measured and expected direction of the field's horizontal component. {{diagram:chart-attitude-kp-sweep The tilt estimate error has a minimum in Kp: on the left gyro drift causes it error b/Kp , on the right trusting a false “down” during acceleration; the a guard moves the minimum from 0.1 to 0.25–0.5 and halves the error.}} What this is in firmware - Betaflight : a Mahony-like quaternion filter, imu_dcm_kp default 2500 → 0.25 after scaling , imu_dcm_ki ; without a compass yaw drifts — irrelevant for Acro, and GPS Rescue uses the GPS course. - INAV : the same class of filter + compass and GPS course, corrections that account for acceleration from GPS. - ArduPilot : DCM a matrix, with correction from GPS velocity as the fallback; the primary one is EKF3 , where attitude is part of the state vector together with velocity, position and sensor biases. A complementary filter is an EKF with constant, non-adaptive gains. - PX4 : EKF2 ekf2 , attitude in vehicle_attitude . Why yaw is special Gravity carries no information about heading: without a compass or GPS course, yaw drifts with the gyro Z bias. In a hover that's ~3°/min, unnoticeable; over 10 minutes it's 30°, and Loiter will spiral the “toilet bowl” is the classic symptom . Yaw sources: compass interference , GPS course while moving not in a hover , dual GPS moving baseline , EKF-GSF estimation from motion, ArduPilot EK3_SRC1_YAW = 8 , external navigation. {{diagram:complementary-filter Complementary filter: the gyro integral is accurate over a short interval, the accelerometer angle over a long one; the weights α and 1 − α blend them.}} {{diagram:attitude-mahony-loop The Mahony loop in Betaflight: the gyro is always integrated, while the Kp·e correction from the accelerometer is applied only after a 25 Hz filter and a 0.9–1.1 g check; Ki is 0 by default in Betaflight.}} practice Calculation lab no hardware : att_lab.py simulates 120 s of IMU data with gyro bias, noise, vibration, sprints and a coordinated turn and compares five estimators. The script and its real output: python att_lab.py — attitude estimation lab: simulated IMU, five estimators, numbers. python3 att_lab.py pure Python 3, no packages import math, random G, FS, T = 9.81, 250, 120.0 gravity, IMU rate Hz, flight length s DT = 1.0 / FS BIAS = math.radians b for b in 0.5, -0.3, 0.2 gyro bias, deg/s - rad/s ARW = math.radians 0.005 gyro noise density, rad/s/sqrt Hz VIB = 2.0 accel vibration amplitude, m/s^2 motors on def truth t : """True roll, pitch, yaw rad and earth-frame linear acceleration NED, m/s^2 .""" r = p = y = 0.0; acc = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 if 20 <= t < 60: smooth tilts, little acceleration r = math.radians 20 math.sin 2 math.pi 0.2 t - 20 p = math.radians 15 math.sin 2 math.pi 0.13 t - 20 elif 60 <= t < 80: sprints: 4 m/s^2 forward/back, 1 s pulses a = 4.0 if int t % 4 == 0 else -4.0 if int t % 4 == 2 else 0.0 p = -math.atan2 a, G ; acc = a, 0.0, 0.0 nose down to accelerate forward elif 80 <= t < 100: coordinated turn: bank 30 deg, V = 15 m/s r = math.radians 30 ; w = G math.tan r / 15.0 y = w t - 80 acc = -G math.tan r math.sin y , G math.tan r math.cos y , 0.0 return r, p, y, acc def euler_to_q r, p, y : cr, sr, cp, sp, cy, sy = math.cos r / 2 , math.sin r / 2 , math.cos p / 2 , math.sin p / 2 , math.cos y / 2 , math.sin y / 2 return cr cp cy + sr sp sy, sr cp cy

title: The Kalman filter in plain terms, and the EKF
summary: EKF3 in ArduPilot and EKF2 in PX4 are the same trick repeated for 24 states. This module explains it in one dimension: prediction from the model, correction from the measurement, covariance as “how unsure I am,” the Kalman gain as the compromise between the two, and the innovation as the “expected v
headings: The problem One Kalman step (scalar) Worked example: two steps by hand Q and R: what they mean and how to tune them Observability: what the filter can learn at all Delays: the filter lives in the past Why this beats a complementary filter Innovations and gates What's in the EKF3 state vector Parameters worth touching Step 1. A 1D altitude filter Step 1b. The Q and R knobs Step 2. A barometer outlier Step 3. Connecting to the log
text: summary EKF3 in ArduPilot and EKF2 in PX4 are the same trick repeated for 24 states. This module explains it in one dimension: prediction from the model, correction from the measurement, covariance as “how unsure I am,” the Kalman gain as the compromise between the two, and the innovation as the “expected vs. observed” difference. You implement a 1D altitude filter from barometer and accelerometer ~30 lines , see what it does when the barometer produces an outlier, and how this looks in the log: XKF4.SV/SP/SH/SM normalized innovations , XKF3 innovations , XKF1/XKF2 states, bias . theory The problem You have a motion model how the state evolves on its own and measurements noisy, sometimes infrequent . You want a state estimate better than either of the two alone, plus an honest estimate of its uncertainty. One Kalman step scalar State x e.g., altitude , uncertainty P variance of the estimate . 1. Prediction : x⁻ = f x from the model: x + v·Δt , P⁻ = P + Q, where Q is the process noise “how wrong the model can be over one step” . 2. Innovation : y = z − h x⁻ — the measurement minus what you expected. S = P⁻ + R is its variance R is the measurement noise . 3. Gain : K = P⁻ / S ∈ 0, 1 . If the measurement is accurate small R , K → 1 and you trust the measurement; if the model is accurate small P⁻ , K → 0 and you ignore the measurement. 4. Correction : x = x⁻ + K·y, P = 1 − K ·P⁻. Everything else is the same scheme with vectors and matrices: P is the covariance matrix, H describes how the state turns into a measurement, K = P Hᵀ H P Hᵀ + R ⁻¹. Extended EKF means the model is nonlinear rotations via a quaternion , and it is linearized around the current point Jacobians . Worked example: two steps by hand Altitude is unknown: x = 0 m, P = 4 m² σ = 2 m — “roughly, give or take two meters” . The barometer has noise R = 1 m². 1. A reading z = 10 m arrives. Prediction with no motion: x⁻ = 0, P⁻ = 4 Q = 0 . S = 4 + 1 = 5, K = 4/5 = 0.8. Innovation y = 10. x = 0 + 0.8·10 = 8 m , P = 0.2·4 = 0.8 m² . The measurement is four times more precise than our guess — and it got 80 % of the weight. 2. One step passes, and the model allows drift Q = 0.1: P⁻ = 0.9. A reading z = 9 m arrives: S = 1.9, K = 0.47, y = 1, x = 8 + 0.47 = 8.47 m , P = 0.53·0.9 = 0.47 m² . The point: K dropped from 0.8 to 0.47 on its own, because the estimate got more precise. After a dozen measurements K will be ~0.1–0.3 and stop falling: Q “pumps up” the uncertainty every step, R keeps it from reaching zero, and an equilibrium sets in. That is exactly what the chart below shows. Q and R: what they mean and how to tune them - R is the rated measurement noise: barometer variance at rest, the σ² of GPS position grows with HDOP . You can measure it: log on the ground, take the signal variance. - Q is how far reality can drift from the model in one step: unmodeled accelerations, bias drift. You cannot measure it directly — it is a tuning knob. - Q too small → the filter is “overconfident”: K is small, the estimate lags behind maneuvers, innovations are systematically large, and if the gates are narrow, measurements start getting rejected and the filter diverges. - Q too large → the filter is “jittery”: K is close to 1, the estimate repeats the measurement noise, and the model is pointless. - Honesty check: the normalized innovation y/√S should be ~N 0, 1 , i.e., its square should average ≈ 1 the NIS test . A mean of 5 means the filter underestimates its uncertainty Q or R too small ; 0.1 means it overestimates it. Observability: what the filter can learn at all You can only estimate what affects the measurements. The Z accelerometer bias is visible because the baro “catches” the altitude drift. Heading without a compass is unobservable in a hover: GPS velocity is zero, and you can turn 180° — the measurements are the same. That is why ArduPilot runs a separate heading estimator based on GPS velocity in motion GSF , and with COMPASS_USE = 0 the EKF waits for the vehicle to pick up speed. Rule of thumb: if a state is unobservable, its P grows, and you see it in the log before you see it in flight. Delays: the filter lives in the past GPS arrives with a 100–200 ms delay, and so do optical flow and external navigation. EKF3 and EKF2 therefore run the filter on a “delayed time horizon”: a measurement is fused with the state at the moment it was taken, and for the control loops the current state is propagated forward using the IMU output predictor . A wrong delay GPS1_DELAY_MS , EK3_FLOW_DELAY is the classic reason innovations grow during maneuvers and drop in a hover. Why this beats a complementary filter A complementary filter is a Kalman filter with a fixed K. A real Kalman filter adjusts K itself: when GPS gives bad data large R from HDOP , trust drops; when there have been no measurements for a while, P grows and the very first measurement is accepted with a large weight. And it estimates sensor biases as states — what Ki does blindly in a complementary filter. Innovations and gates An innovation y with variance S gives the normalized quantity y²/S. In ArduPilot, XKF4.SV/SP/SH/SM velocity, position, height, compass are the square root of the test ratio, i.e., the ratio “innovation / maximum allowed innovation” itself, where the allowance is set by the gates EK3_VEL_I_GATE , EK3_HGT_I_GATE , EK3_MAG_I_GATE , in percent of σ : < 1 — the measurement is accepted, 1 — it is rejected . A healthy flight shows values < 0.5. This is protection against GPS and compass outliers: one bad sample won't break the estimate. But if measurements are consistently outside the gates, the filter “drifts away” on the model until it resets lane switch, reset, EKF failsafe . What's in the EKF3 state vector 24 states: quaternion 4 , NED velocity 3 , NED position 3 , gyro bias 3 , accelerometer bias 3 , Earth field NED 3 , body field 3 , NE wind 2 . Measurements: GPS position/velocity, baro, compass, airspeed, rangefinder, optical flow, external navigation, beacons,

summary: For an autopilot, GPS isn't a “dot on the map” but a noisy measurement with a known (and changing) error. Three conditions Step 2. Multipath Step 3. Settings Step 4. Assessing the need for RTK Script: position scatter in place What you should get and what to record
text: summary For an autopilot, GPS isn't a “dot on the map” but a noisy measurement with a known and changing error. This module explains how a receiver gets pseudoranges and solves for position, where the errors come from the ionosphere, multipath, satellite geometry — HDOP , what multiple constellations give you GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou , how to choose a receiver and an antenna, which u-blox settings matter for flight rate, constellations, dynamic model, SBAS , and what RTK/PPK are, when you need them and when you don't. Lab: GPS quality under different conditions, from the log. theory The principle Each satellite transmits time and its orbit; the receiver measures the signal delay → pseudorange distance + receiver clock error . Four unknowns x, y, z, Δt → at least 4 satellites; more is better redundancy, quality estimation . The signal at the input is ~−130 dBm — weaker than the noise; it's extracted by correlating with a known code. Errors and their magnitudes single-frequency receiver, good conditions Source Error How to reduce it --- --- --- Ionosphere 2–5 m dual frequency L1+L5/L2 , SBAS correction Troposphere 0.5–1 m model Satellite orbit/clock 1–2 m SBAS Multipath reflections from buildings, the ground, the frame 1–10+ m, in jumps antenna with a ground plane, higher above the frame, away from structures Geometry DOP multiplier ×1–×5 many satellites across the whole sky Receiver noise 0.3–1 m a good antenna, no interference Total: 1.5–3 m CEP in an open field, 5–20 m in a city. Velocity from Doppler is much more accurate — 0.05–0.2 m/s; the EKF relies on it more than on position. DOP: geometry HDOP horizontal is an error multiplier from the satellite layout: all satellites on one side of the sky → bad. < 1 is excellent, 1–2 is good; above the threshold ArduPilot won't arm in GPS modes GPS_HDOP_GOOD , stored as HDOP × 100; default 140 = 1.4 . Satellite count is a rough indicator: 6 is the minimum, 12+ is normal with multiple constellations. Constellations GPS USA, L1 C/A , GLONASS Russia , Galileo EU, L1 + E5 , BeiDou China . A multi-constellation receiver u-blox M8/M9/M10, F9P sees 20–30 satellites instead of 8–10: better DOP, faster fix, more robust when part of the sky is blocked. The cost is computational load and update rate: M8 — 10 Hz with 2–3 constellations, M9/M10 — up to 25 Hz, F9P — 20 Hz RTK. Antenna A 25×25 mm ceramic patch on a ground plane is the standard; helical antennas are circularly polarized, better against multipath, and don't need a ground plane. The rule: antenna on top, on a mast, nothing metal nearby, ground plane ≥ 40 mm for a patch. An active antenna with an amplifier is for a long cable. u-blox settings that matter - Rate : 5–10 Hz for a copter ArduPilot GPS_RATE_MS = 200 , in 4.6+ GPS1_RATE_MS → 5 Hz; the EKF doesn't need more, and it overloads the UART/CPU . - Dynamic model : Airborne < 1g/2g/4g — the filter inside the receiver tuned for the dynamics; Pedestrian/Automotive are bad for a drone they smooth and lag . ArduPilot sets GPS_NAVFILTER . - Constellations GPS_GNSS_MODE : GPS + Galileo + GLONASS or GPS + Galileo + BeiDou — not all four at once on an M8 the rate drops . - SBAS GPS_SBAS_MODE : WAAS/EGNOS corrections — slightly more accurate, but in some regions it gets in the way; enable it where there is coverage. - Messages : UBX binary instead of NMEA — more compact, more precise, with quality status; ArduPilot configures a u-blox receiver itself with GPS_AUTO_CONFIG = 1 . RTK and PPK RTK Real-Time Kinematic : a base station at a known position sends carrier-phase corrections RTCM to the rover receiver over radio/4G; accuracy is 1–3 cm with a fix RTK Fixed status , 10–50 cm with float. You need a dual-frequency receiver F9P, UM982 on both ends, the base within ~10–20 km, and a continuous link. PPK is the same but post-processed from logs: it's for photogrammetry, not for flight control. When you need RTK: precision landing, surveying, moving baseline for heading two GPS units → yaw without a compass: ArduPilot “GPS for yaw,” base GPS_TYPE = 17 , rover GPS_TYPE2 = 18 ; in 4.6+ — GPS1_TYPE / GPS2_TYPE . When you don't: regular waypoint flying the EKF and a 2 m error are enough , FPV. RTK doesn't cure multipath or satellite loss under a roof. {{diagram:chart-gnss-hdop-wall A 180° wall removes 4 of 10 satellites, and HDOP rises from 0.82 to 3.48 — above the ArduPilot threshold of 1.4 and the EKF3 threshold of 2.5; the satellite count drops slowly, the geometry sharply.}} {{diagram:gnss-rtk-choice-tree You need RTK only when the task needs centimeters in flight; for waypoint flight 1.5–3 m of plain GNSS is enough, for photogrammetry use PPK.}} How GPS enters the EKF The EKF receives position, velocity, their accuracy estimates GPA.HAcc/VAcc/SAcc and the delay GPS1_DELAY_MS ~ 100–200 ms — the measurement is “old,” the EKF accounts for that . Quality is checked EK3_GPS_CHECK : HDOP, satellite count, velocity drift on the ground before arming is allowed in GPS modes. Glitch protection is the innovation gate see the Kalman module . {{diagram:rtk-chain A standard GNSS solution gives meters; RTCM corrections from a base at a known point give an RTK fix with centimeter accuracy.}} practice Step 1. Three conditions Ground logs, 5 minutes each LOG_DISARMED = 1 : an open field; next to a house wall; under trees. From GPS : NSats , HDop , Status ; from GPA : HAcc , SAcc . Table: the average and the worst for each condition. Step 2. Multipath For the second condition, plot the position GPS.Lat/Lng → meters over 5 minutes in place: the scatter and the jumps. Compare with the field. Match the jumps with XKF4.SP in the log normalized position innovation, √test ratio , if the EKF was running. Step 3. Settings Check GPS_RATE_MS , GPS_GNSS_MODE , GPS_NAVFILTER or the equivalents in INAV/Betaflight: gps_ublox_use_galileo , dynamic model , GPS_AUTO_CONFIG . Record them in the build logbook. Step 4. Assessing the need for RTK For your task — do you need RTK? Justify it

title: EKF and navigation
summary: The EKF is the filter that turns noisy, contradictory sensors into one consistent picture: where the vehicle is, where it is going, and how it is oriented. When ArduPilot "won't arm because of the EKF", "drifts in LOITER", or "flies off on a GPS glitch", the cause is almost always here. This module
headings: Why a filter EKF3, DCM, and lane switching Sources Variances and the failsafe What requires position Case: flying with no compass and no trust in the GPS Reading EKF health in a log Parameters you actually tune Worked example: "EKF variance" in Loiter over a parking lot Place in the system Checking EKF health SITL lab: GPS glitch Lab: sources What you should get and what to record
text: summary The EKF is the filter that turns noisy, contradictory sensors into one consistent picture: where the vehicle is, where it is going, and how it is oriented. When ArduPilot "won't arm because of the EKF", "drifts in LOITER", or "flies off on a GPS glitch", the cause is almost always here. This module explains what the filter does, how to choose its data sources, what variances and lane switching are, and how to read its health in the GCS and in logs. The practical example is a HeeWing with no compass and an unstable GPS. {{lesson:ap-ahrs-choice How to choose between EKF3 and DCM, set up source sets, and work out why the EKF is complaining: a long lesson with GPS, IMU, and compass failure runs in SITL.}} theory Why a filter A gyro is accurate over short intervals but drifts. GPS does not drift, but it is noisy and updates slowly. A barometer knows the altitude but is wrong in wind and when it heats up. A compass knows the heading but is disturbed by current. The EKF extended Kalman filter predicts the state from the inertial sensors hundreds of times per second and corrects that prediction with the infrequent GPS, baro, and compass measurements, weighting each by its stated noise. A measurement that is too far from the prediction is rejected, and that is how GPS glitches are handled. EKF3, DCM, and lane switching - AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 3 selects EKF3 as the main estimator; DCM a simple complementary filter runs in the background as the backup. - Each IMU in EK3_IMU_MASK gets its own core "lane" . The healthiest one is used; when one core degrades, the filter switches to another. EK3_PRIMARY selects the core used on startup. - The fallback to DCM depends on the vehicle type. Copter has none; it has the EKF failsafe instead. Plane and VTOL falls back to DCM when EKF3 is unhealthy or loses navigation position . On Rover in 4.7 the default AHRS_OPTIONS = 3 disables the fallback on loss of navigation: it goes to DCM only if EKF3 is unhealthy or has no attitude. The exact fallback conditions, whether EKF2 is still alive, and which estimator and source set to choose for your vehicle are covered in the ap-ahrs-choice module. Sources EK3_SRC1_ sets where position, velocity, height, and yaw come from: {{diagram:estimation-sources EKF3 fuses all sensors into one estimate: the IMU drives the prediction, and the other sources correct it through innovation gates.}} - EK3_SRC1_POSXY : 0 None, 3 GPS, 4 Beacon, 6 ExternalNav. - EK3_SRC1_VELXY : the same plus 5 OpticalFlow and 7 WheelEncoder. - EK3_SRC1_POSZ : 1 Baro, 2 RangeFinder, 3 GPS. - EK3_SRC1_YAW : 1 Compass, 2 GPS, 3 GPS with Compass Fallback, 8 GSF a yaw estimate from GPS velocity, without a compass . The SRC2 / SRC3 sets are selected in flight with a switch, for example GPS outdoors and optical flow indoors. Variances and the failsafe The filter estimates its own uncertainty in compass, velocity, position, and height. When two of the compass, velocity and position variances exceed FS_EKF_THRESH 0.8 Default, 0.6 Strict, 1.0 Relaxed , or velocity alone exceeds twice it without healthy optical flow , or there is no position estimate, for about 1 s 10 checks at 10 Hz; height is not used here , the EKF failsafe triggers with the action from FS_EKF_ACTION : 0 reports only this value appeared in 4.7 ; 1 switches to Land if the current mode requires position; 2 switches to AltHold; 3 switches to Land from all modes. The pre-arm check is stricter: any single variance above the threshold, height included, blocks arming; "EKF variance" when arming points to a bad compass or GPS and is not a reason to raise the threshold. What requires position LOITER, AUTO, GUIDED, RTL, and PosHold need a healthy position estimate. STABILIZE, ALT_HOLD, and ACRO do not. Hence the rule from the ArduPilot intro module: you choose a mode by which sensors you trust. Case: flying with no compass and no trust in the GPS A HeeWing T1 on its stock F405: there is no compass on board at all, and the GPS was unstable during setup. Instead of forcing the EKF to work with an unreliable heading, the decision was to disable EKF3 and fly on DCM: the aircraft arms and is controlled in the modes that need no position MANUAL, FBWA, ACRO, QSTABILIZE, QLAND , and altitude and position hold are deliberately not used. The alternative for later, once the GPS is stable: EK3_SRC1_YAW = 8 GSF , which gives a heading from GPS without a compass, but only once the aircraft is moving. Reading EKF health in a log XKF4 per core : SV , SP , SH , SM are the square root of the test ratio, that is, the ratio of the innovation to the allowed one set by the gates EK3_VEL_I_GATE , EK3_POS_I_GATE , EK3_HGT_I_GATE , EK3_MAG_I_GATE , in % : < 0.5 is healthy, around 1 the measurement is on the edge of rejection, 1 it is rejected; SS is the filter solution status bitmask which sources are in use ; PI is the primary core index; XKF3 holds the innovations themselves IVN/IVE/IVD velocity, IPN/IPE/IPD position, IMX/IMY/IMZ magnetic field ; XKF2 holds the estimated accelerometer bias, the wind, and the magnetic field; XKF1 holds the state angles, velocities, position and the gyro bias GX/GY/GZ . Messages such as EKF3 IMU0 yaw aligned and EKF3 IMU0 MAG0 ground mag anomaly, yaw re-aligned are automatic resets normal when rare, suspicious when frequent . The math is covered in the "Kalman filter" module, and practical degradation scenarios in "Navigation resilience". Parameters you actually tune EK3_GPS_CHECK GPS quality checks before the filter trusts it , GPS1_DELAY_MS / EK3_FLOW_DELAY / EK3_HGT_DELAY measurement delay, ms , EK3_ALT_SOURCE → EK3_SRC1_POSZ , EK3_RNG_USE_HGT % of the rangefinder's maximum range , EK3_GLITCH_RAD 25 m: beyond it the states are reset to the GPS , EK3_MAG_CAL when to learn the magnetic field in flight , EK3_FLOW_USE , EK3_SRC_OPTIONS . Touch the measurement noise EK3_ _M_NSE and process noise EK3_ _P_NSE only after you understand the Kalman module, and with before/after logs. Worked example: "EK

text: summary In ArduPilot the question "where am I and which way am I pointing" is answered not by one filter but by the AP_AHRS front end with several backends: DCM, EKF3, EKF2, an external AHRS and the simulator. This module works out which of them actually flies the vehicle, when the firmware falls back to DCM by itself, whether EKF2 is still alive, how the EKF3 cores work, the source sets EK3_SRC1..3_ , yaw without a compass GSF , airspeed and wind on a plane, the EKF failsafe, and the messages the pilot sees. The main result is a rule for choosing the estimator and the sources for seven typical vehicles, and a decision tree for when the EKF misbehaves. The lab: seven experiments in SITL ArduCopter and ArduPlane 4.7.2 with real output: GPS loss in Loiter, a switch to optical flow, an IMU failure, a copter with no compass, and a plane with no GPS in wind, with and without an airspeed sensor. theory AHRS in ArduPilot: one front end, several backends The control loops do not ask EKF3 directly. They take attitude, velocity and position from the AP_AHRS object libraries/AP_AHRS , which decides on every loop whose answer to return. That choice is called the active backend _active_EKF_type , and a change of it shows in the GCS as the message AHRS: EKF3 active or AHRS: DCM active . Backend What it is Where it exists in 4.7.2 How to select it Log --- --- --- --- --- DCM a complementary filter on a rotation matrix est-attitude plus position from GPS or dead reckoning everywhere, always computed AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 0 Plane and Rover only or the automatic fallback AHR2 , when an EKF is active EKF3 an extended Kalman filter with 24 states est-kalman everywhere AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 3 the default XKF1…XKF5 , XKFS , XKQ , XKY0 EKF2 the previous generation of the filter only SITL and custom build server builds with the EKF2 option AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 2 , EK2_ENABLE = 1 NKF1…NKF5 , NKQ External AHRS a ready-made INS VectorNav, MicroStrain, InertialLabs, SBG, Trimble, SensAItion, and since 4.7.3 Aeron PLX3 = 10; EAHRS_TYPE on boards with the driver AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 11 the driver's messages SIM the ideal attitude from the simulator SITL only AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 10 new in 4.7 — Three important consequences. First, DCM is updated on every loop whatever is selected AP_AHRS::update calls update_DCM unconditionally , so it is always ready to take over. Second, the AHR2 log message holds the "second" estimator: DCM when EKF3 is active, and EKF3 when the fallback to DCM has triggered with AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 3 with AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 0 there are no AHR2 lines ; comparing ATT and AHR2 is the first check of whether the primary one is lying. Third, EKF3 runs even when it is not active with EK3_ENABLE = 1 : a plane on DCM still logs the full XKF . AHRS_EKF_TYPE: what is allowed on which vehicle The parameter values in 4.7.3 the same as in 4.7.2 : 0 Disabled which means DCM , 2 EKF2, 3 EKF3, 10 Sim, 11 ExternalAHRS. The value 1 EKF1 was removed long ago: with it the board reports the config error EKF1 not available . - Copter, Heli, Sub. The AP_AHRS constructor sets the flag FLAG_ALWAYS_USE_EKF for them: they cannot fly on DCM. The firmware silently turns AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 0 into an EKF EKF2 if it is compiled in, otherwise EKF3 , but the pre-arm check compares the stored value with the actual one and refuses to arm: PreArm: AHRS: not using configured AHRS type verified in SITL, step 2 . On a copter DCM works only for the first seconds after boot, until EKF3 has started, and when EKF3 reports filter faults getFilterFaults ≠ 0 . - Plane and Rover. AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 0 is a legitimate configuration: the vehicle runs on DCM, and position-controlled modes take the position straight from GPS. That is how the compass-less HeeWing from ap-ekf flew. The price: no variances, no innovation gates, no dead reckoning on airspeed with a wind estimate, and lower accuracy during GPS glitches. - Boards with Remote ID. The defaults.parm of the -ODID builds has AHRS_EKF_TYPE 3 @READONLY : you cannot change the estimator on them. EKF2 in 4.7: an honest verdict AP_AHRS_config.h has HAL_NAVEKF2_AVAILABLE 0 by default, with the comment "compiled out by default in 4.5". The Copter 4.5.0-beta1 release notes say "EKF2 removed can be re-enabled with Custom build server ". No board in libraries/AP_HAL_ChibiOS/hwdef of 4.7.2 enables it; only the SITL waf configuration does -DHAL_NAVEKF2_AVAILABLE=1 , plus the EKF2 option in build_options.py for custom.ardupilot.org. If you set AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 2 on standard firmware, AP_AHRS::init quietly replaces it with 3 on the next boot in memory, without writing the parameter ; until the reboot the pre-arm check answers not using configured AHRS type . The EK2_ parameters are still visible in the documentation and in the pdef, which is no sign that the filter is on the board. The verdict: on 4.7 EKF2 is not a choice but a museum piece. You need it only to read an old log NKF or to compare filters in SITL. In SITL it does work: in our Plane run the log had EKF2 IMU0 is using GPS next to EKF3. Yaw without a compass, source sets, the copter's drag-based wind estimate, external navigation with reset_counter : all of that is developed in EKF3, and the source set switch set_posvelyaw_source_set in AP_AHRS calls EKF3 only. DCM: what it can do and when the firmware falls back to it DCM is a complementary filter: the gyro is integrated into a rotation matrix, roll and pitch are pulled toward the accelerometer AHRS_RP_P = 0.2 , and yaw toward the compass or GPS AHRS_YAW_P = 0.2 . Centripetal acceleration in a turn is compensated from GPS velocity AHRS_GPS_GAIN = 1.0, with at least AHRS_GPS_MINSATS = 6 satellites . Yaw for a vehicle that flies forward comes from the compass, but if the compass heading differs from the GPS heading by more than 45° for longer than 2 s at a speed of 3 m/s or more and a wind below 80 % of the ground speed, DCM switches to the GPS heading, a guard against taking off with a bad compass. DCM takes position from GPS AHRS_GPS_U

title: Altitude and position without GPS: baro, rangefinder, optical flow
summary: Indoors, under tree canopy and next to walls GPS is useless, and the baro “breathes.” This module breaks down barometer errors and how they're compensated, what a rangefinder (lidar/ultrasonic/radar) and optical flow give you, how they're connected in ArduPilot and INAV, and how to use `EK3_SRCn_*`
headings: Barometer: where the errors come from Rangefinder Optical flow Building a source set INAV Step 1. Baro Step 2. Rangefinder Step 3. SITL without GPS Step 4. Bench/flight
text: summary Indoors, under tree canopy and next to walls GPS is useless, and the baro “breathes.” This module breaks down barometer errors and how they're compensated, what a rangefinder lidar/ultrasonic/radar and optical flow give you, how they're connected in ArduPilot and INAV, and how to use EK3_SRCn_ to build a source set for the job: indoors, forest, precision landing. The lab is position hold without GPS in SITL optical flow + rangefinder and on the bench. theory Barometer: where the errors come from Altitude from pressure via the standard atmosphere: Δh ≈ −8.4 m per 1 hPa near the ground. Errors: - Weather : pressure changes by 1–3 hPa per hour when a front passes → 10–25 m of drift per hour; relative altitude over a 10-minute flight is ±1–3 m. - Chip temperature : warm-up after power-on drifts by meters BARO_ calibration, ArduPilot TCAL_ENABLED / TCAL_BARO_EXP , foam for thermal stability . - Prop wash and airspeed : dynamic pressure ½ρv² — at 20 m/s that's 2.4 hPa ≈ 20 m! The baro must sit in a “quiet” spot, under foam; the error from the airflow is compensated by BARO1_WCF_ wind pressure compensation; on copters only with EKF3 and tuned EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_ ; BARO_GND_TEMP is only the ground temperature used for the altitude calculation , on copters also the prop-wash effect on takeoff/landing −1…−3 m of false altitude near the ground . - Noise : 0.2–0.5 m RMS unfiltered. The EKF blends the baro with the accelerometer see the Kalman module : fast changes come from the accel, the slow level from the baro; nothing compensates the weather drift relative to the takeoff point except GPS altitude EK3_SRC1_POSZ = 3 or a rangefinder near the ground. Rangefinder - Lidar TFmini-S 12 m, TF02 40 m, Lightware SF20/LW20 100 m, Benewake TF03 180 m : narrow beam, works on any surface except black/mirror-like/water; error 1–3% or ±5 cm. - Ultrasonic MaxBotix : cheap, 5–7 m, noisy from props and wind, poor over grass. - Radar Ainstein, Nanoradar 60 GHz : 30–100 m, works over water and in dust, more expensive. Connection: UART SERIALx_PROTOCOL = 9 , RNGFND1_TYPE per model , I2C TFmini in I2C mode, RNGFND1_TYPE = 25 , DroneCAN RNGFND1_TYPE = 24 . Parameters: RNGFND1_MIN/MAX_CM , RNGFND1_ORIENT = 25 down , RNGFND1_GNDCLEAR sensor height above the ground when parked . What it gives you: height above terrain terrain following, TERRAIN_ and WP_RFND_USE before 4.7 — WPNAV_RFND_USE , precision landing LAND_ALT_LOW , and an EKF altitude source near the ground EK3_SRC1_POSZ = 2 , EK3_RNG_USE_HGT — the percentage of max range up to which the EKF uses the rangefinder . Over tall grass/bushes the rangefinder gives you the “terrain,” not the ground — that's not a sensor error. Optical flow A downward-facing camera PX4Flow, Cheerson CX-OF, Matek 3901-L0X, HereFlow measures the angular rate of image motion rad/s . To get linear velocity you need: height above the surface a rangefinder! and the aircraft's angular rate gyro to subtract rotation. v = flow − ω × h. That's why flow without a rangefinder only gives rough stabilization. Limitations: texture a plain floor, water, snow — doesn't work , lighting night without illumination , height 0.3–10 m typical , speed motion blur . Calibrate FLOW_FXSCALER/FYSCALER in flight: the test is rocking over a textured surface and comparing OF.flowX with OF.bodyX ArduPilot log OF . Connection: FLOW_TYPE 1 PX4Flow I2C, 5 MAVLink, 6 DroneCAN, 7 MSP , orientation FLOW_ORIENT_YAW , offset relative to the IMU FLOW_POS_ . EKF source: EK3_SRC1_VELXY = 5 . Building a source set EKF3 has three source sets EK3_SRC1_ , SRC2 , SRC3 , switched with a switch RCx_OPTION = 90 or a Lua script. Each one has: POSXY , VELXY , POSZ , VELZ , YAW . {{diagram:ekf-source-tree Choosing EKF3 sources for the scenario: with GPS, with flow and a rangefinder, with external navigation.}} Scenario POSXY VELXY POSZ YAW Comment --- --- --- --- --- --- Open field, GPS 3 GPS 3 GPS 1 Baro 1 Compass standard Indoors, textured floor 0 None 5 OptFlow 2 RangeFinder 1 Compass / 0 no GPS; the compass often lies indoors — then yaw 0 and heading is held by the gyro only drift Forest, GPS present but jumping 3 GPS 5 OptFlow 2 RangeFinder low / 1 Baro 1 Compass flow smooths out GPS jumps Precision landing 3 GPS 3 GPS 2 RangeFinder 1 rangefinder near the ground EK3_SRC_OPTIONS = 1 — fuse all velocities use velocities from all configured sources at once . Flying without GPS and without flow is Stabilize/AltHold only; Loiter/Auto are unavailable preflight check “PreArm: Need Position Estimate” . INAV Optical flow opflow_hardware , scale opflow_scale and the rangefinder rangefinder_hardware feed into the INAV position estimator via the weights inav_w_xy_flow_p / inav_w_xy_flow_v the flow weight in position and velocity ; for indoor flights on flow the documentation recommends inav_allow_dead_reckoning = ON “may be useful for indoor navigation with OPFLOW” . Position hold without GPS is POSHOLD mode with flow and a rangefinder set up, over a textured surface. {{diagram:inav-surface-limits Full throttle in SURFACE must give a height below inav_max_surface_altitude: with 250 over a 200 limit, the top 20 % of throttle travel takes the aircraft where the rangefinder is no longer used.}} practice Step 1. Baro A 10-minute log on the ground after power-on: BARO.Alt — the drift from warm-up. Then a hover at 2 m over a flat pad: BARO.Alt against RFND.Dist — see the prop-wash effect on takeoff. Step 2. Rangefinder Connect it, set up RNGFND1_ , check in the GCS that the value when parked = GNDCLEAR . Flight: is RFND.Dist smooth, with no spikes over grass? Record it. Step 3. SITL without GPS ArduPilot SITL --add-param-file with: SIM_GPS1_ENABLE = 0 in older versions SIM_GPS_DISABLE = 1 , FLOW_TYPE = 10 SITL , RNGFND1_TYPE = 100 SITL , EK3_SRC1_POSXY = 0 , EK3_SRC1_VELXY = 5 , EK3_SRC1_POSZ = 2 , EK3_SRC1_YAW = 1 . Take off in Loiter, hold position for 60 s, then move with the sticks: record the position drift XKF1.PN/PE . Repeat with SRC1_POSZ = 1

title: Navigation and link resilience to interference
summary: GNSS and the compass are the most vulnerable sensors on board: the satellite signal is weaker than thermal noise, and the Earth's magnetic field is weaker than the field of a power wire. Degradation can be accidental (construction sites, power lines, your own interference, multipath) or intentional;
headings: Types of degradation and their log signature What the firmware does on its own Designing for resilience Frequency and power planning at the site What's out of scope Step 1. Signatures in SITL Step 2. Configure the reaction Step 3. Field test (civilian) Step 4. Site frequency plan
text: summary GNSS and the compass are the most vulnerable sensors on board: the satellite signal is weaker than thermal noise, and the Earth's magnetic field is weaker than the field of a power wire. Degradation can be accidental construction sites, power lines, your own interference, multipath or intentional; the engineer designs the vehicle so that it notices the degradation and reacts to it safely . This module is civilian: how to recognize the problem from logs NSats, HDOP, innovations, GPS glitch, heading jumps , how to set up backup EKF sources and the behavior on GPS/compass loss, how to plan RC/video frequencies and power at a site with other people's transmitters, and how to test every scenario in SITL. theory Types of degradation and their log signature What's happening GPS.NSats GPS.HDop / GPA.HAcc XKF4.SP/SV Other signs --- --- --- --- --- Partial sky obstruction wall, forest drops gradually grows creep up position “wanders” by meters Multipath normal HAcc jumps SP spikes 1 position jumps, velocity normal Wideband interference your own electronics, someone else's transmitter drops sharply to 0–3 HAcc → hundreds of m SV, SP grow, then GPS glitch coincides with a device switching on/approaching a site; satellite C/N0 drops GRAW /u-center Spoofing “good” fix “excellent” accuracy SP/SV grow: the model disagrees with the measurement position jump with normal satellites; GPS velocity contradicts accel; disagreement with baro/flow Magnetic anomaly/compass interference — — SM 1, yaw reset in XKF messages heading jumps, “toilet bowling,” “Compass variance” The main tool is source disagreement : the EKF compares every measurement with the prediction from the inertial sensors. The inertial sensors aren't affected by external interference — that's why innovations grow first. The second tool is signal quality at the receiver itself: the number of satellites and the signal-to-noise ratio per-satellite C/N0 in u-center; in ArduPilot — raw GPS data logging, GPS_RAW_DATA . The combination “satellites normal, innovations growing” suggests spoofing or a wrong model; “no satellites” suggests jamming or an obstructed sky. What the firmware does on its own - ArduPilot : GPS glitch protection innovation gates; when the radial disagreement exceeds EK3_GLITCH_RAD , 25 m by default, position and velocity are reset to GPS , lane switching between EKF cores, EKF failsafe FS_EKF_ACTION : 0 message only, 1 Land if the mode requires position, 2 AltHold if it requires position, 3 Land from any mode; threshold FS_EKF_THRESH , GPS failsafe via the EKF on loss of position in a mode that requires it — switch to Land/AltHold , yaw source fallback EK3_SRC1_YAW = 3 GPS with compass fallback; GSF yaw estimation from motion — EK3_SRC1_YAW = 8 or automatically with COMPASS_USE = 0 . Dead reckoning from inertial sensors and wind gives tens of seconds of acceptable accuracy, not minutes. - PX4 : EKF2_GPS_CHECK GPS quality check bitmask , accuracy threshold COM_POS_FS_EPH ; loss-of-position failsafe COM_POSCTL_NAVL 0 — RC available: switch to Altitude/Stabilized; 1 — no RC: Descend or flight termination ; u-blox receivers have built-in jamming detection a sensitivity parameter in the GPS driver , and the state is published in the sensor_gps message. - INAV : if there is no position for longer than ~2 s in RTH/WP — Emergency Landing descent in ANGLE at failsafe_throttle , motors cut after failsafe_off_delay ; failsafe_procedure is the reaction to RC loss, not GPS loss; dead reckoning inav_allow_dead_reckoning , inav_allow_gps_fix_estimation estimation without a fix for a wing, based on airspeed + compass . {{diagram:gps-loss-ladder Each firmware steps down the degradation ladder in its own way, but the last step is the same for all: a mode without position and a pilot who can fly it, and the choice of action depends on where you fly.}} Designing for resilience 1. Reduce your own interference see the EMI module : this accounts for 80% of real GPS problems. 2. Backup EKF sources : optical flow + rangefinder for low altitudes; baro as the POSZ backup; a second GPS with GPS_AUTO_SWITCH ; compass + GPS yaw + GSF. 3. A failsafe that fits the scenario : what to do on loss of position depends on the location. Over a field: AltHold and a manual landing. Over people: Land. Over water: don't count on inertial navigation to reach the shore — it won't last; AltHold and a manual return to shore by sight or video. The decision is recorded in the engineering folder with its rationale. 4. GPS-independent modes are always available to the pilot : Stabilize/AltHold on a switch, and the pilot knows how to use them — this is practiced in training. 5. Geofence and altitude : when position degrades, the geofence is useless — account for this in the site risk assessment. Frequency and power planning at the site - A table of occupied video channels and RC bands the “Field Operations” module : a new participant adds themselves to it instead of switching on a transmitter at random. - RC: 2.4 GHz and 900 MHz degrade differently; 900 MHz handles range and obstacles better, 2.4 GHz is more crowded Wi-Fi, other radios . Two receivers on two bands give a backup link. - Power: the minimum that's sufficient per the link budget the “Link Budget” module — extra watts jam your neighbors and heat the VTX; on the ground — minimum power pit mode . - Telemetry: a separate channel 900 MHz/4G/LTE for monitoring status if RC and video are lost. - Legality of bands and power — the “Regulations” module. What's out of scope Methods of creating interference, countering specific jamming systems, bypassing restrictions — outside this course and illegal in most jurisdictions. The course teaches you to detect and safely end the flight , not to “punch through.” {{diagram:degradation-signatures How to tell types of navigation degradation apart from the log: satellites and accuracy, EKF innovations, compass.}} practice Step 1. Signatures in SITL ArduPilot SITL, Loiter at 20 m: -

title: RTK/PPK: base and rover, NTRIP, moving baseline, GPS yaw
summary: В модуле «GNSS» RTK был одним абзацем. Здесь — вся цепочка: как база узнаёт свою точку (survey-in или известные координаты), какие сообщения RTCM3 она шлёт, как они доезжают до ровера (NTRIP-кастер → Mission Planner/QGC → `GPS_RTCM_DATA` → UART приёмника), что значат float/fixed и возраст поправок,
headings: RTK и PPK — одна математика, разное время База: survey-in или известная точка RTCM3: что именно летит от базы Доставка: NTRIP, Mission Planner, MAVLink Состояния fix и возраст поправок Moving baseline: курс по двум антеннам PX4 — коротко Место в системе Шаг 1. Параметры стенда Шаг 2. Дождаться fix 6 и курса Шаг 3. Сломать базовую линию Шаг 4. Точность в SITL и лог Шаг 5. Тип fix против точности на логе ровера Переход на реальное железо
text: summary В модуле «GNSS» RTK был одним абзацем. Здесь — вся цепочка: как база узнаёт свою точку survey-in или известные координаты , какие сообщения RTCM3 она шлёт, как они доезжают до ровера NTRIP-кастер → Mission Planner/QGC → GPS_RTCM_DATA → UART приёмника , что значат float/fixed и возраст поправок, и как два F9P на раме дают курс без компаса moving baseline, «GPS for yaw» . Разобраны параметры ArduPilot 4.7 GPS1_TYPE = 17/18 , GPS1_POS_ , GPS1_MB_ , GPS_DRV_OPTIONS , EK3_SRC1_YAW = 2 и PX4-эквиваленты GPS_UBX_MODE , GPS_YAW_OFFSET , EKF2_GPS_CTRL . Лабораторная: moving baseline в SITL с реальным выводом GPS2_RAW.yaw , лог с GPS.Status = 6 , скрипт «тип fix → точность» на сгенерированном логе ровера, затем стенд из двух F9P. theory RTK и PPK — одна математика, разное время Обе убирают общие для базы и ровера ошибки ионосфера, тропосфера, орбиты, часы через разности фазы несущей и фиксируют целочисленные неоднозначности integer ambiguities . Разница — когда. RTK real-time kinematic PPK post-processed kinematic --- --- --- Когда в полёте, каждую эпоху после полёта, по двум сырым логам Нужна связь база→ровер да, непрерывно радио, 4G, NTRIP нет Что даёт автопилоту позицию 1–3 см в EKF, точную посадку, GPS yaw ничего в полёте; координаты снимков для фотограмметрии Что логировать обычный лог; статус fix RXM-RAWX с обоих приёмников: ArduPilot GPS_RAW_DATA = 1 сообщения GRAW/GRXH/GRXS , PX4 GPS_DUMP_COMM = 2 Цифры для ZED-F9P data sheet ZED-F9P-04B : стандартный PVT 1.5 м CEP 1.0 м с SBAS , RTK 0.01 м + 1 ppm 1 ppm = 1 мм на километр базовой линии; для 20 км — 3 см , сходимость < 10 с при нескольких созвездиях, скорость 0.05 м/с. Из-за «1 ppm» NTRIP-станцию берут не дальше ~50–100 км: на 100 км это 11 см и худшая сходимость. Для своей базы и быстрого fix держат базовую линию короче — 10–20 км est-gnss . База: survey-in или известная точка Ошибка координат базы целиком переносится на ровер — RTK даёт сантиметры относительно базы . Два способа задать точку u-blox CFG-TMODE-MODE : - Survey-in SURVEY_IN : приёмник усредняет свою позицию, пока не выполнены оба условия — минимальная длительность CFG-TMODE-SVIN_MIN_DUR и предел 3D-точности CFG-TMODE-SVIN_ACC_LIMIT . В Mission Planner это поля «SurveyIn Acc m » и «Time s »; типично 2 м и 60 с. Абсолютная точность такой базы — метры, относительная точность ровера — сантиметры: для посадки на ту же площадку хватает, для карты в государственной системе координат — нет. Во время survey-in базе нельзя подавать чужие поправки. - Известные координаты FIXED , CFG-TMODE-POS_TYPE + _HP -ключи с миллиметровой точностью : точка от геодезиста, от многочасового survey-in или от PPK по сети постоянных станций. Mission Planner хранит её «Save»/«Use» — годится, только если база стоит на том же месте. RTCM3: что именно летит от базы Набор, который u-blox рекомендует для базы F9P и который включает Mission Planner ubx_m8p.cs : 1005 и 1230 каждые 5 с, MSM раз в секунду : Сообщение Содержание Зачем --- --- --- 1005 координаты антенны базы ECEF ; 1006 — то же плюс высота антенны без неё ровер не знает, относительно чего считать 1074 / 1084 / 1094 / 1124 MSM4: наблюдения GPS / GLONASS / Galileo / BeiDou псевдодальность, фаза, C/N0 сами поправки; MSM4 компактнее 1077 / 1087 / 1097 / 1127 MSM7: те же созвездия с полной точностью и доплером альтернатива MSM4, набор QGC/PX4; не смешивать с MSM4 в одном потоке 1230 смещения кодовой фазы GLONASS без 1230 или 1033 GLONASS остаётся float даже при RTK fixed 4072.0 проприетарное u-blox: PVT базы для moving baseline обязательно в каждой эпохе для режима MB; для статичной базы не нужно Поток на 1 Гц при четырёх созвездиях — единицы кБ/с; F9P поднимает MB до 5 Гц, но тогда UART2 нужен 460800 бод, а задержка доставки должна быть меньше периода навигации минус 50 мс ≈150 мс для 5 Гц . Ровер перестаёт использовать поправки старше CFG-NAVSPG-CONSTR_DGNSSTO по умолчанию 60 с и падает в 3D/DGNSS. Доставка: NTRIP, Mission Planner, MAVLink NTRIP — HTTP-подобный протокол: кастер caster на порту 2101 отдаёт sourcetable с точками монтирования mount points , клиент логинится и получает поток RTCM. Публичный пример — RTK2go бесплатный, логин — валидный e-mail, пароль none ; коммерческие сети дают виртуальную станцию рядом с тобой. Строка в Mission Planner: http://user:pass@host:2101/MOUNT . Дальше поправки едут в аппарат по телеметрии: Mission Planner → Setup → Optional Hardware → RTK/GPS Inject режет поток на пакеты GPS_RTCM_DATA id 233; flags : бит 0 — фрагментирован, биты 1–2 — номер фрагмента, биты 3–7 — sequence id; data 180 . Старый GPS_INJECT_DATA id 123, 110 байт в MAVLink помечен superseded с 2022-05, ArduPilot его ещё принимает. На борту AP_GPS::handle_gps_rtcm_fragment собирает фрагменты и пишет байты в UART приёмника, выбранного GPS_INJECT_TO 0 — первый, 1 — второй, 127 — все . GPA.RTCMFU/RTCMFD в логе — фрагменты использованные/выброшенные. При двух источниках RTCM драйвер начинает полный разбор сообщений; бит 6 GPS_DRV_OPTIONS включает его принудительно, бит 7 — запрещает. Альтернатива без GCS: радиомодем базы прямо в UART2 ровера. Состояния fix и возраст поправок GPS_RAW_INT.fix_type и GPS.Status в логе — одна шкала AP_GPS::GPS_Status : 0 нет GPS, 1 нет fix, 2 — 2D, 3 — 3D, 4 — DGPS, 5 — RTK float , 6 — RTK fixed . Float — неоднозначности ещё вещественные, точность порядка 10–50 см и «плывёт» практический ориентир, в data sheet u-blox такой цифры нет ; fixed — целочисленные, 1–3 см. У u-blox статус берётся из carrSoln в UBX-NAV-PVT. Важно: драйвер u-blox в ArduPilot не заполняет rtk_age_ms проверено по исходнику 4.6.3 и 4.7.2 , поэтому GPS2_RAW.dgps_age для F9P всегда 0 в GPS_RAW_INT такого поля нет вовсе — возраст поправок смотри в Mission Planner окно RTK или по RTCMFU ; dgps_age честно заполняют только драйверы ERB, NOVA и SBF. EKF3 не различает float и fixed: шум измерения позиции он берёт как max GPA.HAcc, EK3_POSNE_M_NSE ² , а EK3_POSNE_M_NSE у Copter по умолчанию 0.5 м AP_NavEKF3_PosVelFusion.cpp , R_OBS 3 . title: Without GNSS: optical flow, UWB, motion capture and external navigation in the EKF

text: summary В помещении, под мостом и в ангаре GNSS нет, а Loiter, Guided и Auto всё так же требуют позицию. Модуль сводит в одну картину четыре способа дать её EKF без спутников — оптический поток с дальномером, UWB-маяки, motion capture и внешнюю позу по MAVLink — и разбирает ловушки первого запуска: системы координат, задержку и VISO_DELAY_MS , сбросы, арминг без GPS и origin. Лабораторная: ArduCopter 4.6.3 в SITL без GPS летает по VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE из истины с шумом и лагом; развёртка задержки показывает, где EKF начинает отбраковывать данные и что ломается раньше; отдельно — скачок источника с reset_counter и без, перепутанные оси, арминг без origin. Затем перенос на железо: поток с дальномером в комнате, UWB и mocap с критериями приёмки. theory Что именно заменяем GNSS даёт EKF позицию, скорость, иногда высоту и курс. Без него инерциалка уходит на метры за секунды, поэтому каждую величину надо взять у кого-то ещё. Ворота инноваций и «задержанный горизонт» разобраны в est-kalman, здоровье EKF по XKF4 — в ap-ekf, отпечатки отказа GNSS — в nav-resilience; здесь только то, что специфично для полёта без спутников. EK3_SRC_OPTIONS : бит 0 FuseAllVelocities в 4.7 по умолчанию снят, EK3_SRC_OPTIONS = 0 ; в 4.6 был включён, значение 1 , бит 1 AlignExtNavPosWhenUsingOptFlow, бит 3 UsePerCoreEKFSources с 4.7: каждому ядру EKF свой набор источников . Три набора и тумблер RCx_OPTION = 90 — в est-alt-sources. Сценарий POSXY VELXY POSZ VELZ YAW --- --- --- --- --- --- Поток + дальномер 0 5 1 или 2 низко над ровным полом 0 1 UWB 4 0 4 или 1 0 1 Mocap / VIO через VISO_ 6 6, если шлёшь скорость; иначе 0 6 6 или 0 6 Mocap как псевдо-GPS GPS_INPUT 3 3 3 3 2 Компас в помещении врёт от арматуры на десятки градусов: с mocap курс берут из него же EK3_SRC1_YAW = 6 , COMPASS_USE = 0 , с потоком и UWB компас остаётся слабым местом. Оптический поток как источник скорости Датчик выдаёт угловую скорость картинки рад/с ; скорость над полом v = flow − ω_gyro · h est-alt-sources , поэтому без дальномера потока нет. Параметры: FLOW_TYPE 1 PX4Flow, 2 Pixart, 4 CXOF, 5 MAVLink, 6 DroneCAN, 7 MSP, 8 UPFLOW, 10 SITL , FLOW_ORIENT_YAW сантиградусы , FLOW_POS_X/Y/Z , масштаб FLOW_FXSCALER / FLOW_FYSCALER в тысячных: поток умножается на 1 + FXSCALER/1000 , диапазон ±800. В EKF: EK3_FLOW_USE 1 — навигация, 2 — только оценка рельефа , EK3_FLOW_DELAY 10 мс по умолчанию, 0–250 , EK3_FLOW_M_NSE 0.25 рад/с , EK3_FLOW_I_GATE 300 = 3σ , EK3_FLOW_MAX 2.5 рад/с; до 4.7 — EK3_MAX_FLOW . Два следствия. EKF ограничивает путевую скорость: ekfGndSpdLimit = EK3_FLOW_MAX − 1 · h — 1.5 м/с на высоте 1 м. И позиции поток не даёт POSXY = 0 : EKF интегрирует скорость, точка удержания ползёт, а Loiter не поднимется выше RNGFND1_MAX метры; до 4.7 — RNGFND1_MAX_CM , сантиметры . Внешняя позиция: три двери в один EKF - VISO_TYPE = 1 MAVLink . Принимаются VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE , GLOBAL_VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE , VICON_POSITION_ESTIMATE , ATT_POS_MOCAP позиция + ориентация , VISION_SPEED_ESTIMATE и ODOMETRY поза + скорость; только frame_id = MAV_FRAME_LOCAL_FRD и child_frame_id = MAV_FRAME_BODY_FRD , иначе сообщение молча выбрасывается . VISO_TYPE = 2 — T265, 3 — VOXL. Шум: ковариация из сообщения, но не меньше VISO_POS_M_NSE 0.2 м , VISO_YAW_M_NSE 0.2 рад , VISO_VEL_M_NSE 0.1 м/с ; NaN в covariance 0 — «бери из параметров». EKF принимает позу не чаще раза в 20 мс extNavIntervalMin_ms , слать быстрее 50 Гц бессмысленно. - GPS_INPUT GPS1_TYPE = 14 . Мост превращает позу в lat/lon/alt и скорости; EKF думает, что это GPS EK3_SRC1_ = 3 . Курс — поле yaw в сантиградусах, 0 значит «курса нет», север кодируется как 36000. Задержка — GPS1_DELAY_MS . Так сделан официальный пример с Vicon; работает и на платах с 1 МБ флеша, но reset_counter и ориентации нет. - AP_DDS ROS 2 . Топик /ap/tf tf2_msgs/TFMessage , берётся только трансформ odom → base_link ; конверсия в коде x, −y, −z — то есть ось X твоего odom обязана смотреть на «север» EKF. Джиттер-коррекции нет в коде TODO , ошибка 0, сбросов нет. Подключение AP_DDS — в ros2-ardupilot. Через MAVROS: /mavros/vision_pose/pose ENU → VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE NED , конверсию делает плагин. Ловушка 1: системы координат ArduPilot ждёт позицию в NED относительно origin и ориентацию «нос–право–низ» FRD . ROS и почти все mocap отдают ENU / FLU, OptiTrack по умолчанию — Y вверх. Переход ENU → NED: N = y , E = x , D = −z , yaw_NED = π/2 − yaw_ENU . Ошибка в осях не видна на земле: в точке 0, 0, 0 любые оси совпадают, pre-arm проходит шаг 5 .
