text: summary «40 м над землёй» в холмах — это три системы отсчёта и два источника данных о земле: база SRTM на борту и дальномер. Модуль разбирает, как ArduPilot и коротко PX4 следует рельефу, за что отвечают TERRAIN_ , RNGFND , SURFTRAK_ , RTL_ALT_TYPE , что происходит без данных и почему SRTM не видит деревья. Лабораторная — миссия в SITL через гору Маджура перепад 288 м с базой и с дальномером, график истинной высоты над землёй по логу, удар о склон при RTL с неверным типом высоты и terrain failsafe при потере дальномера. theory Три высоты Барометр, GPS и дальномер как источники высоты разобраны в est-alt-sources; здесь — что из них значит «над землёй». Frame точки миссии модуль ap-missions : MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL 0 — над уровнем моря AMSL ; MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT 3 — над точкой арма; MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_TERRAIN_ALT 10, в Mission Planner «Terrain» — над землёй: h_AGL = h_AMSL − h_terrain lat, lon . Откуда взять h_terrain — и есть весь модуль. Источник Что измеряет Дальность / точность Где врёт --- --- --- --- База рельефа на SD-карте «SRTM» модель поверхности DSM , а не голой земли: SRTM — радарная съёмка 2000 г.; тайлы terrain.ardupilot.org собраны из JAXA ALOS, 0–84° широты; сетка TERRAIN_SPACING 100 м типично ±10 м, на вершине лыжного склона замечено 35 м документация ArduPilot деревья, здания, карьеры и отвалы новее съёмки Дальномер вниз лидар/радар расстояние до ближайшей поверхности под аппаратом 7–180 м по модели; ±2–5 см кроны и трава — «земля», вода и чёрный асфальт для лидара, наклон, не видит вперёд База даёт карту заранее профиль проверяется до вылета , дальномер — реальную поверхность, но только под собой. База рельефа на борту TERRAIN_ENABLE = 1 включает базу. Полётник запрашивает недостающие клетки сообщением TERRAIN_REQUEST , GCS Mission Planner, QGC, MAVProxy module load terrain отвечает TERRAIN_DATA блоками 4×4 точки; данные пишутся в APM/TERRAIN/S36E149.DAT файл на градус, 2.5 МБ при шаге 100 м и остаются на SD. База SRTM3 у GCS — 100 м; TERRAIN_SPACING меньше 100 только тратит SD. Состояние — TERRAIN_REPORT pending , loaded , terrain_height , current_height и лог TERR.TerrH/CHeight/Pending/Loaded/ROfs . Пока pending != 0 или нет высоты дома и точек миссии, terrain-миссия не армится: PreArm: waiting for terrain data AP_Terrain::pre_arm_checks . TERRAIN_OFS_MAX 30 м — при арме база сдвигается так, чтобы высота дома совпала с GPS/баро TERR.ROfs ; в лаборатории +1.08 м , не больше этого значения. TERRAIN_MARGIN 0.05 — допуск по координатам при приёме блоков от GCS, не высота безопасности. Единица в метаданных — м, в описании — «centi-meters»; по коду TERRAIN_LATLON_EQUAL : margin × 100 в единицах 1e-7° 0.05 ≈ 5 единиц ≈ 5.6 см, то есть фактически метры. TERRAIN_CACHE_SZ 12 блоков 32×28 по ≈1.8 кБ — кэш в памяти. В 4.7 добавлен бит 2 TERRAIN_OPTIONS «Accept Old Terrain Data»: тайлы, созданные до 24 февраля 2026 г., содержат ошибки старого генератора, без бита 4.7 не армит «terrain data expired, possible errors» — папку APM/TERRAIN удалить и скачать заново. Как Copter держит высоту над рельефом В AUTO точка с frame Terrain — это смещение terr_offset над EKF-началом; источник выбирает AC_WPNav::get_terrain_source : если дальномер вниз настроен и WP_RFND_USE = 1 по умолчанию 1; до 4.7 — WPNAV_RFND_USE , как и все WPNAV_ — дальномер; иначе база, если TERRAIN_ENABLE = 1 . Фолбэка с дальномера на базу нет: нездоровый дальномер при WP_RFND_USE = 1 означает «данных нет». Высота по дальномеру — дистанция × cos наклона AP_SurfaceDistance , наклон ограничен 45° , затем фильтр RNGFND_FILT 0.5 Гц и сглаживание SURFTRAK_TC 1 с . Copter не смотрит вперёд: цель меняется с землёй под аппаратом, климб ограничен WP_SPD_UP 2.5 м/с; до 4.7 — WPNAV_SPEED_UP , 250 см/с , спуск — WP_SPD_DN 1.5 м/с; до 4.7 — WPNAV_SPEED_DN , 150 см/с . Когда ошибка по высоте больше половины WP_TER_MARGIN 10 м , горизонтальная скорость линейно падает до 1 % AC_PosControl::terrain_scaler_D_m , в 4.6 — pos_offset_z_scaler . Правило: на склоне s при скорости V нужен климб V·s ; всё сверх WP_SPD_UP — потеря высоты, пока TER_MARGIN не затормозит. В Loiter, AltHold, PosHold с дальномером работает surface tracking: SURFTRAK_MODE 1 — земля по умолчанию , 0 — выключено, 2 — потолок. Цель — CTUN.DSAlt , измерение — CTUN.SAlt . Выше RNGFND1_MAX метры; до 4.7 — RNGFND1_MAX_CM , сантиметры датчик становится «OutOfRangeHigh», и трекинг молча отпускает цель в баро-высоту. Аплет copter_terrain_brake.lua TERR_BRK_ENABLE , TERR_BRK_ALT , TERR_BRK_HDIST переводит Loiter в BRAKE, если высота над базой упала ниже порога. RTL и возврат через гору RTL_ALT_TYPE = 0 по умолчанию : RTL_ALT_M до 4.7 — RTL_ALT в сантиметрах — над домом, высота возврата max текущая, RTL_ALT_M с конусом RTL_CONE_SLOPE ; гребень выше этого между аппаратом и домом — столкновение. RTL_ALT_TYPE = 1 : RTL_ALT_M — над рельефом, источник как в AUTO. Pre-arm при типе 1: без источника — «RTL_ALT_TYPE is above-terrain but no terrain data», с дальномером — «RTL_ALT_TYPE is above-terrain but RTL_ALT_M above RNGFND_MAX», то есть нужно RTL_ALT_M ≤ RNGFND1_MAX . Документация называет тип 1 «not recommended»: если данных нет в момент RTL, полётник пишет «RTL: no terrain data, using alt-above-home» с дальномером — «RTL: rangefinder unhealthy, using alt-above-home» и идёт на RTL_ALT_M над домом — снова через гребень. Компромисс для холмов: тип 0 и RTL_ALT_M выше самой высокой точки на пути домой плюс запас, либо rally-точки за гребнем. Terrain failsafe Общая логика failsafe — в ap-safety-fs; у рельефа свой, с двумя триггерами ArduCopter/events.cpp , mode_auto.cpp . Первый — таймаут: режим требует рельеф AUTO, Guided, RTL и update_wpnav не получает высоту дольше FS_TERRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000 мс документация пишет 2 с; в коде 4.6.3 и 4.7 — 5 с . Второй — мгновенный: очередная команда миссии с frame Terrain не может задать цель wp_start вернул false . Итог одинаков: «Failsafe: Terrain data missing», ERR Subsys 23 ECode 1 , RTL MODE.Rsn = 11 , на земле — дизарм; RTL, потерявший рельеф,

text: summary ArduPilot is an autopilot, not just a stabilizer. Where Betaflight makes a quadcopter obedient under the sticks, ArduPilot knows where the vehicle is, where it is going, and what to do without a pilot. This module explains how thinking in ArduPilot differs from Betaflight: parameters instead of CLI diffs, flight modes as levels of autonomy, the ground station, pre-arm checks, and hardware requirements. After it the whole "Autonomy" track opens up. theory Versions and parameter names The course is written for the stable ArduPilot 4.7 release Copter and Plane 4.7.3 of November 14, 2026; 4.7.0 was released on July 21, 2026 . Names, units, and defaults are checked against the source of the 4.7.2 tag and the SITL parameters of that build, and the 4.7.3 differences against the source of the 4.7.3 tag: no parameter names were removed or renamed, one default changed, and two parameters were added the "Moving from 4.7.2 to 4.7.3" table below . Labs captured on SITL 4.7.2 are marked as such. The previous release is 4.6.3: where a parameter was renamed or changed its unit in 4.7, the modules give the new name and, once, the old one in parentheses, and all the replacements are collected in the table below. Lab outputs captured on 4.6.3 are left as they are and marked with the version. Earlier renames that still appear in old guides: in Plane from 4.5 ARSPD_FBW_MIN/MAX → AIRSPEED_MIN/MAX , and from 4.6 GPS_TYPE → GPS1_TYPE . Moving from 4.6 to 4.7: what was renamed and what changed 1. Before flashing: save the full parameter list to a file .param and download the logs from the flight controller. According to a developer post in the 4.7.0 release thread, on boards with logs in onboard flash LittleFS the update erases the logs; this has not been verified in the source. 2. Flash over the top, without erasing parameters: on its first boot 4.7 moves the old values to the new names by itself and converts the units cm → m, centidegrees → degrees . A full erase is needed only if you want to start from factory values, and then you have to repeat the calibrations and the setup. 3. What is not carried over: the SRn_ stream rates in MAVn_ they come up at defaults, so set them again ; .param files, Lua scripts, pymavlink scripts, and CI rules with the old names: a parameter with that name no longer exists, and the write silently does nothing; AVOID_ANGLE_MAX : avoidance by leaning was removed from the standard builds in a build with that option the value is moved to AVOID_ANG_MAX . 4. A rollback to 4.6 is possible, but values already changed in 4.7 under the new names are not converted back: to roll back, load the saved 4.6 parameter file. 5. Ground station: update Mission Planner or QGroundControl; an old version shows errors on renamed parameters and does not know the new ones. 6. After the update, compare the new parameter list with the old file using the table below; be sure to check ARMING_SKIPCHK it must be 0 , RTL_ALT_M , ATC_ANGLE_MAX , MAVn_ , and the Loiter behavior. 7. First-flight traps: in 4.7.0–4.7.2 Loiter did coordinated turns by default LOIT_OPTIONS = 1 , and in 4.7.3 the default is 0 again, so Loiter behaves as in 4.6 LOITER_DEFAULT_OPTIONS in AC_Loiter.cpp ; you enable the turns by hand with LOIT_OPTIONS = 1 ; the ATC_INPUT_TC default became 0.10 instead of 0.15, so the sticks are sharper; old terrain tiles cause the pre-arm failure "terrain data expired, possible errors", so delete the APM/TERRAIN folder on the SD card; the Simple and Super Simple modes do not work in 4.7.0, which was fixed in 4.7.1. Was 4.6.3 Now 4.7.3 What changed Since --- --- --- --- ARMING_CHECK ARMING_SKIPCHK the meaning is inverted: a mask of checks to skip ; 0 means all enabled it was 1 , −1 skips all the optional ones it was 0 . text: summary SITL Software In The Loop is the real ArduPilot firmware running on a computer instead of a flight controller, with a physics simulator in place of the real world. Here you can crash a hundred octocopters for free: mix up parameters, turn off GPS in flight, lose a motor. This module shows how to bring up SITL, connect a ground station, control the drone from a Python script, and organize a project so that routes and scenarios live separately. theory How SITL works The firmware is built for Linux and exchanges "sensor readings" and "motor commands" with a physics simulator. Everything else is real: the same parameters, modes, EKF, failsafes, and logs. So whatever you debug in SITL carries over to hardware almost unchanged. Almost, because the simulation has ideal vibration, an ideal link, and an honest GPS unless you degrade them yourself. Technically SITL is a single process: the build/sitl/bin/arducopter binary built with ./waf configure --board sitl && ./waf copter contains both the firmware and a built-in vehicle model selected with --model . The model and the firmware step on a shared clock lockstep : the model computes physics at SIM_RATE_HZ 1200 Hz by default on SITL, libraries/SITL/SITL.cpp:47 , and the firmware runs its main loop at SCHED_LOOP_RATE 400 Hz on Copter on the same simulated clock: roughly three physics steps per firmware loop. The firmware reads the model's "sensors" and outputs PWM to the motors, and the model turns the PWM into thrust. Hence the key property: time in SITL is simulated . You can speed it up, and then a minute of flight passes in 6 seconds, but only if the computer can keep up. Starting it: sim_vehicle.py or the binary directly sim_vehicle.py is a Python wrapper: it builds the firmware, picks the parameter files for the frame, and starts the binary and MAVProxy. For the -f octa-quad frame it passes --defaults copter.parm,copter-octaquad.parm to the binary the frame table is Tools/autotest/pysim/vehicleinfo.py , for -f hexa it passes copter.parm,copter-hexa.parm , and for + / quad only copter.parm . The default start location is the CMAC airfield in Canberra: SIM_OPOS_LAT/LNG/ALT = −35.363261, 149.165230, 584 m, the same as the CMAC line in Tools/autotest/locations.txt -35.363261,149.165230,584,353 : latitude, longitude, altitude above mean sea level in meters, heading in degrees . For a different location use -L <name from the same file, or --home lat,lon,alt,hdg with the binary. For automated tests and CI it is more convenient to start the binary directly, without MAVProxy: fewer processes, full control over the flags, and your pymavlink script becomes the ground station. The command used in this module's practice: build/sitl/bin/arducopter --model + --speedup 10 -w \ --defaults Tools/autotest/default_params/copter.parm,lab.parm \ --home -35.363261,149.165230,584,353 Parameter layers: what overrides what A parameter in SITL gets its value from four layers, and almost every "oddity" of the simulator is a forgotten layer. 1. The default value in the firmware code AP_GROUPINFO . 2. The --defaults files from left to right: each one overrides the previous. sim_vehicle.py --add-param-file my.parm appends a file to the end of that list. 3. The saved values in eeprom.bin in the working folder: everything you changed with param set is stored there and overrides the defaults on the next start. 4. param set in the current session, which is written to layer 3 immediately. The -w --wipe flag erases eeprom.bin at startup, and then only layers 1–2 apply. What follows from this order: if you edit lab.parm and the value does not change, eeprom.bin holds the old one, so start with -w or delete the file. And the other way around: to keep settings between runs as in the Lua lab below , start without -w from the same folder. {{diagram:sitl-param-layers SITL parameter layers: the defaults file sets the default values, but eeprom.bin overrides them; -w erases eeprom.bin, otherwise an edit to the .parm file may have no effect.}} Ports and multiple vehicles The firmware's serial ports are TCP sockets in SITL libraries/AP_HAL_SITL/SITL_State.h:33 : SERIAL0 is tcp:0:wait , port 5760, and the firmware waits for a client on it before starting; SERIAL1 is 5762, SERIAL2 is 5763; SERIAL3 and SERIAL4 are taken by the simulated GPS1/GPS2; SERIAL5…SERIAL8 are 5765…5768. The -I N --instance flag shifts the base port by 10·N SITL_cmdline.cpp:438 : a second vehicle with -I 1 listens on 5770, 5772, 5773. That is how you bring up a swarm of 2–3 vehicles on one machine sim_vehicle.py -n 3 does it for you . MAVProxy holds 5760 and forwards the stream over UDP --out=udp:IP:14550 ; without MAVProxy your script connects to 5760. Time and speedup --speedup N writes the SIM_SPEEDUP parameter 1 by default . In the practice run at --speedup 10 , 101 s of simulated time passed in 10.1 s of real time, exactly 10×. The rule for scripts: measure every interval and timeout in firmware time time_boot_ms in SYSTEM_TIME and GLOBAL_POSITION_INT , not in the computer's time.time . A "wait 20 s" scenario written as time.sleep 20 waits 200 simulated seconds at a 10× speedup. If the computer cannot keep up, the real speedup is lower than the one requested, which is why it is worth measuring, as in step 5. sim_vehicle.py and MAVProxy The sim_vehicle.py script builds the firmware and starts it together with MAVProxy, a console ground station. The key flags: - -v ArduCopter or -v ArduPlane : the vehicle type; - -f octa-quad , -f quad , -f quadplane : the frame model in the simulator -f quad , and a start without -f , is a Quad Plus, FRAME_TYPE = 0 ; a Quad X is -f X ; - --console --map : the console and map windows; - -w : reset the parameters to defaults useful when experiments have gone astray . You connect a ground station QGroundControl, Mission Planner to the MAVProxy output over UDP; it usually finds it by itself. The main path runs in SITL sim_vehicle.py ; parameter names are for Copter 4.7.2, outputs were captured on Copter-4.6.3 ; the steps that do not exist in the simulator are done on the bench with props off and in the field. The lab: a .param before and after, a hover log with MOT_THST_HOVER at 0.2–0.5, and logged RC and battery failsafes. theory The vehicle we use The example for the whole module: an X quad on 7" props, 1.4 kg, a 6S LiPo of 4000 mAh, an H7 flight controller with a barometer and an SD card, a 4-in-1 ESC running BLHeli32/AM32, an ELRS receiver, a GPS with a compass on a mast, analog video. A 2806.5 motor with a 7×3.5 prop gives about 1200 g of thrust module f-aero-props , T/W ≈ 4 × 1.2 / 1.4 = 3.4, and the expected hover throttle is MOT_THST_HOVER ≈ 1/3.4 ≈ 0.29. Version: ArduCopter 4.7 checked against the 4.7.2 source and parameters . Names that differ from 4.6 the full table is in module ap-intro : ARMING_SKIPCHK before 4.7 it was ARMING_CHECK , with the opposite meaning , RTL_ALT_M in meters before 4.7 it was RTL_ALT in centimeters , PSC_D_ACC_P/I before 4.7 they were PSC_ACCZ_P/I , with values 10 times larger . The SITL outputs in the practice section were captured on Copter-4.6.3 and are left unedited. The 17 steps and where each one is done Step What it is in ArduCopter 4.7 Where Details --- --- --- --- --- 1 Firmware, backup _with_bl.hex over DFU, then .apj ; a .param before any change bench, SITL this module 2 Frame, orientation FRAME_CLASS , FRAME_TYPE , AHRS_ORIENTATION SITL ap-intro 3 Ports SERIALn_PROTOCOL : 2 MAVLink2, 5 GPS, 23 RCIN, 16 ESC Telemetry, 42 DisplayPort SITL this module 4 Receiver SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 23 , RC_PROTOCOLS , RC_OPTIONS , RSSI_TYPE = 3 , bind bench link-elrs 5 Channels RCMAP_ , calibration of RCn_MIN/MAX/TRIM bench this module 6 Motor protocol MOT_PWM_TYPE , SERVO_DSHOT_ESC , SERVO_BLH_ SITL, bench f-motors-esc 7 Order, direction Motor Test A–D, SERVO_BLH_RVMASK SITL, bench this module 8 ESCs, idle ESC_CALIBRATION PWM only , MOT_SPIN_ARM/MIN bench this module 9 Accel, compass 6 positions, Onboard Mag Calibration bench SITL ap-ekf 10 Battery monitor BATT_MONITOR , BATT_VOLT_MULT , BATT_AMP_PERVLT , BATT_AMP_OFFSET SITL, bench this module 11 Modes, arming FLTMODE_CH , FLTMODE1..6 , RCx_OPTION , pre-arm SITL ap-intro 12 Failsafe FS_THR_ENABLE/VALUE , BATT_FS_LOW_ACT/CRT_ACT SITL, bench ap-safety-fs 13 OSD OSD_TYPE : 1 MAX7456, 5 MSP DisplayPort bench this module 14 GPS, home, RTL GPS1_TYPE , RTL_ALT_M SITL ap-ekf 15 First hover Stabilize → AltHold → Loiter, MOT_HOVER_LEARN = 2 SITL → field this module 16 First tune notch, QuikTune or AutoTune field ap-tuning 17 Log and backup .BIN , .param , file comparison SITL, field ap-logs {{diagram:ap-setup-flow The 17 setup steps of ArduCopter 4.7: SITL covers more than half of the chain, while bind, radio and ESC calibration, OSD and tuning exist only on hardware, and the props go on only at step 15.}} The bootloader and the two file formats ArduPilot on ChibiOS is installed in two stages. The first time, the board has no ArduPilot bootloader it runs Betaflight or factory firmware , so you write arducopter_with_bl.hex , the bootloader plus the firmware, over DFU: hold BOOT, plug in USB, use STM32CubeProgrammer. A .apj file cannot be flashed this way: only the ArduPilot bootloader understands it. Every later update is a .apj loaded with Mission Planner Install Firmware or Load custom firmware or QGroundControl Vehicle Setup → Firmware; plug the board in after you open the tab . The files are on firmware.ardupilot.org in the folder Copter → stable or stable-4.7.2 → the board name, which matches its hwdef. The STM32 DFU bootloader is in ROM, so you can go back to Betaflight with the same DFU procedure; before you flash, save diff all from the Betaflight CLI. Calibrations that are plain formulas The analog battery monitor in AP_BattMonitor_Analog.cpp : V = V_pin − BATT_VLT_OFFSET × BATT_VOLT_MULT , I = V_pin − BATT_AMP_OFFSET × BATT_AMP_PERVLT . It follows that: - new BATT_VOLT_MULT = old × V_multimeter / V_GCS; - new BATT_AMP_OFFSET = old + I₀ / BATT_AMP_PERVLT , where I₀ is the reading at zero current; - new BATT_AMP_PERVLT = old × I_clamp / I_GCS = old × mAh_charger / mAh_flight_controller. Zero first, slope second: a scale fitted with a wrong zero is correct at one point only. {{diagram:chart-ap-batt-cal Worked example: the sensor actually outputs 0.0125 V + I/44 A/V. With the stock 0 V and 40 A/V the GCS shows 0.50 A at rest and 9.59 A at 10 A on the clamp meter; an offset of 0.0125 V removes the zero error 9.09 A , and the scale 40 × 10/9.09 = 44 gives an exact 10.0 A.}} Motors: output = MOT_SPIN_MIN + MOT_SPIN_MAX − MOT_SPIN_MIN × r, where r is the thrust after the MOT_THST_EXPO linearization; PWM = MOT_PWM_MIN + output × MOT_PWM_MAX − MOT_PWM_MIN . MOT_THST_HOVER 0.125–0.6875, default 0.35 is the motor thrust needed to hover as a fraction of the maximum, so it is ≈ 1 / T/W . A value of 0.2–0.5 corresponds to a T/W from 5 down to 2: below that the throttle is too twitchy, above it there is no margin for maneuvers and wind. Why it will not arm: ARMING_SKIPCHK and the PreArm messages While the vehicle is disarmed, the firmware runs the pre-arm checks once a second, and at the moment of the arm command it runs them again together with the final arming checks. The reason for a refusal arrives as text in a STATUSTEXT message AP_Arming.cpp , check_failed . The prefix tells you when, not what: PreArm: is th

text: summary The OSD in ArduPilot is a separate library, AP_OSD , with five backend types, four item screens, and two parameter screens. This module works through it on ArduCopter 4.7.2: what each OSD_TYPE value means, which SERIALn_PROTOCOL and which MSP_OPTIONS bits analog, HDZero, Walksnail, DJI O3/O4, and legacy DJI need; how to choose the OSDn_TXT_RES grid, exactly how screens switch with each OSD_SW_METHOD , what the OSD_W_ warning levels do, and how the flight controller controls an analog VTX through VTX_ . Power and wiring of the air units and the goggle settings are in bf-hd-osd-video and inav-osd-hd and are not repeated here. The lab needs no hardware and no simulator: from a training parameter file you determine the active screen for given channel values, find the items that are off the grid, pick the "port, OSD type, MSP options" triple for four systems, and find three configuration errors. theory Who draws the OSD: OSD_TYPE OSD_TYPE selects the backend, that is, whoever turns flight controller data into a picture. The default in the source is 0, but a board can set its own value: in the 4.7.2 tree about a hundred board definitions hwdef set 1 and about fifteen set 5. The parameter requires a reboot; while it is 0, the other OSD_ parameters are hidden. OSD_TYPE Name Who draws What else is needed --- --- --- --- 0 None nobody — 1 MAX7456 a chip on the board overlays characters on the analog video; the grid is 30×16 PAL or 30×13 NTSC , and the standard is detected automatically camera and VTX on the board's pads 2 SITL a simulator window a build with SFML sim_vehicle.py --osd 3 MSP the goggles: the flight controller sends only MSP telemetry and item positions and draws nothing itself SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 33 or 32 4 TXONLY nobody; it makes the OSD parameter selection available to other modules the CRSF script on the transmitter — 5 MSP_DISPLAYPORT the goggles draw, in their own font, the characters that the flight controller has placed in cells SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 42 The OSD thread runs with a 100 ms period: 10 times per second the screen is cleared and drawn again. OSD_TYPE2 enables a second backend alongside the first. The typical case is a long-range wing with an analog VTX and an HD system OSD_TYPE = 1 , OSD_TYPE2 = 5 . The compatible pairs are "MAX7456 or SITL" + "MSP or DisplayPort". Two identical types, MAX7456 + SITL, and MSP + DisplayPort do not start; the flight controller then refuses to arm with the message OSD_TYPE2 not compatible with first OSD . Both backends show the same current screen, so for different grids you make two screens and switch between them with a switch. {{diagram:ap-osd-backend-map Three OSD paths in ArduPilot: MAX7456 draws by itself, DisplayPort hands cells to the goggles, and legacy MSP hands over telemetry only. The port protocol and the OSD type must match as a pair: 42 with 5, 33 with 3.}} The port: SERIALn_PROTOCOL and MSP_OPTIONS SERIALn_PROTOCOL Purpose Wires --- --- --- 32 MSP MSP telemetry on request: third-party MSP OSDs, MSP sensors TX and RX 33 DJI FPV telemetry for legacy DJI FPV Goggles V1/V2 without WTFOS : the flight controller answers as Betaflight BTFL TX and RX; TX only with bit 0 of MSP_OPTIONS 42 DisplayPort cell-by-cell output: HDZero, Walksnail, DJI O3/O4, DJI with WTFOS TX and RX 37 SmartAudio analog VTX control one wire on TX 44 IRC Tramp analog VTX control one wire on TX and SERIALn_OPTIONS = 4 half duplex 29 Crossfire VTX VTX control over CRSF TX and RX For 32, 33, and 42 the firmware sets a default baud rate of SERIALn_BAUD = 115 . It is only a default: if the port's baud rate was already saved as something else, it stays that way, so check it by hand. MSP_OPTIONS 0 by default is a bitmask: Bit Value Name What it does --- --- --- --- 0 1 EnableTelemetryMode "push" mode: the flight controller sends packets by itself without waiting for requests. Needed when only one wire runs between the OSD and the flight controller. It works only with protocol 33; for DisplayPort leave it at 0 1 2 — unused 2 4 EnableBTFLFonts DisplayPort: character indexes from the Betaflight font table, and the answer to the firmware type request is BTFL ; decimal packing is disabled in this case 3 8 EnableINAVFonts DisplayPort: characters are translated to the INAV font; overrides bit 2 The character table is selected when the backend starts, so a reboot is needed after changing MSP_OPTIONS . MSP_OSD_NCELLS 0 Auto, 1–14 sets the cell count for the average cell voltage in MSP telemetry; Auto calculates floor V / 4.35 + 1 from the highest voltage seen. Which system needs what System SERIALn_PROTOCOL OSD_TYPE MSP_OPTIONS OSDn_TXT_RES Font --- --- --- --- --- --- Analog, a board with a MAX7456 — 1 — — OSD_FONT 0–4 in the chip HDZero 42 5 0 0 or 1; with 2 the text turns into garbage the ArduPilot font in the goggles Walksnail Avatar 42 5 0 1 the ArduPilot font file is selected in the goggle menu DJI Air Unit/Vista with WTFOS + msp-osd 42 5 0 2 or 1 a font package on the goggles' SD card DJI O3 / O4, stock firmware 42 5 4; 8 if the INAV font is selected in the goggles 1 the Betaflight or INAV font in the goggles DJI FPV V1/V2 without WTFOS 33 3 0 1 with a single wire — the goggles draw the items The HDZero and WTFOS rows follow the ArduPilot wiki; for legacy DJI the wiki also sets bit 2 of MSP_OPTIONS and bit 5 of OSD_OPTIONS , but in the 4.7 code bit 2 affects only DisplayPort protocol 33 always identifies as BTFL , so 0 works. In DJI goggles the custom OSD option must be enabled. With the Betaflight font add bit 5 to OSD_OPTIONS , otherwise the arrows point the wrong way. text: summary In ArduPilot every signal pad is "output n" with an assignable role, SERVOn_FUNCTION : a motor, a control surface, a transmitter channel passthrough, an LED strip, or a plain GPIO pin. This module follows the whole path on ArduCopter 4.7.2 from the function to the microcontroller's timer: the list of functions with their numbers, the SERVOn_MIN/MAX/TRIM/REVERSED range, the SERVO_RATE and RC_SPEED rates, the MOT_PWM_TYPE protocols, timer groups and the messages on a conflict, DShot and bidirectional DShot with the SERVO_BLH_ parameters, ESC telemetry, passthrough, the IOMCU coprocessor, the safety switch, GPIO, and relays. After the module you can lay out motors, servos, an LED strip, and relays across the outputs of a specific board so that the flight controller arms the first time. The lab is a calculation exercise with no hardware and no simulator: an output plan from the hwdef of the MatekH743 board, bitmasks, the servo pulse width in the firmware's integer arithmetic, and finding three errors in a parameter file. theory The pipeline: from function to pin The signal on an output passes through four stages. 1. Source. The motor mixer ctl-allocation , the surface controller, the gimbal, a Lua script, or a transmitter channel writes a value not "to output 3" but to a function: "Motor1", "Elevator", "Script1". 2. SRV_Channel . For every output whose SERVOn_FUNCTION equals that function, the value is converted to microseconds using SERVOn_MIN/MAX/TRIM/REVERSED . One function can be assigned to several outputs. 3. RCOutput . The board driver turns microseconds into what the protocol requires: a PWM pulse, a DShot frame, or an LED strip bit stream. 4. Timer. The channels of one hardware timer drive the pads. The protocol and the rate are set for the whole timer. {{diagram:ap-outputs-pipeline A value goes from the function through SRV_Channel and RCOutput to the timer. The range is set per output, but the protocol and rate are set for the whole timer, so layout errors show up at the last stage.}} Changing SERVOn_FUNCTION requires a reboot. There are 16 outputs; SERVO_32_ENABLE = 1 exposes the parameters of outputs 17–32. SERVOn_FUNCTION : functions by purpose Group Values What it does --- --- --- Utility −1 GPIO; 0 Disabled; 134 / 135 / 136 −1 makes the pad a digital pin; 0 leaves the output free for DO_SET_SERVO and scripts; 134–136 constantly output SERVOn_MIN , TRIM , or MAX Multicopter motors 33–40 Motor1–8; 82–85 Motor9–12; 160–179 Motor13–32 new in 4.7 a mixer output; the motor number follows the frame diagram, not the pad number Transmitter passthrough 1 RCPassThru; 51–66 RCIN1–16; 140–155 RCIN1Scaled–16Scaled 1 is the transmitter channel with the same number as the output; 51–66 are a chosen channel, with microseconds as received; 140–155 are a channel rescaled to the SERVOn_MIN/TRIM/MAX of this output Payload 6–9 Mount1 yaw, pitch, roll, retract ; 12–15 Mount2; 10 CameraTrigger; 27 Parachute; 28 Gripper; 29 LandingGear; 88 Winch gimbal servos, camera shutter, parachute, gripper, landing gear, winch Scripting 94–109 Script1–16 an output controlled from Lua ap-lua LEDs and sound 120–123 NeoPixel1–4; 129–131 ProfiLED1–3; 132 ProfiLEDClock; 138 / 139 Alarm a strip takes a whole timer; so does a buzzer on an output Plane 4 Aileron; 19 Elevator; 21 Rudder; 70 Throttle; 2 / 3 Flap; 24 / 25 Flaperon; 77 / 78 Elevon; 79 / 80 V-tail; 41, 45–47, 75, 76 motor tilt most of these functions are not in the Copter value list; assignment and the direction check are in ap-setup-plane On outputs 140–155 the position freezes on link loss; the bits of SERVO_RC_FS_MSK bit 0 is RCIN1Scaled send the selected outputs to TRIM . Output range: SERVOn_MIN , MAX , TRIM , REVERSED Parameter Default Range Meaning --- --- --- --- SERVOn_MIN 1100 µs 800–2200 the lower pulse limit SERVOn_MAX 1900 µs 800–2200 the upper limit SERVOn_TRIM 1500 µs 800–2200 neutral for signed functions SERVOn_REVERSED 0 0 / 1 reverses the direction Functions come in two types. An angle function surfaces, scripting outputs, RCINnScaled takes a number s from −4500 to +4500, with neutral at TRIM . A range function a plane's flap and throttle, from 0 to 100 takes s from 0 to H, with zero at MIN . The formulas from SRV_Channel.cpp , where ⌊ ⌋ means dropping the fractional part: - angle, s 0: PWM = TRIM + ⌊s · MAX − TRIM / 4500⌋; - angle, s ≤ 0: PWM = TRIM − ⌊ s · TRIM − MIN / 4500⌋; - range: PWM = MIN + ⌊s · MAX − MIN / H⌋. REVERSED = 1 flips the sign of s for an angle and replaces s with H − s for a range. The input is constrained to the limits first. The fraction is truncated, not rounded; the two halves of the travel, up and down, differ if TRIM is not in the middle. Arming is refused with SERVOn_MIN TRIM or SERVOn_MAX < TRIM . On DShot outputs the firmware itself keeps MIN / MAX at 1000/2000 and TRIM at 1000 1500 for reversible ones . Motor rate and protocol Parameter Default Range What it affects --- --- --- --- SERVO_RATE 50 Hz 25–400 all PWM outputs except the "fast" groups RC_SPEED 490 Hz 50–490 a copter's PWM motors; on main processor outputs no more than 400 Hz takes effect; not used for DShot. On a QuadPlane, Q_RC_SPEED MOT_PWM_TYPE 0 0–9 the motor protocol; needs a reboot. text: summary This module covers three sensors that ArduPilot needs configured before the first flight and that most often get configured only halfway: the compass, the airspeed sensor and the battery monitors. Working from the 4.7.2 source, it goes through what the firmware does with the raw compass field offsets, matrix, current compensation , the four calibration methods and the rule for choosing between them, the exact pre-arm failure strings, the bench side of the airspeed sensor and every BATT_MONITOR type from analog to "sum". After the module you choose the compass calibration method for a specific vehicle, check its result by the numbers, and lay out several batteries across monitors so that the failsafe and the OSD look at the right one. The lab is a calculation exercise with no hardware and no simulator: current interference compensation, "large vehicle" offsets, scale corrections for two monitors, a sum mask and three mistakes in a parameter file. theory How to read the module The module covers the bench, not the flight: everything that has to be set and checked on the compass, the pitot tube and the battery sensors before takeoff. The order is: first the compass, with instances and priorities, the field correction formula, the four calibration methods, a selection table and the pre-arm failures; then a short bench part on airspeed; then the battery monitors, with types, thresholds, the "sum" and layouts for several batteries. The first calibration of a single analog monitor is in ap-setup-scratch , and the ARSPD_ parameters for flight are in ap-setup-plane ; they are not repeated here. The behavior is described from reading the source at tag Copter-4.7.2; the firmware was not run in this pass. The compass: instances, priorities, external and internal At boot the firmware finds all magnetometers, gives each one a device ID bus type, bus number, address and chip type in one number and sorts them into three priority slots. The parameters with the suffixes 2 and 3 refer to a priority slot , not to an "internal" or "external" compass. Parameter Default Values Meaning --- --- --- --- COMPASS_ENABLE 1 0 / 1 the drivers and the logging of MAG ; needs a reboot COMPASS_USE , COMPASS_USE2 , COMPASS_USE3 1 0 / 1 whether the compass in slot 1, 2, 3 is used for yaw COMPASS_PRIO1_ID … PRIO3_ID 0 device ID which compass is in the slot; 0 means set automatically; needs a reboot COMPASS_DEV_ID , DEV_ID2 , DEV_ID3 0 read only the device ID the calibration of the slot was saved with COMPASS_DEV_ID4 … DEV_ID8 0 read only detected compasses beyond the three slots up to five COMPASS_EXTERNAL , EXTERN2 , EXTERN3 0 0 Internal; 1 External; 2 ForcedExternal with 0 and 1, auto-detection by bus connection can override the value; with 2 it cannot COMPASS_ORIENT , ORIENT2 , ORIENT3 0 0 None; 2 Yaw90; 4 Yaw180; 6 Yaw270; 8 Roll180; 10 Yaw90Roll180; 12 Pitch180; 14 Yaw270Roll180 and others up to 43; 101, 102 are custom angles the orientation of an external compass relative to the vehicle frame; an internal one follows AHRS_ORIENTATION COMPASS_AUTO_ROT 2 0 Disabled; 1 CheckOnly; 2 CheckAndFix; 3 the same with the same tolerance for 45° rotations the orientation check at the end of a rotation calibration COMPASS_DISBLMSK 0 a bitmask of driver types bit 11 is DroneCAN, bit 7 is IST8310… do not look for chips of this type at startup COMPASS_OPTIONS 0 bit 0 is CalRequireGPS; bit 1 allows a missing DroneCAN compass to be replaced automatically bit 0 is worth setting, see the scale factor below COMPASS_AUTODEC , COMPASS_DEC 1; 0 rad 0 / 1; −3.142…3.142 the declination from the built-in field model by location, or set manually The selection rule. A compass on a mast with the GPS goes in slot 1. The internal compass of a board that sits 2–3 cm from the power wires is disabled: COMPASS_USEn = 0 for its slot usually 2 or 3; go by COMPASS_PRIOn_ID , not by the number . It adds no accuracy but does produce the Compasses inconsistent failure. Do not change COMPASS_DEV_ID by hand: after a reboot the calibration would be tied to someone else's sensor. What the firmware does with the raw field Every measurement goes through correct_field AP_Compass_Backend.cpp in a strictly defined order: B = M · B_raw + OFS · SCALE + MOT · k - OFS is COMPASS_OFS_X/Y/Z , in mG, and it is added hard iron, est-sensors ; - SCALE is COMPASS_SCALE ; it is applied only if it lies within 0.667–1.5, otherwise it is skipped the value 0 means "not set" ; - M is a symmetric matrix: the diagonal is COMPASS_DIA_X/Y/Z 1 by default , off the diagonal are COMPASS_ODI_X xy , ODI_Y xz , ODI_Z yz soft iron ; - MOT is COMPASS_MOT_X/Y/Z ; k depends on COMPASS_MOTCT . COMPASS_MOTCT k Unit of COMPASS_MOT_ --- --- --- 0 no compensation — 1 throttle from 0 to 1 mG at full throttle 2 the current of the first battery monitor, A mG/A The compensation is added after the matrix. With COMPASS_MOTCT = 2 the current is taken only from monitor 1 BATT_ : if it has no current measurement, the correction is silently zero. For the second and third slot the parameters are the same with suffixes: COMPASS_OFS2_ , DIA2 , ODI2 , SCALE2 , MOT2 . There is also per-motor compensation, COMPASS_PMOT_ , for the first compass only; the module does not cover it. In the log the result is in the MAG message the I field is the instance : MagX/Y/Z is the already corrected field, OfsX/Y/Z are the current offsets, MOX/MOY/MOZ is the motor correction at that moment, and Health . Rotation calibration: what fitness is Onboard calibration a button in the ground station or the RCx_OPTION = 171 switch, disarmed only collects 300 samples while the vehicle is rotated with every side toward the ground and fits first a sphere and then an ellipsoid to them. Fitness is the root mean square of the residual: how many milligauss, on average, the points are away from the fitted surface. The lower, the better. The calibration is accepted if all of the following hold: Condition Threshold CompassCalibrator.cpp --- --- fi

text: summary The LED and the buzzer are the only things that report the state of the flight controller when there is neither a ground station nor an OSD nearby: whether it has passed the pre-arm checks, whether it has a position, whether a failsafe has triggered. Working from the ArduCopter 4.7.2 source, this module goes through the AP_Notify library: every NTF_ parameter, the bits of NTF_LED_TYPES and NTF_BUZZ_TYPES , the table of colors and rhythms exactly as the sequences in RGBLed.h define it, the tunes from ToneAlarm.cpp , NeoPixel and ProfiLED strips on outputs 120–123 and 129–132, LEDs driven from a Lua script, motor beeps over DShot, and the lost vehicle sound. After the module you can name the vehicle state and your action from a color and a rhythm, build the masks for specific hardware, and place a strip so that it does not disable your servos. The lab is a calculation exercise with no hardware and no simulator: masks, six LED patterns, a strip plan for a MatekH743, and three mistakes in a parameter file. theory What is in the module and in what order to read it First the structure of AP_Notify and the overall table of NTF_ parameters. Then the LEDs: the bits of NTF_LED_TYPES , the color table of the RGB LED, boards with one or two plain LEDs, NeoPixel and ProfiLED strips, and color control from a script and over MAVLink. Then sound: the two different buzzer drivers, the table of tunes, motor beeps over DShot and finding a crashed vehicle. At the end come the I2C display, a selection table by vehicle class, and the differences between 4.7 and 4.6. Timer groups are not repeated here: they are covered in ap-outputs , and this module only refers to them. The same topic in other firmware: bf-led-buzzer Betaflight , inav-led-pinio-beeper INAV , px4-hardware-peripherals PX4 ; their colors and tunes are their own, and you cannot carry them over from memory. How AP_Notify is built The library has three layers. 1. Flags and events. The rest of the firmware knows nothing about colors or tunes. It sets state flags initialising , armed , pre_arm_check , pre_arm_gps_check , failsafe_radio , failsafe_battery , failsafe_gcs , ekf_bad , gps_glitching , vehicle_lost and others and one-shot events arming_failed , user_mode_change , failsafe_mode_change , waypoint_complete , mission_complete . 2. Devices. At boot the LED drivers are created from the bits of NTF_LED_TYPES , then the display and the sound drivers. Each driver reads the same flags 50 times a second and decides by itself what to show. 3. Hardware. A GPIO pin, an I2C bus, an output with a strip, a DShot command, a DroneCAN node. Two practical conclusions follow. First, all RGB devices the board LED, the I2C LED in a GPS module, a NeoPixel strip, ESC LEDs show the same thing , because they inherit one class, RGBLed . Second, the set of devices is assembled once at boot, so a change of NTF_LED_TYPES , NTF_BUZZ_TYPES , NTF_BUZZ_PIN or NTF_LED_LEN needs a reboot. {{diagram:ap-notify-paths All devices read the flags and events at once: RGB LEDs of any type show one sequence, while motor beeps and ESC LEDs work only when disarmed.}} The NTF_ parameters Parameter Default Values Meaning and selection rule --- --- --- --- NTF_LED_TYPES board dependent: 123079 in SITL; 257 or 455 on many boards with a pad for a strip bitmask, bits 0–19 which LED drivers to create. Add a bit only for hardware that is actually fitted NTF_LED_BRIGHT 3 0 Off, 1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High brightness of RGB devices. When USB is connected the brightness is never higher than Low, whatever the setting. For a strip on the flight controller BEC use 1 or 2 NTF_LED_OVERRIDE 0 0 Standard, 1 MAVLink / Scripting / AP_Periph, 2 OutbackChallenge, 3 TrafficLight the color source. 0 if the pilot watches the LED; 3 if people work around the vehicle; 1 only together with a script or ground station commands NTF_LED_LEN 1 1–32 the number of LEDs in the strip on each NeoPixel or ProfiLED output. Set the actual count NTF_BUZZ_TYPES 5 on boards with CAN, otherwise 1 bitmask: bit 0 Built-in buzzer, bit 1 DShot, bit 2 DroneCAN which buzzers are active; 0 turns sound off entirely NTF_BUZZ_PIN −1 unless the board sets its own GPIO pin number an active buzzer on an arbitrary pin. The driver treats −1 and 0 as no buzzer NTF_BUZZ_ON_LVL 1 0 LowIsOn, 1 HighIsOn the pin level at which the buzzer on NTF_BUZZ_PIN sounds NTF_BUZZ_VOLUME 100 % 0–100 the volume of the tunes a multiplier of the PWM duty cycle ; it has no effect on the NTF_BUZZ_PIN buzzer NTF_DISPLAY_TYPE 0 0 Disable, 1 ssd1306, 2 sh1106, 10 SITL the I2C display NTF_OREO_THEME 0 0 Disabled, 1 Aircraft, 2 Rover the 3DR Solo LEDs; the parameter does not exist in ordinary builds Nothing in this group was renamed between 4.6 and 4.7. The bits of NTF_LED_TYPES and NTF_BUZZ_TYPES The value of a mask is the sum of 2^n over the bits that are set. Bit Weight Driver When to set it --- --- --- --- 0 1 Built-in LED the LEDs on the board itself 1 / 2 2 / 4 ToshibaLED: internal / external I2C bus the RGB LED in older GPS modules 3 8 PCA9685, external bus a PCA9685 expansion board 4 16 Oreo LED 3DR Solo only 5 32 DroneCAN the LED in a GPS module on the CAN bus 6 / 7 64 / 128 NCP5623: external / internal bus the RGB LED in current I2C GPS modules 8 256 NeoPixel a WS2812B or SK6812 strip 9 512 ProfiLED a ProfiLED strip with a clock line 10 1024 Scripting the color is not output but handed to a script: LED:get_rgb 11 2048 DShot LEDs on the ESCs through DShot commands 12 4096 ProfiLED_SPI only boards whose hwdef defines it 13 / 14 8192 / 16384 LP5562: external / internal bus per the GPS module documentation 15 / 16 32768 / 65536 IS31FL3195: external / internal bus per the GPS module documentation 17 131072 DiscreteRGB three separate pins, defined in the hwdef 18 262144 NeoPixelRGB a strip with RGB color order WS2811 : set it instead of bit 8 if red shows as green 19 524288 ProfiLED_IOMCU new in 4.7: an LED through the IO coprocessor on CubeBlack, CubeOrange, CubeYe

summary: SITL without an external simulator computes physics with a simple built-in model and has no idea what a tree, a wall or a camera image is. For vision, obstacle avoidance, precision landing and gimbals you need a world: Gazebo provides physics, lighting, cameras, lidars and rangefinders, and the auto
headings: Which Gazebo How the autopilot talks to the world An SDF world Sensors and the bridge to ROS 2 Speed and resources HITL and SITL Scenario tests Step 1. Iris in Gazebo Step 2. Your own world with a pole Step 3. A camera in ROS 2 Step 4. A scenario test
text: summary SITL without an external simulator computes physics with a simple built-in model and has no idea what a tree, a wall or a camera image is. For vision, obstacle avoidance, precision landing and gimbals you need a world: Gazebo provides physics, lighting, cameras, lidars and rangefinders, and the autopilot works with it as with a real vehicle. This module covers ArduPilot SITL and PX4 SITL paired with Gazebo the new one, gz , how an SDF world is built, adding an obstacle and a camera, bridging images into ROS 2, headless scenario tests for CI, and what HITL is and how it differs from SITL. theory Which Gazebo - Gazebo gz — the new line formerly Ignition . For ROS 2 Jazzy the paired LTS version is Gazebo Harmonic ; it is also the one the ArduPilot plugin recommends. - Gazebo Classic gazebo11 reached end of support in January 2025 — don't carry over old instructions with gazebo --verbose and Classic .world files. - The “ROS 2 — Gazebo” pairing is fixed: mixing versions outside the recommended pairs is a source of hard-to-pin-down problems with building the bridges. How the autopilot talks to the world - ArduPilot : the ardupilot_gazebo plugin the ArduPilotPlugin system in the model . Gazebo computes physics and sensors, the plugin sends the state to SITL and receives motor/servo commands from it; the exchange is JSON over UDP, in lockstep mode the simulation waits for the autopilot, time is synchronized . Launch: in one terminal gz sim -v4 -r iris_runway.sdf , in another sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -f gazebo-iris --model JSON --map --console . The frame name must contain gazebo- , the model must be JSON . - PX4 : Gazebo is built into the SITL build: make px4_sitl gz_x500 ; there are model variants with sensors e.g. gz_x500_depth , gz_x500_mono_cam and planes/VTOL; the world is selected with the PX4_GZ_WORLD variable. - Environment variables: GZ_SIM_SYSTEM_PLUGIN_PATH — where to look for plugins the ardupilot_gazebo build , GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH — models and worlds. An SDF world A world is an SDF XML file: physics the step, e.g. 1 ms , lighting, ground, models. A model is links link with collision geometry collision and visible geometry visual , mass and inertia, joints joint , sensors sensor and plugin systems. An obstacle is a static model: xml <model name="pole" <static true</static <pose 10 0 5 0 0 0</pose <link name="link" <collision name="collision" <geometry <cylinder <radius 0.3</radius <length 10</length </cylinder </geometry </collision <visual name="visual" <geometry <cylinder <radius 0.3</radius <length 10</length </cylinder </geometry </visual </link </model A pole 10 m tall, 10 m east of the world origin ENU: x — east, y — north, z — up . Sensors and the bridge to ROS 2 - Cameras, depth cameras, lidars gpu_lidar , IMUs are sensor elements in the model; they publish to the Gazebo bus gz-transport , list them with gz topic -l . - ros_gz_bridge carries topics between Gazebo and ROS 2: ros2 run ros_gz_bridge parameter_bridge /camera@sensor_msgs/msg/Image@gz.msgs.Image — the topic name, the ROS 2 type, the Gazebo type; @ means both directions, from Gazebo to ROS, from ROS to Gazebo. - A separate plugin, GstCameraPlugin from ardupilot_gazebo , streams camera video over GStreamer H.264, UDP 5600 — like a real camera on a companion; the stream is enabled by a message to the .../enable_streaming topic. An example world with a gimbal and camera is gimbal.sdf ; the Iris gimbal in iris_runway.sdf SITL with gazebo-iris-gimbal.parm is controlled by channels RC6–RC8. - Realism: a perfect camera with no noise or blur fools you — test vision algorithms with noise, lighting changes and motion blur noise parameters go in the sensor description . Speed and resources - Real-time factor RTF — the ratio of simulation speed to real time; with cameras and lidars on a weak machine it drops below 1. Lockstep keeps things correct, but the test takes longer. - Rendering is needed only for image sensors; for logic tests without cameras use the headless server gz sim -s -r world.sdf , for cameras on a machine without a display use --headless-rendering mode. HITL and SITL - SITL — the firmware is built for the computer, everything is virtual. - HITL hardware in the loop — a real flight controller with its own firmware; the sensors are replaced with simulator data over USB/MAVLink, the motors don't spin. It tests the real hardware: timing, CPU load, drivers — what SITL hides. Support and the setup method differ between PX4 and ArduPilot and between versions — follow the documentation for your version. {{diagram:sim-stand-choice-tree The test setup is chosen by what you check: logic without a world needs only SITL, a world without cameras and CI need Gazebo without graphics, vision needs Gazebo with a camera, and flight controller timing and drivers need HITL.}} Scenario tests A scenario is a reproducible flight with a check of the result: “take off to 10 m, fly around the pole, land; no closer than 2 m to the pole, altitude within tolerance.” It runs headless, is checked via MAVLink and the log, and the result is pass/fail for CI the “Configurations in CI” module . One scenario per safety function failsafe, geofence, RTL catches regressions on firmware and parameter updates before the field does. {{diagram:gazebo-sitl Gazebo computes physics and sensors, the plugin exchanges JSON with SITL in lockstep; images go to ROS 2 via ros_gz_bridge, the GCS and tests connect to SITL over MAVLink.}} practice Step 1. Iris in Gazebo Install Gazebo Harmonic and build ardupilot_gazebo following the README dependencies, cmake , make , set GZ_SIM_SYSTEM_PLUGIN_PATH and GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH . Launch iris_runway.sdf and SITL with -f gazebo-iris --model JSON . Take off in GUIDED to 10 m from MAVProxy. Record the RTF in hover. Step 2. text: summary A mission in ArduPilot is a list of commands that the flight controller executes by itself in AUTO mode: take off, fly the waypoints, take a picture, come back. This module explains what a mission is made of, how navigation commands differ from DO and CONDITION commands, how altitude is defined, where home is, and what happens when the link is lost in the middle of a route. The practice runs in SITL on the "route separate from scenario" pattern. theory Three types of commands - NAV : where to fly. NAV_TAKEOFF 22 , NAV_WAYPOINT 16 , NAV_LOITER_TIME 19 , NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH 20 , NAV_LAND 21 . A mission moves from one NAV command to the next. - DO : what to do along the way without changing the route: DO_CHANGE_SPEED 178 , DO_SET_SERVO 183 , DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST 206 , DO_JUMP 177 for loops. - CONDITION : wait for a condition before the next DO command: CONDITION_DELAY 112 , CONDITION_DISTANCE . The numbers in parentheses are MAV_CMD codes: that is how the commands appear in a mission file and in MAVLink. How the list is executed The mission is stored in the flight controller as a numbered list, and seq 0 is always home: on upload the vehicle puts its own home location there, and until home is set it returns zeros in the download in step 4, line 0 is 0.0000000 0.0000000 . The real commands start at seq 1, and the number of commands including home is the read-only parameter MIS_TOTAL . The executor libraries/AP_Mission/AP_Mission.cpp , advance_current_nav_cmd keeps one current NAV command and one current DO command. When the NAV command is complete an intermediate waypoint with no delay: when the trajectory target has reached the waypoint; a waypoint with a stop: when the vehicle is within WP_RADIUS_M ; a takeoff: when the altitude is reached , it moves forward through the list: it starts any DO command it meets and makes the next NAV command current. So a DO command placed after NAV number N runs at the moment of arrival at waypoint N, that is, it applies to the leg to the next waypoint. In the step 4 run you can see this in the lines Mission: 2 ChangeSpeed and Mission: 3 WP in the same second, right after the takeoff completes. A CONDITION command holds the following DO commands until its condition is met, but it does not stop the flight to the current waypoint. DO_JUMP and DO_CHANGE_SPEED DO_JUMP 177 : param1 is the number of the command to jump to seq , param2 is how many times to repeat, with −1 meaning forever. A repeat count of 1 means the section between the target and the jump is flown twice : the first time in sequence, the second after the jump. In the run: waypoints 3→4, Mission: 5 Jump 1/1 , 3→4 again, then the jump is skipped and the mission goes on to command 6. The jump counters are reset when the mission is started again, and a finite counter is also zeroed after its loop completes, so if you send the mission back to the start of the loop it runs again bit 3 of MIS_OPTIONS , DontZeroCounter, turns that off, but it is not listed among the options for Copter ; the number of DO_JUMP commands tracked in one mission is up to 100 on boards in the ≥ 500 kB memory class and 15 on the rest AP_Mission.h:29–33 . The target can also be a DO command: it executes, and the flight continues to the NAV command after it; a target of 0 or ≥ MIS_TOTAL ends the mission. A DO_JUMP with −1 and no exit is an endless circuit until the battery runs down; the only ways out of such a loop are a mode change, by the pilot or the GCS, or a failsafe battery, RC, GCS or geofence action. DO_CHANGE_SPEED 178 : param1 is the speed type 0 airspeed, 1 ground speed, 2 climb, 3 descent , param2 is the speed in m/s, param3 is the throttle in percent −1 means no change; Copter ignores it . On Copter, types 0 and 1 both change the horizontal speed WP_SPD , and 2 and 3 change WP_SPD_UP and WP_SPD_DN ArduCopter/mode_auto.cpp:1991 ; a value ≤ 0 is ignored. The new speed applies until the end of the mission or the next DO_CHANGE_SPEED , and the WP_SPD parameter itself does not change. Leg time The trajectory generator accelerates the vehicle at no more than WP_ACC 2.5 m/s² to the leg speed v and decelerates before the waypoint, and the acceleration changes no faster than the jerk WP_JERK 1 m/s³, AC_WPNav.cpp:37 . For a leg of length d with a stop at each end, when d is noticeably longer than v²/a: t ≈ d / v + v / a + a / J, where J = WP_JERK . Without the last term you get a trapezoidal speed profile, a teaching model with no jerk limit it is what the module's problem calculates . For 100 m with stops: at 5 m/s ≈ 20 + 2 + 2.5 = 24.5 s, at 10 m/s ≈ 10 + 4 + 2.5 = 16.5 s. An independent run in SITL 4.7.2 with a stop at every waypoint waypoints with a 3 s delay gave 24.1–24.6 s and 16.8–16.9 s of movement. In step 4 the intermediate waypoints are flown without stopping , so it does not test the formula: the legs there are shorter, 20.6–21.6 s at 5 m/s ≈ d/v plus the turn and 14.0–14.8 s at 10 m/s, with the first leg after takeoff at 23.2 s. This is a course guideline for the time budget: to the sum of the legs add takeoff, landing, wind, and a 10–20% margin. End of the mission If the last command is an ordinary waypoint and not NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH or NAV_LAND , Copter stays in AUTO when the list ends and holds position ModeAuto::exit_mission : loiter_start ; if the position is bad it switches to LAND, and if the vehicle is already on the ground it disarms. In the run, 20 s after the last waypoint: mode AUTO, 20.0 m, armed, speed 0.01 m/s. A vehicle hovering in AUTO burns battery until the battery failsafe triggers, hence the rule a course guideline : the last command of a mission is NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH or NAV_LAND . MIS_OPTIONS bit 2 ContinueAfterLand lets the mission continue after a NAV_LAND in the middle of the list, for delivery with a landing. Upload and download are a dialog Upload uses the MAVLink Mission protocol: the client sends MISSION_COUNT , then the vehicle requests every command by number ArduPilot

title: Guidance and trajectories: pure pursuit, L1, S-curves, minimum snap

But who decides *which* position to hold at each moment so the vehicle follows the mission line, turns smoothly and doesn't jerk? That's guidance and trajectory generation. This module walks through the layers from the mission down to

Pure pursuit in simulation Step 2. L1 of your own plane Step 3. Trapezoid and S-curve Step 4. SITL: jerk and corner rounding
text: summary The controllers in this course hold angle, velocity and position. But who decides which position to hold at each moment so the vehicle follows the mission line, turns smoothly and doesn't jerk? That's guidance and trajectory generation. This module walks through the layers from the mission down to the controller, the pure pursuit law and its relative L1 in ArduPlane with the lookahead distance formula via NAVL1_PERIOD , velocity profiles — the trapezoid and the jerk-limited S-curve that ArduCopter uses to fly between waypoints — and minimum snap for a quadcopter, with an explanation of why it's “snap” specifically. The simulation code reproduces the module's plots; the lab is to choose the lookahead from the overshoot and the time to converge onto the line. theory Layers: from waypoints to motors 1. Mission — a list of waypoints and actions the “Missions” module . 2. Path — the geometry between waypoints: segments, turn arcs, splines NAV_SPLINE_WAYPOINT . 3. Trajectory — a path with time: where the vehicle must be at time t, with what velocity and acceleration, within the velocity, acceleration and jerk limits. 4. Guidance / tracking — turns the deviation from the path or trajectory into a command acceleration, bank, velocity for the position controller. Path following doesn't care about time — the point is to be on the line. Trajectory tracking requires being at the point on time — for formations, synchronized filming, cooperative maneuvers. Pure pursuit The vehicle “chases” a point on the path that lies a distance L ahead the lookahead distance . If α is the angle between the velocity vector and the direction to that point, the curvature that brings the vehicle onto it along an arc is κ = 2·sin α / L, and the lateral acceleration is a = V²·κ = 2·V²·sin α / L. - Small L — sharp convergence onto the line, overshoot and sensitivity to position noise. - Large L — smooth but slow, and the route corners get “cut.” - Starting 20 m to the side at 10 m/s simulation below : L = 8 m — overshoot ~3 m; L = 20 m — overshoot ~1 m, within the ±1 m corridor after 35 m of path; L = 45 m — within the corridor only after ~90 m. {{diagram:chart-pure-pursuit Pure pursuit from 20 m to the side at 10 m/s: a short lookahead gives overshoot, a long one gives slow convergence onto the line.}} L1 in ArduPlane and NPFG in PX4 L1 is the same lateral acceleration law in ArduPilot with a gain of 4ζ² instead of 2: a = 4ζ²·V²·sin η / L1; at ζ = 0.707 it's exactly pure pursuit , but the lookahead distance grows with speed so that the convergence dynamics don't depend on speed: L1 = 1/π ·ζ·T·V, where T = NAVL1_PERIOD , ζ = NAVL1_DAMPING , V is the ground speed. - Example: V = 18 m/s, T = 17 s, ζ = 0.75 → L1 ≈ 0.318·0.75·17·18 ≈ 73 m. - Reducing NAVL1_PERIOD shortens L1 — sharper turns, risk of weaving tuning is covered in the “ArduPlane Tuning” module . - The lateral acceleration is turned into bank: tan φ = a / g, limited by ROLL_LIMIT_DEG . In PX4, fixed-wing guidance is done by NPFG nonlinear path following guidance : the same lookahead principle plus explicit handling of wind comparable to the airspeed — when the line can't be held, NPFG picks a feasible heading instead of being “blown” sideways. The period and damping parameters NPFG_PERIOD , NPFG_DAMPING mean the same as in L1. Velocity profiles: trapezoid and S-curve - Trapezoid : acceleration at constant rate, cruise, deceleration. Acceleration changes in a step — the jerk the derivative of acceleration is infinite. For a copter, a step in acceleration = a step in tilt: jerking, swinging of the payload and camera, overshoot. - S-curve jerk-limited : acceleration ramps up with limited jerk. A 50 m move with v ≤ 10 m/s, a ≤ 5 m/s², jerk ≤ 10 m/s³: trapezoid — 7.0 s, S-curve — 7.5 s +0.5 s for the acceleration ramp time , but with no steps. - ArduCopter since 4.1 builds the waypoint path from S-curves: velocity, acceleration and jerk are set by the navigation parameters WPNAV_SPEED , cm/s; WPNAV_ACCEL , cm/s²; WPNAV_JERK , m/s³; in Copter 4.7 — WP_SPD , m/s; WP_ACC , m/s²; WP_JERK , m/s³ , and route corners are rounded with radius WPNAV_RADIUS 4.7 — WP_RADIUS_M . {{diagram:chart-scurve Acceleration during a 50 m move: the trapezoid switches acceleration in a step, the S-curve with limited jerk, at a cost of 0.5 s.}} Minimum snap for a quadcopter A quadcopter is a differentially flat system: knowing the position and heading trajectory, you can compute everything else. Thrust is determined by acceleration, the body angular rate by jerk the third derivative of position , and the motor torques by snap the fourth derivative . That's why the trajectory with the minimum integral of snap squared gives the smoothest motor commands. In practice: 7th-order polynomials per axis between waypoints, continuous up to snap at the joints, with coefficients from a quadratic optimization problem Mellinger, Kumar, 2011 . Such trajectories are built on the companion and sent to the autopilot as position targets together with velocity and acceleration feedforward , otherwise the position controller lags. Feedforward: not just position If the companion sends only position, the controller learns it needs to accelerate only once the error already exists — the vehicle lags in turns. SET_POSITION_TARGET_LOCAL_NED lets you send position, velocity and acceleration at once the type_mask : the position controller only has to catch up with the residual error. practice Step 1. Pure pursuit in simulation The script reproduces the module's plot and computes the overshoot and the distance until entering the ±1 m corridor: python import math def pursuit L, y0=20.0, V=10.0, a_max=8.0, T=15.0, dt=0.02 : """Kinematic vehicle, path = the x axis. Returns overshoot m and distance to settle within 1 m.""" x, y, psi = 0.0, y0, 0.0 overshoot, settle_x = 0.0, None for _ in range int T / dt : dx = math.sqrt L L - y y if abs y < L else 0.0 lookahead point on the path alpha = math.atan2 -y, max dx, 0.5 - psi

It is the black box that answers "why" after any strange flight. This module gives you an order of analysis, from vibration to errors, with the exact mess
headings: Two kinds of logs Messages to start with Order of analysis Tools Worked example: analyzing "a 3 m altitude drop in Loiter" Python for your own metrics (pymavlink) What to log in LOG_BITMASK AI log analyzers: where they help and where they get it wrong Place in the system Script: vibration and clipping from a log Lab A real log How to set up a motor failure in SITL What you should get and what to record
text: summary ArduPilot writes a binary DataFlash log .bin to the SD card with hundreds of message types: attitude, altitude, motors, battery, EKF, errors. It is the black box that answers "why" after any strange flight. This module gives you an order of analysis, from vibration to errors, with the exact message and field names, the limits from the documentation, and a Python script for your own plots. theory Two kinds of logs - DataFlash .bin : on board, high rate, everything. This is the main tool. - Telemetry log .tlog : what the GCS saw over the radio. Lower rate and with gaps, but it exists even if the SD card burned together with the vehicle. The LOG_BITMASK parameter sets what is logged; LOG_DISARMED enables logging before arming useful for analyzing pre-arm problems . Messages to start with - VIBE : vibration, with VibeX , VibeY , VibeZ m/s² and Clip , the accelerometer clipping counter. The general limits in the ArduPilot documentation: below 30 is normal, above 60 almost certainly means altitude and position problems; on large props the goal is stricter, below 15 see ap-heavy . Clipping should be zero. - ATT : DesRoll against Roll , DesPitch against Pitch , that is, how well the vehicle keeps up with the desired attitude. A sharp divergence means a mechanical problem or a lack of thrust. - CTUN : altitude control, with ThO throttle output , ThH hover throttle estimate , DAlt / Alt desired and actual altitude , BAlt baro . - BAT : Volt , Curr , CurrTot , Res the estimated internal resistance . Sag under load and actual consumption. - RCIN : the transmitter channels C1…C14 , that is, what the pilot did. - MODE : mode changes and the reason, Rsn . - ERR : errors, with Subsys and ECode . For example, subsystem 2 radio with code 2 means no receiver frames for longer than RC_FS_TIMEOUT 1 s by default ; 11 is a GPS glitch; 16 is a bad EKF variance; 17 is the EKF failsafe; 29 is vibration compensation. - MSG : text messages, including pre-arm ones. - GPS : NSats , HDop . An HDOP below 1.5 is good, above 2.0 is suspicious; fewer than 12 satellites is poor. - XKF1…XKF4 : the internals of EKF3 per core, estimates and variances XKF4 : SV , SP , SH , SM for velocity, position, height, compass . - POWR : the board Vcc . Fluctuations of more than 0.1–0.15 V hint at power problems. Order of analysis 1. Does the log end abruptly? A log that ends in the air means a power loss or a reboot. 2. Vibration VIBE . Nothing else means anything while it is high. 3. Errors ERR , MSG : what triggered and when. 4. Modes MODE : who changed the mode, the pilot or a failsafe. 5. Control ATT , CTUN : whether the vehicle kept up with the commands. 6. Power BAT , POWR : sags and whether they coincide with events. 7. Navigation GPS , XKF4 : position quality and variances at the moment of the problem. Tools Mission Planner Review a Log , MAVExplorer from the MAVProxy package plots by field name, for example graph ATT.Roll ATT.DesRoll , UAV Log Viewer in the browser. For automation use pymavlink.DFReader , which reads a .bin directly in Python. ArduPilot WebTools firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools, the "ArduPilot WebTools" wiki page is a set of browser tools, and the log is not uploaded anywhere: Hardware Report which sensors and firmware were on board, health, sensor offsets, from a log or a .param file , Filter Review the gyro spectrum from batch sampling or raw IMU logging, with trial application of filters , Filter Tool Bode plots of the filters from a .param file , PID Review step response from a log , MAGFit compass calibration from a log, see ap-sensors . How to choose: "what was on board" is Hardware Report; "what to filter with" is Filter Review; "how the rate loop is tuned" is PID Review. Worked example: analyzing "a 3 m altitude drop in Loiter" 1. VIBE.VibeZ is 12 m/s², Clip is 0 → not vibration. 2. ERR / MSG : nothing. 3. CTUN : DAlt is a constant 20 m, Alt drops to 17 m, and BAlt drops with it → a real drop, not an estimation artifact. 4. CTUN.ThO at that moment is 0.78 0.42 before , BAT.Volt goes 21.1 → 18.9 V, BAT.Curr 60 → 95 A: the throttle hit the ceiling on a sagging battery. 5. RCIN.C3 : the pilot did not touch the throttle; MODE has no changes. Conclusion: a lack of thrust with voltage sag on an old battery BAT.Res of 0.09 Ω is high : replace the battery, set MOT_BAT_VOLT_MIN/MAX for compensation, raise the BATT_LOW_VOLT threshold. The method matters more than the conclusion: every step is a specific field. Python for your own metrics pymavlink python from pymavlink import mavutil import pandas as pd def df_of log, msg : m = mavutil.mavlink_connection log ; rows = while x := m.recv_match type=msg, blocking=False is not None: rows.append x.to_dict return pd.DataFrame rows att = df_of "flight.bin", "ATT" err = att.DesRoll - att.Roll .abs print "roll tracking RMS deg:", err.pow 2 .mean 0.5, "p99:", err.quantile 0.99 vibe = df_of "flight.bin", "VIBE" ; print "VibeZ p95:", vibe.VibeZ.quantile 0.95 , "clips:", vibe.Clip.max mavlogdump.py --types ATT,VIBE --format csv flight.bin is a quick export to CSV with no code; in MAVExplorer : graph ATT.Roll ATT.DesRoll , fft for batch sampling spectra ISBH/ISBD , map for the track. Step-response metrics and spectra are in the "Python for data" module. What to log in LOG_BITMASK The default Copter: LOG_BITMASK = 180222 is enough for analyzing a flight, and PID bit 12, the PIDR/PIDP/PIDY messages with P/I/D/FF per axis is already in it, but at 10 Hz. For tuning add bit 0, Fast Attitude +1: ANG , RATE , and PIDx at the loop rate , and IMU_RAW or batch sampling INS_LOG_BAT_MASK while you set up the filters; the log grows several times over, so turn them off afterwards. LOG_FILE_DSRMROT starts a new file on every disarm; LOG_DISARMED = 1 is for ground measurements noise, GPS ; turn it off afterwards or the SD card fills up. The LOG_BITMASK bits in ArduCopter 4.7.2 ArduCopter/defines.h ; the default is DEFAULT_LOG_BITMASK in ArduCopter/config.h : Bit Value Name in the G

text: summary ArduPilot can run Lua scripts right on the flight controller: add modes, read sensors, react to switches. In a training project the main use is fault injection: deliberately breaking a motor or a sensor in SITL and watching how the drone, and you, cope. This module explains how scripting works, how to bind a script to a transmitter switch, and how to build a set of "chaos scripts", each on its own switch. theory How scripting works - It is enabled with SCR_ENABLE = 1 and a reboot. - Scripts .lua live in APM/scripts on the SD card; in SITL, in the scripts folder of the directory the simulator was started from. - Every script runs in its own sandbox and at low priority: flight code matters more, and nobody promises a script an exact schedule. - SCR_HEAP_SIZE sets the memory for scripts. If it is too small, the 4.7 firmware expands the heap by itself in 20 kB chunks and reports Required SCR_HEAP_SIZE over N ; that message is stored as a scripting error and blocks arming Scripting: Required SCR_HEAP_SIZE over N , so raise SCR_HEAP_SIZE to N plus a margin. If expansion is impossible or is disabled with bit 6 of SCR_DEBUG_OPTS , scripts fail with out of memory . If it is too large, the EKF may fail to initialize. - If one script fails with an error including running out of memory inside its own call , only that script is removed. All scripts stop only if the Lua engine itself has died Lua: Engine Error … , then Scripting: stopped , until scripting is restarted. - Scripting is built only for boards with more than 1 MB of flash AP_Scripting_config.h : F405/F411 boards with 1 MB do not have it; F427/F429 boards with 2 MB Pixhawk 1, Cube Black , F7, and H7 do. The update pattern A script is an update function that does the work and returns itself and a delay in milliseconds until the next call. No infinite loops: the scheduler calls the function again. How it works inside libraries/AP_Scripting/lua_scripts.cpp , Copter-4.7.2 . All scripts live in one thread and one Lua state with the shared SCR_HEAP_SIZE memory. The scheduler keeps a list of scripts ordered by next run time, takes the nearest one, and calls its function in protected mode. After it returns, the scheduler checks that exactly two values came back, a function and a number, and schedules the next run at call start time + delay the next_run_ms = start_time_ms + … line . Three consequences follow: - the delay is a minimum , not a period: in the practice run a script with return update, 100 was called on average every ≈ 113 ms 112.8 ms in the step 6 output; SITL, 5× speedup . For "every 0.1 s" logic that is fine; for time-based measurements use millis , not a call counter; - one call is limited to SCR_VM_I_COUNT virtual machine instructions 10000 by default ; exceed that and you get the message <name .lua exceeded time limit and the script is removed. Split heavy work into portions across calls; - if a call returns one value, more than two, or the wrong types, the script is also removed, with the message did not return a delay / returned bad result count , and that blocks arming; a return with no values is the normal end of a one-shot script: it is removed silently, with no message and without blocking arming. An error in a script: what exactly breaks A runtime error indexing nil , a wrong argument type does not crash the firmware and does not stop other scripts, but it removes that script until a reboot. The consequences are visible in the step 6 run: the GCS receives Lua: ./scripts/bad.lua:2: attempt to index a nil value local 't' , the first time with CRITICAL severity, then repeated every 10 s with DEBUG severity, no more than 10 times the text itself is kept for the arming check . Arming is blocked right after the error; the GCS gets the PreArm: Scripting: … line every 30 s, which is the pre-arm reporting period, so in the run it arrived at 30.3 s. An arming attempt gets a COMMAND_ACK with result 4 FAILED and the text Arm: Scripting: … . This is deliberate: the failed script may have been a safeguard, and you must not fly without it. You can turn the check off with bit 4 of SCR_DEBUG_OPTS , but for a safeguard script that means flying without the safeguard and not knowing it. Scripts are read only at startup. A new or fixed file is picked up after a reboot, on the MAV_CMD_SCRIPTING command 42701 with param1 = 3 SCRIPTING_CMD_STOP_AND_RESTART , with an RCx_OPTION = 316 switch Stop-Restart Scripting , or by toggling SCR_ENABLE 0 → 1; that restarts the whole Lua engine without rebooting the flight controller. The firmware does not check whether the vehicle is armed, so the course rule is to restart scripts only on the ground: during the restart all scripted safeguards are off a course guideline . {{diagram:lua-script-lifecycle A script is rescheduled as long as update returns a function and a delay; any error removes it until a reboot and blocks arming through PreArm: Scripting.}} Your own parameters and log messages A script can create its own parameters, which are visible in the GCS and saved like ordinary ones: param:add_table key, "FLT_", 2 reserves a table with a prefix the key is your own table number, different for every script , and param:add_param key, 1, "DELAY", 5 creates FLT_DELAY with a default of 5. A value changed with param set FLT_DELAY 7 is saved to storage and survives a restart, provided the script creates the table with the same key and prefix; the step 6 run does not test this the FLT_ values were not changed there , so test it yourself: change it, restart SITL without -w , and read it back a conclusion from the documentation and the code . Choose a unique prefix: two scripts with the same prefix cannot coexist. logger:write "FLT", "Alt,Mask", "fi", "m-", "0-", alt, mask writes your own FLT message to the .BIN a name of up to 4 characters, with the format as in AP_Logger : f is float, i is int32 , and you can then see it next to RCOU and CTUN in a log analyzer. Reference: SCR_ parameters ArduPilot 4.7.2 The
