text: summary An eight-motor vehicle with 15–17" props is a different animal from a five-inch quad: slow motors, huge inertia, a low thrust-to-weight ratio, and mistakes that cost an expensive payload. This module covers the coaxial X8 layout using a build on two Tarot Ironman 650 frames, thrust and vibration setup in ArduPilot, and verifying fault tolerance before the first flight with a payload. theory X8 OctaQuad : pros and cons An X8 has four arms with two coaxial motors on each: a top one and a bottom one that spin in opposite directions. - Pros: eight motors in the footprint of a quadcopter; one motor failure does not bring the vehicle down; compact for transport. - Cons: the bottom prop works in the wash of the top one, so a coaxial pair produces less thrust than two separate props. The guideline loss is about 15% it depends on the props and the spacing between them . In ArduPilot this is FRAME_CLASS = 4 OctaQuad and FRAME_TYPE = 1 X . The motor order and directions must follow the OctaQuad X diagram in the documentation exactly. Example build The course's training platform: two Tarot Ironman 650 frames, 8 Tarot 4008 380KV motors, 8 Flycolor 45A ESCs, a 6S Li-Ion pack. Low KV and large props are a bet on efficiency and flight time, not on agility. Li-Ion was chosen because the hover current is moderate. Thrust and the throttle curve - MOT_THST_HOVER is the hover throttle; ArduPilot refines it in flight by itself. Altitude hold depends on it. - MOT_THST_EXPO linearizes thrust. Large props usually need a higher value than five-inch props. - MOT_SPIN_ARM and MOT_SPIN_MIN set the spin when armed and the minimum in flight: the motors must spin reliably but not lift the vehicle. - The motor protocol, MOT_PWM_TYPE : DShot if the ESCs support it, otherwise PWM with an ESC calibration. For starting values Mission Planner has the Initial Tune Parameter helper: it calculates the basic filters and limits from the prop size and the battery voltage. Vibration Large, slow props produce low-frequency vibration that is harder to filter. With vibration the EKF starts to drift: in logs you see it as rising VIBE and accelerometer clipping, in flight as altitude loss or IMU failure messages. Fix it in this order of priority: prop and motor balancing, frame stiffness, flight controller damping, and only then filters. The harmonic notch filter INS_HNTCH_ tracks RPM through throttle or ESC telemetry and is the counterpart of Betaflight's RPM filter. Fault tolerance The main reason to pick an octo is to survive a motor failure. That has to be tested, not assumed: in SITL with the motor failure applet see the Lua module , then on the real vehicle at altitude with no payload. Numbers for the course platform X8, 2×Tarot 650, 4008/4006-class 380KV motors calculated from the MN4006 table, 15×5, 6S Li-Ion, ~6 kg From the "Propeller aerodynamics" module: hover ≈ 880 g of thrust per motor including the coaxial loss, ~3.6–3.9 A per motor, ~30 A for the pack; a 6S 20 Ah Li-Ion → ~32 min of hover; MOT_THST_HOVER ≈ 0.35–0.4, which is a fraction of maximum thrust and not the % throttle on the thrust stand 52% in the table : 880 g out of a ~2230 g maximum at 24 V ≈ 0.39, and with voltage compensation the maximum is taken at MOT_BAT_VOLT_MAX 25.2 V, ~2450 g → ≈ 0.36; MOT_HOVER_LEARN will learn the exact value; MOT_THST_EXPO 0.65–0.7 15" ; INS_GYRO_FILTER ≈ 30 Hz between 40 Hz for 10" and 20 Hz for 20" ; ATC_RAT_ _FLTD 15 half the gyro filter, as in ap-tuning ; starting ATC_RAT_RLL_P/I 0.08, D 0.003, ATC_ANG_RLL_P 4.5; ATC_ACC_R/P_MAX ≈ 500–700 deg/s² before 4.7 this was ATC_ACCEL_R/P_MAX in cdeg/s², 50 000–70 000; slower than a 5" ; PSC_D_ACC_P ≈ 0.1 × hover throttle ≈ 0.036; before 4.7 PSC_ACCZ_P ≈ hover throttle, 0.36: the parameter's scaling in 4.7 is 10 times smaller . Arm wiring is 12 AWG with XT90 connectors see the "Redundancy" module . The fundamental motor frequency in hover is ~60–70 Hz per the MN4006 table, 880 g ≈ 3900 RPM ≈ 65 Hz : use INS_HNTCH_ with ESC telemetry, INS_HNTCH_HMNCS = 7 harmonics 1–3 up to 200 Hz , and an INS_HNTCH_FREQ minimum of 50. Motor failure: what the mixer does AP_MotorsMatrix::output_armed_stabilizing allocates roll and pitch first, then yaw which is given at least MOT_YAW_HEADROOM , and throttle gets what is left after the MOT_YAW_HEADROOM reserve 200 by default, in PWM units reserved for yaw . When one motor of an X8 fails, its coaxial partner and the opposite pair take the load; you see a slight sag and higher RCOU on the neighboring channels. The test: the motor_failure_test.lua applet MOT_STOP_BITMASK , a Scripting1 switch , first in SITL -f octa-quad , then in the field at 20+ m with no payload and a spotter. Log every flight; VIBE < 15 is the working goal on large props, and 30 the general limit in the documentation, see ap-logs means go and find the cause. The compass on a large vehicle You cannot calibrate a 6 kg X8 by rotating it in every direction, and 30 A for the pack next to the flight controller makes the internal compass useless. text: summary A wing flies differently: lift depends on speed squared, it has a stall speed, the center of gravity decides whether it is stable at all, and the autopilot does not control "altitude" and "speed" separately but energy TECS . This module gives the calculations you need to do before the first launch lift and wing loading, stall speed and cruise speed, center of gravity position and static margin and ties them to the parameters of ArduPlane ARSPD_ , TECS_ , AIRSPEED_CRUISE/MIN/MAX , TRIM_ and INAV nav_fw_ , fw_ . theory Lift L = ½ · ρ · V² · S · C_L: air density, speed squared, wing area, and the lift coefficient which depends on the angle of attack α and the airfoil; it grows roughly linearly up to the critical angle of 10–15°, and then comes the stall . In level flight L = m·g. - Wing loading W/S g/dm² or N/m² : the higher it is, the faster you have to fly and the worse the aircraft is in thermals and on landing. FPV wings of 1–1.5 m: 30–60 g/dm²; mappers: 40–80; foam trainers: 20–35. - Stall speed : V_s = √ 2·m·g / ρ·S·C_Lmax . C_Lmax for simple airfoils without high-lift devices is 1.0–1.3. Example: m = 1.8 kg, S = 0.35 m², C_Lmax = 1.1 → V_s = √ 2·1.8·9.81/ 1.225·0.35·1.1 ≈ 8.7 m/s. In a turn at bank angle φ the lift has to be higher: V_s φ = V_s/√cos φ, so at 60° of bank the stall comes 41% faster. - Cruise : 1.3–1.6 V_s for economy the best L/D is usually near 1.3 V_s , 2 V_s and above for speed or wind. The minimum safe airspeed in the autopilot is ≥ 1.2–1.3 V_s. - Drag D = ½ρV²·S·C_D; C_D = C_D0 + k·C_L² parasite plus induced . At low speed induced drag dominates it grows as 1/V² , at high speed parasite drag does V² . Minimum power is at a speed slightly below minimum drag: hence "fly slower than you think" for endurance. Center of gravity and stability A wing is stable in pitch if the center of gravity CG is ahead of the neutral point the aerodynamic center of the whole aircraft . The static margin = x_np − x_cg /MAC mean aerodynamic chord ; 5–15% is normal; 0 is neutral it flies but does not recover by itself ; negative is unstable the autopilot cannot save it once the surfaces saturate . For a flying wing no tailplane the neutral point is ≈ 25% MAC the quarter chord with corrections for sweep; the CG goes at 15–20% MAC. Online CG calculators for wings from span, root and tip chord, and sweep do exactly this calculation. An aft CG gives sharp, twitchy responses and a tendency to spin; a forward CG gives a heavy nose, a high landing speed, and a need for a lot of up elevator. Ground check: balance it on your fingers or on stands at the calculated point with the battery and the whole payload. Flight check, the "dive test": from level flight put it into a shallow dive and release the sticks: the plane pulls out to level by itself with a forward CG it does so sharply; with an aft CG it keeps diving or tucks under . Controls and modes Elevons on a wing mix elevator and ailerons; a conventional layout has separate surfaces. The autopilot stabilizes roll and pitch FBWA , holds altitude and heading FBWB , CRUISE , flies waypoints AUTO , returns RTL , and lands the AUTOLAND mode, added in ArduPlane 4.7: a landing without a mission along the takeoff direction, with the approach point placed behind along the takeoff heading and offset by AUTOLAND_DIR_OFF ; in a mission, NAV_LAND . Without an airspeed sensor the autopilot estimates airspeed from GPS and wind, which is worse in wind; with a pitot tube ARSPD_TYPE , calibration with ARSPD_AUTOCAL , ARSPD_RATIO it is accurate. Which speed the autopilot measures: IAS, EAS, TAS A pitot tube measures dynamic pressure q = ½·ρ·V². ArduPilot converts it to airspeed as V = √ ARSPD_RATIO ·Δp AP_Airspeed.cpp:697–708 ; ARSPD_RATIO defaults to 2 and is refined by calibration . With a correct calibration this is equivalent airspeed, EAS: the speed that would give the same pressure at the sea-level density of 1.225 kg/m³. Lift depends on q, not on true airspeed: L = q·S·C_L. So the stall speed in EAS is the same at any altitude, while true airspeed TAS grows as √ ρ₀/ρ . ArduPlane sets all AIRSPEED_ parameters in EAS, and TECS converts them to TAS by multiplying by EAS2TAS AP_TECS.cpp:420 . The module's example V_s = 8.53 m/s EAS in the standard atmosphere: at 1500 m ρ = 1.058, EAS2TAS = 1.076, V_s in TAS is 9.18 m/s; at 3000 m ρ = 0.909, EAS2TAS = 1.161, V_s in TAS is 9.90 m/s. The conclusion: you do not need to change AIRSPEED_MIN for a mountain field, but at the same EAS the ground speed at touchdown is higher, so the ground roll is longer. Ground speed = TAS ± wind, so you cannot see a stall in GPS speed: with an 8 m/s tailwind a wing with a V_s of 8.5 stalls at a ground speed of 16.5 m/s. Do you need an airspeed sensor For an FPV wing in FBWA, no; for AUTO, RTL, and especially VTOL transitions, it is highly desirable. Without a sensor TECS sets the speed weighting to 0 AP_TECS.cpp:995–996 : pitch holds altitude only, and throttle starts from TRIM_THROTTLE and rises linearly with pitch to THR_MAX at the maximum climb pitch and falls to THR_MIN in a dive , plus the turn compensation TECS_RLL2THR AP_TECS.cpp:930–958 , almost as in INAV. So TRIM_THROTTLE must be the throttle of the real cruise, otherwise the airspeed is uncontrolled in wind and in turns. Synthetic airspeed TECS_SYNAIRSPEED , 0 by default exists, but the firmware itself warns in the parameter description about a poor estimate when the wind is inaccurate. Connecting a sensor comes with two traps. ARSPD_USE defaults to 0: the airspeed is logged but not used for control; for control you need 1. ARSPD_AUTOCAL is for a single calibration flight: the firmware saves a new ARSPD_RATIO about once a minute at most, if it has changed by more than 5%, and leaving it enabled is not recommended. Tube installation and calibration are covered in the tuning module. {{lesson:ap-plane-tuning Where to mount the pitot tube, how to calibrate ARSPD_ , and how to set up TECS from test flights.}} TECS: energ

text: summary A plane on ArduPlane 4.7, from a blank flight controller to the first flight, in a 17-step order: output functions for a conventional tail, elevons and a V-tail, the MIXING_GAIN mixer, two checks of control surface direction the stick in MANUAL and the response to tilting in FBWA , trimming, modes, throttle, the ARSPD_ airspeed sensor and flying without one, the airspeed and angle limits, the fixed-wing failsafe with tables of actions by current mode, arming, hand, bungee and runway takeoffs, and a plan for the first flight. The module is theoretical: the practice consists of calculations and reading parameter files with no flight controller and no SITL. The lab: surface pulse widths of three planes through the mixer, the RC failsafe timeline in five scenarios, an ARSPD_RATIO correction, and three mistakes in a parameter file. theory How setting up a plane differs from a copter The common steps firmware, ports, receiver, radio calibration, accelerometer, compass, battery monitor, OSD are done as in ap-setup-scratch , except that the firmware file is arduplane_with_bl.hex and then arduplane.apj . Everything that has to do with the air is different: - the frame has no motors: each output is assigned a control surface function, and the direction of each servo is checked twice; - a plane has a stall speed, so you set airspeed and bank limits, and the failsafe does not "hover in place" but circles and returns; - in automatic modes TECS controls the throttle, with an airspeed sensor or without one; - takeoff is a throw or a ground roll, and the motor can start by itself. {{lesson:ap-ahrs-choice How a plane estimates wind and airspeed, when ArduPlane falls back to DCM, and why without an airspeed sensor the position error without GPS grows several times over.}} Version: ArduPlane 4.7, checked against the 4.7.2 source ArduPlane/version.h : "ArduPlane V4.7.2" . The differences between 4.7 and 4.6.3 in this topic: FS_SHORT_TIMEOUT was removed; ARMING_SKIPCHK replaces ARMING_CHECK opposite meaning, table in ap-intro ; the new AUTOLAND mode number 26 and the "AUTOLAND" values in the failsafe actions; the new TKOFF_THR_IDLE . The airspeed and angle names with explicit units appeared earlier, in 4.5; the old names are given once below, because old guides and other people's parameter files are full of them. Which firmware to take for a first wing: INAV is simpler and runs on cheap FPV flight controllers inav-setup-wing ; ArduPlane is for when you need missions, detailed logs, an airspeed sensor, a QuadPlane. In both cases the first aircraft is a 900–1100 mm foam flying wing or a high-wing pusher: they forgive a rough landing. text: summary A QuadPlane is not "a copter bolted onto a plane". It is the single ArduPlane firmware, which creates a second set of controllers from the ArduCopter libraries when Q_ENABLE = 1 . What confuses a newcomer is not the complexity but the addresses: an "it oscillates" symptom can live in Q_A_RAT_ , in RLL_RATE_ , or in the transition, and each of those three fixes is useless or dangerous when applied to the wrong half. This module splits the aircraft into the plane half, the copter half, and what only a VTOL has: a large table of subsystems, a map of parameter prefixes with the parameter counts in 4.7.2 and where to find them in Mission Planner and QGC, the "hidden until enabled" rule, the tuning order, and above all a table and a tree for "which side do I tune this symptom from". The practice uses ArduPlane 4.7.2 SITL the quadplane model and the source: what the firmware assigns to the outputs by itself after Q_ENABLE , sorting eight symptoms by side, and finding errors in a parameter file. theory One firmware, two sets of controllers A QuadPlane exists only in ArduPlane: there is no separate "VTOL firmware". While Q_ENABLE = 0 it is the ordinary plane from ap-setup-plane . With Q_ENABLE = 1 the QuadPlane::setup function ArduPlane/quadplane.cpp creates the copter objects in memory once, and they are the same classes that run in ArduCopter: Object in ArduPlane Prefix in Plane The same in ArduCopter 4.7 What it does --- --- --- --- AP_MotorsMulticopter Q_M_ 25 parameters MOT_ 24 the lift motor mixer, the thrust curve, hover throttle AC_AttitudeControl_TS derived from AC_AttitudeControl_Multi Q_A_ 61 ATC_ 61 hover angles and rates AC_PosControl Q_P_ 32 PSC_ 32 hover position and altitude AC_WPNav Q_WP_ 10 WP_ 12 waypoints in a VTOL mode AC_Loiter Q_LOIT_ 7 LOIT_ 7 position hold in QLOITER AC_WeatherVane Q_WVANE_ 9 WVANE_ turning the nose into the wind QAutoTune Q_AUTOTUNE_ 4 AUTOTUNE_ hover autotune The numbers are how many parameters have that prefix in the ArduPlane 4.7.2 definitions and in ArduCopter 4.7.2 SITL the count is step 2 of the practice; the ArduCopter definitions themselves list a few more, MOT_ 25 and ATC_ 66, because of helicopter and other frame-specific entries . The matches 61 = 61 and 32 = 32 are no accident: it is the same code with a Q_ prefix. So everything you know about copter tuning from ap-tuning carries over to QuadPlane hover one to one, allowing for the names. The plane half does not go anywhere: RLL_RATE_ , PTCH_RATE_ , RLL2SRV_ / PTCH2SRV_ the fixed-wing angle and rate loops , TECS_ height and speed through throttle and pitch , NAVL1_ track; ArduPlane 4.7 has only L1, and NPFG belongs to PX4 , AIRSPEED_ , and ARSPD_ . Shared by both halves: state estimation AHRS and EKF , GPS, the barometer, the battery monitor, the receiver, SERVOn_FUNCTION , the mission, logging, and the failsafe framework. Who is in control at any moment is decided by the mode QuadPlane::update : - Q modes QSTABILIZE, QHOVER, QLOITER, QLAND, QRTL, QACRO, QAUTOTUNE : the copter set drives the lift motors. The control surfaces are not dead: QSTABILIZE, QHOVER, QLOITER and through it QLAND , QRTL, and QAUTOTUNE also call the fixed-wing stabilize_roll / stabilize_pitch , and QACRO calls the fixed-wing ACRO rate loop mode_q .cpp , so the ailerons move in hover, which is normal and not an error. - MANUAL, ACRO, TRAINING : the transition is forced to "complete" and the copter set does not run: on a 4+1 the lift motors are shut down SHUT_DOWN , on a tilt-rotor the tilting motors go forward and work as cruise motors on stick throttle Tiltrotor::continuous_update , and the fixed ones are stopped. The exception is a tailsitter, whose motors are the forward thrust. - The other fixed-wing modes FBWA, FBWB, CRUISE, AUTO, RTL, LOITER, GUIDED, TAKEOFF… : the plane set is in control, and the copter set comes on only in the transition and for assistance Q-assist . The details per mode are in ap-vtol-modes . The boundary between the halves is the transition. While the airspeed is low, the lift motors hold the aircraft; once the airspeed is reached, their throttle ramps linearly to zero over Q_TRANSITION_MS 5000 ms , and the copter throttle mix factor goes down with it. {{diagram:vtol-anatomy-controllers One set of sensors and one state estimate feed two sets of controllers: the Q modes drive the lift motors, the fixed-wing modes drive the surfaces and the cruise throttle, and the transition and Q-assist are the only place where both run.}} The attitude and airspeed estimate is shared by both halves, and it matters more in the transition than anywhere else: without an airspeed sensor the end of the transition is decided by the AHRS synthetic airspeed, which is ground speed minus the wind estimate. While the lift motors are running, ArduPlane clears the "fly forward" flag update_fly_forward , EKF3 stops estimating wind, and AP_AHRS::_airspeed_EAS takes the estimate from DCM using GPS: in the log XKF2.VWN/VWE = 0, and the wind and airspeed are in DCM.VWN/VWE and DCM.SAs the analysis and a run are in ap-vtol-modes . Without GPS there is no such estimate at all, and a transition in a fixed-wing mode never completes. {{lesson:ap-ahrs-choice Why a QuadPlane without an airspeed sensor completes the transition on the EKF3 synthetic airspeed from GPS and wind, and what is left of that logic on DCM without GPS.}} The big table: plane, copter, and VTOL only Subsystem On a plane ArduPlane On a copter the Q side VTOL only --- --- --- --- State estimation shared: AHRS, EKF3 or DCM the same without an airspeed sensor the transition waits for the AHRS synthetic airspeed from GPS from DCM during the transition Rate loop RLL_RATE_ , PTCH_RATE_ , YAW_RATE_ → surfaces Q_A_RAT_RLL_ , Q_A_RAT_PIT_ , Q_A_RAT_YAW_ → motors both run in the transition, and the fixed-wing integrators are reset until the airspeed is reached Angle loop RLL2SRV_TCONST , PTCH2SRV_TCONST , the limits ROLL_LIMIT_DEG , PTCH_LIM_ _DEG Q_A_ANG_RLL_P , Q_A_

summary: A tilt-rotor VTOL takes off like a multirotor and flies like a plane, tilting its motors on the way. It is one of the most complex ArduPilot platforms: a copter mixer, a plane mixer, and a tilt mechanism all live in one aircraft. This module is written at the level of an experienced pilot and walks
headings: QuadPlane tiltrotor configuration Output functions The main trap: a motor on a servo channel Case: HeeWing T1 Ranger Transitions: the parameters that decide safety Worked example: the first transition Which VTOL to choose: 4+1, tilt-rotor, tailsitter Place in the system Bring-up protocol (props off!) text: summary A tilt-rotor VTOL takes off like a multirotor and flies like a plane, tilting its motors on the way. It is one of the most complex ArduPilot platforms: a copter mixer, a plane mixer, and a tilt mechanism all live in one aircraft. This module is written at the level of an experienced pilot and walks through a real bring-up from scratch of a HeeWing T1 Ranger tricopter wing: output assignment, an incident with a motor that spun up by itself, the limits of an F405, and a transition check on the ground. Which half of a QuadPlane is plane and which is copter, and which side to tune a symptom from, is in ap-vtol-anatomy ; all modes, transitions, Q-assist, and the VTOL failsafes from the source and SITL are in ap-vtol-modes . theory QuadPlane tiltrotor configuration - Q_ENABLE = 1 enables the VTOL side in ArduPlane. Reboot after changing Q_ENABLE , Q_FRAME_CLASS , or Q_FRAME_TYPE . - Q_FRAME_CLASS = 7 is Tri. - Q_TILT_ENABLE = 1 enables tiltrotor functionality the default is 0 ; while it is 0, the other Q_TILT_ parameters are hidden and have no effect. - Q_TILT_TYPE : 0 Continuous ordinary tilt servos , 1 Binary only "up" or "forward" , 2 VectoredYaw the left and right motors tilt independently and provide yaw in hover , 3 Bicopter. - Q_TILT_MASK selects the motors that tilt bit 0 is motor 1 . A tricopter with two tilting front motors uses 3. - Q_TILT_MAX is the tilt angle held while waiting for transition airspeed the default of 45° suits most aircraft . - Q_TILT_RATE_UP / Q_TILT_RATE_DN are the tilt rates in deg/s defaults 40 and 0; Q_TILT_RATE_DN = 0 means use Q_TILT_RATE_UP ; a sensible start is about 15 deg/s. - Q_TILT_YAW_ANGLE is for vectored yaw: how far the motors can tilt back past 90°. Output functions Every output gets a role through SERVOn_FUNCTION : - tricopter motors: Motor1 33 , Motor2 34 , Motor4 36 ; - tilt servos for vectored yaw: TiltMotorFrontLeft 75 , TiltMotorFrontRight 76 ; for an ordinary tilt, TiltMotorsFront 41 ; - surfaces: Elevator 19 , FlaperonLeft 24 , FlaperonRight 25 . Check the function numbers against the documentation for your version: the table grows, but old numbers do not change. The main trap: a motor on a servo channel The outputs of a flight controller are grouped by timer. Within a group all outputs share one protocol and rate: you cannot have DShot for a motor and 50 Hz for a servo on the same timer. If the physical wiring does not match the assigned functions, one of two things happens: a servo receives "throttle" and drives against its stop, or an ESC receives a servo signal and the motor spins up with no command. Case: HeeWing T1 Ranger Configuration: the stock HeeWing F405, a tilt tricopter with two tilting front motors and a fixed rear one. Project requirements: arming only from a transmitter switch, and GPS not required for arming or basic flight. The incident. During a channel check one motor unexpectedly spun up to maximum. The cause was a category mismatch: motor functions had been assigned to outputs physically wired to servos, and the other way around. The project was stopped until everything had been rechecked. How it was sorted out. With the props off, by hand, one output at a time, an "output → device" map was built and checked against the list of 8 devices: 1. elevator; 2. left flaperon; 3. right flaperon; 4. left nacelle tilt servo; 5. right nacelle tilt servo; 6. left tilting motor; 7. right tilting motor; 8. fixed rear motor. After that the functions were reassigned on all 8 channels, and the motors and servos were placed in timer groups with compatible protocols. Hardware limits. An F405 has no Lua scripting, and some features are cut. This build has no compass at all, and the GPS was unstable at the time of setup. So EKF3 is disabled and the DCM attitude estimate is used: the aircraft arms and flies without GPS or a compass, but with no altitude or position hold. The mode set for that decision: MANUAL, FBWA, ACRO, QSTABILIZE for takeoff, QLAND for landing. It is a deliberate trade-off for specific hardware, not a default recommendation. {{lesson:ap-ahrs-choice What a QuadPlane loses on DCM without GPS or a compass: there is no synthetic airspeed, so a transition in a fixed-wing mode without an airspeed sensor never completes.}} Transitions: the parameters that decide safety - Forward VTOL → fixed wing : in the fixed-wing modes with Q_ENABLE the aircraft is held by the VTOL motors until the airspeed from the sensor or, without one, the AHRS synthetic estimate of "ground speed minus wind", which needs GPS; without GPS there is no estimate exceeds the larger of AIRSPEED_MIN the minimum fixed-wing airspeed; before 4.5 it was ARSPD_FBW_MIN and Q_ASSIST_SPEED ; after that the VTOL motor throttle ramps to zero over Q_TRANSITION_MS 5000 ms , which is the time after the threshold and not a timeout; the timeout is Q_TRANS_FAIL ap-vtol-modes . The tilt motors rotate forward at Q_TILT_RATE_DN 0 means Q_TILT_RATE_UP is used, 40 deg/s . An AIRSPEED_MIN that is too low relative to V_s see the "Wing aerodynamics" module means a stall right after the transition. - Back fixed wing → VTOL : on a switch to the Q modes the VTOL motors start immediately; Q_TRANS_DECEL m/s² sets the deceleration; Q_ASSIST_SPEED m/s is the speed below which the VTOL motors assist automatically in fixed-wing modes, as protection against a stall; Q_ASSIST_ANGLE and Q_ASSIST_ALT give assistance at a large attitude error or at low altitude. - VTOL controllers : Q_A_RAT_ VTOL rate PIDs , Q_A_ANG_ , Q_P_ position; in 4.7 these are Q_P_NE_ and Q_P_D_ instead of the 4.6 Q_P_POSXY/VELXY/POSZ/VELZ/ACCZ_ , Q_M_THST_HOVER , Q_M_SPIN_MIN/ARM , Q_WVANE_ weathervaning into the wind . QAUTOTUNE is for the VTOL side; TECS, RLL_RATE_ / PTCH_RATE_ the fixed-wing rate PIDs , and RLL2SRV_ / PTCH2SRV_ TCONST , RMAX are for the wing. - Landing : Q_LAND_FINAL_SPD m/s , Q_LAND_FINAL_ALT ; with Q_RTL_MODE 1–3 an RTL changes to QRTL near home and lands vertically, or RTL_AUTOLAND takes it i

text: summary A QuadPlane has two sets of modes: the Q modes, in which the vehicle is a copter, and the fixed-wing modes, in which it is a plane that the VTOL motors help at low speed. Everything dangerous happens at the boundary, in the transitions, in Q-assist and in the stages of a VTOL landing, and the firmware does almost all of it by itself, on thresholds that you set. Working from the ArduPlane 4.7.2 source, this module goes through each Q mode and its Copter counterpart, what the VTOL motors do in each fixed-wing mode, the forward transition through the states AIRSPEED_WAIT → TIMER → DONE , the back transition and deceleration, every Q-assist trigger, the mission commands NAV_VTOL_TAKEOFF , NAV_VTOL_LAND , DO_VTOL_TRANSITION and the landing stages from the fixed-wing approach to touchdown, QRTL versus RTL, and the VTOL failsafes. The practice consists of real SITL QuadPlane 4.7.2 runs: a forward transition in 9.2 s and 159 m, cyclic Q-assist in CRUISE, a back transition into QLOITER with a 19 m climb, a mission with an airbrake stage, an airspeed sensor failure in the middle of a transition, and an RTL that changes to QRTL. theory Two groups of modes and the boundary between them Who flies the vehicle in each mode is covered in ap-vtol-anatomy ; one consequence matters here. On a QuadPlane, flipping the mode switch does not change the "character" of the vehicle as it does on a copter; it selects which half is responsible for lift . In a Q mode the VTOL motors provide it at any speed. In a fixed-wing mode the wing does, and the VTOL motors run only when the wing lacks airspeed a transition or when something has gone wrong Q-assist . In MANUAL, ACRO and TRAINING the VTOL motors of a 4+1 are always off: these modes have no safety net. The ArduPlane 4.7.2 mode numbers mode.h that you need for FLTMODE1…6 and in the MODE log message: MANUAL 0, FBWA 5, FBWB 6, CRUISE 7, AUTO 10, RTL 11, LOITER 12, TAKEOFF 13, GUIDED 15, QSTABILIZE 17, QHOVER 18, QLOITER 19, QLAND 20, QRTL 21, QAUTOTUNE 22, QACRO 23, LOITER_ALT_QLAND 25. The Q modes and their Copter counterparts Q mode ArduCopter counterpart Throttle stick Position Arming in the mode Notes --- --- --- --- --- --- QSTABILIZE 17 STABILIZE direct motor throttle, curve Q_THROTTLE_EXPO 0.2 no yes stick angles are limited by Q_A_ANGLE_MAX and the fixed-wing ROLL_LIMIT_DEG , PTCH_LIM_ _DEG ; the takeoff mode when GPS is poor QHOVER 18 ALT_HOLD vertical speed: up Q_PILOT_SPD_UP 2.5 m/s , down Q_PILOT_SPD_DN 0 uses the up value , acceleration Q_PILOT_ACCEL_Z 2.5 m/s² no yes after arming, the motors wait for throttle above 10 % throttle_wait ; at a tilt roll and pitch combined beyond twice Q_A_ANGLE_MAX it hands control to the fixed-wing controller for recovery QLOITER 19 LOITER as QHOVER yes, Q_LOIT_ , Q_P_NE_ yes in wind, with Q_FWD_THR_USE the forward motor helps hold position and the nose does not pitch down beyond Q_FWD_PIT_LIM 3° QLAND 20 LAND none except bit 15 of Q_OPTIONS yes no descent at Q_WP_SPD_DN 1.5 m/s down to Q_LAND_FINAL_ALT + 6 m, then a smooth slowdown to Q_LAND_FINAL_SPD 0.5 m/s below Q_LAND_FINAL_ALT 6 m QRTL 21 RTL none yes no Q_RTL_ALT 15 m , Q_RTL_ALT_MIN 10 m ; far from home it flies as a plane and lands vertically QAUTOTUNE 22 AUTOTUNE as QHOVER per the Copter AutoTune library not verified for Plane yes tunes Q_A_RAT_ , Q_A_ANG_ , on the axes in Q_AUTOTUNE_AXES ; not present in every build QACRO 23 ACRO direct throttle no yes Q_ACRO_RLL_RATE 360, Q_ACRO_PIT_RATE 180, Q_ACRO_YAW_RATE 90 deg/s LOITER_ALT_QLAND 25 — none yes — a fixed-wing LOITER descending to Q_RTL_ALT , then QLAND; battery failsafe action 6 Arming in QLAND and QRTL is not allowed _pre_arm_checks returns false . Bit 18 of Q_OPTIONS allows arming only in VTOL modes and in AUTO when the current nav command is NAV_VTOL_TAKEOFF : a guard against taking off in FBWA at full forward-motor throttle. In all Q modes the control surfaces work together with the motors: in QACRO through the fixed-wing ACRO rate controller mode_acro.run , in the others through stabilize_roll / stabilize_pitch . Fixed-wing modes on a VTOL: what the VTOL motors do Mode VTOL motors When they run Trap --- --- --- --- MANUAL, ACRO, TRAINING 4+1: off; tiltrotor: the tilting motors point forward and work as forward motors never neither transition nor assistance; switching from a hover to MANUAL means a fall FBWA, STABILIZE, AUTOTUNE transition and Q-assist airspeed below the threshold, attitude outside the limits, low altitude a transition in FBWA near the ground with the throttle below half: no acceleration, you hang on the VTOL motors FBWB, CRUISE transition and Q-assist the same the throttle stick sets the airspeed: at zero it is AIRSPEED_MIN ; if Q_ASSIST_SPEED is higher, assistance cycles on and off step 2 of the practice AUTO per the mission commands NAV_VTOL_ are VTOL throughout; waypoints are fixed-wing with a transition NAV_TAKEOFF and NAV_LAND on a QuadPlane execute as VTOL unless bits 1 and 2 of Q_OPTIONS are set RTL transition and Q-assist; near home, QRTL per Q_RTL_MODE see the QRTL section with Q_RTL_MODE = 0 the plane loiters over home and does not land LOITER, CIRCLE, TAKEOFF, GUIDED transition and Q-assist the same Q_GUIDED_MODE = 1 switches to VTOL flight and hovers when the GUIDED destination is reached Assistance in fixed-wing modes is possible at all only when starting the VTOL motors is safe: auto throttle is not suppressed, or the stick throttle is above zero, or the vehicle is flying VTOL_Assist::should_assist . On the ground with the throttle at zero they do not start by themselves. The forward transition step by step A forward transition begins when you or the mission switch from a Q mode to a fixed-wing mode other than MANUAL, ACRO or TRAINING. The logic is SLT_Transition::update in quadplane.cpp , with three states that are also logged as QTUN.Trn : 1. AIRSPEED_WAIT Trn = 0 . The message "Transition started airspeed X". The VTOL motors hold altitude as in a hover hold_hov

It means seven steps in the right order: parameters for the size of the vehicle → first stable flight → evaluation → harmonic notch on the motor noise → manual or QuikTune roll/pitch tune → AutoTune axis by axis → input shaping for feel. This module wa
headings: Step 1. Parameters before the first flight Steps 2–3. First flight and evaluation Step 4. Harmonic notch Step 5. Manual roll/pitch tune or QuikTune Step 6. AutoTune Step 7. Input shaping What to look at afterwards Place in the system Step 1. SITL Step 2. Notch in the field Step 3. QuikTune or manual Step 4. AutoTune in the field What you should get and what to record
text: summary Tuning ArduCopter does not mean "run AutoTune". It means seven steps in the right order: parameters for the size of the vehicle → first stable flight → evaluation → harmonic notch on the motor noise → manual or QuikTune roll/pitch tune → AutoTune axis by axis → input shaping for feel. This module walks through them with the parameters and a log check for each ATT , RATE , VIBE , spectra from batch sampling or raw IMU logging , explains what AutoTune does internally and why it needs the noise to be below a threshold , and shows how to set up a notch that tracks ESC telemetry or throttle. The lab runs in SITL and in the field. theory Step 1. Parameters before the first flight The starting values depend on the prop size the "Setting the Aircraft Up for Tuning" page : INS_GYRO_FILTER 80 Hz for 5", 40 for 10", 20 for 20" and larger , ATC_RAT_ _FLTD/FLTE/FLTT the D, error and target filters of the rate controllers; for D use half the gyro filter , MOT_THST_EXPO 0.65 for 10", 0.55 for 5" , MOT_SPIN_ARM/MIN , MOT_THST_HOVER it is learned with MOT_HOVER_LEARN = 2 , ATC_THR_MIX_MAN , PSC_D_ACC_P/I before 4.7 these were PSC_ACCZ_P/I ; the scaling in 4.7 is 10 times smaller: 0.1 and 0.2 of the hover throttle instead of 1 and 2 matched to the hover throttle, ATC_INPUT_TC stick feel . For large or heavy vehicles start with reduced PID gains ATC_RAT_RLL_P/I 0.05–0.1 instead of 0.135, D 0.002–0.004 . Steps 2–3. First flight and evaluation Fly Stabilize or AltHold at minimum weight with a full battery the "most agile configuration" . In the log: RATE.RDes vs RATE.R desired vs achieved rate should track without oscillation; compare ATT.DesRoll with ATT.Roll ; VIBE.VibeX/Y/Z < 15–30 m/s² 30 is the general limit in the documentation, 15 is the goal for large props , Clip = 0; CTUN.ThO hover throttle; a learned MOT_THST_HOVER of 0.2–0.5 . If it oscillates right away, cut P and D by 30–50% and do not fly on. Step 4. Harmonic notch Motor noise gets into the D term and heats the motors; a low-pass filter with a low cutoff adds delay see the "Signals and spectra" module . A notch removes only the motor frequencies: 1. Find the frequency : batch sampling INS_LOG_BAT_MASK = 1 selects the first IMU; INS_LOG_BAT_OPT : 0 logs raw pre-filter data, 2 samples post-filtering, 4 samples pre- and post-filter at 1 kHz or, on an H7 with 4.5+, raw IMU logging INS_RAW_LOG_OPT ; fly a hover with gentle maneuvers; view the spectrum in MAVExplorer, the Filter Review Tool, or your own Python. 2. Enable it : INS_HNTCH_ENABLE = 1 , then reboot. 3. Mode INS_HNTCH_MODE : 3 is ESC Telemetry the best one: it tracks every motor and needs ESC telemetry or BLHeli bidirectional DShot ; 1 is Throttle INS_HNTCH_REF = hover throttle, INS_HNTCH_FREQ is the frequency in hover, and the center frequency is rescaled by √ throttle/ref ; change REF when the payload changes ; 4 is Dynamic FFT in flight F7/H7; only one of INS_HNTCH and INS_HNTC2 may use mode 4 ; 0 is Fixed. 4. Bandwidth and depth : INS_HNTCH_BW about half of FREQ, in throttle mode and with ESC telemetry alike; much narrower, ≈ FREQ / number of motors, with Multi-Source , INS_HNTCH_ATT 40 dB is typical , INS_HNTCH_HMNCS harmonics bitmask: 3 = 1st and 2nd, 7 = 1–3; "three harmonics are usually safe" , INS_HNTCH_OPTS bit 1 is Multi-Source, one notch per motor; bit 2 updates at loop rate with bidirectional DShot; bit 5 uses the minimum frequency on RPM source failure; do not combine bits 0 and 4 double and triple notch , because with both set only the double notch is applied . 5. Verify : take a log with post-filter batch sampling INS_LOG_BAT_OPT = 2 ; the motor peaks should drop by 20+ dB; the second set, INS_HNTC2_ , is for a frame resonance fixed frequency . Step 5. Manual roll/pitch tune or QuikTune This is mandatory before AutoTune: AutoTune starts from the current gains and aborts when the signal is noisy. QuikTune the Lua applet VTOL-quicktune.lua , enabled with QUIK_ENABLE , with the switch set by RCx_OPTION = 300 or QUIK_RC_FUNC raises P and D until the first oscillation and backs them off by QUIK_GAIN_MARGIN %. By hand: raise D until it oscillates → −30%, raise P until it oscillates → −30%, I = P on roll and pitch. Step 6. AutoTune What it does: in AltHold or Loiter it commands a series of short twitches on one axis, measures the response, and looks for the highest rate D, then rate P I = P on roll and pitch, I = 0.1·P on yaw , then angle P that still give the target overshoot. Parameters: AUTOTUNE_AXES bitmask: 1 roll, 2 pitch, 4 yaw, 8 yaw D; on large vehicles tune one axis per flight , AUTOTUNE_AGGR 0.05–0.10, default 0.075 since 4.6 0.1 in 4.5 and earlier ; higher is more aggressive and more tolerant of noise, lower gives a softer tune , AUTOTUNE_MIN_D the lower bound for D, so it does not go to zero on a noisy vehicle , AUTOTUNE_GMBK new in 4.7, default 0.25: the tuned P and D gains are reduced by this fraction for extra stability margin, so the result on 4.7 is softer than on 4.6; 0 applies no reduction . Conditions: wind < 3 m/s, 20+ m of altitude and clear space, a full battery, the notch already set up. The result is saved only if you disarm with the switch on or in AUTOTUNE mode the message is "AutoTune: Saved gains for …" ; RCx_OPTION = 180 lets you switch between the original and the tuned gains to compare them. The ATUN summary and ATDE detail of every twitch log messages show where it stopped; the GCS progress messages, such as "AutoTune: Roll Rate D Up 25%", are in the log too. A sign of success: the final ATC_RAT_ _D values are above AUTOTUNE_MIN_D × 1 − AUTOTUNE_GMBK 0.000375 by default , because the saved D is already reduced by GMBK. Step 7. Input shaping ATC_INPUT_TC 0.15 is smooth → 0.05 is sharp; the Copter 4.7 default is 0.10, in 4.6 it was 0.15 , ATC_ACC_R/P/Y_MAX deg/s²; before 4.7 these were ATC_ACCEL_R/P/Y_MAX in cdeg/s² , ATC_RATE_R/P/Y_MAX , ATC_ANG_ _P AutoTune sets them; you can soften them . None of this is about stability. It is about feel

text: summary The transmitter channels above the fourth are, in ArduPilot, switches and knobs with an assignable role: RCx_OPTION binds one of more than 130 auxiliary functions to a channel, and the TUNE parameter turns a knob into a control for a single gain right in flight. Using the ArduCopter and ArduPlane 4.7.2 source, this module works out how the firmware reads a switch the 1200 and 1800 µs thresholds, the 200 ms debounce, what happens at power-up , which function numbers a copter and a plane actually need, which of them bring the vehicle down, how the value from a knob is calculated, and why it is not saved. After the module you can lay out switches without dangerous combinations and tune one gain within a narrow range. The lab is a calculation exercise with no hardware and no simulator: a timeline of switch events, knob values, and finding three errors in a layout. theory Two kinds of channels: mode and aux - The mode channel is set by FLTMODE_CH 5 by default on Copter . It is a 6-position switch: boundaries at 1231, 1361, 1491, 1621, and 1750 µs divide the channel into positions 1–6, and the position selects FLTMODE1 … FLTMODE6 . - An aux channel is any channel 1–16 with an RCx_OPTION other than 0. It is read as a three-position switch: LOW, MIDDLE, HIGH. The exceptions: 94 VTX power is read as a six-position switch, and 212–217 gimbal axes and 219 , 220 tuning knobs take the whole channel value. One channel cannot be both: arming is refused with PreArm: Mode channel and RC5_OPTION conflict . One function on two channels gives PreArm: Duplicate Aux Switch Options AP_Arming.cpp , lines 826–831 . On the transmitter side a switch is a channel mix on a switch source: EdgeTX outputs 988, 1500, and 2012 µs for the three positions, and a knob outputs the whole range link-edgetx . How the firmware reads a switch The read_aux_all task runs 10 times per second and only with a healthy RC link: on Copter the switches are not read at all during a radio failsafe. What Value in 4.7.2 Where in the source --- --- --- A pulse counts as invalid ≤ 800 or ≥ 2200 µs RC_MIN_LIMIT_PWM , RC_MAX_LIMIT_PWM LOW < 1200 µs AUX_SWITCH_PWM_TRIGGER_LOW HIGH 1800 µs AUX_SWITCH_PWM_TRIGGER_HIGH MIDDLE 1200…1800 µs inclusive read_3pos_switch Debounce time 200 ms SWITCH_DEBOUNCE_TIME_MS Aux polling rate 10 Hz Copter and Plane Copter.cpp:161 , Plane.cpp:134 Mode channel polling rate 250 Hz on Copter, 7 Hz on Plane Copter.cpp:151 , Plane.cpp:72 Reversing a switch RCx_REVERSED = 1 and bit 7 128 in RC_OPTIONS ALLOW_SWITCH_REV There is no hysteresis: the "dead band" between the thresholds is the MIDDLE position. A channel sitting at 1795 µs is in the middle for the firmware, not high; a two-position switch with incomplete travel 1250…1750 never triggers. A function is called on a change of position, not continuously. The new position has to hold for 200 ms: on the tick where it is first seen, the time is remembered; the function is called on the first tick where at least 200 ms have passed. With polling every 100 ms, 200–300 ms pass between the flick and the action. If the position changes again during that time a three-position switch passing through the middle, a 180 ms glitch , the count starts over and the intermediate position is not executed. Every call is logged as an AUXF message: function the number , pos 0 LOW, 1 MIDDLE, 2 HIGH , source 0 INIT, 1 RC, 2 button, 3 MAVLink, 4 mission, 5 scripting , index , result . For some functions a line such as RC7: MotorEStop HIGH arrives in Messages. The same function can be triggered without a transmitter by the MAV_CMD_DO_AUX_FUNCTION command from a ground station and by the DO_AUX_FUNCTION mission item. {{diagram:ap-aux-eval-flow A switch is executed on a change of position after 200 ms; on the first receiver frame every function is executed except four: arming 153, 154, 165 and parachute release 22 only remember the position.}} What happens at power-up There are two stages. 1. Initialization init_aux_all , before flight . The position is read once; if the receiver has not delivered a frame yet, it counts as LOW. For "state" functions their action is called with the INIT source: 3 , 13 , 14 , 31 , 32 , 39 , 84 , 11 , 21 , 23 , 46 , 65 , 165 , 166–169 , 219 , 220 , and others. For "event" functions modes, 153 , 81 , relays, 9 , scripting, 94 nothing is done at this stage. 2. The first receiver frame. The remembered position of a channel is initially "none" −1 , so any current position counts as a change and is executed after 200 ms, LOW included. A relay switch in HIGH turns the relay on 200 ms after the link appears, and a 4 switch in HIGH tries to engage RTL. The exception is the four functions for which init_position_on_first_radio_read returns true : 153 ArmDisarm, 154 ArmDisarm with AirMode, 165 Arm/E-Stop, and 22 parachute release. For them the first position read is only remembered. If you switch on the transmitter with the arming switch in HIGH, nothing happens; to arm, you have to lower the switch and raise it again. Functions by purpose The numbers are checked against enum class AUX_FUNC in RC_Channel.h of the Copter-4.7.2 tag. "C" means available on Copter, "P" on Plane. Group Number: function --- --- Copter modes HIGH engages; otherwise return to the mode channel, if that mode is still active 4 RTL, 16 AUTO, 18 LAND, 33 BRAKE, 42 SmartRTL, 52 ACRO, 55 GUIDED, 56 LOITER, 68 STABILIZE, 69 POSHOLD, 70 ALTHOLD, 72 CIRCLE, 99 AUTO RTL, 2 FLIP, 37 THROW, 151 TURTLE Plane modes 4 RTL, 16 AUTO, 51 MANUAL, 52 ACRO, 55 GUIDED, 56 LOITER, 72 CIRCLE, 77 TAKEOFF, 92 FBWA, 98 TRAINING, 108 QRTL, 150 CRUISE, 170 QSTABILIZE, 183 AUTOLAND new in 4.7 , 96 re-read the mode channel; the modes themselves, their numbers, and a plane's FLTMODE_CH are in ap-setup-plane Arming and motors C, P 153 ArmDisarm, 154 ArmDisarm with AirMode, 81 Disarm, 165 Arm/E-Stop, 31 Motor Emergency Stop, 32 Motor Interlock C Waypoints and trims 5 Save Trim C , 7 Save WP C , 24 reset the mission to the start,

text: summary A camera, a gimbal, a gripper and a winch use the same flight controller outputs as the motors, but mistakes here look different: the vehicle flies normally, yet there are no pictures, the gimbal points at the sky or the payload is lying in the parking area. Working from ArduCopter 4.7.2, this module follows a command from a switch, a mission or MAVLink to a servo, a relay or a port: the CAM1_TYPE and MNT1_TYPE types, the trigger and shutter feedback parameters, the conversion of a servo gimbal angle to microseconds, the GRIP_ gripper, the WINCH_ winch, and the moment DO commands execute in a mission. After the module you choose the camera trigger method, the gimbal type and the release mechanism for specific hardware, and you know which output will move on the ground while the safety switch is on. The lab is a calculation exercise with no hardware and no simulator: a gimbal servo pulse, the trigger distance and the number of pictures in a survey, the georeferencing error, an output plan with a release, and three mistakes in a parameter file. theory What is in the module and in what order to read it The module answers "where to plug it in and what to write", not "how the protocol works": the manager and device roles in MAVLink Gimbal v2 and gimbal control from code are covered in payload-gimbal , and the overlap and GSD calculation in per-mapping . First comes the common path of a command, then three blocks: the camera, the gimbal, and payload release gripper, winch, relay . Each block has a parameter table followed by a selection table with a rule. Read the safety section before the lab: in the lab you work out which outputs stay live while the safety switch blocks the rest. Output functions, timer groups, GPIO and relays are not repeated here, they are in ap-outputs ; switch thresholds and behavior are in ap-aux-tune . The path of a command: source → library → output Neither a switch nor a mission writes to an output directly. The source calls a library AP_Camera , AP_Mount , AP_Gripper , AP_Winch , the library picks a driver from the TYPE parameter, and the driver is what moves the servo, toggles the relay or sends a frame to the port. {{diagram:ap-payload-paths Three payload paths: the command arrives at the library, the TYPE parameter selects the driver, and what leaves is a servo pulse, a relay level, UART or MAVLink. Camera type 4 depends on the gimbal driver.}} Three consequences follow. First, the driver is created at boot, so a change of CAM1_TYPE , MNT1_TYPE , GRIP_ENABLE , GRIP_TYPE or WINCH_TYPE needs a reboot. Second, while TYPE is 0, a command is accepted and silently does nothing. Third, one output can have several sources: a gripper is released by a switch, by a mission and by a failsafe, and each of them has to be accounted for. There are two cameras and two gimbals: CAM1_ , CAM2_ , MNT1_ , MNT2_ . There is one gripper and one winch. The camera: CAM1_TYPE and the trigger parameters CAM1_TYPE Driver What it does on a trigger --- --- --- 0 None nothing 1 Servo puts the CAM1_SERVO_ON pulse on the output with function 10 CameraTrigger for the time CAM1_DURATION , then CAM1_SERVO_OFF 2 Relay turns on the relay with RELAYn_FUNCTION = 4 Camera for the time CAM1_DURATION 3 GoPro in Solo Gimbal only in builds with the 3DR Solo gimbal 4 Mount passes the trigger to the gimbal driver Siyi, Topotek, Viewpro, Xacti 5 MAVLink sends MAV_CMD_DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL with the fifth parameter set to 1 to all components 6 MAVLinkCamV2 sends MAV_CMD_IMAGE_START_CAPTURE to the camera component type MAV_TYPE_CAMERA , compid 100 for the first camera ; only on boards with more than 1 MB of flash 7 Scripting increments a request counter, and a Lua script takes the picture ap-lua 8 RunCam control of a RunCam camera over UART SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 26 ; this driver does not take a photo on a trigger, its trigger function returns failure Parameter Default Range Meaning --- --- --- --- CAM1_DURATION 0.1 s 0–5 how long the servo or relay is held; counted in updates of 20 ms CAM1_SERVO_ON / CAM1_SERVO_OFF 1300 / 1100 µs 1000–2000 the PWM value when the shutter is activated and deactivated; written as is, SERVOn_MIN/MAX are not involved CAM1_RELAY_ON 1 0 / 1 whether the relay goes Low or High when it triggers CAM1_TRIGG_DIST 0 m 0–1000 a trigger every N meters; 0 is off CAM1_INTRVAL_MIN 0 s 0–10 the minimum time between photos CAM1_FEEDBAK_PIN −1 −1…127 the shutter feedback pin; −1 and 0 are off; needs a reboot CAM1_FEEDBAK_POL 1 0 / 1 0 TriggerLow: the pin goes low on trigger; headings: Order is what matters most Preparation before the first tune Airspeed sensor: installation and calibration AUTOTUNE of roll and pitch TECS from test flights L1 navigation Automatic landing PX4: the same stages Place in the system Step 1. SITL plane Step 2. AUTOTUNE Step 3. TECS Step 4. L1 Step 5. Landing (SITL)
text: summary "Wing aerodynamics" explained why a plane flies and what TECS is; "Tuning ArduPilot" explained how a copter is tuned. This module gives the order for tuning a plane in ArduPlane, which decides whether AUTO holds altitude and track or oscillates: preparation control surfaces, center of gravity, airspeeds , AUTOTUNE of roll and pitch in the air, TECS from test flights with concrete numbers, the L1 navigation controller on a rectangular mission, and automatic landing with a flare. The PX4 equivalents are at the end: the names differ including NPFG navigation , but the logic is the same. theory Order is what matters most Inner loops before outer loops: roll and pitch surfaces → angles → TECS height and speed through throttle and pitch → navigation track through roll → landing. A poorly tuned pitch loop looks like "TECS oscillates in altitude", and a poor roll loop looks like "L1 weaves". If you start with the outer loop, you are fixing a symptom. Preparation before the first tune - Surfaces and reversals. In FBWA, tilt the plane by hand: the ailerons and elevator must oppose the tilt. In MANUAL the sticks must move the surfaces the correct way. A mistake here is a crash on the very first launch in a stabilized mode. Everything in plane setup up to this point output functions, the elevon and V-tail mixers, both direction checks, the airspeed sensor, failsafe, and the first flight is covered in ap-setup-plane . - Center of gravity from the calculation in "Wing aerodynamics"; slightly nose-heavy is safer. - Airspeeds Plane 4.5+, m/s : AIRSPEED_MIN ≥ ~1.2 times the stall speed , AIRSPEED_CRUISE , AIRSPEED_MAX ; SCALING_SPEED is the typical cruise speed; set it before tuning and leave it alone afterwards, because all PID values are scaled from it. - Surface limits. RLL2SRV_RMAX and PTCH2SRV_RMAX_UP/DN are the maximum rates the plane can actually achieve; RLL_RATE_SMAX and PTCH_RATE_SMAX are set for the servo speed. - Trimming. In FBWA in level flight use SERVO_AUTO_TRIM = 1 or manual trims; PTCH_TRIM_DEG is the pitch angle offset for level flight. - A rally point and tested failsafes. Airspeed sensor: installation and calibration Whether you need one, and the full ARSPD_ table, are in ap-setup-plane . In short: on a QuadPlane it is strongly recommended, because the transition completes at an airspeed of max AIRSPEED_MIN , Q_ASSIST_SPEED , and without a sensor that is a synthetic estimate from GPS and the wind estimate: a wind error shifts the moment of completion, and without GPS the transition never completes at all Q_TRANSITION_MS is the time after the threshold is reached, not a timeout; see ap-vtol-modes . It is useful in wind, for a slow wing, and for automatic landing; the ArduPilot documentation does not recommend one on a first plane because it is extra setup. If you fit one, do it before AUTOTUNE and TECS, because SCALING_SPEED , AIRSPEED_MIN , and the TECS limits are then based on its readings. Step 1. Type and range. A digital I²C sensor MS4525DO, MS5525, SDP3x, DLVR, ASP5033, AUAV or DroneCAN; analog sensors, according to the ArduPilot documentation, are almost out of production and hold their zero worse when the temperature changes. Choose the range from the highest airspeed you will see a dive, a head-on gust : Δp_max = V_max² / ARSPD_RATIO . Take a sensor limit with a margin of ≥ 1.5 × Δp_max an estimate , not a rule from the documentation . With ARSPD_RATIO = 2 : Sensor Limit, Pa Speed limit, m/s --- --- --- DLVR 5″ H₂O 1245 49.9 DLVR 10″ H₂O 2491 70.6 MS4525DO ±1 psi 6895 117 Example: V_max = 30 m/s → 450 Pa, 675 Pa with the margin 2.7″ H₂O , so a DLVR 5″ is enough; an MS4525 also works, but it runs in the bottom 10% of its scale. Step 2. Location. The static holes on the side of the tube must be at least 1 cm ahead of the nose. If the prop is in the nose, put the tube on the wing, at least 30 cm from the fuselage, outside the prop wash. On a QuadPlane the same rule applies to the lift props an estimate : in hover the tube sees their wash as airspeed . Shield the sensor from light. Step 3. Zero. The firmware takes the zero offset at power-up, so cover the tube loosely against the wind. To get a warning when the calibration was done with the tube uncovered, set ARSPD_OFF_PCNT Plane, % of AIRSPEED_MIN , 0 disables . The documentation says the DLVR needs no zero calibration, but in the 4.7.2 source only SDP3x and NMEA skip it set_use_zero_offset , so cover a DLVR too. Step 4. Ratio. Fly two opposite legs at the same throttle along the wind: the average ground speed GPS.Spd ≈ the airspeed. Example: 24 and 16 m/s → 20 m/s; ARSP.Airspeed shows 18 → ARSPD_RATIO = 2 × 20/18 ² = 2.47. That is within the 1.5–3.0 range; outside it you have a leak in the tubing or a bad location. The other way is ARSPD_AUTOCAL = 1 and flying circles with frequent heading changes on a straight route the estimate does not converge , then setting it back to 0. Up to 500 m above sea level ARSP.Airspeed differs from true airspeed by less than 3% ISA: √ 1.225/1.167 = 1.024 , so you can ignore the correction. Step 5. Log check. ARSP.U = 1 otherwise ARSPD_USE = 0 and TECS does not see the sensor , ARSP.H = 1 for the whole flight, ARSP.Offset barely changes from one power-up to the next, and on opposite legs the average ARSP.Airspeed matches the average GPS.Spd within ±1 m/s an estimate . AUTOTUNE of roll and pitch - Enabling: AUTOTUNE mode on the flight mode switch, or a switch with RCx_OPTION = 107 in FBWA/FBWB/CRUISE. - AUTOTUNE_LEVEL is the target aggressiveness: the default is 6 75 deg/s . Use 2–3 for slow, large wings and gliders; go above 7 only after tuning at a lower level. - AUTOTUNE_AXES selects the axes to tune; yaw only with YAW_RATE_ENABLE = 1 . - Maneuvers: sharp stick reversals with a short pause at full deflection, one axis at a time; learning happens only while the demanded rate is high enough. Without telemetry do at least 20 reversals per axis, preferably more, until the completion message

text: summary ArduPilot has seven independent failsafes radio, GCS, battery, EKF, dead reckoning, vibration, geofence plus the pre-arm checks, and each has an action, a threshold, and exceptions. This module treats them as a system: what exactly triggers, in what order, and how they interact for example, a low battery during an RTL caused by radio loss , how to run an FMEA of your platform failure → how to detect it → what to do → how to test it , and how to test every scenario in SITL before flying . The lab is an FMEA table with 10+ failures and a test log. theory ArduCopter failsafe map Failsafe Trigger Parameters Actions values --- --- --- --- Radio RC the receiver stops sending frames no pulses or the throttle channel is below FS_THR_VALUE for 3 consecutive reads PWM, 910–1100 FS_THR_ENABLE , FS_THR_VALUE 0 Disabled, 1 RTL, 3 Land, 4 SmartRTL or RTL, 5 SmartRTL or Land, 6 DO_LAND_START or RTL, 7 Brake or Land GCS no heartbeat from the ground station for FS_GCS_TIMEOUT 5 s by default FS_GCS_ENABLE , FS_GCS_TIMEOUT 0 Disabled, 1 RTL, 3 SmartRTL or RTL, 4 SmartRTL or Land, 5 Land, 6 DO_LAND_START or RTL, 7 Brake or Land the numbering differs from FS_THR_ENABLE ; relevant for Guided and telemetry control Low battery voltage < BATT_LOW_VOLT with the BATT_LOW_TIMER timeout or remaining capacity < BATT_LOW_MAH BATT_FS_LOW_ACT 0 Warn only, 1 Land, 2 RTL, 3 SmartRTL or RTL, 4 SmartRTL or Land, 5 Terminate, 6 DO_LAND_START or RTL, 7 Brake or Land Critical battery voltage < BATT_CRT_VOLT the same BATT_LOW_TIMER timeout or remaining capacity < BATT_CRT_MAH BATT_FS_CRT_ACT the same values; the default is 0, warn only, so you set the action explicitly usually 1 Land EKF variances FS_EKF_THRESH FS_EKF_ACTION 0 Report only added in 4.7 , 1 Land if the mode requires position, 2 AltHold, 3 Land always Dead reckoning the EKF has lost its position and velocity sources and relies only on wind estimates the message is Dead Reckoning started FS_DR_ENABLE default 2 , FS_DR_TIMEOUT default 30 s, 0–120 0 Disabled, 1 Land, 2 RTL, 3 SmartRTL or RTL, 4 SmartRTL or Land, 6 DO_LAND_START or RTL; only in modes that require position; after FS_DR_TIMEOUT dead reckoning ends and the EKF failsafe triggers Vibration EKF vertical velocity and position innovations both positive with high velocity variance for 1 s a symptom of clipping/aliasing FS_VIBE_ENABLE modified altitude estimation and control ERR FAILSAFE_VIBE, "Vibration compensation ON" Geofence leaving the circle, polygon, or altitude limit FENCE_ENABLE , FENCE_TYPE , FENCE_ACTION , FENCE_ALT_MAX , FENCE_RADIUS , FENCE_MARGIN 0 Report Only, 1 RTL or Land, 2 Always Land, 3 SmartRTL or RTL or Land, 4 Brake or Land, 5 SmartRTL or Land Options what to do instead of the default action FS_OPTIONS bitmask continue if in Auto on RC failsafe bit 0 , continue if in Auto on GCS failsafe bit 1 , continue if in Guided on RC failsafe bit 2 , continue if landing bit 3 , continue if in pilot controlled modes on GCS failsafe bit 4 Then there are the pre-arm checks ARMING_SKIPCHK is a bitmask of checks to skip , 0 means all enabled; before 4.7 it was ARMING_CHECK , a mask of enabled checks, 1 meaning all : compass, GPS, INS, parameters, voltage, geofence. Disable them one at a time and only when you understand why. The table of bits and of seventeen common PreArm: messages with cause and fix is in ap-setup-scratch "Why it won't arm" . ArduPlane is built differently: RC loss is caught by THR_FAILSAFE with the THR_FS_VALUE threshold, and the action is split into a short one FS_SHORT_ACTN and a long one FS_LONG_ACTN after FS_LONG_TIMEOUT ; the action table and the timeline are in ap-setup-plane "Fixed-wing failsafe" . The rest of this module is Copter only. How they interact - Priority: a critical battery overrides everything Land ; a low battery during an RTL caused by radio loss takes the battery action usually also RTL, but it can be Land; choose it deliberately . - RTL requires position: on an EKF failsafe the action degrades to Land or AltHold. - RTL first climbs to RTL_ALT_M meters; before 4.7 it was RTL_ALT in centimeters; the minimum altitude above home for the return, 15 m by default; if the vehicle is already higher, it returns at its current altitude . Near home the climb is limited by the RTL_CONE_SLOPE cone default 3 : h_ret = min max RTL_ALT_M , h , max 3·d, h , where d is the distance to home, so directly above home there is no climb worked through in ap-sitl . It then flies home, loiters for RTL_LOIT_TIME , and lands RTL_ALT_FINAL_M = 0 ; before 4.7, RTL_ALT_FINAL in cm . Over obstacles higher than RTL_ALT_M that means a collision; the altitude fence is one more limiter. - SmartRTL returns along the path already flown a point memory, SRTL_POINTS . It is good in forest and between buildings, but the memory must not fill up. - Geofence: a breach triggers the action; FENCE_MARGIN is the distance the automatic modes keep from the fence a warning on entering it needs FENCE_OPTIONS bit 2 ; the pre-arm check does not let you arm outside the fence. - The FS_OPTIONS "continue if in Auto on RC failsafe" bit is for BVLOS missions flown under an authorization; without one, leave it off. Geofence: types, enabling, polygons FENCE_TYPE is a bitmask, 7 by default: bit 0 1 is the max altitude FENCE_ALT_MAX 100 m , bit 1 2 is the circle FENCE_RADIUS centered on home 300 m, 30–10000 , bit 2 4 is the inclusion/exclusion circles and polygons uploaded from the ground station, bit 3 8 is the min altitude FENCE_ALT_MIN default −10 m, range −100…100 . The floor is not in the default, and even when configured it is enabled only once the vehicle has climbed above FENCE_ALT_MIN ; otherwise you could not take off. There are three ways to enable it; choose one: - FENCE_ENABLE = 1 : the fence is enabled from boot, including on the ground before arming; - FENCE_AUTOENABLE = 3 AutoEnableOnlyWhenArmed : it is enabled on arming and disabled on disarming; for a copter this is the practical value. In ArduCopt

title: Companion: why, and where the boundary is
summary: A flight controller does one job: it keeps the vehicle in the air and executes simple commands, thousands of times a second, and it is never allowed to hang. Anything heavier (computer vision, planning, network links, your own mission logic) lives on the companion computer. This module draws the lin
headings: Who is responsible for what How they talk The "advise, don't control" rule Typical platforms Protocols and roles MAVLink routing Latency, and what to hand to the companion Power, heat, failure Three typical architectures Where it fits in the system Picking a platform for the job Architecture checklist before a project Observer code and what you should see Lab
text: summary A flight controller does one job: it keeps the vehicle in the air and executes simple commands, thousands of times a second, and it is never allowed to hang. Anything heavier computer vision, planning, network links, your own mission logic lives on the companion computer. This module draws the line between the two, walks through typical setups from an ESP32 to a Jetson, and explains the core rule: the companion advises, the FC decides. theory Who is responsible for what - Flight controller FC : stabilization, navigation, failsafes, the mixer. Hard real time, minimal latency, proven code. It has to keep flying even if the companion hangs, reboots, or burns out. - Companion: everything else. Vision, neural networks, map processing, complex behaviors, the internet, cloud logging, the operator interface. {{diagram:companion-system Companion computer and flight controller: the FC keeps the vehicle in the air; the companion sees, plans, and talks to the network.}} The line is drawn by reliability: whatever the vehicle would crash without goes on the FC; whatever it would merely return home without goes on the companion. How they talk Over MAVLink, on a UART an FC telemetry port or over a network. The companion is a separate component in the same MAVLink system. It can: - read telemetry and parameters; - switch the vehicle to GUIDED and send position or velocity targets; - upload and start missions; - receive status text messages and vehicle state. What it does not do: drive the motors directly or replace stabilization. Even under offboard control the FC enforces its own limits and failsafes. The "advise, don't control" rule The companion proposes "fly to point X at speed Y". The FC checks the geofence, the battery, and EKF health, then executes the request or rejects it. If the companion stops sending commands, the FC falls back to safe behavior on its own after a timeout: in Copter, velocity, acceleration, and angle targets last GUID_TIMEOUT 3 s , after which velocity targets are zeroed the vehicle brakes and holds and angle targets level out with zero climb rate no position hold, so it drifts with the wind . That is why the GCS failsafe and the GUIDED timeouts are part of the design, not an obstacle. Typical platforms - ESP32 / ESP32-S3: a microcontroller with Wi-Fi and BLE. Telemetry to a phone, a MAVLink bridge over Wi-Fi, sensors, status indication, small scripted behaviors. No Linux, but instant boot and well under a watt. - Raspberry Pi: Linux, Python, a camera. MAVLink routing, video streaming, mission scripts, logs. The standard first companion. - Jetson / Orange Pi with an NPU: when you need neural networks in real time. Protocols and roles ArduPilot expects MAVLink 2 with SERIALx_PROTOCOL = 2 ; PX4 on its companion port speaks the same MAVLink or uXRCE-DDS for ROS 2. A companion in the classic sense is rare with Betaflight/INAV: they have MSP, and an onboard computer is usually there only for video and telemetry. MAVLink routing One FC port, several consumers a GCS over 4G, a script on the companion, a logger : you need a router. Use mavlink-router C++, a systemd service, a config file with UART/UDP/TCP endpoints or mavproxy.py --master=/dev/ttyAMA0 --out=udp:gcs-ip:14550 --out=udp:127.0.0.1:14551 : every client gets a copy of the stream, and commands flow back to the FC. Run the companion UART at 921600 baud SERIALx_BAUD = 921 ; otherwise MAVn_ streams SRn_ before ArduPilot 4.7 at 10–50 Hz saturate the port. Streams are requested by the companion REQUEST_DATA_STREAM / MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL ; they are not on by default. {{diagram:mavlink-routing A typical onboard MAVLink routing layout with a companion computer.}} Latency, and what to hand to the companion The "companion → FC → response" loop: 1–5 ms on the UART, plus FC processing, plus the velocity loop dynamics of 0.3–1 s. That is fine for "fly to a point" and for target following the "Target tracking and target-based control" module , but not for stabilization. The companion must not: drive the motors, replace the EKF other than feeding ExternalNav as a source , or bypass failsafes. The companion may: send GUIDED/Offboard targets, run missions, set parameters, provide ExternalNav or optical flow as a source, handle the camera and video, push logs to the cloud, run the operator interface. Power, heat, failure A Raspberry Pi 4/5 draws 0.6–3 A at 5 V depending on load and USB peripherals, so size the BEC for 5 A the Pi 5 PSU spec : give it a dedicated 5 V/5 A BEC, not an FC pad the "Connecting Peripherals" module . A Jetson Orin Nano draws 7–15 W up to 25 W in the Super configuration and its devkit barrel jack takes 9–20 V it ships with a 19 V supply ; 5 V/4 A is the old 2019 Jetson Nano figures from the comp-jetson-nano module . A heatsink and airflow are mandatory: once it throttles on temperature, latency grows unpredictably. A companion failure a hang, a reboot, a broken UART link is something the FC must survive: GUIDED timeouts, a GCS failsafe with a deliberately chosen action, and a pilot with a companion-free mode on a switch. Test it by pulling the UART in SITL or on the bench. Three typical architectures 1. Telemetry and bridge: an ESP32 running bridge firmware MAVLink over Wi-Fi/BLE to a phone, DroneBridge-style . It decides nothing; it only relays. 2. Pi + camera + scripts: a Raspberry Pi 4/5, mavlink-router, Python mission scripts, a video stream to the GCS, optical flow/rangefinder over MAVLink. The standard for learning and prototypes. 3. Jetson + ROS 2: detection/VIO on the GPU, PX4 over uXRCE-DDS or ArduPilot over MAVROS/AP_DDS, nodes with safeguards the "Target tracking and target-based control" module . For serious autonomy. Starter code for 2 and 3 is in examples/ in the course repository. Where it fits in the system - Takes in: telemetry and parameters from the flight controller over a UART in MAVLink comp-mavlink ; 5 V power from a dedicated BEC, not from an FC pad el-peripherals . - Puts out: G

text: summary MAVLink is the language the flight controller speaks with the ground control station, the companion computer, telemetry radios, and your scripts. Everything you did in SITL through pymavlink was MAVLink. This module takes the protocol apart far enough for you to write your own clients: the packet structure, system and component, the heartbeat, acknowledged commands, parameters, telemetry streams. Two tools to choose from: pymavlink low level, everything visible and MAVSDK a high-level API . theory The packet MAVLink 2 is a binary protocol over UART, UDP, or TCP. A packet holds the start marker 0xFD , the length, flags, a sequence number, system_id , component_id , a three-byte message ID, the payload, and a CRC. The checksum includes a "seed" derived from the message definition, so both sides must use the same definitions dialect . Messages are defined in XML: common.xml holds the common set, ardupilotmega.xml the ArduPilot extensions. Libraries for C, Python, and other languages are generated from the XML. System and component system_id is the vehicle 1 by default ; component_id is what is inside it: the autopilot 1 , a camera, a gimbal, an onboard computer. A GCS is usually system 255. Commands are addressed to a system + component pair; an onboard computer is a separate component of the same system. Heartbeat HEARTBEAT ID 0 is sent once a second by every participant: vehicle type, autopilot, mode, arming state. No heartbeat means no connection, which is why every client starts with wait_heartbeat . A missing GCS heartbeat for longer than the timeout is the GCS failsafe. Core messages - Telemetry from the vehicle: SYS_STATUS 1 , ATTITUDE 30 , GLOBAL_POSITION_INT 33 , RC_CHANNELS 65 , BATTERY_STATUS 147 , STATUSTEXT 253, text messages, pre-arm ones included . - Commands: COMMAND_LONG 76 with a MAV_CMD_ code and seven parameters; the reply is COMMAND_ACK 77 with the result. Example codes: MAV_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM 400 , MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF 22 , MAV_CMD_DO_SET_MODE 176 . - Stream rates: MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL 511 requests a specific message at a given interval; MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE 512 requests it once. - Parameters: PARAM_REQUEST_READ 20 → PARAM_VALUE 22 ; writing is PARAM_SET 23 , confirmed by the same PARAM_VALUE . - GUIDED control: SET_POSITION_TARGET_LOCAL_NED 84 and SET_POSITION_TARGET_GLOBAL_INT 86 set a position or velocity target; the basis of offboard control from a companion. - Missions: MISSION_COUNT 44 , MISSION_ITEM_INT 73 , MISSION_REQUEST_INT 51; when receiving a mission, ArduPilot 4.7 sends MISSION_REQUEST 40 and accepts MISSION_ITEM_INT in reply , MISSION_ACK 47 : the exchange from the missions module. The acknowledgment rule A command without a COMMAND_ACK check is hope, not control. MAV_RESULT_ACCEPTED 0 means "accepted"; any other code is a rejection, and the reason usually arrives in a STATUSTEXT . pymavlink vs MAVSDK - pymavlink is a thin wrapper over the protocol: you see every message, which suits learning, troubleshooting, and anything non-standard. The code is verbose. - MAVSDK C++, Python offers high-level actions: arm , takeoff , goto_location , telemetry subscriptions. Faster for writing applications, less visibility into what happens inside. Historically closer to PX4, but it works with ArduPilot. A MAVLink 2 frame byte by byte FD len incompat_flags compat_flags seq sysid compid msgid 3 payload len crc 2 signature 13 . Bit 0 of incompat_flags means the packet is signed; the signature is the first 48 bits of a SHA-256 hash of secret key + header + payload + CRC + link_id + timestamp , not an HMAC it protects against spoofed commands over an open radio link; you set the key in Mission Planner/QGC, and it reaches the autopilot in a SETUP_SIGNING message . The checksum is CRC-16/MCRF4XX over the frame plus the message's CRC_EXTRA byte from the XML : mismatched dialects mean "silence". The payload is shortened by truncating trailing zero bytes which is why len is smaller than the struct size . Parameters in PARAM_VALUE are always a float 32 bit : ArduPilot converts integers to float with a C cast, PX4 encodes them byte-wise; the value type is in param_type MAV_PARAM_TYPE , an easy thing to trip over in pymavlink. {{diagram:mavlink2-frame A MAVLink 2 frame: header, system and component IDs, payload, CRC with CRC_EXTRA, optional signature.}} Telemetry streams: who sets the rate ArduPilot sends streams according to the MAVn_ parameters of each MAVLink channel MAV3_EXTRA1 for ATTITUDE, MAV3_POSITION for GLOBAL_POSITION_INT, MAV3_RAW_SENS for RAW_IMU… , in Hz; before 4.7 these were SRn_ , numbered from zero SR2_EXTRA1 is today's MAV3_EXTRA1 , and SRn_ values are not carried over on upgrade. The modern way is MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL 511 from the client: an interval in µs −1 disables, 0 restores the default . PX4 uses MAV_x_MODE profiles Normal/Onboard/OSD… . A 921600-baud port carries ~90 KB/s: ATTITUDE at 50 Hz + position GLOBAL_POSITION_INT at 10 Hz + RAW_IMU at 50 Hz, in MAVLink 2 frames of 40, 40, and 41 bytes payloads of 28, 28, and 29 bytes + 12 bytes of header and CRC, unsigned , comes to ~4.5 KB/s, with room to spare; at 57600 ~5.8 KB/s at 10 bits per byte the same set would take ~77 % of the port, and a telemetry radio's air link is also shared half-duplex and cut down by ECC, which is why anything above 5–10 Hz saturates it. Worked example: a reliable command python def cmd m, command, params, retries=3, timeout=1.0 : """Send COMMAND_LONG and wait for a matching ACK; retry on timeout; raise on rejection.""" p = list params + 0 7 - len params for _ in range retries : m.mav.command_long_send m.target_system, m.target_component, command, 0, p t0 = time.time while time.time - t0 < timeout: ack = m.recv_match type="COMMAND_ACK", blocking=True, timeout=timeout if ack and ack.command == command: if ack.result == mavutil.mavlink.MAV_RESULT_ACCEPTED: return True if ack.result == mavutil.mavlink.MAV_RESULT_IN_PROGRESS: continue raise RuntimeErr
