text: summary INAV has four ways to change a setting without a laptop: adjustments on a switch adjrange , the Adjustments tab , stick commands while disarmed, profile switching control, battery, mixer and the CMS menu in the OSD. This module goes through them from the INAV 9.1.0 source: the adjrange format and its limits 20 ranges, 4 slots , all 61 function numbers with their step and limits, the step timing immediately and then once every 500 ms , where the value is written and which actions save it to EEPROM — including the unexpected ones. Separately — the stick command table from rc_controls.c and how all of this differs from Betaflight. The practice is a calculation exercise: decode and write adjrange lines, work out the value after a series of holds, decide what survives a reboot and find three errors in a config. theory Four mechanisms and which of them work in the air This module is about changing INAV settings without a laptop and without wrecking the aircraft in the process. The reading order is this: first the overall map of the four mechanisms the table below , then adjrange — the line format, slots, the step and its timing, the full function table; after that — what gets into EEPROM and when, stick commands, profiles and the CMS menu. At the end come the procedure for adjusting PIDs in the air, the differences from Betaflight and the dangers. Read the “Dangers” section before the first adjrange line on your own aircraft: three items in it function 54 on a multirotor, a duplicate function in a slot, a two-position switch are ways to crash the aircraft with a single configuration line. The starting PIDs and their tuning order are in inav-mc-tuning , the OSD elements for feedback in inav-osd-hd , the diff all backup in inav-cli-backup . Mechanism Arm state What it changes Saving --- --- --- --- adjrange the Adjustments tab armed and disarmed one number per step: PIDs, rates, expo, TPA, fixed-wing cruise throttle, VTX power not saved by itself Stick commands disarmed only profile, calibrations, level trim, missions, saving some commands write EEPROM themselves Profiles the MIXER PROFILE 2 mode and logic conditions — in flight; sticks and the CLI — on the ground a whole set of settings at once the active profile number is an ordinary setting in RAM CMS the OSD menu disarmed only PIDs, rates, filters, navigation, VTX, OSD the SAVE+EXIT item Everything that is changed on the fly takes effect immediately. One step too many in multirotor D means hot motors, an error in nav_fw_cruise_thr means a wing that does not hold its speed in RTH. So the mechanics come first, then the practice. adjrange : two channels and a slot The command format cliAdjustmentRange in fc/cli.c , all seven fields are required: adjrange <index <slot <range channel <start <end <function <adjustment channel Field Allowed Meaning --- --- --- index 0…19 the line number, MAX_ADJUSTMENT_RANGE_COUNT 20 slot 0…3 MAX_SIMULTANEOUS_ADJUSTMENT_COUNT 4 ; in the Configurator this is “Slot 1…4” range channel 0…29 AUX1 = 0 “CH 5” in the Configurator ; selects what to adjust start, end 900…2100, step 25 stored as a step number 0…48; the range is active when start ≤ channel < end function 0…60 the number from the table below, 0 — the line is disabled adjustment channel 0…29 the switch that moves the value; may be the same as the range channel Step number = value − 900 / 25 with the fractional part dropped, and the value is first constrained to 900…2100. Enter 1310 — 1300 is stored, enter 1690 — 1675 is stored. A line with start ≥ end never triggers. If even one field is out of range, the whole line is zeroed and the CLI prints a parse error. A slot is a place for one active function. On every cycle of the receiver task processRx in fc/fc_core.c ; the task is event-driven — it runs once per received radio link frame, that is, 50 times a second on a 50 Hz link and 150 times on a 150 Hz link the firmware goes through the lines in index order: an active line takes its slot if it is free; an inactive line frees the slot if the slot holds its function. Three consequences follow: - one function at a time works in one slot; with two active lines the slot goes to the line with the lower index; - a selector position for which there is no line is a safe “off”; - the same function must not be put in one slot twice the analysis is below, in the dangers . The official Inflight Adjustments.md in the 9.1.0 tag claims that a slot “retains its state” when the channel leaves the range and that the function numbers are 0–56. The 9.1.0 source says otherwise: the slot is freed, and the functions are 0–60. Trust the source. Adjustments are not processed while the CLI is open the slots freeze in their current state: both adjustment functions are simply not called , nor without a receiver signal or during failsafe the slots are freed ; there are no steps in any of the three cases. Step mode only: threshold, repeat, signals All 60 entries of defaultAdjustmentConfigs have ADJUSTMENT_MODE_STEP . The select-by-position mode ADJUSTMENT_MODE_SELECT is compiled under USE_INFLIGHT_PROFILE_ADJUSTMENT , and that macro is commented out in rc_adjustments.h . An absolute mode, “knob = value”, does not exist in INAV at all. - The adjustment channel above 1700 PWM_RANGE_MIDDLE + 200 — plus one step, below 1300 — minus one step. The thresholds are hard-coded and do not depend on mid_rc . - The first step comes in the same cycle in which the channel crossed the threshold. While the switch is held, the step repeats once every 500 ms RESET_FREQUENCY_2HZ . Returning to the middle re-arms the slot at once, so short presses are faster than holding. - The number of steps for a hold of length T: n = 1 + ⌊T / 0.5 s⌋ . To get n steps, hold for at least n − 1 · 0.5 s. The accuracy is one receiver cycle: the first repeat comes one cycle earlier than 500 ms, the following ones — after 500 ms rounded up to a cycle. - If the slot became active when the switch was already deflected, the step

text: summary A flight controller on INAV reports about itself over several protocols and accepts commands from outside over several as well, and all of them share the same UARTs. This module works through them from the INAV 9.1.0 source: the port function bits and the rules by which two functions coexist on one UART; what exactly goes out over CRSF, SmartPort, LTM and MAVLink and how often; which incoming MAVLink messages the handler really understands the list is short ; how the MSP receiver and the MSP RC OVERRIDE mode work and what happens to them on a link loss; what a Bluetooth bridge and a ground station need. The practice is a calculation exercise: decode a serial dump and find the conflicts, compute the MAVLink byte budget for SiK and ELRS, build an msp_override_channels mask and find three errors in a config. theory The map: who talks to whom This module is about how an INAV flight controller exchanges data with the radio, a ground station and a companion computer. The reading order: first the protocol map the table below and the port rules — who coexists with whom on one UART; then the “downlink” protocols in turn: CRSF, SmartPort, LTM, MAVLink with its settings and the short list of what INAV accepts; after them — “uplink” control over MSP: the MSP receiver, MSP RC Override and the command MSP2_INAV_SET_AUX_RC ; at the end radio bridges and ground stations. The sections on MAVLink “fly here”, MSP RC Override and SET_AUX_RC contain safety warnings — they are about cases where someone other than the pilot controls the channels. Port assignment during the initial setup is in inav-setup-scratch , the downlink bandwidth in link-elrs , the sensors on the radio in link-edgetx , mission upload in inav-missions . Protocol Port function bit · number Direction Who reads it Baud rate --- --- --- --- --- CRSF telemetry none of its own: it rides on the receiver port RX_SERIAL 6 · 64 down + MSP both ways an EdgeTX radio through ELRS / Crossfire 420000, fixed SmartPort TELEMETRY_SMARTPORT 5 · 32 down on polling + MSP FrSky X-series receivers, the radio 57600, fixed LTM TELEMETRY_LTM 4 · 16 down only antenna trackers, OSDs, ground stations with LTM support from the telemetry field, AUTO = 19200 MAVLink TELEMETRY_MAVLINK 8 · 256 down + a narrow set of commands up MAVLink ground stations, a companion, an ADS-B receiver from the telemetry field, AUTO = 57600 MSP MSP 0 · 1 request — reply INAV Configurator, mobile apps, a companion script, HD video inav-osd-hd from the MSP field, 115200 by default HoTT, IBUS, SMS 3 · 8, 9 · 512, 19 · 524288 down Graupner and FlySky radios, a SIM800 modem 19200, 115200, from the telemetry field {{diagram:inav-telemetry-port-map Telemetry to the radio goes over the receiver port and needs no port function of its own; LTM, MAVLink and SmartPort take separate UARTs; MSP is the only protocol through which the flight controller is configured, and there are no more than three ports with it.}} Telemetry is enabled by feature TELEMETRY : without it the TELEMETRY task 500 Hz, idle priority is not started, and all the protocols are silent at once, including CRSF. While the CLI is open, telemetry is stopped too. Ports: the function mask and what is compatible with what The line serial <id <mask <msp <gps <telemetry <peripheral in detail — inav-cli-backup : id 0…7 — UART1…UART8, 20 — USB VCP, 30 and 31 — SoftSerial. The mask is the sum of the bits from io/serial.h . A function can be added and removed by bit number: serial 2 +4 , serial 2 -4 . Bit Number Function Bit Number Function --- --- --- --- --- --- 0 1 MSP 9 512 TELEMETRY_IBUS 1 2 GPS 15 32768 LOG 2 4 unused the former FrSky D 18 262144 ESCSERIAL ESC telemetry 3 8 TELEMETRY_HOTT 19 524288 TELEMETRY_SIM 4 16 TELEMETRY_LTM 23 8388608 SMARTPORT_MASTER 5 32 TELEMETRY_SMARTPORT 25 33554432 MSP_OSD DisplayPort 6 64 RX_SERIAL 26 67108864 GIMBAL 7 128 BLACKBOX 27 134217728 GIMBAL_HEADTRACKER 8 256 TELEMETRY_MAVLINK The rules of isSerialConfigValid : 1. Ports with MSP — from 1 to 3 MAX_MSP_PORT_COUNT , and USB VCP counts. 2. No more than two functions on a port. 3. Only two kinds of pair are allowed: MSP + one of {HOTT, SMARTPORT, LTM, MAVLINK, IBUS, BLACKBOX, LOG} or RX_SERIAL + one of {LTM, IBUS}. 4. Everything else is an error: MAVLink + SmartPort, MSP + DisplayPort, MSP + GPS, RX_SERIAL + MAVLink. If even one rule is violated, validateAndFixConfig resets the whole port table to the board default on saving and loading. The symptom: after save the receiver and the GPS are gone although you touched one port. On a port shared with MSP telemetry runs only while armed while disarmed the port belongs to MSP . telemetry_switch = ON changes the condition: the TELEMETRY mode appears, and the port is switched with a switch rather than by arming. On a dedicated port telemetry always runs. There are four baud rate fields — one per role of the port: MSP, GPS, telemetry, peripherals DisplayPort, ESC, gimbal . The values allowed in the CLI are from the table baudRates : 1200…2470000; 0 in the telemetry field means AUTO . The Ports tab in Configurator 9 offers fewer: MSP 2400…230400, telemetry AUTO and 1200…460800. A mission in the configurator Step 2. The same mission in the CLI Step 2b. A CLI generator from a list of coordinates Step 3. Flight Lab
text: summary An INAV mission is a list of waypoints with actions that the aircraft executes in NAV WP mode. This module shows what a waypoint consists of, which actions exist WAYPOINT, POSHOLD_TIME, RTH, JUMP, SET_POI, LAND , how to write a mission through the configurator and through the CLI with the wp command, where the altitude lives, and how INAV protects you from taking off with the “wrong” mission. theory Waypoint structure In the CLI: wp <n <action <lat <lon <alt <p1 <p2 <p3 <flag . - lat , lon — degrees × 10⁷ 123456789 = 12.3456789° . - alt — centimeters; bit 0 of p3 selects relative to home 0 or above mean sea level 1 . - action : 1 WAYPOINT, 3 POSHOLD_TIME, 4 RTH, 5 SET_POI, 6 JUMP, 7 SET_HEAD, 8 LAND. - p1 : for WAYPOINT and LAND — the speed to the waypoint cm/s; multirotor only; used when 50 ≤ p1 ≤ nav_max_auto_speed 1000 , above that it is clipped to nav_max_auto_speed , below 50 the aircraft flies at nav_auto_speed ; for POSHOLD_TIME — the time in seconds; for RTH — p1 0 allows landing; for JUMP — the target index. - p2 : for POSHOLD_TIME — the speed to the waypoint the same rules as for p1 of WAYPOINT ; for JUMP — the number of repeats. - p3 — a bitfield: bit 0 1 — the altitude type, bits 1–4 2, 4, 8, 16 — the user action 1–4 flags of this waypoint. p3 = 6 — altitude relative to home, actions 1 and 2 set. - flag : 0 — an ordinary waypoint, 165 0xA5 — the last waypoint of the mission, 72 0x48 — the waypoint takes the home coordinates instead of lat / lon the same as a waypoint with lat = lon = 0 . The CLI rejects any other flag. Capacity: NAV_MAX_WAYPOINTS = 120 waypoints for all missions together target/common.h 9.1.0 ; in 9.1.0 only FISHDRONEF4 sets its own value — 60, and there are no official builds of that target SKIP_RELEASES . The waypoint number starts at 0 in the CLI and at 1 in Mission Control. JUMP rules: checked at arming A JUMP error does not surface in flight: arming is blocked by the NAV flag navigationIsBlockingArming , navigation.c 9.1.0 . The rules in CLI numbering from 0 : 1. A JUMP cannot be the first waypoint of a mission. 2. The target p1 is the number of an existing waypoint: p1 is less than the number of waypoints. 3. You cannot jump to an adjacent waypoint or to itself: for a JUMP with number n the targets n − 1, n and n + 1 are forbidden. 4. The target is a waypoint with coordinates: WAYPOINT, POSHOLD_TIME or LAND not RTH, SET_POI, SET_HEAD or another JUMP . 5. p2 repeats is not less than −1; −1 means forever. The check: the list wp 0 1 … , wp 1 1 … , wp 2 1 … , wp 3 6 0 0 0 0 2 0 0 , wp 4 4 0 0 0 1 0 0 165 — a JUMP with number 3 to waypoint 0 twice, the rules are met. With p1 = 2 adjacent arming is blocked. In Mission Control the numbers are one higher: there the same target is waypoint 1. wp load loads the list from EEPROM, wp save saves it, wp reset clears it. When restoring from a backup inav-cli-backup the wp lines of a diff all go into RAM only: an ordinary save does not write them, and after a reboot the list will be the old one. The mission is saved by wp save before save ; it validates the list the last waypoint has flag 165 and at the same time writes all unsaved CLI settings to EEPROM itself — run it when the paste output has no red lines. Execution NAV WP mode is activated with a switch. The aircraft flies from waypoint to waypoint at nav_auto_speed or the speed from p1 , and the waypoint acceptance radius is nav_wp_radius . A mission saved with wp save does not get into memory by itself after power-up: nav_wp_load_on_boot = OFF, and it is loaded by wp load a repeat wp load with a mission already loaded unloads it , by the button in Mission Control or by the load stick command inav-adjustments . Set it to ON if the aircraft flies the same mission without a laptop in the field. JUMP gives loops, SET_POI points the camera at a point of interest, LAND lands at the waypoint. Protection against the wrong mission If a mission is loaded whose first waypoint is farther than nav_wp_max_safe_distance , arming is blocked. This protects against the scenario “arrived at a different field with yesterday's mission”. The bypass is the yaw stick held right while arming in Mode 2 the left stick down and right , regardless of nav_extra_arming_safety , and it is exactly that, a bypass; 0 in nav_wp_max_safe_distance 100 m by default disables the check. nav_extra_arming_safety = ALLOW_BYPASS the default in 9.1, as in 8.0 concerns a different block — arming without a GPS fix. Several missions multi-mission Up to 9 missions sit one after another in a single waypoint list navigation.c , USE_MULTI_MISSION is present in all targets : each ends with a waypoint with flag 165, and the end of the whole file is one more entry with flag 165 and the RTH action right after the last mission. Mission Control saves and loads such a file as a whole, and wp save writes it to EEPROM. wp save resets the selected mission to 1 navigation.c , so select the mission again after saving. The active mission is nav_wp_multi_mission_index 1–9, default 1 , and the OSD shows its number. There are four ways to select a mission: Method When it works How --- --- --- CLI, Configurator disarmed set nav_wp_multi_mission_index = 2 , save Stick command disarmed, throttle low roll right — next, roll left — previous, yaw and pitch centered adjrange , function 59 armed, not in WP mode the adjustment channel steps by 1 from 1 to the number of missions inav-adjustments The MISSION CHANGE mode id 59 armed, with two or more missions while the mode is active NAV WP does not start, and every activation of the NAV WP switch moves to the next mission in a cycle; turn MISSION CHANGE off and the selected mission is loaded The check before takeoff: the mission number in the OSD is the one you need, and its first waypoint is closer than nav_wp_max_safe_distance . summary: A flying wing on INAV is the cheapest route to long-range flying with navigation. But a wing is not a quadcopter: there is no hover, there is a stall, throttle does not equal altitude, and a reversed elevon ends the flight in the first second of the launch. This module takes you through the setup: t
headings: The AIRPLANE platform Fixed-wing modes Throttle and speed Autolaunch Autotune Flaperons, soaring and zero throttle Fixed-wing failsafe The default numbers and how to set them Autolaunch: detection settings Fixed-wing landing A worked example: the first flight of a 1 m wing Place in the system Step 1. Mixer and reverses Step 2. Modes and safety Step 3. First flight Step 4. Autotune
text: summary A flying wing on INAV is the cheapest route to long-range flying with navigation. But a wing is not a quadcopter: there is no hover, there is a stall, throttle does not equal altitude, and a reversed elevon ends the flight in the first second of the launch. This module takes you through the setup: the AIRPLANE platform and the mixer, reverses and trims, the MANUAL/ANGLE/ACRO/CRUISE modes, hand launch with autolaunch, FF autotune and what changed in it, and failsafe for a fixed wing. theory The AIRPLANE platform platform_type = AIRPLANE opens up the airplane mixer Flying Wing: two elevons, one motor , flaps, the fixed-wing modes and fixed-wing navigation. The quadcopter modes disappear. Fixed-wing modes - MANUAL — direct control of the servos, no stabilization. It must always be on a switch: it is the last resort. - ACRO — rate stabilization. - ANGLE / HORIZON — self-leveling. - NAV CRUISE — holds heading and altitude, the stick corrects the heading. - NAV RTH, NAV WP — as on a multirotor, but without hovering: over home the wing circles loiter or flies a landing approach. Throttle and speed Three key settings: nav_fw_cruise_thr — the cruise throttle in navigation, nav_fw_min_thr and nav_fw_max_thr — the limits. In navigation a fixed wing gains altitude with pitch angle and throttle together; a cruise throttle that is too low in a climb leads to a stall. Autolaunch The NAV LAUNCH mode: the aircraft waits for the throw, detects the launch from the acceleration, after nav_fw_launch_motor_delay smoothly brings the throttle up to nav_fw_launch_thr , and holds the climb angle nav_fw_launch_climb_angle until the nav_fw_launch_timeout timeout or until the sticks are moved. A hand launch without autolaunch means a motor at full throttle next to your fingers; autolaunch was invented precisely to prevent that. Autotune AUTO TUNE is a modifier on top of ANGLE/HORIZON/ACRO; it does not work in MANUAL. It tunes the feedforward per axis and, in ACRO/HORIZON, the rates. Autotune does not touch P and I — a change from old versions; they are tuned by hand before or after. You need to fly with sharp inputs on all three axes for several minutes; an axis without sharp inputs will not be tuned. The result is not saved automatically: after landing, disarm and give the save stick command or save in the CLI . Three autotune settings of 9.1.0 settings.yaml , pid_autotune.c explain almost every complaint that “autotune did nothing”: Setting Default What it does Rule --- --- --- --- fw_autotune_min_stick 50 % the response is recorded only while the stick input after deadband and expo exceeds this smooth inputs of a third of the travel are not counted at all: make them sharp and nearly full; the first changes on an axis come only after 5 s of such inputs 250 samples of 20 ms fw_autotune_rate_adjustment AUTO AUTO — the rates are adjusted up and down to match the capabilities of the airplane; LIMIT — down only, never above the starting rates; FIXED — the rates are not adjusted in ANGLE the rates are never changed, with any value: ANGLE commands an angle, not a rate fw_autotune_max_rate_deflection 90 % 50…100 the target percentage of maximum mixer output used for determining the rate lower — lower rates and more control surface travel in reserve The check after the flight: in ANGLE only fw_ff_roll , fw_ff_pitch , fw_ff_yaw changed; in ACRO or HORIZON with AUTO — also roll_rate , pitch_rate , yaw_rate . If the rates did not change in ACRO with AUTO, check whether FIXED is set and whether the stick deflection was large enough. {{diagram:inav-autotune-tree What autotune changes depends on the mode underneath: in ANGLE — only feedforward, the rates — only in ACRO/HORIZON and not with FIXED, P and I — never; without sharp stick inputs above 50 % nothing changes.}} Flaperons, soaring and zero throttle - Flaperons. set has_flaps = ON makes the FLAPERON mode id 34 available; while it is active, smix input 14 FEATURE FLAPS equals flaperon_throw_offset 200 µs , and both ailerons go down by that amount on top of roll. The rule: input 14 is fed to both aileron servos so that both ailerons go down; the servos are mounted mirrored, so their weights have opposite signs smix 4 2 14 100 20 -1 and smix 5 3 14 -100 20 -1 in inav-mixer-vtol . The bench check: FLAPERON on — both ailerons went down, and roll still moves them in opposite directions. The smix lines and the pulse calculation are in inav-mixer-vtol . - Soaring SOARING, id 56 . It works only on top of NAV POSHOLD loiter or NAV COURSE HOLD navigation.c : navigation stops holding altitude, pitch floats freely within nav_fw_soaring_pitch_deadband 5° , and with nav_fw_soaring_motor_stop = ON the motor stops. For thermals and for saving battery on a glider; navigation still holds the course or the circle. - Zero throttle in ANGLE. fw_min_throttle_down_pitch 0, in tenths of a degree, up to 450 lowers the nose when the throttle is below nav_fw_cruise_thr : the addition grows linearly from 0 at cruise throttle to the full value at throttle 1000 pid.c . An example: 50 5° , nav_fw_cruise_thr = 1400, throttle 1200 → nose down by 5 × 1400 − 1200 / 400 = 2.5°. Without it a wing in ANGLE at closed throttle holds level and loses speed. It is tuned in flight with adjrange function 52 inav-adjustments . Fixed-wing failsafe The RTH procedure is the obvious choice when GPS is available. LAND on a fixed wing is a downward spiral with set angles, that is, a controlled impact. On a fixed wing a check of failsafe_throttle under load is mandatory for LAND without altitude sensors; DROP simply shuts the motor off . The default numbers and how to set them nav_fw_cruise_thr = 1400, nav_fw_min_thr = 1200, nav_fw_max_thr = 1700 throttle PWM units ; the throttle-to-pitch coupling nav_fw_pitch2thr = 10 throttle added per degree of pitch — a simplified TECS: nose up → more throttle ; the climb/dive angles nav_fw_climb_angle = 20°, nav_fw_dive_angle = 15°; the loiter radius nav_fw_loiter_radius = 7500 c

text: summary RTH from inav-gps answers the question “at what altitude to fly home”. This module answers the rest: where you must not fly geozones , where to actually land safehome , which way to return trackback and how a fixed wing builds a landing pattern with a glide slope instead of a spiral into the ground fwapproach and nav_fw_land_ . Everything is worked through from the INAV 9.1.0 source: the CLI line formats, the units, the defaults, the geometry the code builds, and the cases where the protection silently turns itself off. The lab needs no hardware: decode the zones and decide what INAV does in eight aircraft positions, select a safehome, build the approach pattern for a given wind and find three errors in a config. theory Four mechanisms and what connects them This module covers four add-ons to RTH: geozones, safehome, trackback and fixed-wing autoland. Read in order: first the common units and the coordinate conversion this section , then geozones — the line format, the “inside” test, initialization and arming, the zone actions and their link to RTH; after them safehome and trackback, and at the end fwapproach and the approach geometry. The sections on zone actions and on aborting a landing contain warnings about cases where the automation takes control away or flies the aircraft down: read them before the first flight with zones. Basic RTH and home are in inav-gps , the old fixed-wing landing and the wind estimate in inav-wing , fixed-wing failsafe in inav-setup-wing , the rangefinder for the flare in inav-sensors-extra . All four work on top of RTH and store coordinates the same way: latitude and longitude are integers, degrees × 10⁷; altitudes are in centimeters . 50.0012600° is written as 500012600 . Coordinates from maps with six decimal places are padded with a zero to seven. Inside the firmware everything is converted to local centimeters from the first GPS fix point geoConvertGeodeticToLocal in navigation_geo.c : - north: x = Δlat × 1.113195 cm; - east: y = Δlon × 1.113195 × cos origin latitude cm. Δlat and Δlon are differences of the integer values. One unit of latitude is 1.11 cm, one unit of longitude at latitude 50° is 0.716 cm. These two formulas solve all the practice of this module. Mechanism CLI command How many Build condition --- --- --- --- Geozones geozone , geozone vertex , feature GEOZONE 63 zones id 0–62 , 126 vertices for all of them USE_GEOZONE : more than 512 KB of flash and GPS Safehome safehome 8 indexes 0–7 USE_SAFE_HOME , present everywhere Trackback the nav_rth_trackback_ settings 50 points, a ring buffer everywhere Fixed-wing approach fwapproach 17 slots: 0–7 for safehomes, 8–16 for missions USE_FW_AUTOLAND , present everywhere The condition MCU_FLASH_SIZE 512 target/common.h cuts off the STM32F411 and F722: they have no geozone command at all. F405, F427, F745, F765, H743, AT32F435 have it. Geozones: the zone line and the vertex line The zone format exactly eight numbers, otherwise Parse error : geozone <id <shape <type <min alt <max alt <sea level <action <vertex count Field Values What matters --- --- --- shape 0 — circular, 1 — polygon a circle takes 2 vertices, a polygon — 3 or more type 0 — exclusive NFZ, no-fly zone , 1 — inclusive FZ, fly zone min alt, cm 0 — “from the ground, no action at the lower limit” for the lower limit to work from the ground, use −1 or lower max alt, cm 0 — no upper limit at run time it becomes INT32_MAX sea level 0 — relative to home altitude, 1 — above mean sea level at initialization the home altitude is subtracted from both altitudes action 0 NONE, 1 AVOID, 2 POS_HOLD, 3 RTH on a multirotor AVOID is replaced with POS_HOLD vertex count 1…126 must match the number of geozone vertex lines The vertex format: geozone vertex <zone id <vertex idx <lat <lon . The vertices of a polygon are numbered from 0 counterclockwise , and the sides do not cross. For a circle vertex 0 is the center, and in vertex 1 the lat field holds the radius in centimeters geoZoneInit : radius = geoZoneVertices i - lat ; lon is not used. Service forms: geozone and geozone vertex without arguments print the tables, geozone reset id erases a zone with its vertices, geozone vertex reset zone idx — the vertices. The zone editor lives in the Configurator on the Mission Control tab the Geozones button, saving — “Save Eeprom Geozones and reboot” . The documentation explicitly asks you not to edit zones by hand in the CLI: the editor checks the vertex order and crossings, the CLI does not. Reading the lines and moving them through diff all is fine inav-cli-backup . Two CLI traps in 9.1.0. The id check is written as idx MAX_GEOZONES_IN_CONFIG , so geozone 63 … is accepted although the array ends at 62: do not use id 63. And number the zones consecutively from 0: geoZoneInit in places indexes the working array with the zone number from the config, and gaps break the altitude handling. When the aircraft is “inside” a zone isInGeozone checks the plan view first, then the altitude: - circle: the distance to the center is less than the radius; - polygon: a ray crossing test isPointInPloygon , and a point on a side also counts as inside; - altitude: z ≥ min or min = 0 and z ≤ max , z being the altitude above the home point. Three consequences follow. An NFZ with min alt = 3000 has no effect on the ground: you can stand under it, arm and fly below 30 m. An FZ with a 120 m ceiling is already “not yours” at 125 m: the aircraft is considered outside the FZ. And an FZ with a non-zero min alt does not contain the takeoff point, so arming will be forbidden — the setting geozone_safehome_as_inclusive exists for exactly this case. Initialization and arming The zones are converted to local coordinates once — when the position estimate first becomes valid geozoneUpdate → geoZoneInit , so a reboot is needed after editing zones. At that moment: - an inclusive zone that the aircraft is not in and whose nearest vertex is more than 2 km away GEOZONE_INCLUSE_IGNORE_DISTANCE is

text: summary The mixer is the last software layer between the controllers and the hardware: it turns three stabilization commands and throttle into numbers for every motor and every servo, and the microcontroller timers turn those into pulses on the pads. This module goes through all of it from the INAV 9.1.0 source: the platform types, the mmix lines including throttle values of −1 and −1.05…−2 , the smix rules and all 61 input sources, the servo command, the servo_ settings, the assignment of outputs to timers and timer_output_mode , the tables for elevons, a V-tail, flaperons and differential, gimbals and the head tracker, the two mixer profiles and the VTOL transition. The practice needs no hardware and no simulator: derive the mmix of a hex from the geometry and compare it with the preset, calculate servo pulses with the servos.c formula, lay out the outputs of a real MATEKF405TE board for 4 and 5 DShot motors and find three errors in a 4+1 VTOL config. theory Where the mixer sits {{diagram:inav-mixer-signal-path The motors get only the three PID commands and throttle; the servos — any of the 61 sources. After that the timer decides everything: one timer — one function.}} The PID controllers output axisPID ROLL/PITCH/YAW in the range ±500. The motor mixer mixTable , mixer.c adds them to throttle using the mmix table. The servo mixer servoMixer , servos.c computes the servos from the smix rules and the servo parameters. The firmware has no ready-made tables: the presets “Quad X”, “Flying Wing” and the others live in the Configurator js/model.js and on loading simply write the mmix / smix lines. The theory of control allocation is in ctl-allocation; this is how it is written down by hand. Platform type platform_type is stored in the mixer profile and enables a set of flags mixerUpdateStateFlags : Value What it enables Consequence --- --- --- MULTIROTOR default MULTIROTOR, ALTITUDE_CONTROL multirotor PIDs and navigation, AIRMODE, HEADFREE TRICOPTER the same plus tri_unarmed_servo : the tail servo works even when disarmed AIRPLANE AIRPLANE, FIXED_WING, ALTITUDE_CONTROL, MOVE_FORWARD_ONLY fixed-wing PIDs, MANUAL, autolaunch, autotrim, autotune, FLAPERON with has_flaps ROVER , BOAT FIXED_WING, MOVE_FORWARD_ONLY, no ALTITUDE_CONTROL no ALTHOLD and no AIRMODE, a throttle ceiling of 1850 instead of 2000 HELICOPTER the same flags as MULTIROTOR there is no separate swashplate logic in mixer.c The documentation docs/Mixer.md , the description of the setting names MULTIROTOR, AIRPLANE and TRICOPTER as implemented. The details of the airplane platform are in inav-wing. mmix : motors The syntax: mmix <n <throttle <roll <pitch <yaw , n = 0…11 MAX_SUPPORTED_MOTORS 12 , and mmix reset erases the table. The formula mixer.c:537–540, 628 : text motor n = pitch·P + roll·R − yaw·Y + constrain throttle command · throttle P, R, Y are axisPID , ±500. The signs of the weights per docs/Mixer.md : a positive roll — the motor speeds up on a roll to the right so it is on the left ; a positive pitch — it speeds up when the nose goes down it is at the rear ; a positive yaw — it speeds up on a clockwise turn, that is, its prop spins counterclockwise. The minus before yaw in the formula is not a mistake: rcCommand YAW is the stick with the opposite sign fc_core.c:404 . The setting motor_direction_inverted = ON flips the sign of the whole yaw column at once props-out , and the table does not have to be touched. A line from the geometry: a motor on an arm at azimuth φ clockwise from the nose, all arms of the same length — roll = −sin φ , pitch = −cos φ . For Quad X φ = 45°, 135°, 225°, 315° that gives ±0.707; the preset scales the table to ±1 — the PIDs compensate for the common factor of an axis, and what matters is the ratios between the motors. text mmix 0 1.000 -1.000 1.000 -1.000 rear right, prop clockwise mmix 1 1.000 -1.000 -1.000 1.000 front right mmix 2 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 rear left mmix 3 1.000 1.000 -1.000 -1.000 front left The check: throttle 1500, a roll request of +100 → the right motors at 1400, the left at 1600, and the aircraft rolls right. The throttle column is not only a throttle scale: throttle Behavior mixer.c:636–644 --- --- 0 < t ≤ 1 an ordinary motor 0 an empty line: mmix , diff and the motor count stop at the first such line −1.05 < t < 0 written as −1 the motor is stopped but the line is occupied — a “placeholder” so that the following lines are not lost −2.0 ≤ t ≤ −1.05 stopped; with MIXER TRANSITION active it spins at −t × 1000 µs regardless of the stick −1.2 → 1200, which is 20 % of the range . Does not work with REVERSIBLE_MOTORS . Below −2.0 the motor is stopped and never spins mixer.c The number of motors is counted over both profiles: a motor “exists” if its throttle ≠ 0 in at least one of them mixer.c:117–137 . smix : servo rules The syntax: smix <rule <servo <input <weight <speed <lc . rule 0…35 MAX_SERVO_RULES , servo 0…17, weight −1000…1000 %, speed 0…255, lc — the number of a logic condition −1…63 −1 — the rule always works; a false condition zeroes the input of the rule, see inav-ipf . Rules for the same servo are summed. The table is read up to the first rule with weight 0. speed limits the rate of change of the input: speed × 10 units per second, 0 — no limit; with weight 100 and standard endpoints that is the “10 µs/s per unit” from the documentation. The input sources inputSource_e , servos.h:26–89 — 9.1.0 has 61 of them, id 0…60: id Source Value --- --- --- 0, 1, 2 stabilized roll, pitch, yaw axisPID , ±500; in MANUAL — the sticks 3 stabilized throttle the throttle command − 1500; −500 when disarmed 4–7 RC roll, pitch, yaw, throttle the channel − 1500, bypassing stabilization 8–11, 15–22, 42–43 RC CH5–CH8, CH9–CH16, CH17–CH18 the channel − 1500 44–59 RC CH19–CH34 only boards with 512 KB of flash USE_34CHANNELS 12, 13 GIMBAL PITCH, GIMBAL ROLL pitch ±90° and roll ±180° → ±500; only with the CAMSTAB mode, otherwise 0 14 FEATURE FLAPS flaperon_throw_offset with the FLAPERON mode

text: summary The INAV Programming Framework IPF is a way to add logic to the aircraft without Lua and without a companion computer: “if farther than 100 m — raise the VTX power”, “if the voltage is below a threshold — activate RTH”, “switch a channel on a condition”. Logic conditions are executed right in the firmware and work with telemetry, flight modes, mission waypoints and global variables. This module explains the model a condition = an operation + two operands , the CLI syntax, GVARs and typical uses, including a comparison with Lua in ArduPilot. theory The model - Logic Condition — one line of “code”: an operation on one or two operands, with a result that is true/false or a number. - Operand — a number, an RC channel, a flight parameter distance to home, voltage, altitude, speed , a flight mode, another condition, a GVAR, a mission waypoint. - Activator — another condition that must be true for this one to be executed −1 — always . - GVAR — global variables, integers; by default the limits are −32768…32767, and the command gvar <i <default <min <max can widen them they are stored as int32 ; they can be read, written, increased and used in the servo mixer. - Programming PID — four configurable controllers whose output is available as an operand. CLI syntax logic <rule <enabled <activatorId <operation <opA type <opA value <opB type <opB value <flags Operand types: 0 — Value, 1 — Get RC Channel, 2 — Flight, 3 — Flight Mode, 4 — Logic Condition, 5 — GVAR, 6 — Programming PID, 7 — Waypoints. Operations: comparisons equal, greater than, lower than , logic AND, OR, NOT , arithmetic, Set/Increase/Decrease GVAR, Override Throttle Scale, Override RC Channel, Set VTx Power Level and others. In 9.0 operations 55 Set Gimbal Sensitivity and 56 Override Minimum Ground Speed and flight operands 46–49 minimum ground speed, wind speed and direction, relative wind offset were appended to the lists; the old numbers did not shift. Configurator 9 also has the JavaScript Programming tab marked as beta : JavaScript code is transpiled into the same logic conditions, so the limitations stay the same. The 9.1.0 numbers: how to build a logic line without the configurator The numbers are taken from programming/logic_condition.h 9.1.0. They have not changed since 8.0.1: operations 0–54 and flight operands 0–45 are in the same places, and 9.x only appended new ones at the end. The workflow is this: 1. Input — a rule as a phrase: “if <quantity <comparison <threshold , then <action ”. 2. Decision — for the quantity you choose the operand type table 1 and the number within the type tables 2–4 . You convert the threshold into the units of the operand: 3.5 V per cell → 350, 30 m of altitude → 3000 cm. The comparison or the action is the operation number table 5 . 3. Check — you enter the line in the CLI, the logic command without arguments prints the rule back, and the Programming tab shows its live value. If the value does not look like the quantity an altitude of 12 at 12 m of flight , the units or the operand type are mixed up. Table 1 — operand types: Type What the value field holds Example --- --- --- 0 the number itself 0 100 — the constant 100 1 the RC channel number, indexed from 1 1 6 — the raw value of AUX2 channel 6 , 1000–2000 µs 2 the number of a flight parameter table 2 2 1 — the distance to home 3 the number of a flight mode table 3 , the value is 0/1 3 2 — RTH is active 4 the number of another logic condition, its value 4 0 — the result of rule 0 5 the GVAR number 0–7, its value 5 1 — the contents of GVAR 1 6 the Programming PID number 0–3, its output 6 0 — the output of PID 0, −1000…1000 7 the number of a waypoint parameter table 4 7 6 — user action 1 is active on this leg Table 2 — the key flight operands type 2 , units from logic_condition.c : No. Quantity Unit No. Quantity Unit --- --- --- --- --- --- 0 time since arming s 14 throttle position % 0–100 1 home distance m 15 / 16 / 40 roll / pitch / yaw heading deg 2 trip distance m 17 is armed 0/1 3 RSSI % 0–99 22 is RTH 0/1 4 battery voltage 0.01 V 23 is landing 0/1 5 average cell voltage 0.01 V 24 is failsafe 0/1 6 current 0.01 A 28 3D home distance m 7 current drawn mAh 29 / 44 LQ uplink / downlink % 8 GPS sats pcs 31 GPS valid 3D fix 0/1 9 ground speed cm/s 33 / 42 active control / battery profile 1–3 11 air speed pitot cm/s 38 active mixer profile number 12 altitude cm 45 uplink RSSI dBm 13 vertical speed cm/s 47 / 48 9.x wind: speed / direction cm/s / deg, −1 = no estimate Table 3 — flight modes type 3 , the value is 1 while the mode is active: 0 FAILSAFE, 1 MANUAL, 2 RTH, 3 POSHOLD LOITER on a fixed wing , 4 CRUISE, 5 ALTHOLD, 6 ANGLE, 7 HORIZON, 8 AIRMODE, 9 USER1, 10 USER2, 11 COURSE HOLD, 12 USER3, 13 USER4, 14 ACRO, 15 WP mission, 16 ANGLE HOLD. These are the framework's own numbers, and they do not match the mode numbers in aux RTH is 10 there . Table 4 — waypoints type 7 : 0 a mission is in progress 0/1 , 1 the current waypoint index from 1 , 2 / 3 the action of the current / next waypoint, 4 the distance to the next waypoint m , 5 the distance from the previous waypoint m , 6–9 user action 1–4 on this leg 0/1 , 10–13 user action 1–4 on the next leg. How a user action turns into PINIO is in inav-missions and inav-led-pinio-beeper . Table 5 — operations: No. Operations How to read A and B --- --- --- 0–3 TRUE, = , , < comparison of A with B 4–6 LOW, MID, HIGH A is an RC channel: < 1333, 1333–1666, 1666 µs 7–12 AND, OR, XOR, NAND, NOR, NOT A, B — usually type 4 other rules 13 STICKY A sets the latch, B resets it 14–17, 40, 43, 44 + , − , × , ÷ , modulo, MIN, MAX the result is a number; division by 0 returns A 18–20 Set / Increase / Decrease GVAR A — the GVAR number as a value type 0 , B — a number 21 Set IO Port an I²C IO expander pin 0–7, value 0/1 22 Override Arming Safety bypasses all arming checks, including throttle 23, 29 Override Throttle Scale % , Override Throttle µs B is not needed 24, 26–28 Swap Roll & Yaw, Invert Roll/Pitch/Yaw

The strip: decode and write Step 2. PINIO and a distance-based shutter Step 3. When it beeps Step 4. The strip current and three errors Moving to real hardware
text: summary A flight controller with INAV has three “utility” outputs: the LED pin a WS2812 strip or plain PWM , up to four PINIO switches VTX power, a camera switcher, a shutter and the beeper, which the motors help over DShot. This module works through them from the INAV 9.1.0 source: the format of led , color , mode_color with all the function letters, the led_pin_pwm_mode modes and the ledpinpwm command, the USER1–4 mode numbers for pinio_box1..4 , the full list of beeper conditions and the rules of the DShot beacon. Separately — what INAV has for a camera RunCam control, mission user actions, logic conditions and what it does not: a ready-made “shot every N meters” function does not exist in the firmware, and it is assembled from four rules. After this module you can read and write strip lines, build a PINIO setup and a distance-based shutter, predict when the aircraft will beep and calculate the strip current. The lab is a calculation exercise, without hardware. theory Three outputs and who controls them This module is about the outputs of the flight controller that do not drive motors or servos: the LED strip and the LED pin, the PINIO pins, the beeper and beeping with the motors. The reading order: first the map of “which output is switched by what” the table below ; then the strip — hardware and the timer, the led line, colors; then the LED pin in PWM mode, PINIO with the USER modes and the path from logic to PINIO; at the end the beeper, the DShot beacon, lights and the camera. The section on overriding an RC channel with logic operation 38 contains a safety warning: read it before you write the first rule. The output layout and the timers are in inav-mixer-vtol , the logic conditions themselves in inav-ipf , the user actions of waypoints in inav-missions . Output What switches it Where it is configured --- --- --- LED pin: a WS2812 strip firmware events arm, battery, GPS, failsafe, sticks , the LEDS OFF mode feature LED_STRIP , led , color , mode_color LED pin: 24 kHz PWM the ledpinpwm command, a logic condition with operation 52 led_pin_pwm_mode PINIO 1–4 any mode of the Modes tab, usually USER1–4 pinio_box1..4 , aux Beeper 24 firmware conditions, the BEEPER mode beeper , beeper_pwm_mode Motors as a beeper the same conditions, only while disarmed dshot_beeper_enabled , dshot_beeper_tone A logic condition inav-ipf can drive only the LED pin directly. It reaches PINIO by a detour: with operation 38 it overrides the RC channel that carries the range of a USER mode. A mission action a user action in p3 , inav-missions switches nothing by itself — it is only an operand for the logic. {{diagram:inav-led-pinio-beeper-flow A switch controls PINIO and the beeper through modes, a logic condition — the LED pin directly and PINIO through a channel override; a mission user action is visible only to the logic.}} The strip: hardware, the timer, the limits A WS2812 has three wires: 5 V, GND, DIN. The driver drivers/light_ws2811strip.c sends 800 kHz from a 2.4 MHz timer through DMA and always transmits a frame for 128 LEDs LED_MAX_STRIP_LENGTH 128 ; the same in 9.1.0 and in 8.0.1 . The palette has 16 colors LED_CONFIGURABLE_COLOR_COUNT . The strip task runs 100 times a second. Power: the course assumes 0.06 A per LED at full white el-power-design , about 20 mA per color channel bf-led-buzzer . The INAV documentation advises separate power from as few as 20 LEDs. INAV has no overall brightness control like ledstrip_brightness in Betaflight: you reduce the current by lowering V in color . The colors of the warnings and the indicators are hard-coded at full brightness. The timer. The strip is enabled only with feature LED_STRIP . The output is the WS2811_PIN of the board, as long as it has the TIM_USE_LED flag in the timer table; if the flag is removed, the first pin with this flag is taken. The conflict rule checkPwmTimerConflicts in drivers/pwm_mapping.c : with the feature enabled, every output on a timer that has a channel with the LED flag is skipped when motors and servos are assigned. The command timer_output_mode <timer LED sets the flag on all channels of the timer inav-mixer-vtol — that is how the strip is moved to a servo output on a board without a dedicated pad, but all the outputs of that timer are lost for motors and servos. Not enough outputs — arming is blocked by PWMOUT . One more check: if WS2811_PIN shares a timer with SoftSerial and both features are enabled, the firmware silently clears LED_STRIP at boot. The led line led <index <x ,<y :<directions :<functions :<color — index 0…127 in wiring order. - x, y — 0…15, stored in 4 bits each 17 becomes 1 . 0,0 is north-west, nose at the top. - Directions — the letters N E S W U D ; only the F function needs them. - Functions — one base letter and any overlays; the letters can be entered in any order, and the CLI prints the base one first and the overlays in the order T O B N I W E . - Color — a palette index 0…15 16 and more becomes 0 ; for the H function — the RC channel number. The line led <i 0,0::: clears the entry. The LEDs are counted up to the first empty entry: 0,0::C:0 is also zero and cuts the strip off. Letter Base function What it shows --- --- --- C Color a color from the palette F Flight mode the mode color from mode_color by direction A Arm state disarmed — special color 0, armed — special color 1 L Battery a hue by the charge percentage: 329 pink at 0 %, 359 red at 20 %, 119 green at 100 %; WARNING — blinks at 1 Hz, CRITICAL — at 4 Hz S RSSI the same scale by RSSI; below 50 % it blinks slowly, below 20 % — fast G GPS no satellites — special color 5; a fix — blinks with color 7 by the number of satellites; satellites without a fix — with color 6 on a background of 5 R Thrust ring a running light, faster with throttle; while disarmed every second LED is lit H Channel a hue by the value of an RC channel, the channel number is in the color field Letter Overlay Action --- --- --- T Throttle shifts the hue of the base color w

SITL and QGC Step 2. Modes Step 3. Parameters and the log What you should get and what to write down Lab
text: summary PX4 is the other big open-source autopilot next to ArduPilot. It grew out of academia and leans toward research work: a modular architecture, strict interfaces and deep ROS 2 integration. This module shows how PX4 differs from ArduPilot in practice ground station, flight modes, parameters, simulation, hardware requirements and when to pick it. theory PX4 versus ArduPilot Both are complete autopilots with navigation, missions and companion computer interfaces. They differ in character: - Ecosystem. PX4 sits in the Dronecode Foundation next to the standards Pixhawk, MAVLink, MAVSDK , with QGroundControl as its native GCS. ArduPilot is community-run, has Mission Planner and supports a huge range of hardware. - Architecture. PX4 is a set of modules that talk over the uORB message bus; you can stop and restart any module at runtime. ArduPilot is more monolithic but runs Lua scripts on board. - ROS 2. PX4 connects natively through uXRCE-DDS, so PX4 topics show up in ROS 2 directly. ArduPilot 4.5+ also has a native DDS client AP_DDS , with a smaller set of topics. - Tuning. PX4 has mature multicopter and fixed-wing autotuning, and its parameters are grouped by control loop MC_ RATE_ , MC_ _P , MPC_ . Rule of thumb: research, computer vision and ROS 2 point to PX4; exotic hardware, Lua on board and a large community of practitioners point to ArduPilot. Both fly. Ground control station QGroundControl handles firmware, airframe selection, calibration, parameters, missions and log download .ulg . It also works with ArduPilot, but for PX4 it is the main tool. Multicopter flight modes - Manual/Stabilized : attitude is stabilized, throttle is manual. - Acro : the sticks command angular rates. - Altitude : holds altitude. - Position : holds position using GNSS; the sticks command velocity. - Hold , Return , Land , Takeoff , Mission , Orbit , Follow Me : autonomous modes. - Offboard : setpoints come from a companion computer. As everywhere, you pick a mode by which sensors you trust. Position will not engage without a reliable GNSS fix. In the source src/modules/commander/ModeUtil/mode_requirements.cpp , v1.17.0 and v1.18.0 the requirements of the manual modes are nested: Acro needs angular rate, Stabilized adds attitude, Altitude adds altitude, Position adds local position, and all four need manual control input. If an estimate is lost in flight, PX4 drops one step down: from Position to Altitude, and without an altitude estimate to Stabilized since 1.17 this is not configurable; see COM_POSCTL_NAVL in the upgrade table . {{diagram:px4-mode-ladder Each mode up the ladder needs one more estimate and holds one more quantity for the pilot; when an estimate is lost, PX4 drops one step down.}} Parameters and logs Parameters are set in QGC or from the console with param set/show . ULog files .ulg contain every uORB topic enabled for logging; analyze them in Flight Review web or with pyulog . Hardware The standard is a Pixhawk-compatible flight controller FMUv5/v6, H7 . PX4 needs more resources than Betaflight, and F4 boards running it are rare. Simulation make px4_sitl gz_x500 starts SITL with Gazebo and the x500 quadcopter model; QGC connects on its own. For ROS 2 this is the same setup as with the real vehicle. First setup in QGroundControl: the order that matters 1. Firmware Firmware → PX4 stable and airframe Airframe → frame type; it sets CA_AIRFRAME , CA_ROTOR_COUNT , the geometry and the starting parameters . Changing the airframe resets parameters. 2. Sensors : compass rotate through every axis , gyro keep still , accelerometer 6 orientations , level horizon; board orientation in SENS_BOARD_ROT , external compass orientation is detected automatically. 3. Radio : stick calibration, RC_MAP_ ; flight modes on switches Flight Modes , and a kill switch, which is mandatory for tests. 4. Motors : Actuators, for output assignment and protocol DShot/PWM is chosen per timer group in Actuators, PWM_MAIN_TIMx , testing each motor with the props off , and checking spin direction against the airframe diagram. 5. Power : BAT1_N_CELLS , voltage divider and current calibration against a multimeter or power meter, the BAT_LOW_THR / BAT_CRIT_THR thresholds. 6. Safety : actions on RC loss COM_RC_LOSS_T = 0.5 s by default, NAV_RCL_ACT , on GCS data link loss NAV_DLL_ACT , default 0, disabled, so you enable it yourself , on low battery COM_LOW_BAT_ACT , the geofence GF_ , the return altitude RTL_RETURN_ALT ; kill switch RC_MAP_KILL_SW stops the motors immediately, in any mode and in the air the full matrix is in px4-safety-return . Preflight checks report to QGC as text "Preflight Fail: …" ; the CBRK_ circuit breakers disable them, and only belong on the bench. QGC pages: what is configured where How to use it: start from what you need to configure, find the page in the table, and check the result in Parameters after a reboot, using the parameters in the "What it writes" column. Page names are from QGC Stable 5.0 PX4 . text: summary One multirotor, from a blank flight controller to a logged first hover on PX4 1.18 the lab output was captured on v1.15.4 , in the order of 17 setup steps. You go through half the steps in SITL make px4_sitl sihsim_quadx or gz_x500 + QGroundControl : airframe, motor geometry, motor test, modes, failsafe with failure injection, autotune, the log and a parameter export. The rest is on the bench without props and in the field: the _CONFIG ports, a CRSF/ELRS receiver, radio calibration, DShot or PWM with ESC calibration, BAT1_V_DIV and BAT1_A_PER_V from a multimeter and the charger, a first hover in Position. The lab: exported parameters, a motor test against the geometry, RC loss and low battery in a ULog, and a Flight Review report of the first flight. theory What is new here and what is a reference The px4-intro module gives the general order of the QGC screens, px4-architecture the modules and uORB, px4-control the cascade and tuning. Motor protocols are in f-motors-esc, the receiver and ELRS binding in link-elrs, the CRSF frame and UART wiring in link-protocols. Here is what the course did not yet have for PX4: ports, RC input, Actuators, power, failsafe with testing, the hover, the backup. {{diagram:px4-setup-flow Of the 17 steps, SITL covers airframe, motor test, modes, failsafe, RTL, autotune and the log; the receiver, ESCs, sensors and power are done only on hardware, and props go on at step 15.}} Three things PX4 does differently - A port is assigned to a function, not a function to a port. Each service has its own _CONFIG / _CFG parameter: MAV_0_CONFIG TELEM1 by default , MAV_1_CONFIG usually for TELEM2, 0 = Disabled by default , GPS_1_CONFIG GPS1 , RC_PORT_CONFIG , RC_CRSF_PRT_CFG , MSP_OSD_CONFIG , DSHOT_TEL_CFG . After choosing the port, reboot, and then the port baud rate SER_<port _BAUD appears: SER_GPS1_BAUD 0 = Auto , for MAVLink on TELEM1 SER_TEL1_BAUD 57600 . MAV_0_RATE is not the port baud rate but the ceiling of the MAVLink stream in bytes/s 1200; 0 = baud/20 . PX4 will neither forbid nor warn about two drivers on one port: you have to free the port by setting the other _CONFIG to Disabled. The fmu-v6x port numbers, the parameters of all the peripherals GPS, compass, rangefinders, airspeed sensor, DroneCAN, OSD and how to find a port conflict by the Conflicting config line in dmesg are covered in px4-hardware-peripherals . - An output is assigned to a function. In Actuators each output gets a function: PWM_MAIN_FUNCn / PWM_AUX_FUNCn = 101…112 for Motor 1…12. The protocol is chosen per timer group PWM_MAIN_TIMx / PWM_AUX_TIMx : −5 / −4 / −3 = DShot150 / 300 / 600, since 1.18 −8 / −7 / −6 = the same with bidirectional DShot, −1 = OneShot, 50…400 = PWM, Hz; the value −2 = DShot1200 existed only in 1.15 and was removed in 1.16 . The geometry is in CA_ : CA_ROTOR_COUNT , CA_ROTORn_PX/PY m, FRD from the center of mass , CA_ROTORn_KM 0 CCW, < 0 CW . - Failsafe comes with a delay. Most actions first give Hold for COM_FAIL_ACT_T = 5 s the pilot can take over , then the action. SITL starts with different defaults than a flight controller: COM_RC_IN_MODE = 1 MAVLink joystick only , COM_LOW_BAT_ACT = 3 2 before 1.16 , SYS_FAILURE_EN = 1, MC_AT_EN = 1, SDLOG_MODE = 1. Do not carry a .params file from SITL over to a vehicle. RC input: CRSF/ELRS Two drivers. crsf_rc is a dedicated CRSF driver: port RC_CRSF_PRT_CFG , telemetry RC_CRSF_TEL_EN . rc_input is the generic one: it parses CRSF among others RC_INPUT_PROTO : −1 auto, 6 CRSF on the RC_PORT_CONFIG port. Which one your firmware has depends on the board and version, and you can see it by which parameter QGC shows. In 1.17 the fmu-v6x, fmu-v6xrt and fmu-v5x default builds include the crsf_rc , sbus_rc , dsm_rc , ghst_rc set and do not include rc_input : there ELRS is set up through RC_CRSF_PRT_CFG . fmu-v5 has both that set and rc_input ; fmu-v6c has neither checked against default.px4board v1.17.0 . Before 1.17 it was different: the fmu-v6x default build had rc_input RC_PORT_CONFIG , and crsf_rc required your own build via make <board boardconfig with rc_input disabled; the CRSF Telemetry page of the 1.17 documentation still describes that procedure. The RC IN port through the Pixhawk IO processor understands SBUS/DSM/PPM/ST24/SUMD, but not CRSF: ELRS is connected to a UART TELEM2, GPS2 . Power: how PX4 computes voltage, current and remaining charge From analog_battery.cpp : V = V_adc · BAT1_V_DIV , I = V_adc − BAT_V_OFFS_CURR · BAT1_A_PER_V . Both coefficients are in the numerator, so calibration is a proportion: What Formula What to measure with --- --- --- Divider BAT1_V_DIV_new = BAT1_V_DIV_old × V_multimeter / V_QGC a multimeter on the balance lead or the XT60 Current BAT1_A_PER_V_new = BAT1_A_PER_V_old × mAh_charger / mAh_log the charger after a flight; a clamp meter for a cross-check Remaining charge battery.cpp : the cell voltage, corrected for the load + R · I , where R is BAT1_R_INTERNAL if it is ≥ 0, otherwise the resistance PX4 estimates in flight; default −1, initial estimate 0.005 Ω per cell; without a current sensor there is no correction , is interpolated linearly between BAT1_V_EMPTY 3.6 V and BAT1_V_CHARGED 4.05 V . With BAT1_CAPACITY 0 the current integral is added to this; the documentation recommends ≈ 90 % of the rated capacity. Thresholds: BAT_LOW_THR 0.15, BAT_CRIT_THR 0.07, BAT_EMERGEN_THR 0.05. Before 1.16 the formula was different: BAT1_R_INTERNAL defaulted to 0.005 Ω, and without a current sensor throttle · BAT1_V_LOAD_DROP was added the parameter was removed in 1.16 . The action is COM_LOW_BAT_ACT : 0 warning the default on a flight controller , 2 Land, 3 Return at critical and Land at emergency. Hover throttle and thrust-to-weight MPC_THR_HOVER 0.5 is the starting value. In flight the hover thrust estimator refines it the hover_thrust_estimate topic; in 1.18 it is always on, and the MPC_USE_HTE switch was removed . text: summary The whole Safety page in QGroundControl and what stands behind it in the PX4 1.18.0 code: why the vehicle will not arm, how disarm differs from kill and from flight termination, how commander picks one action out of a dozen failure flags, how many seconds pass before it, and whether you can take over with the sticks. Separately, Return mode: where it flies, at what altitude the cone formula from rtl.cpp , and how it lands. After the module, given a parameter list and a timeline of events, you can say what the vehicle will do at every second, and find configuration errors before the flight. The practice needs no simulator: working through a ready-made set of parameters and events with a reference, plus a bank of numeric problems. theory What is new here and what is a reference px4-intro names the Safety page parameters and gives the 1.15 → 1.17 and 1.17 → 1.18 migration tables. px4-setup-scratch tests two chains in SITL, RC loss and low battery step 6 . What a position loss means from the estimator's point of view is in nav-resilience. Here are all the conditions at once, the logic of choosing between them, and Return in full. Values and ranges are checked against the v1.18.0 source commander_params.yaml , failsafe.cpp , rtl.cpp ; where a name or default differs in 1.15–1.17, that is stated. Parameters removed in 1.18 are named once, in parentheses, as "before 1.18". QGC screen names depend on the version: in QGC 5.0 this is a single Safety page low battery, RC loss, data link loss, geofence, Return, Land, kill ; newer builds split it into Failsafes and Return & Land. The parameters are the same. Three ways to stop the motors Action What happens to the outputs Reversible What triggers it --- --- --- --- Disarm disarmed values PWM_MAIN_DISn yes, by arming again the RC_MAP_ARM_SW switch, a stick gesture, auto-disarm after landing; in the air it is rejected "Disarming denied: not landed" , except for a command from the transmitter in manual modes with direct throttle Stabilized, Acro : always in 1.18 before 1.18 with COM_DISARM_MAN = 1 Kill disarmed values at once, the vehicle stays armed yes: flip the switch back within 5 s hard-coded in Commander.cpp in 1.18; before 1.18 COM_KILL_DISARM , 0…30 and the motors run again; later, disarm and arm again RC_MAP_KILL_SW threshold RC_KILLSWITCH_TH 0.75 ; the MAN_KILL_GEST_T gesture −1 disabled : both sticks down and outward Flight termination failsafe values PWM_MAIN_FAILn , the DO_PARACHUTE command to the parachute no, only a reboot the Terminate action of any failsafe; the failure detector only with CBRK_FLIGHTTERM = 0 Kill in the air is a crash. It is for the ground and for the first seconds of takeoff. Termination is for vehicles with a parachute: the outputs go to their failsafe values to open the parachute and stop the motors what each function outputs with FAILn = −1 is in px4-outputs-servos . Arming: the sequence 1. Safety button. CBRK_IO_SAFETY = 22027 by default in 1.15 and 1.16 too : no button is required, even if there is one on the GPS module. Set 0 and arming is rejected with "Press safety button first" until you press it. COM_FORCE_SAFETY = 1 restores the lock on every disarm. 2. Prearm. COM_PREARM_MODE : 0 disabled default , 1 after the safety button, 2 always, 5 s after boot. In prearm the servos and other "non-thrust" outputs work; the motors stay stopped output states are in px4-outputs-servos . 3. The arm command. Gesture: left stick down-right throttle < −0.8, yaw 0.9 , right stick centered, held for 1 s hard-coded in ManualControl.cpp in 1.18; before 1.18 COM_RC_ARM_HYST , 100…1500 ms ; MAN_ARM_GESTURE = 1. If RC_MAP_ARM_SW is assigned, the gesture is disabled. COM_ARM_SWISBTN = 1 turns the switch into a button with the same hold. The switch threshold is RC_ARMSWITCH_TH 0.75. 4. No takeoff, disarm. COM_SPOOLUP_TIME + COM_DISARM_PRFLT = 1 + 10 = 11 s after arming without liftoff. A plane has COM_DISARM_PRFLT = −1 rc.fw_defaults so as not to interfere with a hand or catapult launch. 5. Arming is not allowed in Return, Land, Precision Land, Orbit, Follow : change the mode first. Arming: the checks table "why won't it arm" QGC shows the reasons Preflight Fail: … messages ; commander check reruns the checks and prints the result of the previous evaluation, OK or FAILED, and the fresh reasons arrive a second later as messages in QGC and in dmesg . Below are the checks that have a parameter. Check Parameter Default Range / values Note --- --- --- --- --- Arming allowed at all COM_ARMABLE 1 0 / 1 0 locks it during maintenance Accelerometer inconsistency COM_ARM_IMU_ACC 0.7 m/s² 0.1…1.0 recalibrate on a warmed-up board Gyro inconsistency COM_ARM_IMU_GYR 0.25 rad/s 0.02…0.3 the same Compass inconsistency COM_ARM_MAG_ANG 60° 3…180, −1 off external compass orientation Strong magnetic interference COM_ARM_MAG_STR 2 0 off, 1 deny, 2 warning GPS checks EKF2_GPS_CHECK COM_ARM_WO_GPS 1 0 deny, 1 warning, 2 off in 1.15: 0 GPS required, 1 not required Battery charge COM_ARM_BAT_MIN −1 −1…0.9 −1 means BAT_CRIT_THR is the threshold; in 1.15 the default is 0 5 V power, module count COM_POWER_COUNT , CBRK_SUPPLY_CHK 1; 0 0…4; key 894281 the key disables all power checks USB connected CBRK_USB_CHK 197848 0 denies arming with USB the check is off by default CPU / RAM load COM_CPU_MAX , COM_RAM_MAX 95 % −1…100 in SITL COM_CPU_MAX = −1; COM_RAM_MAX appeared in 1.16 SD card none before 1.18 COM_ARM_SDCARD — — in 1.18 always a warning only; on boards without SD the check is removed at build time Hardfault files on the card COM_ARM_HFLT_CHK 1 0 / 1 ESC telemetry COM_ARM_CHK_ESCS 0 0 / 1 only for ESCs with telemetry; since 1.18 with 1, an ESC going offline or an ESC fault including overheating and overspeed in flight counts as a motor failure → COM_ACT_FAIL_ACT Valid mission COM_ARM_MIS_REQ 0 0 / 1 Remote ID COM_ARM_ODID 0 0 off, 1 warning, 2 deny arming, 3 Return, 4 Land, 5 Terminate 3–5 since 1.18 also deny arming and trigger the action on Remote I

summary: Everything in PX4 1.18.0 that sits between a receiver channel and a firmware action: how `rc_update` turns microseconds into −1…+1, at which boundaries the mode channel splits into the six `COM_FLTMODE1…6` slots, how the individual switches work (arm, kill, Return, VTOL transition, landing gear) and

Normalization, slot and switches Step 2. The parameter under the knob Step 3. Acro rate Step 4. Layout and three errors Moving to real hardware
text: summary Everything in PX4 1.18.0 that sits between a receiver channel and a firmware action: how rc_update turns microseconds into −1…+1, at which boundaries the mode channel splits into the six COM_FLTMODE1…6 slots, how the individual switches work arm, kill, Return, VTOL transition, landing gear and what the sign of the RC_ _TH thresholds means, how a channel goes straight to an output through RC_MAP_AUXn , and how a transmitter knob changes a parameter in flight through RC_MAP_PARAM1…3 . After the module you can name the mode slot and the state of every switch from a table of pulses, compute the parameter value under a knob and the Acro rate with the formula from the source, and build a switch layout for your vehicle. The lab needs no hardware and no simulator: four calculations with a reference on the page. theory What the module covers and in what order to read it The module describes one chain: channel → normalization → three consumers sticks, switches, parameter tuning . Read it in this order: normalization and mode slots first, since every calculation rests on them; then the individual switches and the choice of control source; then AUX and knob tuning; at the end, the parameters the pilot feels in the sticks and a layout table for three vehicle types. Arming, kill and failsafe are covered in detail in px4-safety-return , outputs in px4-outputs-servos ; here is only what the transmitter does. The transmitter side is in link-edgetx and link-elrs . The equivalents in other firmware: ap-aux-tune ArduPilot and inav-adjustments INAV . The path of a channel: from receiver to command The receiver driver publishes input_rc : up to 18 channels in microseconds. On every message the rc_update module does three things: 1. normalizes each channel by RCn_MIN/TRIM/MAX/REV into the −1…+1 range rc_channels ; 2. collects the sticks, flaps and six AUX into manual_control_input , and the switch positions into manual_control_switches ; 3. no more than once a second, recomputes the parameters bound to the RC_MAP_PARAMn knobs. Next, manual_control picks the source the RC or a MAVLink joystick, COM_RC_IN_MODE , catches stick gestures and turns a switch position change into an action_request , which commander executes. {{diagram:px4-rc-flow Switches, mode slots and tuning knobs are handled only by rc_update; a MAVLink joystick reaches manual_control bypassing it, so the joystick has none of them.}} Three properties of this chain explain the "strange" behavior: - Switches act on edges. A command goes out only when the position changes. The first packet received is only remembered: an arm switch left on when power is applied does not arm. The mode from the slot is applied at once, though, but only while the vehicle is disarmed. - After a link loss and recovery the positions are remembered again without any action: in the air the mode stays whatever the failsafe chose until you flick a switch. - Protection against garbage. Positions are published when two packets in a row gave the same result; the first 100 ms after the signal returns are ignored; the signal counts as lost if there are fewer than four channels. Switches are processed only when the active control source is the RC. When you fly with the QGC joystick, the slots, kill and the transmitter's arm switch stay silent. Calibration and channel normalization Radio calibration in QGC the "Radio" step in px4-setup-scratch writes: Parameter Default Range Meaning --- --- --- --- RC_CHAN_CNT 0 0…18 how many channels the GCS saw during calibration; 0 means not calibrated RC_MAP_ROLL , RC_MAP_PITCH , RC_MAP_YAW , RC_MAP_THROTTLE 0 0…18 stick channel number; 0 means not assigned RCn_MIN 1000 µs 800…1500 low end of channel n RCn_TRIM 1500 µs 800…2200 center RCn_MAX 2000 µs 1500…2200 high end RCn_REV 1 −1 / 1 −1 flips the sign The RC counts as calibrated when RC_CHAN_CNT 0 and at least one of the four sticks is assigned. The RCn_DZ parameters a per-channel deadzone, 10 µs on channels 1–8 were removed in 1.17: there is now a single deadzone, MAN_DEADZONE , and it is applied in the modes, not in the channel. The formula from rc_update.cpp is piecewise linear through three points min, −1 , trim, 0 , max, +1 : v ≤ MIN → −1 MIN < v ≤ TRIM → v − TRIM / TRIM − MIN TRIM < v ≤ MAX → v − TRIM / MAX − TRIM v MAX → +1 RCn_REV < 0 → the result gets a minus sign The code computes a segment as a = y₂ − y₁ / x₂ − x₁ , b = y₁ − a·x₁ , y = a·v + b . Example: a channel with 1000/1500/2000, pulse 1620 µs. Upper segment: a = 1/500 = 0.002, b = 0 − 0.002·1500 = −3, y = 0.002·1620 − 3 = 0.24 . Channel 988/1500/2012, pulse 1100: a = 1/512, y = 1100 − 1500 /512 = −0.781 . Two caveats. The halves of the scale are scaled separately: if TRIM is not in the middle, the same shift in microseconds gives a different value up and down. And for the throttle channel the firmware itself replaces TRIM with MIN + MAX /2 if QGC wrote TRIM = MIN . Mode slots: RC_MAP_FLTMODE and COM_FLTMODE1…6 RC_MAP_FLTMODE 0 disabled, 1…18 a channel splits one channel into six slots. For each slot the COM_FLTMODEn parameter assigns a mode; −1 the default means the slot is empty, and switching to it does nothing. The code computes the slot number like this v is the normalized value; the result drops the fractional part : slot = int v + 1.05 ·6 + 1/6 / 2.1 + 1/6 + 1, at most 6 The boundaries do not fall at 1/6 of the range: the slot step is 0.35, and the first and last slots are narrower than the rest. Slot Normalized v Pulse at 1000/1500/2000, µs EdgeTX channel weight for the middle of the slot --- --- --- --- 1 below −0.786 up to 1106 −100 % 2 −0.786 … −0.436 1107…1281 −61 % 3 −0.436 … −0.086 1282…1456 −26 % 4 −0.086 … +0.264 1457…1631 +9 % 5 +0.264 … +0.614 1632…1806 +44 % 6 +0.614 and above from 1807 +100 % {{diagram:chart-px4-rc-mode-slots The channel center falls into slot 4: a three-position switch selects slots 1, 4 and 6, a two-position one 1 and 6; slots 2, 3 and 5 are reachable only with a mixed channel.}} Se

Output plan from `timer_config.cpp` Step 2. Servo pulse Step 3. Signs of `CA_SV_CSn_TRQ_*` Step 4. The `REV` mask and three errors Moving to real hardware
text: summary The Actuators screen in QGroundControl and what stands behind it in the PX4 1.18.0 code: how a value travels from the controller to the pin, which functions you can put on an output and under which numbers, what PWM_AUX_MINn / MAXn / DISn / FAILn / CENTn / REV / TIMn mean, why a servo and a DShot motor cannot share a timer group, how MAIN IO differs from AUX FMU , how to describe control surfaces with CA_SV_ , and what PX4 uses instead of relays. After the module you can lay out motors, servos and a camera trigger across outputs from the board's timer_config.cpp and compute a servo pulse the way mixer_module does. The lab needs no hardware and no simulator: an output plan for fmu-v6x, a microsecond calculation, the signs of CA_SV_CSn_TRQ_ and a parameter set with errors; you check the answers against the reference on the page. theory The path of a value: from torque to pulse PX4 has no single "motor mixer". The chain has four links: 1. Controllers output normalized torque on three axes and thrust. 2. control_allocator splits them across the actuators according to the CA_ geometry and publishes two topics: actuator_motors 0…1, −1…1 for reversible ones, NaN means "motor stopped" and actuator_servos −1…+1 . The math of the split is in the ctl-allocation module and is not repeated here. 3. mixer_module is a library inside every output driver. For each output it looks at the output's function, takes the value from the right source and converts −1…+1 into a number for the driver. 4. The driver pwm_out , dshot , px4io , uavcan passes the number to the MCU timer or onto the bus. {{diagram:px4-outputs-pipeline The allocator only knows "Motor 3" and "Servo 2"; which pin they end up on, with what limits and in which arming state, is decided by mixer_module inside the output driver.}} Conversion to microseconds is output_limit_calc_single : - a NaN value → DIS ; - if the output's bit is set in REV , the value changes sign; - the normal case: µs = MIN + v + 1 / 2 · MAX − MIN , rounded lroundf ; in 1.18 already in the driver, PWMOut.cpp ; - since 1.17 , if the function is Servo, Gimbal or Landing Gear Wheel and CENTn is set 800…2200 : two lines, v < 0 → MIN + v + 1 · CENT − MIN , v ≥ 0 → CENT + v · MAX − CENT . For motors the allocator outputs 0…1, and mixer_module first stretches that to −1…+1 2·v − 1 , so 0 % thrust gives MIN , not DIS . Output functions Each output gets one function: the <prefix _FUNCn parameter. The numbers come from output_functions.yaml ; a comment in the file forbids changing them, so they are the same in 1.15–1.17. Function Number Value source Note --- --- --- --- Disabled 0 — no pulse at all Constant Min / Constant Max 1 / 2 constant −1 / +1 the output holds MIN or MAX Motor 1…12 101…112 actuator_motors does not work in prearm Servo 1…15 201…215 actuator_servos surfaces, then tilt servos; before 1.18 Servo 1…8 201…208 Peripheral via Actuator Set 1…6 301…306 MAV_CMD_DO_SET_ACTUATOR the PX4 "relay" Landing Gear 400 the landing_gear topic down −1, up +1 Parachute 401 constant −1 +1 on termination RC Roll / Pitch / Throttle / Yaw / Flaps 402…406 manual_control_setpoint RC channel passthrough RC AUX 1…6 407…412 RC_MAP_AUX1…6 AUX channel passthrough Gimbal Roll / Pitch / Yaw 420…422 gimbal_controls with MNT_MODE_OUT = 0 Gripper 430 the gripper topic release −1, grab +1 Landing Gear Wheel 440 landing_gear_wheel nose wheel IC Engine Ignition / Throttle / Choke / Starter 450…453 internal combustion engine control since 1.16 Camera Trigger 2000 the camera_trigger driver FMU pins only Camera Capture 2032 input: camera feedback FMU pins only PPS Input 2064 PPS input from the GNSS FMU pins only RPM Input 2070 RPM sensor input FMU pins only, since 1.16 The "Servo n" source is not a specific servo but the n-th actuator of type "servo" in the geometry: on a plane Servo 1 is the CA_SV_CS0 surface; on a tiltrotor with four surfaces and two tilt servos, Servo 5 and 6 are the motor tilt the allocator adds the surfaces first, then the tilts . Output parameters The prefix depends on the board. On a board with an IO processor Pixhawk 6X, 6C the IO outputs are PWM_MAIN_ and the FMU outputs are PWM_AUX_ . On a board without IO and with its own firmware Kakute H7, Pixhawk 6U the FMU outputs are called PWM_MAIN_ , and there is no PWM_AUX_ . The exception is boards without IO that run the firmware of an "older sibling" with IO the Pixhawk 6C Mini on fmu-v6c : there the FMU outputs stay PWM_AUX_ , even though the case says MAIN. Go by the tabs of the Actuators screen, not by the case. DroneCAN outputs are the separate UAVCAN_EC_ and UAVCAN_SV_ sets module el-dronecan .
