title: ROS 2 + ArduPilot: AP_DDS and MAVROS, one node, two routes
summary: ArduPilot has two routes into ROS 2. **AP_DDS** is a DDS client built into the firmware (the same principle as uXRCE-DDS in PX4): `/ap/*` topics in ENU and standard ROS types, services for arming and mode changes, velocity control via `/ap/cmd_vel`. **MAVROS** is a MAVLink ↔ ROS bridge that works wi
headings: AP_DDS: how to connect it What AP_DDS publishes and accepts The order of actions in ArduPilot MAVROS Comparing the routes One state machine, two wrappers Step 1. SITL with DDS Step 2. A square via AP_DDS Step 3. The same square via MAVROS Step 4. Comparison What you should get and what to record Step 8. Runnable checks (run by the author)
text: summary ArduPilot has two routes into ROS 2. AP_DDS is a DDS client built into the firmware the same principle as uXRCE-DDS in PX4 : /ap/ topics in ENU and standard ROS types, services for arming and mode changes, velocity control via /ap/cmd_vel . MAVROS is a MAVLink ↔ ROS bridge that works with any firmware and with the full set of MAVLink features, at the cost of an extra layer. This module takes both apart from the source code and documentation, compares them with the PX4 route and shows how the same state machine from the ros2-px4 module flies a square on ArduPilot via AP_DDS. Lab: a square in SITL via AP_DDS, then via MAVROS, and a comparison table of latency and convenience. theory AP_DDS: how to connect it In the firmware there is a DDS client libraries/AP_DDS ; outside, there is a micro-ROS agent micro_ros_agent that exposes the data on the ROS 2 DDS network. - Parameters: DDS_ENABLE = 1 ; UDP transport — DDS_UDP_PORT default 2019 and the agent address DDS_IP0..3 ; serial transport — SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 45 on the port you need. DDS_DOMAIN_ID is the ROS 2 domain. - SITL: a build with DDS support ./waf configure --board sitl --enable-DDS , run sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --enable-DDS , agent: ros2 run micro_ros_agent micro_ros_agent udp4 -p 2019 . - ArduPilot-specific message types come from the ardupilot_msgs package in the ArduPilot repository, Tools/ros2/ardupilot_msgs : Status , GlobalPosition , the services ArmMotors , ModeSwitch , Takeoff . {{diagram:uxrce-scheme The scheme is the same as in PX4: a client in the firmware, an agent on the companion, regular ROS 2 topics outside.}} {{diagram:ros2-ap-dds-boot-race The ArduPilot client pings the agent in batches of 10 × 1 s and writes “exiting” after each, but does not give up: an agent that comes up at the 35th second connects on the next ping.}} What AP_DDS publishes and accepts Topic/service Type Purpose --- --- --- /ap/pose/filtered geometry_msgs/PoseStamped local pose from the EKF relative to home, ENU the firmware writes base_link into header.frame_id /ap/twist/filtered geometry_msgs/TwistStamped velocity /ap/geopose/filtered , /ap/navsat geographic_msgs/GeoPoseStamped , sensor_msgs/NavSatFix global pose, GNSS /ap/battery , /ap/status , /ap/rc sensor_msgs/BatteryState , ardupilot_msgs/Status , ardupilot_msgs/Rc battery; armed, mode, flying, external_control, failsafe /ap/tf_static , /ap/clock , /ap/time tf2, time mounts, clock for sim time /ap/cmd_vel input geometry_msgs/TwistStamped velocity in GUIDED; frame map ENU or base_link /ap/cmd_gps_pose input ardupilot_msgs/GlobalPosition global target in GUIDED /ap/arm_motors , /ap/mode_switch , /ap/prearm_check , /ap/experimental/takeoff services arm, mode Copter mode number: GUIDED = 4, LAND = 9 , pre-arm, takeoff Important: AP_DDS converts ENU ↔ NED itself — for cmd_vel based on header.frame_id map — world ENU, base_link — body . So unlike with PX4, your ROS node lives entirely within ROS conventions. QoS: poses and velocities are BEST_EFFORT, /ap/status and tf_static are RELIABLE + TRANSIENT_LOCAL a BEST_EFFORT subscriber is compatible with both . The order of actions in ArduPilot ArduCopter arms only in a mode that allows arming GUIDED does and only after the pre-arm checks. Takeoff in GUIDED is a separate command the takeoff service = MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF ; without it, the vehicle on the ground ignores horizontal setpoints. The sequence in the node: GUIDED → arm → takeoff alt → velocity/position setpoints → LAND. The velocity setpoint timeout in GUIDED is GUID_TIMEOUT seconds : if cmd_vel stops arriving, the vehicle stops. This is the same “proof of life” principle as Offboard in PX4. {{diagram:ap-dds-guided-seq The order matters: GUIDED, arm, a separate takeoff and only then the cmd_vel stream in the map frame; if it goes silent, the aircraft stops after GUID_TIMEOUT.}} MAVROS MAVROS is a node that holds the MAVLink connection and distributes it across plugins: /mavros/state connection, armed, mode , /mavros/local_position/pose , /mavros/setpoint_position/local , /mavros/setpoint_velocity/cmd_vel , the services /mavros/cmd/arming , /mavros/set_mode , /mavros/cmd/takeoff , /mavros/mission/push , parameters, geofences, full access to any MAVLink message via mavros_msgs/Mavlink . It also converts ENU ↔ NED. Launch: ros2 launch mavros apm.launch fcu_url:=udp://:14550@ connecting to SITL or to a router on the companion . When MAVROS is better than AP_DDS: you need functionality that AP_DDS doesn't have missions, parameters, camera, arbitrary MAVLink messages ; you have a mixed fleet one codebase for ArduPilot and PX4 via MAVLink ; the firmware has no DDS. When AP_DDS is better: fewer layers and lower latency, standard ROS types, no MAVLink traffic on the companion for the ROS part. Comparing the routes PX4 uXRCE-DDS ArduPilot AP_DDS MAVROS --- --- --- --- What's on the wire uORB structs over XRCE DDS client, standard ROS types MAVLink Coordinate frame on the ROS side NED/FRD you convert yourself ENU/FLU the firmware converts ENU/FLU MAVROS converts Version compatibility px4_msgs = PX4 version, _vN suffixes ardupilot_msgs from the same branch MAVLink dialect, stable Feature coverage everything in dds_topics.yaml the /ap/ set, growing almost all of MAVLink External control Offboard, stream 2 Hz GUIDED, GUID_TIMEOUT GUIDED/Offboard via setpoint_ One state machine, two wrappers ap_dds_square.py uses the same OffboardFSM as the PX4 node. The only differences are in the wrapper: observations come from /ap/status and /ap/pose/filtered ENU → NED for the state machine , the “external control mode” = GUIDED, the arm request becomes “GUIDED first, then arm”, after reaching altitude — the takeoff service, the state machine's position setpoints are turned into velocity a P controller limited to 3 m/s on /ap/cmd_vel in the map frame. The safeguard logic and all the state machine tests remain valid. practice Step 1. SITL with DDS bash mkdir -p ~/ardu_ws/src && cd ~/ardu_ws vcs import --recurs

title: Architecture of an onboard ROS 2 application: nodes, lifecycle, watchdog
summary: A single node that does everything works exactly until the first error in its least reliable part — usually perception. An onboard application must survive a camera dropout, a hung neural network and a process restart without losing control of the vehicle. This module gives you an architecture that
headings: Four roles Managed nodes (lifecycle) Freshness watchdog Parameters and configuration Deployment Debugging and profiling Step 1. Watchdog tests Step 2. A four-node skeleton Step 3. Perception and position failures Step 4. Autostart
text: summary A single node that does everything works exactly until the first error in its least reliable part — usually perception. An onboard application must survive a camera dropout, a hung neural network and a process restart without losing control of the vehicle. This module gives you an architecture that makes that possible: a split into bridge, perception, decision and safeguards; managed nodes lifecycle with explicit states; a data-freshness watchdog with OK/DEGRADED/FAILSAFE levels and hysteresis; parameters and configuration; containers and autostart; debugging from bags and profiling. Lab: a four-node skeleton in which killing the perception node puts the system into DEGRADED and losing position puts it into FAILSAFE, verified by tests. theory Four roles Role What it does What it doesn't do Criticality --- --- --- --- Bridge uXRCE-DDS agent / AP_DDS / MAVROS translates the autopilot protocol into topics makes no decisions critical Perception camera/lidar → targets, obstacles, pose doesn't command the vehicle non-critical degradation Decision mission, state machine picks setpoints from targets and state doesn't read sensors directly critical Safeguards watchdog, application geofence, battery watch freshness and limits, have veto power don't plan critical {{diagram:ros2-graph Four roles in the node graph: bridge, perception, decision, safeguards.}} The direction rule: decision subscribes to perception and to the safeguards; the safeguards can stop decision; perception knows nothing about decision. No non-critical node may sit on the “autopilot status → setpoints” path. Managed nodes lifecycle A regular node starts working as soon as it is launched. A lifecycle node rclpy.lifecycle / rclcpp_lifecycle goes through explicit states: unconfigured → inactive → active → finalized , with the transitions configure , activate , deactivate , cleanup , shutdown , each with its own callback that can return an error. What this gives you on board: - configuration open the camera, load the model is separated from operation — you see the error before takeoff; - a node can be “paused” deactivate without killing the process — for example, to turn perception off during landing; - a manager nav2_lifecycle_manager or your own brings the system up in the right order and knows who failed to come up. {{diagram:ros2-lifecycle Lifecycle node states: configuration is separated from operation, pausing doesn't kill the process.}} {{diagram:ros2-executor-gaps In one group with inference the 20 Hz setpoint timer waits: a 400 ms hang breaks the setpoint stream for 400 ms; inference in its own group on a second thread leaves an even 50 ms step.}} Freshness watchdog Every input message has a maximum allowed age. The watchdog examples/ros2-docker/.../watchdog.py , no ROS inside stores the time of the last message for each input and outputs a single system level: - OK — everything is fresh; - DEGRADED — a non-critical input targets from the camera is stale: the mission continues, the function tracking is suspended; - FAILSAFE — a critical input autopilot status, pose is stale: decision stops commanding and requests a hold/landing. Hysteresis: an input counts as recovered only if it stays fresh continuously for recover_s for example, 1 s — otherwise a “flickering” camera will switch tracking on and off several times a second. The watchdog is a separate node with its own timer; it doesn't command the autopilot itself, it publishes the level that decision subscribes to. The last line of defense is the autopilot itself Offboard/GUIDED timeouts : if the whole application crashes, the vehicle still switches to a safe mode. Parameters and configuration Everything that differs between vehicles camera offsets, thresholds, rates, topic names goes into YAML parameters passed through launch. The add_on_set_parameters_callback callback validates new values range, type and can reject them — that way an operator in the field can't set a threshold of 10 m instead of 1 m. Secrets VPN keys, cloud tokens don't go into ROS parameters, but into files with access permissions or into the service's environment variables. Deployment - Container : an image with ROS 2, the dependencies and your package; image version = onboard software version. docker compose with restart: unless-stopped and network_mode: host DDS discovery inside containers on a bridge network is harder . - Autostart : a systemd service that runs ros2 launch or compose after the network is up and after the serial port appears After= , BindsTo=dev-ttyAMA0.device . - Logs : ros2 bag record of the key topics, split into files --max-bag-duration , --max-bag-size ; automatic deletion of old files with --max-bag-files exists only in newer rosbag2 versions, in Humble/Jazzy you have to clean up disk space yourself + journald; after an incident — download the bag together with the autopilot log. - Time : chrony/NTP on the companion, synchronization with the autopilot TIMESYNC/uXRCE — otherwise the bag and the autopilot log won't line up. Debugging and profiling - Replaying a bag into the decision and safeguard nodes module ros2-basics is the main tool. - ros2 topic hz/bw/delay — rate, bandwidth and latency relative to header.stamp . - Profiling: top / htop per process, py-spy record for Python nodes, ros2_tracing LTTng for callback latencies; on a Jetson — tegrastats CPU/GPU/temperature . - Executor: heavy callbacks the neural network go into a separate callback group MutuallyExclusiveCallbackGroup with a MultiThreadedExecutor , otherwise the 20 Hz setpoint timer will wait for inference to finish. practice Step 1. Watchdog tests bash cd examples/ros2-docker/ws/src/uav_ros2_labs python -m pytest -q test/test_watchdog.py Work through test_hysteresis_on_flapping_input : why the level is still DEGRADED after 0.5 s of recovery. Step 2. A four-node skeleton Build a uav_app package with the nodes bridge_monitor subscribes to autopilot status/pose , perception_stub publishes targets at 10 Hz, c

title: Navigation and obstacle avoidance: maps, planners, setpoints
summary: The autopilot knows how to fly to a point. To fly to a point **without crashing into things**, you need a map, a planner and a chain from the plan to setpoints — and an honest understanding of what the autopilot can already do on its own (ArduPilot: BendyRuler and Dijkstra, PX4: collision prevention
headings: What the autopilot can do without you Map representations Global planning Local planning and reaction Nav2 and drones From plan to setpoints Step 1. A* with tests Step 2. Braking distance Step 3. Flying around an obstacle in Gazebo Step 4. Unknown space
text: summary The autopilot knows how to fly to a point. To fly to a point without crashing into things , you need a map, a planner and a chain from the plan to setpoints — and an honest understanding of what the autopilot can already do on its own ArduPilot: BendyRuler and Dijkstra, PX4: collision prevention and where you need your own logic on the companion. This module covers map representations occupancy grid, costmap, 3D voxels , global and local planning A , Dijkstra, reactive methods , obstacle inflation and path smoothing, the role of Nav2 and why it's “ground-based”, and how a plan turns into GUIDED/Offboard setpoints with velocity and altitude limits. Lab: A on a grid with tests, then flying around an obstacle in Gazebo using lidar data. theory What the autopilot can do without you - ArduPilot : proximity sensors PRX1_TYPE , including MAVLink OBSTACLE_DISTANCE → simple avoidance stop/slide in Loiter, AVOID_ENABLE , AVOID_MARGIN and object avoidance in automatic modes: OA_TYPE = 1 BendyRuler reactive, searches for a way around , 2 Dijkstra over polygon geofences, a global path around known no-go zones , 3 a combination. Parameters OA_MARGIN_MAX , OA_BR_LOOKAHEAD . - PX4 : collision prevention in Position mode CP_DIST — the minimum distance, from OBSTACLE_DISTANCE /ROS 2 ObstacleDistance , limits velocity toward the obstacle. This works and has been flight-tested — start with it. You need your own navigation on the companion when: the map has to be built and stored indoor flight, a forest , the path must be globally optimal in an unknown environment, or there is a higher-level goal survey an object, fly to a point found by the camera . Map representations - Occupancy grid , 2D: a cell holds the probability of being occupied in ROS nav_msgs/OccupancyGrid : 0–100, −1 — unknown . It's updated from rangefinder/lidar rays: along the ray — free, at the end — occupied log-odds, to accumulate evidence . - Costmap : occupancy + inflation + layers static, obstacles, geofences . Inflating by the vehicle radius plus a margin lets you plan for a point rather than for a body. - 3D : OctoMap an octree of voxels , ESDF/TSDF a field of distances to the nearest obstacle: Voxblox, nvblox . For flight at different altitudes a 2D grid isn't enough, but 2D at a fixed altitude is a good start. - Unknown = occupied by default: fly only where you've already seen that it's free. Otherwise the planner will route the path “through a wall” it hasn't seen yet. Global planning A\ on a grid: a search for the shortest path from start to goal with a heuristic an estimate of the remaining distance . If the heuristic never overestimates it's admissible , the path is optimal. For an 8-connected grid — the octile distance dx + dy + √2 − 2 ·min dx, dy . No “cutting the corner” diagonally between two occupied cells. Dijkstra is A with a zero heuristic slower, but the same solution . For large 3D spaces — sampling-based methods RRT , PRM . The raw A path is a cell-by-cell “staircase”. Smoothing shortcut : drop intermediate points as long as the straight segment is free; then apply the dynamics limits velocity, acceleration, jerk when building the trajectory. Local planning and reaction The global plan is built from a map that is already out of date by flight time. The local layer reacts to what is visible right now: vector fields VFH , dynamic window DWA , MPC, or simply “stop and replan”. Rates: global — 0.5–2 Hz, local — 10–20 Hz, setpoints — 20–50 Hz. The layers should be separate nodes module ros2-app-arch , and the last line of defense is the autopilot simple avoidance / collision prevention and the geofence. {{diagram:planning-layers Navigation layers and their rates; the last line of defense is the autopilot.}} Nav2 and drones Nav2 is the ROS 2 navigation stack: the BT navigator behavior trees , planners NavFn, Smac , controllers DWB, MPPI , costmap layers, recovery. It's designed for ground robots 2D, non-holonomic models . For a multicopter at constant altitude you can use it holonomic model, cmd_vel → GUIDED/Offboard velocities , but 3D planning, altitude and flight dynamics are beyond its scope. Many drone projects take the costmap layers and the BT ideas from Nav2, and write their own planner or take one from research stacks for example, EGO-Planner, Fast-Planner — for the experienced . From plan to setpoints 1. A path in the map frame ENU → intermediate points spaced 1–3 m apart. 2. Limits: the maximum velocity near obstacles depends on the sensor range and the braking distance: v ≤ √ 2·a·d , altitude within a corridor above the ground by rangefinder and below the geofence , yaw along the direction of travel if the camera must look forward. 3. Sending: PX4 — TrajectorySetpoint position and/or velocity, NED — convert! , ArduPilot — /ap/cmd_vel ENU, frame map or position targets via MAVROS. 4. Execution monitoring: deviation from the path threshold → stop and replan; goal unreachable → hold and notify the operator. practice Step 1. A with tests bash cd examples/ros2-docker/ws/src/uav_ros2_labs python -m pytest -q test/test_grid_planner.py Read grid_planner.py : inflation, the octile heuristic, the no-corner-cutting rule, shortcut. Add a test: the path with inflation is longer than the path without it, but not shorter than the straight line. Step 2. Braking distance For a vehicle with a maximum deceleration of 3 m/s² and a lidar with a reliable range of 8 m, calculate the maximum safe velocity with a 2 m margin and a 0.3 s reaction delay. Compare with the simple avoidance parameters of your firmware. python """ros2-nav lab: Dijkstra vs A vs weighted A , inflation, shortcut, unknown cells, log-odds. Run from examples/ros2-docker/ws/src/uav_ros2_labs: python3 nav_lab.py""" import heapq, math, random, sys sys.path.insert 0, "." from uav_ros2_labs.grid_planner import inflate, line_free, path_length, shortcut def search grid, s, g, w : """8-connected grid search; w = heuristic weight 0 Dijkstra, 1 A , 1 weighted A .""" d

title: From ROS 1 to ROS 2: reading old projects and porting them
summary: ROS 1 Noetic reached end of support in May 2025, but half of the open drone projects, papers and tutorials are on ROS 1: MAVROS 1, catkin workspaces, XML launch files, `rospy`. This module teaches you to read such a project quickly (“what matters here and what depends on what”), to know how ROS 1 co
headings: How ROS 2 differs in substance How to read a ROS 1 project in 30 minutes Port or bridge Typical code replacements (Python) MAVROS 1 → MAVROS 2 Step 1. Reading the project Step 2. Reference data Step 3. Porting Step 4. Report Step 5. A worked port on a synthetic flight (done, without ROS)
text: summary ROS 1 Noetic reached end of support in May 2025, but half of the open drone projects, papers and tutorials are on ROS 1: MAVROS 1, catkin workspaces, XML launch files, rospy . This module teaches you to read such a project quickly “what matters here and what depends on what” , to know how ROS 1 concepts map to ROS 2, to decide whether to port or run side by side through a bridge, and to port a small package. Lab: porting a ROS 1 node to ROS 2 while preserving its behavior, verified on recorded data. theory How ROS 2 differs in substance ROS 1 ROS 2 What it changes --- --- --- roscore master — a central name server no master, DDS discovery no single point of failure; you need domains/discovery limits TCPROS/UDPROS DDS with QoS you have to think about QoS module ros2-basics rospy , roscpp rclpy , rclcpp a different API, but the same ideas catkin, catkin_make / catkin build ament, colcon build a different build, package.xml format 3 XML launch .launch Python/XML/YAML launch .launch.py logic in the launch file parameters in a global server parameters per node rosparam → ros2 param against a specific node rosbag .bag ros2 bag SQLite3/MCAP converters exist rosbags tf tf2 also existed in ROS 1 almost unchanged nodelets components composable nodes several nodes in one process without copying MAVROS 1 MAVROS 2 mavros in ROS 2 the same plugins, different service names/QoS How to read a ROS 1 project in 30 minutes 1. The root : package.xml / CMakeLists.txt — dependencies which sensors, whether it's MAVROS, whether it's OpenCV . 2. Launch files launch/ .launch — what gets started, with which parameters and remaps. This is the “system diagram”. 3. Nodes scripts/ .py , src/ .cpp : find init_node , Subscriber , Publisher , Service , Timer / Rate . Draw the graph: what it listens to, what it publishes. 4. Parameters config/ .yaml , rospy.get_param — what is configurable. 5. Messages msg/ , srv/ — custom types. 6. MAVROS specifics : /mavros/setpoint_ , /mavros/set_mode , /mavros/cmd/arming — where the project controls the vehicle and in which coordinate frame. The result is a node graph as in ros2-basics and a list of external dependencies. With it, you can see what the port will cost. Port or bridge - ros1_bridge — a bidirectional bridge for topics/services between ROS 1 and ROS 2 with both running. It requires a compatible build the same message types on both sides , historically Noetic + Foxy/Humble from source. Now that Noetic support has ended, this is a temporary solution. - Porting — the right path for living code. The order: messages → library code without ROS pull it out! → nodes → launch → tests on recorded data. - Running ROS 1 in a container — to “see how it used to work” and to record reference data before porting. Typical code replacements Python ROS 1 rospy ROS 2 rclpy --- --- rospy.init_node "n" rclpy.init ; node = Node "n" rospy.Subscriber "/t", T, cb node.create_subscription T, "/t", cb, qos rospy.Publisher "/t", T, queue_size=10 node.create_publisher T, "/t", 10 rospy.Rate 20 ; while not rospy.is_shutdown : ... rate.sleep node.create_timer 0.05, tick ; rclpy.spin node rospy.get_param "~alt", 5.0 node.declare_parameter "alt", 5.0 ; node.get_parameter "alt" .value rospy.ServiceProxy "/s", S req cli = node.create_client S, "/s" ; cli.call_async req rospy.Time.now node.get_clock .now rospy.loginfo ... node.get_logger .info ... The main shift in thinking: the while loop with rate.sleep is replaced by a timer and callbacks , and a synchronous service call inside a callback by an asynchronous one, otherwise the node will block itself the same executor services the response . {{diagram:ros2-distro-timeline Support windows by year: in November 2026 Humble until May 2027 , Jazzy, Lyrical and the outgoing Kilted are alive; Noetic and the bridge to it are already past the line.}} {{diagram:ros2-sync-call-deadlock A synchronous cli.call in a callback takes the executor's only thread: there is no one to deliver the reply, and timer ticks are lost; call_async returns at once, and setpoints go out every 50 ms.}} MAVROS 1 → MAVROS 2 The topic names are mostly the same /mavros/state , /mavros/local_position/pose , /mavros/setpoint_position/local , but: telemetry QoS is sensor data; some services and parameters have been renamed; launch is ros2 launch mavros apm.launch fcu_url:=... or px4.launch . For PX4 in ROS 2, people usually move from MAVROS to uXRCE-DDS module ros2-px4 ; for ArduPilot — to AP_DDS where its features are enough module ros2-ardupilot . {{diagram:ros1-migration What to do with an old ROS 1 project: a temporary bridge, a port, MAVROS 2, or a rewrite based on its ideas.}} practice Step 1. Reading the project Take an open ROS 1 drone project for example, the offboard example from the PX4 documentation for ROS 1 / MAVROS, or any repository with MAVROS 1 . In 30 minutes, draw the node graph, the list of dependencies and where the project controls the vehicle. Step 2. Reference data If you can, run the project in a ROS 1 Noetic container with SITL and record a rosbag of the node's inputs and outputs. If not, use a bag from open sources or synthetic inputs. Step 3. Porting Port one node up to ~200 lines : the logic without ROS goes into a separate module with pytest tests like offboard_fsm.py , the node is a thin rclpy wrapper. Convert the bag to the ROS 2 format the rosbags package: rosbags-convert and check that the outputs of the ported node match the reference ones. Step 4. Report A table: what was replaced, how many lines of logic became testable without ROS, what behavior differences were found usually QoS and time . The lab counts as done when you have the graph of the original project, the ported node with logic tests and a comparison of the outputs on the same data. Step 5. A worked port on a synthetic flight done, without ROS Steps 1–4 need a real project and ROS; this step runs on any machine with Python 3 and shows the whole cycle on a small node. The “descent guard” node

title: PID
summary: Proportional-integral-derivative controller: P reacts to the current error, I accumulates the steady-state error, D damps fast changes.

title: Feedforward (FF)
summary: A contribution to the motor command taken directly from stick movement, before any error appears. Speeds up the start of a move.

title: Setpoint
summary: The desired angular rate (from sticks and rates) that the PID compares the gyro readings against.

title: Gyro
summary: A three-axis angular rate sensor. The main stabilization sensor, read thousands of times per second.

title: T/W (thrust-to-weight)
summary: The ratio of the maximum thrust of all motors to the takeoff weight. 2:1 is the minimum for controlled flight.

title: Mixer
summary: A table that converts throttle, roll, pitch and yaw into a command for each motor depending on the frame type.

title: KV
summary: Motor RPM per volt with no load. Low KV for big props, high KV for small ones.

title: ESC
summary: Electronic speed controller: commutates the phases of a brushless motor based on commands from the FC.

title: DShot
summary: A digital FC → ESC protocol: a 16-bit packet with a checksum, no calibration. The number is the speed in kbit/s.

title: Bidirectional DShot
summary: DShot with a return channel: the ESC reports motor eRPM. The basis of the RPM filter.

title: RPM filter
summary: A bank of narrow notch filters at each motor's rotation frequency and its harmonics, driven by bidirectional DShot data.

title: Dynamic notch
summary: An automatic notch filter that finds peaks in the gyro spectrum and suppresses them.

title: D-term
summary: The derivative term of the PID. Sensitive to noise: with poor filtering it heats up the motors.

title: Blackbox
summary: Betaflight log: gyro, setpoint, PID, motors, RC at a high rate, for post-flight analysis.

title: Bounce-back
summary: Gyro rebound in the opposite direction after the stick stops; a metric of underdamping.

title: Entry lag
summary: Time from the start of a setpoint move until the gyro reaches 50% of it. The "sluggish on the sticks" metric.

title: Propwash
summary: Shaking when the vehicle flies into its own turbulent downwash, usually during descent.

title: diff all
summary: A Betaflight CLI command that outputs only the differences of the configuration from the defaults. The unit for storing a config.

title: Resource remap
summary: Reassigning a function (motor, UART, LED) to another board pad via the CLI.

title: craft_name
summary: The craft name in the Betaflight config. A reliable drone identifier for scripts instead of a COM port number.

title: UART
summary: Serial port: receiver, GPS, VTX, telemetry. Wires crossed over, common GND.

title: Inverted signal
summary: UART with inverted logic levels: idle is low. The SBUS standard; F4 can't invert in hardware.

title: SBUS
summary: A receiver → FC protocol from Futaba/FrSky: 100 kbaud, 8E2, inverted, one-way.

title: CRSF
summary: The TBS Crossfire and ExpressLRS protocol: a regular UART, full duplex, channels and telemetry over a single port.

title: ELRS (ExpressLRS)
summary: An open-source radio control system: choice of packet rate, telemetry ratio, 2.4 GHz and 900 MHz.

title: Packet rate
summary: The number of control packets per second. Higher means lower latency and worse sensitivity.

title: LQ (link quality)
summary: Fraction of successful packets out of the last 100. RSSI is the power margin; you need both together.

title: VTX
summary: Video transmitter. Controlled by the FC over SmartAudio/Tramp/MSP according to the VTX table.

title: vtxtable
summary: The table of VTX bands, channels and power levels in Betaflight. FACTORY sends the channel number, CUSTOM sends the frequency.

title: OSD
summary: Telemetry overlaid on the video in the goggles: voltage, time, link, warnings.

title: Arming disable flags
summary: Betaflight flags that prevent arming (RXLOSS, THROTTLE, ANGLE, MSP…). Visible via status and in the OSD.

title: Failsafe
summary: Behavior on link loss. In Betaflight: Stage 1 (guard time) and Stage 2 (DROP, AUTO-LAND, GPS_RESCUE).

title: BEC
summary: An onboard voltage regulator (5/9/12 V) for the FC, receiver, camera and VTX.

title: C rating
summary: A battery's rated discharge current as a multiple of its capacity. Usually inflated; trust the log and the internal resistance.

title: Voltage sag
summary: The voltage drop under current across the battery's internal resistance: I × R.

title: Cloud Build
summary: Building Betaflight firmware on the server for a selected set of options (defines).

title: Target
summary: A firmware variant for a specific board: MCU, gyro, pins.

title: ArduPilot
summary: An open-source autopilot: Copter, Plane, Rover, Sub. Navigation, missions, Lua, companion.

title: FRAME_CLASS / FRAME_TYPE
summary: ArduPilot parameters: frame type (Quad=1, Hexa=2, Octa=3, OctaQuad=4, Tri=7) and layout (X=1, Plus=0…).

title: Pre-arm checks
summary: ArduPilot checks before arming: calibrations, EKF, link, parameters. A PreArm message is a hint, not an obstacle.

title: GCS
summary: Ground control station: Mission Planner, QGroundControl, MAVProxy. Talks to the FC over MAVLink.

title: SITL
summary: Software In The Loop: the real firmware running on a PC with a physics simulator in place of sensors.

title: MAVProxy
summary: ArduPilot's command-line ground station in Python. Launched together with SITL.

title: pymavlink
summary: Python MAVLink library: connection, reading messages, commands. Low level, everything visible.

title: MAVSDK
summary: A high-level SDK on top of MAVLink (C++, Python): arm(), takeoff(), telemetry subscriptions.

title: MAVLink
summary: The FC ↔ GCS/companion protocol: packets with a message ID, system_id, component_id and a CRC based on the XML definition.

title: Heartbeat
summary: A MAVLink message sent once per second by every participant: type, mode, armed state. No heartbeat, no link.

title: COMMAND_ACK
summary: MAVLink command acknowledgment with a result. A command without an ACK check is hope, not control.

title: GUIDED
summary: An ArduPilot mode in which position/velocity targets are set by an external source (GCS, companion).

title: NED
summary: North-East-Down coordinate frame: Z points down, climbing is negative Z.

title: EKF
summary: Extended Kalman filter: fuses IMU, GPS, baro and compass into a single estimate of position, velocity and attitude.

title: Lane switching
summary: EKF switching between cores (per IMU) to a healthier one.

title: DCM
summary: A simple complementary attitude filter in ArduPilot. A backup to the EKF; works without GPS and compass.

title: DataFlash
summary: ArduPilot's onboard binary log (.bin): VIBE, ATT, CTUN, BAT, ERR, XKF and hundreds of other messages.

title: VIBE
summary: An ArduPilot log message with per-axis vibration and an accelerometer clipping counter. Below 30 is normal.

title: Mission
summary: A list of commands for AUTO mode: NAV (where to go), DO (what to do), CONDITION (when).

title: Home
summary: Copter's arming point. RTL returns here, not to the pilot.

title: Lua scripts (ArduPilot)
summary: Onboard scripts: switches, sensors, scenarios. Require ≥2 MB of flash, do not run on F4.

title: Fault injection
summary: Deliberate injection of failures (motor, sensor) in SITL to test the behavior of the vehicle and the pilot.

title: OctaQuad (X8)
summary: Four arms with two coaxial motors each. Fault tolerance at the cost of ~15% thrust loss.

title: QuadPlane
summary: VTOL in ArduPlane: takes off like a multirotor, flies like a plane.

title: Tilt-rotor
summary: VTOL with tilting motors. Q_TILT_* parameters, TiltMotor* output functions.

title: SERVOn_FUNCTION
summary: The function of an FC output in ArduPilot: motor, tilt servo, control surface. A mismatch with the wiring is dangerous.

title: Companion computer
summary: An onboard computer for vision, scenarios, networking. It advises via GUIDED; the FC decides.

title: mavlink-router
summary: A MAVLink router: one UART, many consumers over UDP/TCP.

title: systemd service
summary: A way to start a script on a Linux companion automatically and restart it after a crash.

title: EdgeTX
summary: Open-source radio firmware (TX16S and others) with Lua scripts and an AUX port in Lua mode.

title: ESP32
summary: A microcontroller with Wi-Fi and BLE: peripherals, MAVLink bridge, radio companion.

title: Kt (torque constant)
summary: Motor torque per amp of current, Kt = 60/(2π·KV) N·m/A; low KV = high torque per amp.

title: FSPL
summary: Free-space signal loss: 20·log(d) + 20·log(f) + 32.44 dB; +6 dB per doubling of range.

title: Link budget
summary: The sum of power, antenna gains and losses minus FSPL versus receiver sensitivity; margin ≥ 10–15 dB.

title: SWR
summary: Standing wave ratio: the fraction of power reflected by the antenna back into the transmitter; 1.0 is ideal, ≤ 2 is acceptable.

title: Circular polarization
summary: The field rotates (RHCP/LHCP); less sensitive to orientation and reflections; never mix RHCP and LHCP.

title: Low-ESR capacitor
summary: An electrolytic/polymer capacitor on the power bus that absorbs voltage spikes caused by wire inductance during ESC switching.

title: Smoke stopper
summary: A current limiter (bulb/resistor) in series with the positive lead at first power-up: a short circuit won't burn the board.

title: Hard iron / soft iron
summary: Compass errors: a constant offset from magnetized parts (hard iron) and field distortion from ferromagnetic materials (soft iron); calibrated with offsets and a matrix.

title: Bias
summary: The sensor output at zero input; for a gyro it integrates into attitude drift; estimated by the EKF.

title: Quaternion
summary: Four numbers with unit norm describing attitude without gimbal lock; the firmware standard.

title: Complementary filter
summary: Fusing the gyro (high frequencies) with the accelerometer/compass (low frequencies) using fixed coefficients; a special case of the Kalman filter.

title: Innovation
summary: The difference between a measurement and the filter's prediction; if the normalized innovation exceeds the gate, the measurement is rejected.

title: Kalman gain
summary: The weight given to a measurement versus the prediction, computed from the covariances; the adaptive counterpart of the complementary filter's K.

title: HDOP
summary: A multiplier on GNSS horizontal error due to satellite geometry; < 1 is excellent, > 2.5 is poor.

title: RTK
summary: Real-Time Kinematic: carrier-phase corrections from a base station give centimeter accuracy; requires a pair of dual-frequency receivers.

title: Optical flow
summary: The angular rate of the image moving under the camera; combined with rangefinder altitude and the gyro, it gives linear velocity.

title: EK3_SRC
summary: EKF3 source sets (position, velocity, altitude, heading): GPS, baro, rangefinder, optical flow, external navigation; switchable in flight.

title: Phase margin
summary: Degrees short of −180° at the loop's unity-gain frequency; delay eats into it linearly with frequency.

title: Damping ζ
summary: A parameter of a second-order loop: ζ ≈ 0.7 gives ~5% overshoot; low ζ means bounce-back and ringing.

title: Aliasing
summary: Frequencies above fs/2 showing up at false frequencies after sampling; fixed with an anti-aliasing filter and full-rate logging.

title: Group delay
summary: The delay a filter adds to the useful signal; PT1 ≈ 1/(2π·fc).

title: Welch's method
summary: Spectrum estimation by averaging FFTs over overlapping windows; resolution fs/nperseg.

title: Overshoot
summary: Response overshoot past the setpoint after a step, in percent; related to damping.

title: TECS
summary: Total energy control for a wing: throttle sets the total energy, the elevator sets the split between altitude and airspeed.

title: Stall speed
summary: V_s = √(2mg/(ρ·S·C_Lmax)); in a turn it grows as 1/√cos φ.

title: Stability margin
summary: The distance of the CG ahead of the neutral point as a fraction of MAC; 5–15% is normal.

title: Harmonic notch (ArduPilot)
summary: Harmonic notch filter `INS_HNTCH_*` with tracking by throttle, ESC telemetry or FFT.

title: AUTOTUNE
summary: Automatic tuning of rate/angle gains from a series of "twitches" on an axis in hover.

title: FMEA
summary: Failure Modes and Effects Analysis: failure → effect → detection → RPN → mitigation → verification.

title: Dead reckoning
summary: Dead reckoning from inertial sensors and wind without external measurements; accurate for seconds to tens of seconds.

title: DroneCAN
summary: A protocol over CAN for autopilot peripherals: nodes with IDs, standard messages, 120 Ω terminators.

title: CAN arbitration
summary: Resolving simultaneous transmission: a dominant 0 wins, the lower ID wins without losing time.

title: DMA
summary: Direct memory access: peripherals exchange data with memory without the CPU (DShot, SPI gyro, UART).

title: Jitter
summary: Variation in a task's actual period; grows with locking and long interrupts.

title: Work queue (PX4)
summary: Prioritized work queues in which most PX4 modules run on NuttX.

title: Traceability matrix
summary: A requirement ↔ test ↔ result table; empty cells are open requirements.

title: ADR
summary: Architecture Decision Record: context, options, decision, consequences.

title: VIO
summary: Visual-inertial odometry: position and attitude from features in frames and the IMU; drift of 0.5–2% of distance traveled.

title: ExternalNav
summary: External navigation source for EKF3 (VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE/ODOMETRY), `EK3_SRC* = 6`.

title: Precision / Recall
summary: Fraction of correct detections among those found / fraction found among the true ones; the confidence threshold trades one for the other.

title: Glass-to-glass latency
summary: Time from an event in front of the camera to its appearance on the screen; measured with a timer in the frame.

title: Offboard (PX4)
summary: Control mode from a companion with a setpoint stream ≥ 2 Hz; timeout COM_OF_LOSS_T.

title: Spot welding
summary: Spot welding nickel strip to 18650/21700 cells; soldering to cells is not allowed.

title: BMS
summary: Battery management system: voltage/current/temperature protection and balancing; cutting off discharge in flight is dangerous.

title: Thrust stand
summary: Measuring a motor's thrust/current/power with a prop; checking the build sheet's calculations against reality.

title: Engineering folder
summary: Requirements with IDs, tests and a project changelog are a mandatory part of every capstone project.

title: Troubleshooting tree
summary: A "symptom → branch → measurement → cause" sequence of checks for finding a fault.

title: Near miss
summary: A near miss with no damage; the main source of improvements to the field protocol.

title: L1 navigation
summary: ArduPlane's guidance algorithm: the vehicle aims at a point on the route line a distance L1 ahead and commands lateral acceleration based on the angle to it. The NAVL1_PERIOD sets how aggressive it is.

title: Pure pursuit
summary: "Pursuit" guidance: a point at lookahead distance L is chosen on the path, and the vehicle turns toward it with curvature 2·sin(η)/L. A larger L is smoother but cuts corners.

title: S-curve (jerk-limited)
summary: A jerk-limited velocity profile: acceleration ramps up smoothly instead of stepping. This is how ArduPilot (WP_JERK) and PX4 build trajectories.

title: Chirp
summary: A test signal whose frequency rises smoothly from f₀ to f₁. The response to it is used to build the loop's frequency response.

title: Coherence
summary: A measure from 0 to 1 of how much of the output is linearly explained by the input at a given frequency. Below ~0.6, a point on the frequency response is not worth using.

title: AP_Periph
summary: ArduPilot firmware for DroneCAN peripheral nodes: GPS, compass, airspeed sensor, ESC adapter on a separate STM32.

title: Node ID
summary: A node's number on the DroneCAN bus (1–127). Set statically or assigned by the dynamic node allocation (DNA) server on the autopilot.

title: Conducted interference
summary: Noise conducted along power and ground wires (ripple from ESCs and converters), not through the air. Fixed with an LC filter and a low-ESR capacitor at the source.

title: DRC
summary: Design Rule Check: automatic check of a board for clearances, trace widths and vias against the fab's rules. Zero DRC errors is the condition for sending it to production.

title: Gerber
summary: The set of board layer files (copper, solder mask, silkscreen, outline) plus a drill file: what the fab receives.

title: Clamp meter
summary: An instrument that measures current from the magnetic field around a wire without breaking the circuit. DC requires a Hall-effect clamp.

title: Fault tolerance
summary: The vehicle's ability to survive the failure of a single component (motor, BEC, receiver) and land under control. A quadcopter does not have it for motors; a hexa and an X8 can, given spare thrust, well-designed power and a firmware response verified in SITL or on a bench.

title: Cold solder joint
summary: A cold solder joint: dull, lumpy, with poor wetting. Holds on the bench and fails under vibration.

title: Strain relief
summary: Securing a wire near a solder joint or connector so bending and vibration don't break the strands at the joint.

title: Config diff
summary: A line-by-line comparison of two parameter dumps. A config in git plus a diff before flight shows what changed since last time.

title: Weight budget
summary: A table of the weights of all components versus the target takeoff weight. Determines the thrust-to-weight ratio and flight time before you buy anything.

title: Ohm's law
summary: U = I·R: the voltage across an element equals the current times the resistance. Power P = U·I.

title: Bluejay
summary: Open-source firmware for ESCs on 8-bit EFM8 BB21 and BB51 (BB1 only up to version 0.18.1), the successor to BLHeli_S, with bidirectional DShot for the RPM filter.

title: AM32
summary: Open-source firmware for 32-bit ARM ESCs (STM32, AT32, GD32, etc.), a replacement for BLHeli_32.

title: Frame resonance
summary: The frequency at which a frame or arm oscillates on its own. If it matches the motor speed frequency, vibration grows and the gyros get noisy.

title: Moment of inertia
summary: A measure of resistance to rotation: J = Σ m·r². Mass far from the center makes the vehicle sluggish in roll and pitch.

title: Remote ID
summary: Broadcasting the ID, coordinates and altitude of the vehicle and the pilot during flight (Bluetooth / Wi-Fi). A regulatory requirement in many countries.

title: MAVLink signing
summary: A MAVLink 2 mechanism: every packet is signed with a shared secret key and a timestamp. Rejects foreign commands and replays of intercepted ones.

title: Scheduler
summary: The part of the firmware that runs tasks at a given rate and priority: gyro loop, PID, RX, OSD. The first thing you look for when reading the source.

title: Position hold
summary: GPS position hold mode: the vehicle counters wind drift by itself. In INAV it is NAV POSHOLD.

title: INAV
summary: A Cleanflight fork with navigation: position hold, RTH, missions, wings and rovers.

title: Logic condition (INAV)
summary: A line of the INAV Programming Framework: a condition on flags and values whose result triggers an action or feeds other conditions.

title: Waypoint
summary: A mission waypoint: coordinates, altitude and an action (fly-through, loiter, RTH, landing).

title: Elevons
summary: The two control surfaces of a flying wing that combine elevator and ailerons: deflected together for pitch, in opposite directions for roll.

title: OpenIPC
summary: Open-source firmware for IP cameras that turns them into a digital FPV transmitter over Wi-Fi adapters in packet injection mode.

title: SiK
summary: Open-source firmware for 433/868/915 MHz telemetry modems with frequency hopping; used by 3DR Radio and RFD900.

title: Rotation matrix
summary: An orthogonal 3×3 matrix with determinant 1 that transforms a vector from one coordinate frame to another. Its inverse equals its transpose.

title: Gimbal lock
summary: Loss of one degree of freedom in Euler angles at ±90° pitch: roll and yaw become the same axis. That is why quaternions are used internally.

title: Natural frequency ωn
summary: The frequency at which an undamped second-order system oscillates. Together with ζ it sets the settling time and overshoot.

title: Euler method
summary: The simplest numerical integration: x(t+dt) = x(t) + f(x)·dt. Unstable with a large step, hence the loop-rate requirements.

title: Covariance
summary: A measure of how two quantities vary together. The EKF covariance matrix describes how confident the filter is in each component of the state.

title: Component ID
summary: A component's number within a vehicle in MAVLink (autopilot 1, camera 100, gimbal 154, etc.). Together with the system ID it forms the address.

title: System ID
summary: The vehicle's number on a MAVLink network (1–255). Two vehicles on the same network must have different ones: in ArduPilot 4.7 the parameter is MAV_SYSID.

title: CRC_EXTRA
summary: A byte computed from the message definition and mixed into the MAVLink CRC. Catches dialect version mismatches between sender and receiver.

title: MAVLink dialect
summary: XML description of a message set (common, ardupilotmega, development). Both sides must be built from the same dialect.

title: UDP broadcast / unicast
summary: Ways of delivering MAVLink over a network: broadcast goes to everyone on the subnet, unicast goes to a single address. Over 4G/NAT and L3 VPNs (WireGuard, Tailscale, OpenVPN tun) only unicast works; broadcast only passes through L2 tunnels (ZeroTier, OpenVPN tap).

title: MAVROS
summary: A ROS package that bridges MAVLink to ROS topics and services. Superseded by uXRCE-DDS for PX4; for ArduPilot it remains alongside AP_DDS.

title: MAVLink microservice
summary: A protocol on top of messages for one task: parameters, missions, commands, FTP. Defines the exchange order and retries on packet loss.

title: Root cause
summary: The cause lies in the process, not in a person or a part: why the failure was possible at all. You eliminate it, or the crash repeats with a different part.

title: Vehicle log
summary: A record of flight time, battery cycles, replacements and incidents for each vehicle. The basis for life-based scheduled maintenance.

title: Density altitude
summary: The altitude in the standard atmosphere with the same air density as right now. Heat and high elevation raise it, and props produce less thrust.

title: Gimbal Manager
summary: A role in the MAVLink Gimbal v2 protocol: the component that parses requests from the GCS and companion and commands the gimbal (Gimbal Device).

title: OBSTACLE_DISTANCE
summary: A MAVLink message with 72 sectors of distances to obstacles around the vehicle. ArduPilot and PX4 use it to brake and avoid.

title: INT8 quantization
summary: Converting network weights and activations from float to 8-bit integers. Speeds up inference 2–4× on NPU/TensorRT at the cost of a small accuracy loss; verified on a validation set.

title: Camera matrix K
summary: Camera intrinsics: focal lengths f_x, f_y in pixels and the principal point c_x, c_y. Maps a ray to a pixel and back; found by checkerboard calibration.

title: LANDING_TARGET
summary: A MAVLink message the companion uses to send the autopilot the angular offset or position of a marker for precision landing.

title: GSD
summary: Ground Sample Distance: how many centimeters of ground one image pixel covers. GSD = altitude · pixel size / focal length.

title: Image overlap
summary: The fraction of shared area between adjacent frames along and across the route. For photogrammetry it is usually 70–80 % along and 60–70 % across.

title: Image-plane error
summary: The target's offset from the image center (or a set point) in pixels or normalized coordinates. The outer tracking loop turns it into a velocity command.

title: Jetson Orin
summary: A family of NVIDIA modules with an Ampere GPU (Orin NX/AGX also have DLA accelerators) for onboard inference. A typical companion for PX4 and ArduPilot.

title: uORB
summary: PX4's internal publish-subscribe message bus between modules. uXRCE-DDS exposes selected uORB topics to ROS 2.

title: Cascaded controller
summary: Nested loops: position commands velocity, velocity commands angle, angle commands angular rate. The inner loop is tuned first and made several times faster than the outer one.

title: Lifecycle node
summary: A ROS 2 node with explicit unconfigured → inactive → active states and transitions between them. Gives controlled startup and shutdown of an onboard application.

title: AP_DDS
summary: The eProsima Micro XRCE-DDS client built into ArduPilot: publishes state to ROS 2 and accepts commands without MAVLink; on the ROS 2 side it is served by an agent (`micro_ros_agent` or Micro XRCE-DDS Agent).

title: QoS
summary: Quality of Service in ROS 2: reliability, queue depth, durability. A publisher and a subscriber with incompatible QoS don't connect, and there is no error: the subscriber simply receives nothing (the log only shows an "incompatible QoS" warning).

title: tf2
summary: The ROS library for the tree of coordinate frames over time: map → odom → base_link → camera. Answers where the sensor was at the moment a frame was captured.

title: ros1_bridge
summary: A bridge that forwards topics between ROS 1 and ROS 2 during a migration. Requires both distributions to be installed side by side.

title: Costmap
summary: A costmap in Nav2: cells weighted by traversability, built from obstacles with an inflation margin. Paths are planned on it.

title: uXRCE-DDS
summary: The PX4 bridge to ROS 2: a client in the firmware and the Micro XRCE-DDS Agent on the companion pass uORB topics as ROS 2 topics.

title: SDF
summary: Simulation Description Format: XML description of a Gazebo world and models: links, joints, sensors, plugins.

title: Flight Review
summary: PX4's web service for analyzing ULog logs: setpoint tracking, vibration, spectrograms and step-response estimation with no software to install.

title: UART port (TX/RX)
summary: Serial port: TX of one device goes to RX of the other. In Betaflight each UART is assigned a function on the Ports tab.

title: Ground loop
summary: A closed loop through the common wire via two ground paths, where noise current is induced. Fixed by joining grounds at a single point.

title: VLOS / BVLOS
summary: Visual Line of Sight: flying within the pilot's direct sight, the baseline requirement of most regulations. BVLOS (beyond visual line of sight) requires a separate authorization or category.

title: Figure of merit (FM)
summary: Hover efficiency of a rotor: the ratio of the ideal momentum-theory power T^1.5/√(2ρA) to the power actually consumed. System FM is computed from the electrical power in the motor table; for small props with a motor and ESC it is 0.5–0.6.

title: Disk loading
summary: Thrust divided by the total prop disk area, N/m². Hover power per unit of thrust grows as its square root: the larger the disk for the same mass, the more grams per watt.

title: Mass fraction
summary: The share of the takeoff mass taken by a group (frame, battery, payload, powertrain). It lets you close the budget: m = mass without the frame / (1 − frame fraction).

title: Load cell
summary: An elastic element with a Wheatstone bridge of strain gauges: the output is proportional to the force and the excitation voltage (sensitivity in mV/V, typically 1.0 mV/V at full scale). The basis of a thrust stand and of scales.

title: HX711
summary: A 24-bit ADC for a load-cell bridge: channel A with a gain of 128 or 64, channel B with 32; 10 or 80 samples/s; serial output over the DOUT/PD_SCK lines. Holding PD_SCK high for longer than 60 µs puts the chip into power-down.

title: Neutral point
summary: The CG position at which the plane's pitching moment does not depend on the angle of attack (dCm/dα = 0). The CG is placed ahead of it by the static margin: 5–15 % MAC, 5–10 % for a flying wing.

title: Horizontal tail volume coefficient (V_h)
summary: V_h = S_h·l_h/(S·MAC): the horizontal tail area times its moment arm, divided by the wing area and MAC. The larger it is, the farther aft the neutral point; trainers and FPV planes typically have 0.4–0.7.

title: Drag polar
summary: C_D as a function of C_L, usually C_D = C_D0 + k·C_L², k = 1/(π·e·AR). It gives the maximum lift-to-drag ratio, the maximum-range speed V_md and the minimum-power speed V_mp.

title: Effectiveness matrix
summary: A 6×N matrix B: column i holds the moments and forces that motor i produces at a unit command. In PX4 it is computed from CA_ROTORn_* as M = CT·(p × a) − CT·KM·a, F = CT·a; the mixer is its (pseudo)inverse.

title: Pseudoinverse
summary: A generalization of the matrix inverse to non-square and singular B: it gives the minimum-norm u that solves B·u = target (or the closest one in the least-squares sense). PX4 builds the mixer this way for any geometry and recomputes it when a motor fails.

title: Mixer desaturation
summary: Shifting the motor commands along one axis's vector to bring them back into the 0…1 range. The order sets the priority: in PX4 thrust, then roll/pitch, with yaw clipped first; airmode allows raising thrust to keep control authority.

title: vbat_scale / ibata_scale
summary: Betaflight voltage and current sensor scales. Voltage is directly proportional to vbat_scale (new = old × V_multimeter / V_FC); current is inversely proportional to ibata_scale, in mV per 10 A (new = old × mAh_FC / mAh_charger).

title: motor_output_reordering
summary: A Betaflight 4.5 array: mixer motor i is output on the MOTOR pad with index reordering[i]. It fixes the motor order without resoldering or timer remapping; the Reorder motors dialog writes it.

title: Maiden hover
summary: The first liftoff of an assembled aircraft to 1–1.5 m for 60 s in ANGLE with Blackbox recording and abort criteria set in advance: flipping on liftoff, oscillations, hover throttle outside 12–60 %, hot motors.

title: vbat_scale (INAV)
summary: INAV voltage divider coefficient (1100 = an 11:1 divider × 100). Readings are directly proportional to it: new = old × V_multimeter / V_INAV.

title: current_meter_offset
summary: INAV current sensor zero offset; per the source, in units of 0.1 mV, it removes offset/scale amps from the reading. Calibrated against the idle current: new = old + (I_INAV − I_ammeter) × scale.

title: MSP RX
summary: Receiving RC channels over the MSP protocol (MSP_SET_RAW_RC) instead of a radio receiver; in INAV SITL, a way to feed stick input from a script or a ground station (receiver_type = MSP).

title: Servo autotrim
summary: Automatic adjustment of the servo centers (servo mid) in level flight: INAV averages the control surface deflections and saves the new centers on disarm. The SERVO AUTOTRIM mode or feature FW_AUTOTRIM.

title: Control surface throw
summary: The angle a control surface deflects from neutral at full stick. On a wing it is measured with a ruler at the trailing edge: h = c·sin δ.

title: Loiter (circling)
summary: A wing flying a circle of a set radius around a point instead of hovering. The required bank: tan φ = V²/(g·R); it is limited by nav_fw_bank_angle.

title: ArduPilot bootloader (.apj / _with_bl.hex)
summary: A small program at the start of flash that accepts new firmware over USB. The first time, it is written together with the firmware as a _with_bl.hex file via DFU; after that you update with an .apj file from Mission Planner or QGroundControl.

title: MOT_SPIN_ARM / MOT_SPIN_MIN
summary: ArduCopter motor output fractions: SPIN_ARM is the spin right after arming, SPIN_MIN is the lower limit of controllable thrust (at least SPIN_ARM + 0.03). Set from the spin-up threshold in Motor Test.

title: MOT_THST_HOVER
summary: ArduCopter hover thrust as a fraction of maximum (≈ 1/(T/W)); learned in flight with MOT_HOVER_LEARN = 2. Working range 0.2–0.5.

title: ULog
summary: PX4 onboard log format (.ulg): records selected uORB topics with timestamps, parameters and messages; analyzed with Flight Review or pyulog.

title: SIH (Simulation-In-Hardware)
summary: A simplified physics simulator built into PX4: the model runs inside the firmware (on a PC as SITL or on the flight controller itself), with no Gazebo and no external visualizer.

title: Control allocation (CA_*)
summary: The PX4 block that distributes the required moments and thrust among the actuators according to the given geometry: CA_ROTOR_COUNT, the CA_ROTORn_PX/PY positions and the CA_ROTORn_KM rotation direction.

title: adjrange
summary: A Betaflight CLI command for in-flight adjustments: adjrange <slot 0–29> 0 <range channel> <start> <end> <function> <adjustment channel> [<center> <scale>]. The function number is the position in defaultAdjustmentConfigs[] + 1; in 4.5 it differs from the enum from 25 on. Changes live in RAM until saved.

title: Step and absolute adjustment
summary: The two adjrange modes. Step (center = 0): the channel above mid_rc + 200 gives +1, below mid_rc − 200 gives −1, repeating every 500 ms. Absolute (center ≠ 0): value = center + (rc − 1500)·scale/500 on every channel change, with a jump when the slot activates.

title: vtx (VTX on a switch)
summary: The Betaflight CLI command vtx <slot 0–9> <aux> <band> <channel> <power> <start> <end>: sets the VTX band, channel and power index by the position of an AUX channel. Slots are checked on every RC frame and the slot that fired last time is skipped, so overlapping slots take turns overriding each other; band and channel change only until the first arm, power always.

title: Actual rates
summary: The Betaflight rate model (the default since 4.3): rc_rate×10 is the center sensitivity, srate×10 the maximum in °/s, expo changes only the shape of the curve between them.

title: Super rate
summary: A parameter of the Betaflight rate model: divides the angular rate by (1 − |x|·s), raising the end of the stick curve; together with RC rate it sets the maximum 200·r/(1 − s).

title: RC smoothing
summary: A PT3 filter on setpoint, throttle and feedforward at the PID loop rate; in auto mode the cutoff = max(15, ⌊f_rx·1.5/(1 + factor/10)⌋) Hz from the measured packet rate.

title: Runaway takeoff prevention
summary: Betaflight protection against a “taz” on the first takeoff: disarm and the RUNAWAY flag if |pidSum| ≥ 600 while rotating faster than 15 °/s (yaw 50 °/s) for longer than 75 ms. It is disabled until reboot after 500 ms of confident flight (throttle ≥ 20 % with stick input or ≥ 40 %).

title: Yaw spin recovery
summary: A Betaflight mode for a yaw spin above the threshold (AUTO: max_yaw + max(25 %, 200 °/s), 500–1950 °/s): it zeroes roll/pitch and I, gives all thrust to stopping the rotation, and exits 100 °/s below the threshold after 20 ms.

title: PREARM
summary: A Betaflight mode that is a second arming key: with a range set, arming is possible only with PREARM on, and it must be toggled after every arm (NOPREARM flag). In 2025.12 the toggle can be waived with prearm_allow_rearm.

title: MSP DisplayPort
summary: The protocol by which the flight controller tells digital goggles (DJI, Walksnail, HDZero) over a UART which character to draw in which cell of the OSD grid. In Betaflight 4.4+ it is the VTX port function (MSP + DisplayPort): mask 131073 = MSP + VTX_MSP; in ArduPilot SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 42 and OSD_TYPE = 5.

title: HD OSD canvas (osd_canvas)
summary: The size of the HD OSD character grid in columns and rows. In Betaflight 4.5 the default is 53×20, but the goggles report their own (HDZero 50×18) with MSP_SET_OSD_CANVAS. The firmware clamps elements outside the canvas to the edge instead of scaling them.

title: VTX_MSP (port function 131072)
summary: Bit 1 << 17 of the serial mask in Betaflight: VTX control and DisplayPort over MSP. On its own, without MSP or Serial RX, it is invalid — isSerialConfigValid() resets the whole port config to defaults.

title: NTRIP
summary: Networked Transport of RTCM via Internet Protocol: an HTTP-like protocol in which a caster (usually port 2101) serves RTCM correction streams by mount point; the client is the GCS or the rover's modem.

title: Moving baseline (GPS yaw)
summary: An RTK mode where the base sits on the same frame: the rover solves the vector between the antennas to centimeter accuracy, and its direction is the aircraft's heading. In ArduPilot GPS1_TYPE 17 / GPS2_TYPE 18 and EK3_SRC1_YAW 2; the heading is available on the ground, without moving.

title: Survey-in
summary: A u-blox base station mode (CFG-TMODE-MODE) in which the receiver averages its position up to a set duration and accuracy limit; it gives centimeter relative RTK accuracy but only meter-level absolute accuracy.

title: AGL (height above terrain)
summary: Above Ground Level: height above the ground under the aircraft, h_AGL = h_AMSL − h_terrain. In a mission it is frame MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_TERRAIN_ALT (10); ArduPilot takes the terrain height from the onboard database (TERRAIN_ENABLE) or a rangefinder. Not to be confused with height above the takeoff point.

title: Terrain database (SRTM)
summary: A grid of ground heights at TERRAIN_SPACING (100 m) that the ArduPilot flight controller requests from the GCS (TERRAIN_REQUEST / TERRAIN_DATA) and stores on the SD card in APM/TERRAIN. It is a surface model with a typical error of ±10 m: it barely sees trees and buildings.

title: Surface tracking
summary: Holding height above the surface with a rangefinder in ArduCopter Loiter, AltHold and PosHold (SURFTRAK_MODE: 0 — off, 1 — ground, 2 — ceiling). When the rangefinder goes out of range, the target silently returns to barometric altitude.

title: UWB (ultra-wideband beacons)
summary: Ultra-Wideband: a tag on the aircraft measures ranges to fixed anchors by pulse time of flight, and the position is found by trilateration with 10–30 cm accuracy in line of sight. In ArduPilot: BCN_TYPE (1 Pozyx, 3 Nooploop), no more than 4 anchors, EK3_SRC1_POSXY = 4; beacons give no heading, a compass is needed.

title: Motion capture (mocap)
summary: A system of infrared cameras (OptiTrack, Vicon, Nokov) that gives a rigid body's pose from reflective markers to millimeter accuracy at 100+ Hz. It reaches the autopilot as VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE / ODOMETRY (EK3_SRC1_* = 6) or as pseudo-GPS through GPS_INPUT; the main traps are axes, latency and jumps.

title: EKF origin
summary: The lat/lon/alt point from which the EKF computes its local NED position. With GPS it is set automatically at the first fix; without GPS the GCS or a bridge sets it with SET_GPS_GLOBAL_ORIGIN once per boot, otherwise the pre-arm “AHRS: waiting for home”.

title: Map matching
summary: Absolute localization by camera: a frame rectified for altitude and heading is matched by features against a georeferenced orthophoto; a homography with RANSAC maps the frame center to a map pixel and that to latitude and longitude. Unlike visual odometry, the error does not grow with distance traveled.

title: VPR (visual place recognition)
summary: Coarse localization by image: every map tile is compressed into one global descriptor (NetVLAD, AnyLoc), and the frame looks for the k nearest. It answers “which tile does this look like”; only a following geometric check with local features gives a coordinate and confidence.

title: GPS_INPUT
summary: MAVLink message #232: an external source poses as a GNSS receiver (lat/lon, velocity, fix_type, horiz_accuracy, ignore_flags). ArduPilot accepts it with GPSn_TYPE = 14; the receiver is considered healthy at an average rate of about 5 Hz, and horiz_accuracy becomes the EKF3 measurement noise.

title: Glass-to-command (vision loop latency)
summary: The time from light hitting the sensor until the autopilot accepts the command based on that image: exposure + readout + capture + undistort + detector + tracker + geolocation + transport. It is measured with timestamps at every stage; it, not FPS, limits the gain of the tracking loop.

title: Target lock and reacquisition
summary: The rule for choosing one track among several confirmed ones: keep the ID while the track is alive, and after a loss take a new one only within a radius of the last position. Without it the tracker switches to a similar stationary object (a rock, a shadow) that collects more hits than the moving target.

title: TIMESYNC
summary: MAVLink message #111: the companion sends ts1 (its own nanoseconds, tc1 = 0), the autopilot replies with the same ts1 and its own tc1. Clock offset = tc1 − (ts1 + RTT/2); this is how frame timestamps are converted into the autopilot's time_boot_ms to match them with ATTITUDE and the log.

title: nvpmodel (Jetson power mode)
summary: A Jetson utility that sets the power ceiling: how many CPU cores are on and the maximum CPU, GPU and memory frequencies. The Jetson Nano has MAXN (10 W, 4 cores, GPU 921.6 MHz) and 5 W (2 cores, GPU 640 MHz); the Orin Nano Super has 15 W, 25 W and MAXN_SUPER. The budget applies to the CPU and GPU rails, not to the whole board with peripherals.

title: tegrastats
summary: The standard Jetson utility: at a set interval it prints a line with memory, the load and frequency of every CPU core, GPU load and frequency (GR3D_FREQ), zone temperatures and power per rail in mW (POM_5V_IN on the Nano, VDD_IN on the Orin). A GPU frequency drop under full load is a sign of throttling.

title: TensorRT engine
summary: A neural network execution plan compiled for a specific GPU and TensorRT version (an .engine file), built from ONNX at the chosen FP32, FP16 or INT8 precision. It does not move between boards: you move the ONNX and build the engine on the target Jetson.

title: WS2812 (addressable LED)
summary: An LED with a built-in driver: 5 V, GND and one 800 kHz data line, 24 bits per LED (GRB), chained DIN → DOUT. Up to ~60 mA at full white; the input reads “1” from 0.7·VDD, so 3.3 V from the FC is marginal. In Betaflight: `resource LED_STRIP`, the pin's timer and DMA, up to 32 LEDs (64 with LED_STRIP_64).

title: DShot beacon
summary: Motor beeping: Betaflight sends the ESC the DShot command BEACON1…5 (`beeper_dshot_beacon_tone`) on the RX_LOST and RX_SET conditions of the `beacon` command (both off by default in 4.5). Never while armed or with the motors running, no earlier than 1.2 s after disarming, no more often than ~0.5 s (RX_SET) or ~1 s (RX_LOST).

title: LED strip profile (RACE / BEACON / STATUS)
summary: Betaflight `ledstrip_profile`: STATUS — every LED per its `led` line (functions and overlays), RACE — the whole strip in one color (`ledstrip_race_color`, BLACK = by the VTX frequency), BEACON — blinking twice a second by default. In RACE/BEACON an active failsafe and the BEEPER mode switch on blinking 4 times a second. From the radio: function 30 in `adjrange`.

title: MCU timer (output group)
summary: A hardware counter of an STM32/AT32 (TIMx) with a shared prescaler and period and up to 4 channels on pins. All outputs of one timer run at one frequency and one protocol: a 50 Hz servo and DShot on the same timer are incompatible. The map: timer show, timer <pin> list.

title: SERVO_TILT
summary: A Betaflight feature: two gimbal servos (pitch, roll) and the CAMSTAB mode. In CAMSTAB the pulse = middle + rate·angle_in_tenths_of_a_degree/50, i.e. rate/5 µs per degree of frame tilt.

title: Channel forwarding
summary: The Betaflight feature CHANNEL_FORWARDING: receiver AUX channels, starting from channel_forwarding_start, are output to the remaining servo outputs as is, without the min/max limits of the servo command.

title: TTFF (cold, warm, hot start)
summary: Time to first GNSS fix. Cold: no ephemerides or time (u-blox M8/M10: 26–29 s); warm: the ephemerides are stale (> 4 h); hot: fresh ephemerides in BBR with V_BCKP alive (1 s).

title: PDOP
summary: The multiplier of the GNSS 3D position error due to satellite geometry. Betaflight 4.5 shows and uses PDOP specifically (not HDOP): around 1.0 is good.

title: gpspassthrough
summary: A Betaflight CLI command: a direct USB ↔ GPS UART bridge until reboot, so that u-center can read and configure the module through the flight controller.

title: Turtle mode (crash flip)
summary: The Betaflight FLIP OVER AFTER CRASH mode (aux id 35): when arming with the mode on, the FC sends the ESCs DShot command 21 (reverse), and the stick spins the motors of one side backwards to flip the aircraft off its back. DShot only; to exit: disarm, switch off, arm again.

title: Dynamic idle
summary: A Betaflight controller that uses bidirectional DShot eRPM to keep the slowest motor at no less than dyn_idle_min_rpm × 100 rpm by raising the lower limit of all motors (up to 15 %, up to 5 % on the ground). With it, dshot_idle_value is ignored; without telemetry it is silently off.

title: Launch control
summary: A Betaflight mode for a race start (aux id 49): after arming in ACRO the aircraft holds the tilt set by the stick with the I term scaled by launch_control_gain until throttle exceeds launch_trigger_throttle_percent (20 %).

title: Acro (Rate mode)
summary: The Betaflight mode without self-leveling (ANGLE and HORIZON off): the stick sets the angular rate, and with the stick released the aircraft keeps its current tilt.

title: USB Joystick (EdgeTX)
summary: A mode in which an EdgeTX radio connects to a computer over USB as a HID joystick for a simulator: in Classic, channels 1–8 go to axes and 9–32 to buttons.

title: Mode 2
summary: A radio stick layout: left stick — throttle and yaw, right stick — pitch and roll; the throttle stick is not spring-centered.

title: BNF / PNP / RTF
summary: Ways an aircraft is sold. BNF (bind-and-fly): built and set up, with a receiver; you bind your own radio. PNP: without a receiver. RTF: a kit with a radio, goggles and a charger; the radio and goggles of such a kit usually do not suit your next aircraft.

title: Hall-effect gimbal
summary: A radio stick assembly where a contactless magnetic sensor measures the position instead of a wiper potentiometer: it does not wear out, and there is less signal jitter at center.

title: Multi-protocol module (4-in-1, MPM)
summary: A radio module with four chips (CC2500, NRF24L01, A7105, CYRF6936) running the MULTI-Module firmware: FrSky, FlySky, Spektrum DSM and other older protocols. It does not support ExpressLRS.

title: Whoop
summary: A 65–85 mm micro copter with ducted props, usually on a single cell (1S): 15–25 g without the battery, 0702–0802 motors at 22,000–30,000 KV, 3–7 minutes of flight. The main platform for indoor flying and practice.

title: 5-in-1 AIO
summary: A micro board that combines the flight controller, four ESCs, a receiver and an analog VTX. It weighs 3–5 g; the price is few free UARTs, often no flash for Blackbox, and a failure of one part means replacing the whole board.

title: ELRS SPI receiver
summary: An ELRS radio chip soldered onto the flight controller and connected over SPI, without its own MCU or firmware: Betaflight runs the protocol. In 2025.12 it is ELRS 3 (OTA version 3) and does not link with a 4.x transmitter; 2026.6 has the ELRSV4 build option.

title: Logical switch (EdgeTX)
summary: A virtual radio switch L01…L64: a condition on sources (a<x, AND, Sticky, Edge) with a delay and an AND switch; on a telemetry sensor it is false while there is no telemetry.

title: Special function (EdgeTX)
summary: A radio action triggered by a switch or logical switch: Play Value, Play Track, SD Logs, Override, Vario, Screenshot and others; up to 64 per model plus global ones.

title: Receiver No. (EdgeTX)
summary: A model number 0–63 that the radio reports to the RF module; ExpressLRS uses it for Model Match, and a copied model inherits the original's number.

title: osd_video_system (INAV)
summary: An INAV setting that sets the OSD character grid and the output method: AUTO/PAL/NTSC — analog (30×16 or 30×13), HDZERO — 50×18, AVATAR, BFHDCOMPAT and DJI_NATIVE — 53×20, DJIWTF — 60×22, BF43COMPAT — 30×16. Unlike Betaflight, the goggles do not report the grid: with a wrong value, elements near the edge are not visible.

title: OSD layout (osd_layout)
summary: One of the four sets of OSD element positions in INAV (0 — main, 1–3 — alternative, enabled by the OSD ALT 1–3 modes or operation 32 of the programming framework). CLI line: osd_layout <layout> <element> <column> <row> <V|H>; it is stored as the word x | y << 6 | 0x2000.

title: Custom OSD element (osd_custom_elements)
summary: An INAV OSD element built by the user from three parts (text up to 15 characters, an icon, a number from a GVAR or a logic condition) with a visibility condition. INAV 8–9 has eight of them, numbered 147–149 and 154–158 in the layout.

title: Mixer profile
summary: An INAV set of the platform type, the mmix and smix tables and the transition settings. There are two profiles (one on F411); the MIXER PROFILE 2 mode switches them in flight, and mixer_control_profile_linking ties control profiles to them. The basis of VTOL in INAV.

title: Transition mixing (MIXER TRANSITION)
summary: An INAV mode for accelerating a VTOL before the profile change: input 38 of the smix rules becomes 500, and motors with a throttle value from −1.05 to −2.0 in mmix output −throttle × 1000 µs regardless of the stick. It does not work in navigation modes other than ALTHOLD.

title: Flaperons
summary: Ailerons that also work as flaps: both deflect down by a common angle on top of the roll command. In INAV: has_flaps = ON, the FLAPERON mode and input 14 in smix with the value flaperon_throw_offset.

title: OSD backend (OSD_TYPE)
summary: How ArduPilot outputs the OSD: 1 — the MAX7456 chip draws into analog video, 5 — MSP DisplayPort (the goggles draw the cells), 3 — MSP telemetry for older DJI, 2 — the SITL window, 4 — no output. OSD_TYPE2 sets a second simultaneous backend.

title: OSDn_TXT_RES
summary: The character grid of screen n in ArduPilot with MSP DisplayPort: 0 — 30×16, 1 — 50×18, 2 — 60×22. Set per screen; element coordinates are not recalculated when the grid changes.

title: Pit mode
summary: The minimum power mode of a video transmitter for setting up on the ground near other pilots. In ArduPilot it is bit 0 of VTX_OPTIONS; bits 1 and 2 clear it on arming and restore it on disarming.

title: Flight termination (PX4)
summary: The irreversible failsafe action in PX4: the outputs go to their failsafe values (PWM_MAIN_FAILn), and the parachute gets a deploy command; it is cleared only by a reboot. Triggering it from the failure detector is allowed by writing CBRK_FLIGHTTERM = 0.

title: Circuit breaker (CBRK_*)
summary: A PX4 parameter that disables a check or protection only when an exact key number is written (for example CBRK_IO_SAFETY = 22027); protection against accidental disabling.

title: Rally point (safe point)
summary: An alternative landing point set in the flight plan; the PX4 Return mode picks the nearest of the points RTL_TYPE allows: home, a rally point or the start of the mission's landing sequence.

title: IOMCU
summary: The second microcontroller on Pixhawk and Cube family boards: it drives the MAIN 1–8 outputs, the receiver input and the safety button. In ArduPilot its output groups are fixed (1–2, 3–4, 5–8), DShot on them is enabled with BRD_IO_DSHOT, and BLHeli passthrough does not work.

title: EDT (Extended DShot Telemetry)
summary: An extension of bidirectional DShot: besides ESC rpm it sends temperature, voltage, current and a load figure over the signal wire. In ArduPilot it is enabled with values 3 and 4 of SERVO_DSHOT_ESC and logged as EDT2; it needs ESC firmware with EDT support.

title: RELAYn_PIN
summary: The GPIO pin number driven by relay n in ArduPilot (before 4.5: RELAY_PIN, RELAY_PIN2…). The number comes from GPIO(g) in the board's hwdef; if the pin belongs to a PWM output, that output needs SERVOn_FUNCTION = -1.

title: Aux function (RCx_OPTION)
summary: An action bound to a radio channel in ArduPilot with the RCx_OPTION parameter: a mode, arming, a relay, motor stop and so on. The channel is read as a three-position switch (LOW below 1200 µs, HIGH above 1800 µs), the function is called on a position change after a 200 ms delay and logged as AUXF.

title: Debounce
summary: The time a new switch position must stay unchanged before the system reacts to it. In ArduPilot it is 200 ms for aux channels and the mode channel (SWITCH_DEBOUNCE_TIME_MS); a shorter pulse is not executed.

title: Transmitter tuning (TUNE)
summary: Tuning one ArduCopter parameter with a radio knob in flight: a channel with RCx_OPTION = 219, the parameter number in TUNE, the values at the ends of travel in TUNE_MIN and TUNE_MAX. The value depends linearly on the knob position and is written only to RAM and to the PTUN log; in Plane the TUNE_CHAN and TUNE_PARAM parameters do the same job.

title: Output function (PX4, `PWM_*_FUNCn`)
summary: A number that links a physical output to the source of its value: 101–112 Motor, 201–208 Servo, 301–306 Peripheral via Actuator Set, 400 Landing Gear, 401 Parachute, 407–412 RC AUX, 430 Gripper, 2000 Camera Trigger.
