The list is output_functions.yaml; mixer_module converts the value to microseconds by MIN/MAX/CENT/REV.

title: `PWM_AUX_REV` (reverse mask)
summary: A PX4 bit mask: bit n−1 flips the sign of output n's normalized value before conversion to microseconds, mirroring the range around (MIN + MAX)/2 or CENT. This is how servo mechanics are matched to the rule “positive command — trailing edge up” without touching the signs of CA_SV_CSn_TRQ_*.

title: `PWM_AUX_CENTn` (servo center, PX4 1.17)
summary: The neutral of a PWM servo in microseconds on an FMU output; −1 means a straight line from MIN to MAX. If set, −1…0 maps to MIN…CENT and 0…+1 to CENT…MAX, and the firmware zeroes CA_SV_CSn_TRIM. Conversion: CENT = MIN + (MAX − MIN)/2 · (1 + TRIM).

id: g:CLI batch mode (batch start / batch end)
title: CLI batch mode (batch start / batch end)
summary: An INAV CLI mode that counts errors in pasted lines: `diff` and `dump` start their output with `batch start`, and if there is at least one `### ERROR` line the first `save` does not write the configuration but prints the error count. It protects against saving a half-applied file.

title: Control profile (control_profile)
summary: One of three sets of PIDs, navigation gains, rates, TPA and EZ Tune in INAV (126 settings in 9.1.0). Selected with `control_profile 1…3` (`profile` in INAV 7), by the battery profile (`use_control_profile`), or following the mixer profile (`mixer_control_profile_linking`). A plain `diff` prints only the active one.

title: Full chip erase
summary: A Configurator flasher option: before writing the firmware, the whole microcontroller flash including the configuration area is erased. The INAV release notes require it when changing the major version (7 → 8, 8 → 9). After it the board starts with defaults and the configuration is restored from `diff all`; Configurator 9.1 offers automatic restore only when flashing with this option.

title: V-tail
summary: A tail of two angled surfaces that together work as both the elevator and the rudder. In ArduPlane the halves are assigned the functions VTailLeft (79) and VTailRight (80); the firmware mixes the commands: left = (elevator + rudder) × MIXING_GAIN, right = (elevator − rudder) × MIXING_GAIN.

title: ARSPD_RATIO
summary: The airspeed sensor scale in ArduPilot: V = √(Δp × ARSPD_RATIO), where Δp is the differential pressure in pascals. The default is 2; after calibration it is usually 1.5–3.0. GPS correction: new = old × (V_GPS / V_indicated)²; ARSPD_AUTOCAL enables in-flight fitting.

title: Short and long failsafe (ArduPlane)
summary: The two stages of a plane's response to losing radio control. The short one starts right after the loss is detected (RC_FS_TIMEOUT plus 0.2 s) and is chosen by FS_SHORT_ACTN, usually CIRCLE; the long one comes FS_LONG_TIMEOUT after the last good frame and is chosen by FS_LONG_ACTN, usually RTL. The action depends on the mode at the moment of the event; FS_SHORT_TIMEOUT was removed in 4.7.

title: EZ Tune (INAV)
summary: The ten ez_* settings in an INAV control profile and the ez_tune.c formulas that, with ez_enabled = ON, rewrite the PIDs, rates, expo and filters from the slider positions at every boot. It is not autotuning: manual PID values are not kept while EZ Tune is on.

title: Control Derivative (mc_cd_*)
summary: A term of the INAV multirotor controller proportional to the rate of change of the setpoint: kCD = mc_cd / 7270. The counterpart of feedforward in Betaflight: it speeds up the stick response and does not affect disturbance rejection.

title: Toilet bowl (spiraling in POSHOLD)
summary: The aircraft circling around the hold point with a growing radius. The cause is a heading error (compass) that points the position correction past the point; navigation PIDs do not fix it. In the air: switch to ANGLE immediately.

title: Port parameter (PX4, `*_CONFIG` / `*_CFG`)
summary: A driver parameter that holds the UART number: 101–103 TELEM 1–3, 201–202 GPS 1–2, 300 RC, 401 EXT2, 1000 Ethernet, 0 — driver off. The rc.serial boot script starts the driver on that port at SER_<port>_BAUD; a reboot is needed, and two drivers cannot share a port.

title: `MAV_n_RATE` (MAVLink stream limit)
summary: The outgoing stream limit of a MAVLink instance in PX4, in bytes per second, not baud; 0 means baud/20, half the bandwidth of an 8N1 port. If the sum of “size × rate” of the streams exceeds the limit, the rates of all non-constant messages are multiplied by (limit − constant) / scalable, within 0.05…1.

title: GPS blending (`SENS_GPS_MASK`)
summary: Combining two receivers into one vehicle_gps_position solution in PX4: a receiver's weight is inversely proportional to the square of its reported error (speed, eph, epv, per the mask bits) and averaged over the enabled metrics. With mask 0 or without accuracy data, a hard selection by SENS_GPS_PRIME is used.

title: Adjustment slot
summary: A place for one active adjrange function in INAV: 4 slots (0…3), 20 lines. An active line takes a free slot, an inactive one frees it if its function is in it; with two active lines the slot goes to the line with the lower index. One function cannot be put into one slot twice.

title: Stick command
summary: A combination of end positions of the four sticks (LOW below min_check, HIGH above max_check) held for 0.4 s while disarmed: saving settings, calibrations, horizon trim, profile selection (in INAV with feature TX_PROF_SEL), missions, entering CMS. It does not work while armed, with the CLI open or in the CMS menu.

title: TX_PROF_SEL
summary: An INAV feature that allows selecting control profile and battery profile 1–3 with stick commands while disarmed. Changing the profile with the sticks writes the whole config to EEPROM; selecting a battery profile disables BAT_PROF_AUTOSWITCH auto-selection until reboot.

title: Geozone (FZ / NFZ)
summary: An area on the map with an altitude range that INAV 8+ takes into account when arming, in flight and during RTH. Inclusive (FZ) is a zone you must stay inside; exclusive (NFZ) is one you must not enter. Each zone has an action at the boundary: NONE, AVOID, POS_HOLD or RTH. CLI commands geozone and geozone vertex, feature GEOZONE, a board with more than 512 KB of flash.

title: RTH trackback
summary: An INAV return mode in which the aircraft first flies back along recorded points of its own path (up to 50 points) and only then directly home. Enabled with nav_rth_trackback_mode (ON or FS); the distance is limited by nav_rth_trackback_distance in meters.

title: Fixed-wing landing approach (fwapproach)
summary: An INAV record with the parameters of a landing site: loiter altitude, landing point altitude, the pattern side and two landing headings (positive — the reverse heading is also allowed, negative — this one only). Slots 0–7 are tied to the safehome with the same index, 8–16 to missions. From it INAV builds the downwind, base leg, final, glide and flare.

title: Pitot tube and indicated airspeed (IAS)
summary: A sensor of the difference between total and static pressure from which airspeed is computed. INAV computes indicated airspeed without an altitude correction: V = pitot_scale × √(2 × |ΔP| / 1.225). The sensor type is pitot_hardware (MS4525, MS5525, DLVR-L10D, ADC, MSP, VIRTUAL); the pressure zero is taken at every power-up.

title: Virtual pitot (pitot_hardware = VIRTUAL)
summary: An INAV airspeed estimate without a pressure sensor: GPS ground speed minus the component of the estimated wind along the nose, taking vertical speed into account. The wind estimate exists only on a plane; without it the full GPS speed is used. In 9.x the same estimate replaces a real pitot if its reading falls outside 30–200 % of it.

title: SURFACE (surface following in INAV)
summary: An INAV multirotor mode on top of ALTHOLD or POSHOLD: altitude is held above the surface by the rangefinder, and the throttle stick sets the height from 0 to nav_max_terrain_follow_alt. It needs both a barometer and a rangefinder; when a reliable AGL height is lost, the aircraft descends by itself. Planes do not have this mode.

title: LTM (LightTelemetry)
summary: A one-way telemetry protocol for narrow links: frames of `$T` + a type letter (A, G, S, O, N, X) + data + a checksum. INAV 9.1 has three schedules: NORMAL 303, MEDIUM 164 and SLOW 105 bytes/s; port function 16.

title: MSP RC Override
summary: An INAV mode in which the main receiver's channels marked in the `msp_override_channels` bit mask are replaced with values from `MSP_SET_RAW_RC`. Failsafe is still based only on the main receiver; after MSP frames stop, the values are held for 400 ms + `failsafe_delay` × 100 ms.

title: Port function mask
summary: The second field of a `serial` line: the sum of the UART function bits (MSP 1, GPS 2, LTM 16, SmartPort 32, RX_SERIAL 64, MAVLink 256 and so on). In INAV a port may have no more than two functions, and only the pairs MSP + telemetry / Blackbox or RX_SERIAL + LTM / IBUS; otherwise the port table is reset.

title: PINIO
summary: A discrete flight controller output (up to four, pins defined by the board) that follows a mode on the Modes tab. In INAV the mode is set by its permanent id in pinio_box1..4, usually USER1–4 (47, 48, 57, 58); logic controls it only through an RC channel override with operation 38.

title: User action (INAV mission action)
summary: Bits 1–4 of a mission waypoint's p3 field (values 2, 4, 8, 16). They turn nothing on by themselves: logic conditions see them as operands 6–13 of the “mission” type — “action active on this leg” and “on the next one”. Not the same as the USER1–4 modes.

title: LED Pin PWM
summary: An INAV LED pin mode: instead of a WS2812 strip, or together with it, the pin outputs 24 kHz PWM with a 0–100 % duty cycle. Enabled with the ledpinpwm command or logic operation 52; the idle behavior is set by led_pin_pwm_mode (SHARED_LOW, SHARED_HIGH, LOW, HIGH).

title: Control loop
summary: A closed chain “measurement → controller → actuator → plant → measurement again”: the angular rate loop, the angle loop, the position loop; in a nested scheme the inner loop is faster than the outer one. A rate loop is the angular rate control loop.

title: PID loop (looptime)
summary: The periodic run of the controller calculation in the firmware: at 8 kHz, once every 125 µs. The loop rate is how many times per second it runs, loop jitter is the spread of the period. Do not confuse it with the control loop: the control loop is what is connected to what, the PID loop is how often it is recomputed.

title: MagFit
summary: ArduPilot compass calibration from a flight log: the measured field from MAG messages is compared with the world model's expected field for the aircraft's coordinates and attitude, and offsets, scale, the DIA/ODI matrix and the COMPASS_MOT current compensation are fitted. The tool lives outside the firmware — in ArduPilot WebTools and in MAVExplorer.

title: Fitness (compass calibration)
summary: The root mean square of the residual between the compass readings and the fitted ellipsoid, in milligauss; smaller is better. ArduPilot accepts a rotation calibration if fitness is no more than COMPASS_CAL_FIT (16 by default) for an external compass in the first slot and twice that for the others.

title: Sum monitor (BATT_MONITOR = 10)
summary: A virtual ArduPilot battery monitor: it adds up the current and the consumed mAh of the monitors selected by the BATTn_SUM_MASK bits (bit 0 is monitor 1) and averages the voltage. Mask 0 means “all monitors numbered higher than mine”; unhealthy members are skipped without a warning.

title: AP_Notify
summary: The ArduPilot library that shows the vehicle's state with LEDs, a buzzer and a display. The firmware code sets flags (armed, pre-arm checks, failsafe, EKF) and events, and the device drivers selected by the NTF_LED_TYPES and NTF_BUZZ_TYPES masks turn them into a color, a pattern or a tune 50 times per second.

title: ProfiLED
summary: An addressable LED strip with two signal lines, data and clock. In ArduPilot the data comes from outputs with SERVOn_FUNCTION = 129–131 and the clock from output 132 in the same timer group; the type is enabled by bit 9 in NTF_LED_TYPES. Cube boards have a separate variant through the coprocessor (bit 19, since 4.7).

title: Lost Vehicle Sound (RCx_OPTION = 30)
summary: An ArduPilot switch function: the up position turns on a repeating locate sound on the buzzer and, while disarmed, on the motors over DShot. It does not arm the aircraft and works only while the receiver delivers channels, so it does not replace a standalone beacon.

title: Hot shoe feedback
summary: A signal from the camera's flash hot shoe to a GPIO pin of the flight controller at the moment the shutter fires. In ArduPilot it is set with CAM1_FEEDBAK_PIN and CAM1_FEEDBAK_POL; with it the command time is logged as TRIG and the frame time as CAM, and the geotag error from camera lag disappears.

title: Electropermanent magnet (EPM)
summary: A gripper that holds the payload's steel plate without drawing current and switches with a short pulse. In ArduPilot it is GRIP_TYPE = 2: the driver gives a GRIP_GRAB or GRIP_RELEASE pulse for 0.5 s and returns the output to GRIP_NEUTRAL; GRIP_REGRAB repeats the grab periodically.

title: Servo gimbal
summary: A camera gimbal on ordinary servos without its own controller. In ArduPilot it is MNT1_TYPE = 1: the flight controller subtracts the aircraft's tilt and converts the angle into a pulse linearly between SERVOn_MIN and SERVOn_MAX using the MNT1_*_MIN/MAX limits; a gimbal with its own controller needs type 7.

title: MAVLink Shell (`nsh` / `pxh` over MAVLink)
summary: The PX4 shell available over a MAVLink link through SERIAL_CONTROL messages with the device SERIAL_CONTROL_DEV_SHELL: QGC → Analyze Tools → MAVLink Console or Tools/mavlink_shell.py. It shows only the output of the command run in it; messages from other modules are read with dmesg. On the flight controller it is nsh (NuttX), in SITL it is pxh.

title: Startup default (`param set-default`)
summary: The middle layer of a PX4 parameter value: the default that the board scripts, the airframe and config.txt write over the firmware default at every boot. It is kept only in RAM. Only values that differ from the startup default go into the parameter file, so a value equal to it changes together with the airframe after a firmware update.

title: Used parameter (used, `param touch`)
summary: A PX4 parameter that at least one module or script has accessed after boot; marked with x in the param show output. QGC receives only used parameters from the firmware, so the parameters of a driver that is not running or of a disabled instance (MAV_1_* with MAV_1_CONFIG = 0) are not in the list even though they are in the build.

title: Mode slot (PX4, `COM_FLTMODEn`)
summary: One of the six segments of the `RC_MAP_FLTMODE` channel to which `COM_FLTMODE1…6` assigns a flight mode. The boundaries on the normalized scale: −0.786, −0.436, −0.086, +0.264, +0.614 (step 0.35); the channel center is slot 4, so a three-position switch selects slots 1, 4 and 6.

title: Switch threshold (PX4, `RC_*_TH`)
summary: A fraction 0…1 of channel travel that p = 0.5·v + 0.5 is compared with. A positive threshold enables the function when p > threshold, a negative one when p < |threshold|. The default is 0.75; the mirrored threshold for switching on in the down position is −0.25.

id: g:`PARAM_MAP_RC` (binding a knob to a parameter)
title: `PARAM_MAP_RC` (binding a knob to a parameter)
summary: The MAVLink message with which the GCS binds an `RC_MAP_PARAM1…3` channel to a PX4 parameter: param = clamp(value0 + scale·rc, min, max), where rc is the knob's normalized value, recomputed no more than once a second. The binding is kept in RAM (`rc_parameter_map`) and lost on reboot, while the written parameter value is kept.

title: Primary control (gimbal, PX4)
summary: The sysid/compid pair from which the PX4 gimbal manager accepts GIMBAL_MANAGER_SET_ATTITUDE and DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_PITCHYAW setpoints; it is assigned with DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE, and other senders get DENIED. `gimbal status` and GIMBAL_MANAGER_STATUS show the current owner.

title: `TRIG_MIN_INTERVA`
summary: The minimum interval between shutter releases in the PX4 camera_trigger driver, in ms (default 1). An earlier release is skipped, not delayed: when shooting by distance a whole frame drops out and the spacing doubles. Set it to the camera's minimum cycle.

title: Shutter feedback (`CAM_CAP_FBACK`)
summary: A signal from the camera's hot shoe to an FMU output with the Camera Capture function (2032): the PX4 camera_capture driver records the moment the shutter fires, so the camera_capture topic is built from real frames, not from trigger commands. It removes the v · τ geotag error and shows missed frames.

title: Quad-chute (PX4 VTOL)
summary: A forced transition of a VTOL from plane mode or a transition back to hover. In PX4 1.17 it triggers on minimum altitude (VT_FW_MIN_ALT), an uncommanded descent (VT_QC_ALT_LOSS), altitude loss during the transition (VT_QC_T_ALT_LOSS, 20 m by default), roll and pitch (VT_FW_QC_R/P), a transition timeout or an external command. After it commander executes COM_QC_ACT, but only in Mission, Hold and takeoff.

title: Airspeed envelope (FW_AIRSPD_*)
summary: The four calibrated airspeeds of a PX4 plane: STALL, MIN, TRIM (cruise), MAX. In a turn PX4 raises MIN and STALL by √n, n = 1/cos(bank); with WEIGHT_BASE/WEIGHT_GROSS by a further √(GROSS/BASE). Starting values: STALL = V_s, MIN = 1.25 V_s, TRIM ≥ MIN·√n at FW_R_LIM.

id: g:Airspeed scaling of the control surfaces (FW_ARSP_SCALE_EN)
title: Airspeed scaling of the control surfaces (FW_ARSP_SCALE_EN)
summary: A correction of the PX4 plane rate loop: s = FW_AIRSPD_TRIM / max(V, FW_AIRSPD_STALL); the P, I, D contribution is multiplied by s² and FF by s, because a surface's moment grows as V². Without a sensor in use, V = FW_AIRSPD_TRIM.

title: Shutter angle
summary: Shutter speed expressed as a fraction of the frame period: t = (angle/360)/fps. The 180° rule: t = 1/(2·fps), e.g. 1/120 s at 60 fps; a smaller angle makes motion choppy, a larger one blurs it. For heavy stabilization in Gyroflow use 90° or less: blur cannot be removed from a frame.

title: ND filter (stops, density)
summary: A neutral gray filter that passes 1/N of the light: ND8 is 12.5 %, 3 stops (log2 N), optical density 0.9 (lg N). An action camera without an aperture needs it to get a shutter-angle exposure in the sun; the number of stops needed is log2(t·2^EV/N²) at ISO 100.

title: Jello
summary: A wavy bending of straight lines in the frame: a rolling shutter sensor captures the rows at different moments while the camera vibrates from the props, motors or a frame resonance. It is fixed mechanically (balancing, camera mounting), not by flight controller filters; Gyroflow removes it only partly.

title: A2 CofC (A2 Certificate of Competency)
summary: A pilot certificate for subcategory A2 of the Open category (EU, UK): on top of A1/A3, self-practice and an additional theory exam (in the EU with the authority, ≥ 75 %); valid for 5 years.

title: Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate
summary: The FAA certificate for any non-recreational flying of small UAS: the UAG test at a testing center, form 8710-13 in IACRA, a TSA check; it stays current with online training every 24 calendar months.

title: good first issue
summary: An issue label in the tracker of an open-source project (for example ArduPilot) that the maintainers consider doable for a newcomer to the code base; a first contribution starts with one, with a docs fix or with a reproduced bug.

title: Radiometric thermal camera
summary: A thermal camera that measures and records the surface temperature in every pixel (quantitative thermography), not just relative brightness; you need it when the report must contain degrees. Accuracy depends on the set emissivity and needs at least 3 × 3 pixels on the target.

title: Application rate
summary: The volume of product per unit area, L/ha. Together with the swath width B and the speed v it sets the pump flow Q = q·B·v·60/10,000 L/min and the area per sortie S = V_tank/q.

title: Part 137 AAOC (Agricultural Aircraft Operator Certificate)
summary: The FAA agricultural aircraft operator certificate (form 8710-3); for UAS it is issued after obtaining an exemption number, including from § 107.36, which prohibits a small UAS from carrying hazardous materials.

title: Synthetic airspeed
summary: An airspeed estimate without a sensor: ground speed minus the EKF3 wind estimate (or DCM from GPS). ArduPlane uses it for the QuadPlane transition and TECS; without GPS it does not exist.

title: Tailsitter
summary: A VTOL that takes off and lands on its tail and pitches 90° to fly on the wing; in ArduPlane it is Q_TAILSIT_ENABLE, and the transition ends at the Q_TAILSIT_ANGLE angle (45°).

title: Q-assist
summary: Help from the QuadPlane lift motors in a plane mode without a mode change: at a speed below Q_ASSIST_SPEED (at once), an altitude below Q_ASSIST_ALT or an angle error above Q_ASSIST_ANGLE (after Q_ASSIST_DELAY).

title: Airbrake (a VTOL landing stage)
summary: The QuadPlane landing stage in which the lift motors spin up as an air brake; it starts at a distance of V²/(2·Q_TRANS_DECEL) + 2V from the waypoint and lasts at least 1 s.

title: QRTL
summary: The QuadPlane return mode with a vertical landing (number 21): near home it returns in hover at Q_RTL_ALT, from far away it flies as a plane and lands through the airbrake and POSITION1 stages.

title: AHRS (AP_AHRS)
summary: In ArduPilot, the front end of attitude, velocity and position estimation: every loop it picks the active backend (EKF3, DCM, EKF2, external AHRS, SIM) and hands its answer to the control loops; a change shows as the line “AHRS: EKF3 active” or “AHRS: DCM active”, and the selection parameter is AHRS_EKF_TYPE.

title: GSF (EKF-GSF, yaw estimator)
summary: A bank of five small filters with different initial headings inside EKF3 that finds the heading without a compass from the agreement of IMU accelerations with GPS velocity; EK3_SRC1_YAW = 8 makes it the heading source, and with a compass it is used for an emergency yaw reset (EK3_GSF_USE_MASK, no more than EK3_GSF_RST_MAX times per flight). Log XKY0.

title: EKF source set (EK3_SRCn)
summary: The five parameters EK3_SRCn_POSXY, _VELXY, _POSZ, _VELZ, _YAW that set where EKF3 takes position, velocity, height and heading from; there are three sets, the active one is changed in flight by a switch with RCx_OPTION = 90, by MAV_CMD_SET_EKF_SOURCE_SET or from Lua, and is logged in XKFS.SS.

title: Motor imbalance indices
summary: Three numbers from the medians of the motor outputs on a level segment of the log, in % of the average: pitch = rear pair minus front, roll = left minus right, yaw = diagonal 1+4 minus 2+3 (Betaflight Quad X). A CG offset gives only pitch/roll, motor tilt only yaw, and one weak motor gives three indices of the same size ≈ w/2.

title: Swap test
summary: Swapping the props, then the motors, between corners with the same rotation (in Quad X, 1 and 4 or 2 and 3), with a new log. If the imbalance moved with the prop, it is the prop; with the motor, the motor; if it stayed, the ESC, the arm or the mount. The mass does not move, so the CG estimate before and after must match.

title: motorOutput (Blackbox header)
summary: A Betaflight log header line with the lower and upper bounds of the motor command. For DShot the default is 158,2047 (dshot_idle_value 550, motor_output_limit 100), with dynamic idle 48,2047. Percent of travel = (motor − low)/(high − low)·100.

title: Feedforward jitter multiplier
summary: A factor 0…1 with which Betaflight damps FF for a small stick step per packet: in 4.5.3 it is 1 − (1 − (Δ + Δprev)/(2j))² for Δ < j, where j = feedforward_jitter_factor (default 7); in 2025.12 it is min(1, ((Δ + Δprev)/2 + 1)/(1 + j)). Logged in debug FEEDFORWARD_LIMIT[0] in percent.

title: Feedforward boost
summary: An addition to feedforward from setpoint acceleration: boost/1000·Δv·f_rx (feedforward_boost, default 15, 0…50). It compensates for the motor spin-up lag at the start of a sharp stick movement; in 4.5.3 on all axes, in 2025.12 only on roll/pitch.

title: Duplicate RC packet
summary: A packet in which the channel has not changed because the radio updates channels less often than the link transmits (for example the EdgeTX mixer at 4 ms on ELRS 500 Hz). Betaflight 4.5.3 substitutes the previous setpoint rate for the first duplicate and zero for the following ones; in 2025.12 this extrapolation is disabled for CRSF.

title: A/B comparison (ABA, ABBA)
summary: A comparison of two setups that differ in one parameter: A is the control, B the change, one flight program, several flights per arm. The ABA or ABBA order splits the drift of conditions (wind, heating, battery) almost evenly between the arms; AAAAA BBBBB blocks put all the drift on the difference.

title: Permutation test
summary: A check of whether a difference between groups is random: all splits of the numbers into two groups of the same size are enumerated, and p is the share of splits where the difference of means is at least the observed one. Normality is not needed; the minimum two-sided p with n flights per arm is 2 / C(2n, n), so with n ≤ 3, p < 0.05 is unreachable.

title: Tracking error
summary: How far the angular rate lags behind the commanded one: the RMS of setpoint − gyroADC over a maneuver segment, °/s. In Betaflight Blackbox it is computed from the setpoint[0..2] and gyroADC[0..2] fields.

title: TPA (Throttle PID Attenuation)
summary: A D multiplier (and P with tpa_mode = PD) in Betaflight that falls linearly from tpa_breakpoint to 1 − tpa_rate/100 at full throttle: 0.35 with the 65/1350 defaults. Low-throttle TPA (tpa_low_*) weakens D near zero until the first pass of tpa_low_breakpoint after power-up.

title: Thrust linearization (thrust_linear)
summary: A Betaflight mixer correction: motor command = x·(1 + k·(1 − x)²), k = thrust_linear/100. It raises the slope near zero to 1 + k, at x = 1/3 the slope is 1 again; the collective throttle is divided in advance by 1 + (k − k²/2)(1 − t)² so the hover point does not move.

title: Sag compensation (vbat_sag_compensation)
summary: A Betaflight cut of the top of the motor range by the cell voltage under load: from 0 at vbat_warning_cell_voltage to (4.20 − V_warn)/4.20 at 4.20 V (16.7 % at 100 % and a 3.50 V threshold). The 4.20 V top point is hard-coded.

title: Anti-gravity
summary: A temporary boost of I (Ki + 0.34·AG) and P on roll and pitch during fast throttle changes in Betaflight: the throttle derivative, weighted toward low throttle, through a PT2 at anti_gravity_cutoff_hz and the anti_gravity_gain gain. Against the nose dip on punch-outs and chops.

title: Throttle boost
summary: Throttle boost in the Betaflight mixer: t + throttle_boost/10 · (t − PT1(t)), cutoff throttle_boost_cutoff (15 Hz by default). It hides the motor spin-up lag; TPA and anti-gravity see the throttle without the boost.

title: eRPM
summary: The electrical rpm of the motor that the ESC reports over bidirectional DShot (in Betaflight in units of 100). Mechanical rpm = eRPM / (number of magnets / 2); the fundamental harmonic frequency = rpm / 60.

title: RPM filter fade range
summary: The band rpm_filter_fade_range_hz above rpm_filter_min_hz in which the notch weight rises linearly from 0 to 1 (default 50 Hz above 100 Hz). Below min_hz the notch is pinned at min_hz with weight 0, i.e. off.

title: Harmonic weight (rpm_filter_weights)
summary: A share of 0–100 % for each RPM filter harmonic: output = w·notch + (1 − w)·input, so the depth at the center is limited to 20·lg(1 − w): 80 % → −14 dB, 50 % → −6 dB; 0 passes the harmonic.

title: Commutation timing (motor timing, advance)
summary: How early the phases switch relative to the back-EMF zero crossing, in electrical degrees: the ESC commutes 30° − angle after the zero. Bluejay: steps 1–5 = 0 / 7.5 / 15 / 22.5 / 30° (default 4 = 22.5°); AM32: byte 10–42 = (byte − 10)·0.9375°. Higher gives more rpm and more margin against desync, but a hotter motor.

title: Demag compensation
summary: Protection against desync: after commutation the current in the switched-off winding decays (demagnetization) and can hide the back-EMF zero. Bluejay computes a demag metric and above a threshold (Low 160, High 130) cuts power for a step; AM32 waits 1.25 intervals for a missed zero, coasts and recovers with power reduced by 1/32–1/8 (`demag_comp` 2–4).

title: EDT safety arm
summary: An ESC setting (Bluejay: EDT safety arm, AM32: `input_type` = 4): the motor does not accept throttle until the flight controller sends DShot command 13 (enable EDT). Betaflight sends it on every arming attempt only if `dshot_edt = ON` and bidir DShot is working; otherwise the aircraft arms but the motors do not spin.

title: BUILD KEY
summary: The 32-character Betaflight cloud build key baked into the firmware (BUILD_KEY): the status command prints it as the line “BUILD KEY: …”; with it, build.betaflight.com/api/builds/<key>/json returns the list of build options. A local build has no key.

title: Custom Defines
summary: The Expert Mode field in the Betaflight flasher: extra build flags separated by spaces without the USE_ prefix (the server adds it), for example RANGEFINDER, GPS_LAP_TIMER, TRANSPONDER.

title: CLOUD_BUILD
summary: The flag a Betaflight cloud build is compiled with: it turns off the classic feature set of common_pre.h, so only what is in the options list goes into the firmware (DShot must also be listed explicitly). Locally it is set with OPTIONS="CLOUD_BUILD USE_…".

title: UID (ExpressLRS)
summary: The 6-byte address of an ELRS link: the first 6 bytes of the MD5 of the string -DMY_BINDING_PHRASE="phrase". Bytes 2–5 set the hopping seed, 4–5 the CRC seed; UID4 and UID5 are sent in the clear in the SYNC packet. Not encryption.

title: Model Match
summary: An ELRS feature: the module mixes the receiver number from EdgeTX (0…63) into the low 6 bits of UID5 in the SYNC packet; a receiver with a different stored number keeps the link but does not pass channels to the flight controller (“Model Mismatch”).

title: LBT (Listen Before Talk)
summary: The ELRS CE_LBT build mode for the EU (EN 300 328): before every transmission the radio measures the channel RSSI and skips the packet if it is not below the threshold (−71 dBm for LoRa at 100 mW). Power is limited to 100 mW; TQly shows the share of allowed transmissions.

title: rxfail (channel value on link loss)
summary: The Betaflight CLI `rxfail <channel> <a|h|s> [µs]`: what the FC puts into a channel 300 ms after packets are lost, armed or disarmed. `a` — sticks and throttle only (center, minimum), `h` — the last value (the default for AUX), `s` — a fixed value in 25 µs steps within 750–2250. AUXn = index 3 + n; `rxfail <3 + n> s 2000` on the BEEPER channel turns the buzzer on at link loss.

title: WAS_EVER_ARMED
summary: The Betaflight flag “the aircraft has armed since power-up”: set in `disarm()` (except a disarm from a crash flip) and kept until reboot. In 4.5 RX_LOST does not sound without it, so an FC that rebooted from an impact stays silent; in 2025.12 the RX_LOST condition was replaced with “no USB”.

title: Lost model alarm (standalone buzzer)
summary: A buzzer with its own cell or supercapacitor: connected to the aircraft's 5 V, it starts beeping when that power is gone. The only source of sound if the main battery came off in the crash: the FC buzzer, the DShot beacon and the ESC beacon are silent without it.

title: OSD element position (osd_*_pos)
summary: The 16-bit value of an OSD element in Betaflight: x in bits 0–4 and 10 (up to 63), y in bits 5–9, visibility in OSD profiles 1–3 in bits 11–13, the display variant in bits 14–15; without a profile bit the element is hidden.

title: OSD profile (osd_profile)
summary: One of three visibility masks of OSD elements in Betaflight: positions are shared, bits 11–13 in osd_*_pos differ; switched in the CLI, CMS or from a switch through adjrange with function 29.

title: MAX7456 font (.mcm)
summary: 256 characters of 12×18 px at 2 bits each in the non-volatile memory of the analog OSD chip; characters 160–255 are the 288×72 px boot logo, so uploading another font replaces the logo too.

title: Lua widget (EdgeTX)
summary: A /WIDGETS/<name>/main.lua script for a color radio that returns a table with name, options, create, update, refresh, background; it draws in its screen zone while the zone is visible, otherwise its background runs.

title: getSourceValue (EdgeTX Lua)
summary: An EdgeTX 2.12 Lua API function: returns the value of a source and the isCurrent and isFresh flags; after telemetry is lost it returns the last value with isCurrent = false, whereas getValue returns 0.

title: CPU limit (EdgeTX Lua)
summary: The error with which EdgeTX stops a widget call that runs longer than ~20,000 Lua instructions (a hook every 200 instructions); the widget is disabled and the error text is written into its zone.

title: mavsdk-grpc
summary: A PyPI package with the old gRPC client of MAVSDK-Python (import mavsdk_grpc): since MAVSDK v4 the name mavsdk is taken by the native binding, and the old API lives under this name.

title: Mission placeholder item (ArduPilot)
summary: The first item of a plan, uploaded into seq 0 only to take up the slot: ArduPilot keeps home there and overwrites what was uploaded, so without a placeholder the first waypoint of the route is lost.

title: MAVn_* (MAVLink channels, ArduPilot 4.7)
summary: The parameter group of a MAVLink channel in ArduPilot 4.7+: stream rates (MAVn_EXT_STAT, MAVn_POSITION …) and options; n is the sequence number of the MAVLink channel (the console is MAV1), not the SERIAL number. Before 4.7: SRn_*.

title: GUID_TIMEOUT
summary: An ArduCopter parameter: after how many seconds without new velocity, acceleration or angle targets GUIDED zeroes the setpoint (3 s by default, 0.1–5 s); position targets have no timeout.

title: MAV_COMP_ID_ONBOARD_COMPUTER (191)
summary: The standard compid of an onboard computer: the companion runs under its vehicle's sysid and this compid so that the autopilot accepts it as its own component.

title: micro-ROS Agent
summary: A process on the companion (micro_ros_agent) that accepts a Micro XRCE-DDS session from the client in the firmware over UDP or UART and creates a participant, topics and services in the ROS 2 DDS network on its behalf.

title: DDS_MAX_RETRY
summary: An AP_DDS parameter: the number of agent pings in one batch (10 by default, 0 — no batches); after a failed batch the GCS gets “No ping response, exiting”, but in 4.7.2 the client keeps trying.

title: Copy-on-Write (pandas 3)
summary: A pandas mode that is always on since version 3.0: any selection from a table behaves as a copy. The chain `df[col][mask] = v` does not change the original table (pandas raises ChainedAssignmentError); make the edit in one step: `df.loc[mask, col] = v`.

title: ArduPilot batch sampler (ISBH/ISBD)
summary: Logging batches of raw IMU samples at the sensor rate for spectral analysis: `INS_LOG_BAT_MASK` selects the IMU, `INS_LOG_BAT_CNT` (1024 by default) the batch length. The ISBH header carries the type (0 — accelerometer, 1 — gyro), the multiplier `mul` and the rate; the value in rad/s = ISBD.x / ISBH.mul.

title: merge_asof
summary: Joining two pandas tables by the nearest time instead of an exact match: every row of a slow message (ATT, 10 Hz) gets the nearest row of a fast one (RATE, 400 Hz) no further than `tolerance`. Both tables must be sorted by time.

title: MSP (MultiWii Serial Protocol)
summary: The binary protocol the Configurator and scripts use to talk to Betaflight over the same port as the CLI. A v1 frame: `$M<`, length, command, data, XOR checksum; reply `$M>`, error `$M!`. Identifying the board without entering the CLI: MSP_API_VERSION (1), MSP_FC_VARIANT (2), MSP_FC_VERSION (3; in 2025.12 the year − 2000), MSP_NAME (10), MSP_UID (160).

title: validateAndFixConfig
summary: A Betaflight function (config/config.c) that silently fixes incompatible combinations of settings on save and at every boot: for example it zeroes a d_max smaller than D (2025.12), resets the GPS-RESCUE failsafe_procedure to DROP without feature GPS, and turns off dshot_bidir without DShot. That is why values are re-read with get after save.

title: Non-interactive CLI (STX/ETX, Betaflight 2025.12)
summary: A CLI mode for programs: byte 0x02 enters the CLI without echo, prompt or the arming block, the firmware replies 0x02 and executes the lines sent; byte 0x03, or no first byte within 2 s of entering, ends the session without a reboot (reply 0x03). Not present in 4.5.x.

title: Action pinning by SHA
summary: Referring to a GitHub Actions action by the full commit SHA (`uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5…  # v7.0.1`) instead of a tag: the owner can move a tag to another commit, a SHA does not move. The version stays in a comment and is updated in a separate PR.

title: Mutation test
summary: Testing the test itself: introduce one breakage into a known-good config (for example `FS_THR_ENABLE = 0`) and make sure the CI or the SITL test turns red with exactly one error. A test that does not fail on the mutant protects nothing.

title: Fleet manifest (fleet.yaml)
summary: A file in the config repository that records the stack, the firmware version and the config path for every aircraft, and the obstacle height for a site. It is checked with JSON Schema; the invariant script takes the version from it to pick the rules, and the site-dependent thresholds.

title: Error budget (uncertainty budget)
summary: A table of contributions to the uncertainty of a result with each one's share of the variance u_i²/u_c²; it shows which experiment will reduce the total and which refinement is useless (in the R-02 example the scale contributes 0.3 %).

title: Expanded uncertainty U
summary: U = k·u_c, where u_c is the combined standard uncertainty; with k = 2 the interval y ± U covers about 95 % for a normal distribution (GUM, JCGM 100:2008).

title: Guard band
summary: A decision rule for conformity that takes uncertainty into account (JCGM 106:2012): the requirement y ≥ L is met if y − U ≥ L, not met if y + U < L, and otherwise “not proven”.

title: Callback group
summary: A set of ROS 2 node callbacks with a concurrency rule: MutuallyExclusive runs them one at a time, Reentrant at the same time; the node's default group is MutuallyExclusive, so a MultiThreadedExecutor without your own groups gives no parallelism.

title: RxO (requested vs offered)
summary: The QoS compatibility rule in ROS 2/DDS: there is a connection only if for every policy (reliability, durability, deadline, liveliness, lease) the subscriber requests no more than the publisher offers; otherwise the subscription silently receives no data.

title: Node composition (component container)
summary: Loading several rclcpp nodes written as components into one process (`component_container`, `_mt`, `_isolated`); with `use_intra_process_comms` messages are passed by pointer without serialization; rclpy has no such mechanism.

title: Focal length in pixels (f_px)
summary: f_px = f / p_mode = (W/2)/tan(HFOV/2): the factor that converts angles into pixels; it enters the K matrix, the GSD, rotational blur (ω·t·f_px) and rolling shutter skew. For the CM3 at 2304×1296 it is about 1693 px.

title: Motion blur
summary: The smearing of a point during the exposure: v·t/GSD from translation and ω·t·f_px from rotation; at altitude rotation dominates (1/500 s, 90°/s — 5.3 px vs 0.7 px from 10 m/s at 50 m).

title: Frame readout time (rolling shutter readout)
summary: The interval t_r between the exposure of the first and last rows of a rolling shutter sensor, no longer than the frame period; during a rotation it gives a skew of up to ω·t_r·f_px (90°/s at 30 fps and f_px 1693 — up to 89 px).

title: Thermal runaway
summary: Self-heating of a lithium cell faster than ~10 °C/min: from ~80 °C exothermic reactions heat the cell by themselves, from ~135 °C the separator melts and an internal short begins, from 180 °C the cathode releases oxygen, so smothering the flame does not put it out — it has to be cooled.

title: SEI (solid electrolyte interphase)
summary: The protective film on the anode surface of a lithium cell; it breaks down from about 90 °C, releasing flammable gases — one of the causes of swelling and the first stage of thermal runaway.

title: Storage voltage
summary: The cell voltage for storage and transport: 3.80–3.90 V for LiPo (Gens Ace spec), 3.6–3.7 V for Li-Ion; a charger's Storage mode brings the pack to it by charging or discharging.

title: Mission Planner
summary: The ArduPilot ground station for Windows (1.3.83 as of November 2026): the full parameter list, calibrations, missions, MAVFtp, DataFlash log analysis.

title: QGroundControl (QGC)
summary: A cross-platform ground station for PX4 and ArduPilot (Windows, macOS, Linux, Android; 5.1.5 as of November 2026); the main GCS for PX4.

title: MSP API version
summary: The version number of the MSP protocol that a Betaflight/INAV flight controller reports to the configurator (2025.12 — 1.47); the configurator uses it to decide whether it can configure this firmware: Betaflight App 2026.6.2 accepts ≥ 1.44.

title: colcon
summary: The ROS 2 workspace build tool (replacing catkin_make / catkin build): `colcon build --symlink-install`, `colcon test`; the result is the build/, install/, log/ directories, the environment is `source install/setup.bash`.

title: RMW (ROS middleware)
summary: The ROS 2 layer through which nodes communicate over DDS or Zenoh; the implementation is chosen by `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION`, `rmw_fastrtps_cpp` by default; nodes with different RMWs generally cannot see each other.

title: ROS_DOMAIN_ID
summary: The DDS domain number: participants in different domains do not discover each other; the safe range on Linux is 0–101. It replaces the isolation a separate roscore gave in ROS 1.

title: Mahony filter
summary: A complementary attitude filter on a quaternion: the error e = (−a/|a|) × v between the measured and expected “down” is mixed into the angular rate as Kp·e + Ki·∫e. Without Ki it leaves a constant tilt error b/Kp. Used in Betaflight (imu_dcm_kp 0.25) and INAV.

title: Madgwick filter
summary: An attitude filter that at every step takes a normalized gradient descent step of fixed size β (in units of the quaternion derivative, ≈ 2β rad/s of angular rate) toward the direction of gravity from the accelerometer; β = √(3/4)·ω̄_β. Not used in Betaflight, INAV, ArduPilot or PX4; common in Arduino and ROS (imu_filter_madgwick).

title: Angle random walk (ARW)
summary: The growth of angle error from gyro white noise: σ = N·√t, where N is the noise density in °/s/√Hz (0.005 °/s/√Hz = 0.3 °/√h). Over 2 minutes that is hundredths of a degree — attitude is spoiled by bias (b·t), not by noise.

title: Current shunt
summary: A fraction-of-a-milliohm resistor in the power path; the current is found from the drop U = I·R amplified by an op-amp. 0.25 mΩ at 100 A gives 25 mV and 2.5 W of heat. Linear, but the amplifier's zero offset needs an offset calibration.

title: Two-point current sensor calibration
summary: Finding a sensor's slope and offset from two or more currents measured with a clamp meter (a low and a high current). Unlike a calibration from one flight's mAh, it is accurate over the whole range: with a 50 mV sensor offset a one-point calibration is off by +74 % at 2 A, a two-point one by less than 0.5 %.

title: Nyquist frequency
summary: Half the sampling rate f_s/2: everything above it shows up after digitizing at a false frequency |f − k·f_s|. An oscilloscope with 10k points of memory at 100 ms/div samples at 10 kHz and draws 24 kHz ESC ripple as 4 kHz.

title: Antispark (precharge)
summary: Charging the power bus capacitor through a resistor before the main contact closes: an XT90-S connector or a switch with a resistor. 10 Ω with 1040 µF gives 2.5 A instead of hundreds of amps, done in 5τ = 52 ms; without it every 6S connection loses ~0.33 J in a spark on the pins.

title: LC filter quality factor (Q)
summary: How many times the filter amplifies interference at its resonance f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)): Q = √(L/C)/(DCR + ESR). 22 µH and 470 µF with a polymer capacitor (ESR 0.01 Ω) give Q 3.6, a +11 dB peak; with ESR 0.15 Ω it is +2.9 dB, but the attenuation at the ESC frequency is worse.

title: Inductor saturation current (I_sat)
summary: The current above which the inductor core saturates and the inductance drops sharply: the LC filter stops working exactly at the current peak. For a VTX power filter choose I_sat ≥ 1.5 × the branch's peak current (course guideline).

title: MESSAGE_VERSION (the _vN suffix)
summary: A constant in a PX4 message definition (.msg). If it is greater than 0, the uXRCE-DDS client adds the suffix _vN to the ROS 2 topic name: VehicleLocalPosition version 1 goes as /fmu/out/vehicle_local_position_v1. The version is bumped on an incompatible change of fields (VehicleStatus: v1 in PX4 1.17, v4 in 1.18).

title: dds_topics.yaml
summary: A file in src/modules/uxrce_dds_client of the PX4 firmware listing the uORB topics that the uXRCE-DDS client publishes to ROS 2 (/fmu/out) and receives (/fmu/in), with a rate_limit. A topic missing from the file is missing in ROS 2; the list changes only by rebuilding the firmware.

title: JetPack
summary: The NVIDIA software package for Jetson modules: Jetson Linux (L4T: kernel, drivers, Ubuntu) plus CUDA, TensorRT, cuDNN. The JetPack version determines Ubuntu and therefore the ROS 2 distribution: as of November 2026, JetPack 7.2.2 is Ubuntu 24.04 (Jazzy), JetPack 6.2.x is Ubuntu 22.04 (Humble).

title: Super Mode (Jetson Orin)
summary: The higher-power modes of the Orin Nano and Orin NX introduced in JetPack 6.2 (for example 25 W and MAXN SUPER on the Orin Nano 8 GB, 67 TOPS instead of 40). Available only if the board is flashed with a configuration with the -super suffix; check with sudo nvpmodel -q.

title: I²C pull-up
summary: A resistor from the SDA or SCL line to the supply: devices on an I²C bus only pull the line to ground, and the pull-up raises it to “1” by charging the bus capacitance. The resistance is limited from below by the output current (≥ 967 Ω at 3.3 V and 3 mA) and from above by the allowed rise time: Rp ≤ t_r / (0.8473·Cb).

title: CAN terminator
summary: A 120 Ω resistor between CAN_H and CAN_L at each of the two ends of a CAN/DroneCAN bus; it suppresses reflections. On an unpowered bus a multimeter between H and L reads 60 Ω with correct termination and 120 Ω if one terminator is missing.

title: 5V-tolerant input
summary: A pin of a 3.3 V microcontroller that withstands 5 V on its input without damage. Most STM32 pins are, but not all (pins with analog functions are not); when in doubt, use a divider or a level shifter.

title: Lockstep (SITL)
summary: A SITL mode in which the firmware and the physics model step on a shared simulated clock: the model computes a step at SIM_RATE_HZ (1200 Hz), the firmware replies with PWM. That is why time can be sped up (--speedup), and intervals in scripts must be measured by time_boot_ms.

title: eeprom.bin
summary: The SITL parameter storage file in the working directory; the values saved in it override the --defaults files. The -w switch erases it at startup.

title: RTL cone (RTL_CONE_SLOPE)
summary: A limit on the Copter return altitude near home: the altitude is no more than d·RTL_CONE_SLOPE (3 by default), but not below the current one. Right above home RTL does not climb to RTL_ALT_M.

title: SCR_VM_I_COUNT
summary: The Lua VM instruction limit per call of an ArduPilot script (10000 by default); exceeding it gives the message “exceeded time limit” and stops the script until reboot.

title: Script parameter table (param:add_table)
summary: A Lua script's own parameters with a unique prefix and a table key; they are visible in the GCS and saved like ordinary parameters.

title: DO_JUMP
summary: Mission command 177: jump to command param1, param2 repeats (−1 — forever). A repeat count of N gives N + 1 passes of the segment.

title: MAVLink mission protocol
summary: The mission upload/download dialog: MISSION_COUNT, then the receiving side requests each command with MISSION_REQUEST_INT by number, and at the end MISSION_ACK (0 — accepted).

title: EIRP (effective isotropic radiated power)
summary: Transmitter power plus antenna gain minus cable loss, in dBm: what you would have to feed into an isotropic antenna for the same field. Regulatory power limits are written in EIRP.

title: Fresnel zone
summary: An ellipsoid around the line of sight in which most of the received energy forms; the radius of the first zone at the middle of the path is 17.32·√(d/(4f)) m (d in km, f in GHz). Keep at least 60 % of the radius clear.

title: Radio horizon
summary: The maximum line-of-sight range with standard refraction (k = 4/3): ≈ 4.12·(√h₁ + √h₂) km with antenna heights in meters. Beyond the horizon the link is lost regardless of the budget margin.

title: Load factor (n)
summary: The ratio of lift to weight; in a coordinated turn n = 1/cos φ. The stall speed grows as √n; ArduPlane uses it to limit the bank (STALL_PREVENTION).

title: Equivalent airspeed (EAS)
summary: The speed that at sea level (ρ = 1.225 kg/m³) would give the same dynamic pressure. The stall is constant in EAS at any altitude; the AIRSPEED_* parameters in ArduPlane are set in EAS, and the true airspeed TAS = EAS·√(ρ₀/ρ).

title: STALL_PREVENTION
summary: ArduPlane protection against a stall in a turn: the bank is limited to arccos(1/n_max), n_max = (V/AIRSPEED_STALL)², no lower than 25°, and the TECS minimum speed is raised by √n. With AIRSPEED_STALL = 0, AIRSPEED_MIN is taken as the stall speed.

title: EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax)
summary: A set of templates for wording requirements with the keywords WHILE (state), WHEN (event), IF … THEN (unwanted behavior), WHERE (option) and an always-active form. Proposed at Rolls-Royce (Mavin et al., 2009).

title: Verification methods I/A/D/T
summary: Inspection, analysis (including models and SITL), demonstration and test per the NASA Systems Engineering Handbook §5.3; the method is stated for every requirement.

title: RPN (Risk Priority Number)
summary: The product of the severity, occurrence and detection ratings (S·O·D, each 1–10) in FMEA; it sets the order in which risks are closed, but takes only 120 distinct values and hides high severity, so lines with S ≥ 9 are reviewed separately.

title: Log-odds (occupancy grid)
summary: Storing a cell's occupancy probability as L = ln(p/(1 − p)): every beam hit or pass adds a constant, and back p = 1 − 1/(1 + e^L). L is clamped from above and below so the map can update when an obstacle leaves.

title: Weighted A*
summary: A* with the heuristic multiplied by w > 1: it expands fewer cells, but the path is no longer guaranteed to be the shortest; the guarantee is no longer than w × the optimum.

title: Dijkstra (OA_TYPE = 2, ArduPilot)
summary: The ArduPilot object avoidance planner for the geofence: it moves the vertices of exclusion polygons out by OA_MARGIN_MAX along the bisector and finds the shortest path on the visibility graph; it works in Auto, Guided and RTL only with the geofence enabled.

title: Frozen pose
summary: A VIO failure in which tracking is lost but the bridge keeps sending the last pose with new timestamps. The EKF innovation stays small and the gates do not catch it; in ArduCopter 4.7.2 SITL the aircraft drifted 6–10 m in 20 s with XKF4.SP ≤ 0.01. The fix is a detector on the companion: if the pose has not moved 1 mm in 0.5 s, stop publishing.

title: reset_counter (MAVLink)
summary: A field of VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE and ODOMETRY: a value incremented by one tells the EKF that a pose jump is a source reset (VIO reinitialization, a SLAM loop closure), and the filter moves the estimate in one step instead of rejecting it at the gates.

id: g:Unobservable degrees of freedom of VIO
title: Unobservable degrees of freedom of VIO
summary: Position x, y, z and heading: the camera and the IMU know them only relative to the first frame, so their error grows without bound (drift). Scale, roll and pitch are observable — gravity and accelerations set them — but monocular VIO needs accelerated motion for scale.

title: Pseudorange
summary: The range to a satellite measured by the receiver: the signal propagation time × c, including the receiver clock error c·Δt (1 ms is 300 km). That is why Δt is the fourth unknown, and a solution needs at least 4 satellites.

title: UERE (user equivalent range error)
summary: The total error of one pseudorange (ionosphere, troposphere, orbit, multipath, receiver noise), usually a few meters for a single-frequency receiver. The horizontal position error ≈ HDOP × UERE.

title: Multipath
summary: Receiving a satellite signal reflected from buildings, the ground or the frame together with the direct one or instead of it: the pseudorange gets longer, and the position jumps by meters to tens of meters with a normal number of satellites. The fix is antenna placement, a ground plane and a helix antenna; RTK does not remove it.

text: Build sheet: weight, motors, props, battery, T/W, estimated flight time Board map: UARTs, power pads, BEC Photo of the motors with rotation direction A preflight checklist for your own drone Project engineering folder: requirements with IDs, what was tested and how, changelog (see the "Engineering Method 101" module) All numbers taken from datasheets or measurements, with sources cited Calculated hover current checked against a measurement (wattmeter, current sensor in the log or thrust stand), discrepancy explained Motor directions checked without props and match the diagram The checklist includes items on props, battery, antennas and area Every requirement traces to a test or measurement, with the result recorded

title: Onboard electrical system, with calculations

title: An aircraft built to a spec
summary: An aircraft design for a given mission: calculations, a powertrain test on the stand (or from the dataset), stability or mixer, prediction compared with measurement
text: The spec in numbers: payload, flight time, wind, dimensions, margin A sizing script in the repository with a closed mass budget and the configuration choice Thrust stand data for the chosen motor/prop pair (your own or from the module dataset): g/W, C_T, uncertainty budget For a wing: CG and static margin; for a non-standard multirotor: the effectiveness matrix and a saturation check If the aircraft is built: a hover or flight log and a comparison with the prediction Every number in the spec traces to a calculation, and every calculation to a datasheet, a stand measurement or a flagged assumption Mass budget closed, the calculation reproduces with a single command Predicted flight time or hover current checked against a measurement (or the dataset), discrepancy explained Configuration choice justified by comparing at least two options

title: Your own attitude filter
summary: A complementary filter or a simple EKF in Python/ESP32, validated on real IMU data against a reference

title: An X8 octo with payload or a VTOL wing
summary: parameters, a SITL mission, a real flight, log analysis
text: A parameter file with a date and the rationale for key decisions A mission run in SITL on the target frame (octa-quad or quadplane) Motor failure test in SITL (octo) or an output map and a ground transition test (VTOL) A real flight log and its analysis: VIBE, ERR, ATT, BAT Project engineering folder: requirements with IDs, what was tested and how, changelog (see the "Engineering Method 101" module) Pre-arm passes without disabling checks Radio/GCS/battery failsafes configured before autonomous flight Log analysis starts with vibration and errors For VTOL: arming only from a switch, tilt checked on the ground Every requirement traces to a test or measurement, with the result recorded

title: Your own logic + an ESP32 module
summary: a working module, an exchange protocol, a README and tests
text: Repository: firmware/, lua/ or a companion service, docs/ Exchange protocol: every message, its fields, who is allowed to send it README with installation and usage Tests: echo/heartbeat, timeout, companion failure Demo in SITL (and in the air only with a geofence and a pilot) Project engineering folder: requirements with IDs, what was tested and how, changelog (see the "Engineering Method 101" module) The undefined state is the safe one (FLIGHT, radio off) Protection against dangerous in-flight actions duplicated on both sides Every MAVLink command is confirmed by ACK A companion failure doesn't affect the FC, demonstrated by a test Every requirement traces to a test or measurement, with the result recorded

title: Target tracking
summary: The companion detects an object in video and makes the vehicle follow it in SITL/in the field via GUIDED/Offboard
text: Camera → detector → command pipeline Latency and FPS measurements Demo in SITL with a simulated camera Safety protocol: geofence, timeouts, pilot Project engineering folder: requirements with IDs, what was tested and how, changelog (see the "Engineering Method 101" module) Frame-to-command latency measured and below 150 ms Target loss leads to a hover, not wandering Real flight only with a geofence and a pilot Every requirement traces to a test or measurement, with the result recorded

title: An INAV aircraft from scratch
summary: A quadcopter or wing on INAV, set up from a blank board: a 5-waypoint mission and a tested failsafe with return to home
text: Platform choice (quadcopter or wing) and a build sheet: weight, motors, battery, estimated flight time The `diff all` configuration before and after setup, with a comment on every changed parameter Calibration record: voltage and current vs. a multimeter and charger, compass, accelerometer (wing: CG, control surface throws) SITL rehearsal of the setup: `diff all`, arming flags, restoring the configuration on a blank board; flight and RTH in SITL are optional (they require RealFlight or X-Plane) Log of a real flight: position hold, a 5-waypoint mission, failsafe from a switched-off radio with return to home A one-page setup card for your aircraft The configuration restores from `diff all` on a blank board without manual edits Voltage error under 0.05 V per cell, consumed mAh within 5 % of the charger Failsafe tested: the log shows the signal loss, the switch to RTH and the landing or loiter over home RTH landing within 5 m of the launch point (wing: loiter over home at the set altitude) Every anomaly in the log explained or fixed

title: PX4 from scratch to a mission
summary: A PX4 multirotor set up in QGroundControl from a blank board: SITL rehearsal, failsafe matrix, mission and ULog analysis
text: SITL rehearsal (Gazebo or SIH): the same airframe, the same motor geometry, the mission and every failsafe scenario The parameter file after setup with comments on the changed values Failsafe matrix: RC loss, telemetry loss, low battery, geofence breach, with the expected and observed action in SITL and on hardware Vehicle Setup record: sensors, radio, Actuators (geometry and motor test), power (voltage divider and current sensor vs. a multimeter) ULog of a real flight and a Flight Review report: hover in Position, mission, RTL If you have no hardware yet: the full SITL set now, the hardware part submitted later against the same criteria Every row of the failsafe matrix tested and confirmed by a log Motor test matches the geometry in Actuators: number, position and direction of each motor Voltage in QGC differs from the multimeter by no more than 0.05 V per cell The Flight Review report has no unexplained warnings; vibration and attitude tracking analyzed

title: Project 1: Web GCS: telemetry, map, flight modes
summary: A ground control station in the browser: the backend reads MAVLink and serves telemetry over WebSocket; the frontend draws the vehicle on a map, shows the flight mode, battery and STATUSTEXT, and can arm and change modes with confirmation.
text: Python 3, pymavlink, asyncio WebSocket (websockets) JS, Leaflet, no framework ArduPilot SITL MAVLink → JSON bridge over WebSocket: HEARTBEAT, GLOBAL_POSITION_INT, ATTITUDE, SYS_STATUS, STATUSTEXT A page with a map and a vehicle marker, mode and battery on a panel Commands from the browser: arm/disarm and mode changes via COMMAND_LONG waiting for an ACK, response in the UI Robustness: link loss detected within 3 s (heartbeat timeout), reconnection without a page reload Recording a session to a tlog and replaying it in the same UI Bridge tests (pytest) pass on a fake vehicle, including packet loss Telemetry latency in the UI ≤ 300 ms on localhost (measurement in the report) A command without an ACK is not shown to the user as executed Link loss and recovery displayed without a reboot A README: one-command launch with SITL, screenshot, architecture Backend and frontend code separated, WebSocket protocol described in docs/

title: Project 2: Fleet telemetry to the cloud + dashboard
summary: Each vehicle publishes compressed telemetry to MQTT through its companion; a service stores it in a time-series database, Grafana displays the fleet, and alerts fire on battery, link loss and EKF.
text: MQTT (Mosquitto) Python-ingest InfluxDB or TimescaleDB Grafana Docker Compose Topic schema and message format (JSON/CBOR), version in every message Publisher on the companion: 1–5 Hz, buffering while the network is down Ingest into the database with schema validation and a vehicle tag Fleet dashboard: map, battery, flight modes, link Alerts: battery, no data for > 10 s, EKF failsafe Ingest test: 3 fake vehicles × 10 min with no lost records A 60 s network outage loses no data (the buffer resends it) The message schema is versioned; old clients do not break ingest Dashboard and alerts deploy with a single docker compose up Traffic volume per vehicle per hour described

title: Project 3: Log analysis service
summary: A report with findings from a flight log: vibration and clipping, battery sag and internal resistance, errors, GPS, attitude tracking error. Every finding has a threshold and an explanation; the report is a single HTML file.
text: Python, pymavlink blackbox_decode (Betaflight) matplotlib → embedded SVG/PNG pytest on synthetic logs DataFlash analysis: VIBE, BAT, ERR, GPS, ATT, MODE, MSG Checks with thresholds and severity, JSON output HTML report with plots and a flight-mode timeline Betaflight Blackbox input via blackbox_decode EKF checks (XKF4) and regression tests on your own logs Tests on synthetic logs with known defects pass Non-zero exit code on any FAIL-level finding (suitable for CI) Every finding includes the value, the threshold and what to do about it The report opens without internet Tested on at least 3 of your own real logs; conclusions match manual analysis

title: Project 4: Detector + tracker + following in Gazebo
summary: A simulated camera → detector (YOLO-nano or color-based) → tracker → controller that keeps the target centered in the frame at a set distance using velocity setpoints in Offboard/GUIDED.
text: ROS 2 Humble Gazebo + PX4 or ArduPilot SITL OpenCV, ONNX Runtime examples/ros2-docker Camera stream from Gazebo into ROS 2, FPS measured Detector with metrics on a recorded bag A tracker with IDs and prediction during dropouts Follow controller (starter: follow.py, a pure function with limits and a target-loss watchdog), latency measured A simulator scenario with a moving target and target loss Camera → command latency measured and ≤ 150 ms When the target is lost for > 1 s, the vehicle hovers instead of continuing to move Velocities limited, the Offboard timeout does not trigger in normal operation Test on a bag: the detector finds the target in ≥ 90 % of frames Video: 2 minutes of following without losing the target

title: Project 5: Precision landing on a marker in simulation
summary: ArUco marker on the landing pad, downward-facing camera, marker pose estimation, LANDING_TARGET to the autopilot (or velocity control), landing with an error below 15 cm.
text: OpenCV ArUco MAVLink LANDING_TARGET or ROS 2 ArduPilot PLND / PX4 precision land Gazebo A synthetic camera in SITL without Gazebo (starter: target_sim.py + lt_sender.py), then ArUco on the Gazebo camera Conversion to the vehicle frame (FRD/NED) Sending LANDING_TARGET, verification in the log SITL landing in wind Failure: marker lost below 2 m Landing error ≤ 15 cm in 9 out of 10 runs Marker loss is handled: climb away or a normal landing, not a crash Constant camera latency measured and set in PLND_LAG Coordinate frames verified by a test The log shows the autopilot using the target README and video

title: Project 6: Route inspection with georeferenced findings
summary: A mission along a line (power line, pipeline, fence), distance-based image capture, automatic georeferencing of frames, and a report with findings on a map.
text: ArduPilot missions, CAM1_TRIGG_DIST / DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST EXIF/XMP geotags Python, Leaflet report Mission generator along a polyline with overlap Distance-based triggering, CAM log with shutter feedback (CAM1_FEEDBAK_PIN) Matching frames to CAM log entries, writing geotags Tagging findings and a map report Georeferencing accuracy checked against control points Every frame has coordinates, discrepancy with the log ≤ 1 frame The report opens offline, findings are clickable Georeferencing accuracy measured against control points Mission tested in SITL before flight README

title: Project 7: Photogrammetry on an open dataset
summary: An orthomosaic and a terrain model from an open image dataset using OpenDroneMap; accuracy assessment at checkpoints and an analysis of what it depends on.
text: OpenDroneMap (Docker) QGIS Python for the metrics Running ODM on an open dataset Orthophoto and DEM, viewed in QGIS Accuracy metric at checkpoints (starter: checkpoints.py; GCPs are not included in the evaluation) Experiment: overlap and resolution versus accuracy A plan for your own survey mission with GSD calculation Orthophoto and DEM produced, run parameters saved RMSE at checkpoints computed and explained An experiment with two settings and a conclusion GSD and overlap calculation for your own mission README

title: Project 8: MAVLink component on ESP32 + SITL twin
summary: An ESP32 as a full MAVLink component: its own heartbeat and compid, a sensor (rangefinder or current) in DISTANCE_SENSOR/BATTERY_STATUS, and command handling. A Python twin of the same component passes the same tests against SITL and a fake vehicle.
text: ESP-IDF or PlatformIO, C c_library_v2 Python twin (examples/mavlink) ArduPilot SITL Python twin passes the tests (starter: virtual_rangefinder.py) ESP32 firmware: UART MAVLink, heartbeat, DISTANCE_SENSOR Receiving COMMAND_LONG with ACK The autopilot uses the component (RNGFND1_TYPE=10), verified in the log Test bench: ESP32 ↔ USB-UART ↔ SITL on a PC The twin and the firmware behave identically on the same test suite The component doesn't interfere with others: correct sysid/compid, rate ≤ the declared one The autopilot sees the sensor, RFND in the log shows plausible values UART loss does not hang the firmware (watchdog) README, wiring diagram

title: Project 9: 4G/Wi-Fi bridge with reconnection and encryption
summary: The companion maintains the GCS ↔ vehicle link over a cellular network: VPN (WireGuard), MAVLink routing, reconnection, prioritizing commands over telemetry, and behavior on link loss.
text: WireGuard mavlink-router Python or Go tc/netem to simulate a bad network VPN between the companion and the server, auto-reconnect MAVLink routing through a tunnel Simulating loss and latency (netem), measurements Reducing the telemetry rate on a poor link Vehicle-side failsafe on GCS loss tested At 20 % loss and 300 ms latency, commands get through with acknowledgment 30 s dropout: the link recovers on its own Traffic encrypted, outward-facing ports closed Vehicle behavior on GCS loss matches the parameters and is verified in SITL Report with measurements

title: Project 10: CI/CD for a fleet
summary: The fleet's parameters and scripts live in git; every commit runs a failsafe test and a mission in SITL, compares parameters against a reference, and builds an artifact for deployment to the vehicle.
text: GitHub Actions ArduPilot SITL pymavlink parameters in .param, Lua scripts Fleet repository: parameters per vehicle, shared and individual Workflow: SITL + failsafe test (starter ci.yml) Parameter diff against a reference, with each change explained Mission test and log check by the grader Deployment: an artifact with parameters and a checklist Every PR runs the SITL tests; a red test blocks the merge A change to a critical parameter without a comment fails the check SITL logs saved as an artifact Deployment is reproducible: the same parameter set from a tag README

title: Project 11: A Lua safeguard package with tests
summary: A set of ArduPilot Lua scripts for your mission (vibration monitoring, polygon geofence, payload protection), each with a SITL test and clear behavior when the script itself fails.
text: ArduPilot Lua scripting SITL pymavlink tests Script skeleton: parameters, rate, logging, error handling The first safeguard and its SITL test Two more safeguards Behavior on script error: safe mode Parameter documentation Every safeguard has a SITL test that triggers it An error in the script doesn't leave the vehicle unprotected Script parameters documented CPU and memory measured README

title: Project 12: Companion module for the TX16S radio
summary: An ESP32 module in the radio's bay: receives CRSF telemetry, shows it on its own display or sends it to a phone over BLE/Wi-Fi, plus an EdgeTX Lua script on the radio. Developed against an emulator before the hardware.
text: ESP32, ESP-IDF/PlatformIO CRSF EdgeTX Lua + the EdgeTX simulator Parsing CRSF telemetry on the ESP32 with tests on recorded frames EdgeTX Lua script in the simulator Sending to a phone (BLE or Wi-Fi) Mounting and power inside the radio Field test The CRSF parser passes tests on recorded frames, including corrupted ones The radio keeps control when the module hangs Lua script works in the simulator and on the radio Power consumption measured README with a diagram
